Истраживачки рад усмерен је на аутоматско препознавање говора деце у морфолошки богатим језицима, са посебним нагласком на адаптацију акустичких модела и регуларизацију језичких модела за јувенилне говорнике са нестандардном прозодијом. Чланови групе користе лабораторију за обраду говорног сигнала опремљену вишеканалним микрофонским решеткама, анехоичном комором и рачунарском инфраструктуром за обуку дубоких неуронских мрежа. Предаје предмете из области дигиталне обраде сигнала и говорних технологија на основним и мастер студијама.
Open to: заједнички пројекти са компанијама у области образовних технологија и говорних интерфејса; уговорна истраживања везана за прилагођавање АПГ система специфичним домен-условима; надзор индустријских докторанада; приступ опреми лабораторије (анехоична комора, микрофонске решетке, GPU кластер); студентске стручне праксе у области обраде говора.
Industry experience: У периоду 2016–2017. године сарађивао је са компанијом за развој образовног софтвера из Новог Сада на интеграцији говорног интерфејса у апликацију за учење читања, у улози спољног саветника за обраду говора.
Notes: Тренутно води два дипломска рада и један мастер рад везане за тему пројекта EduVoice-RS-HU; капацитет за нове пројекте је умерен до краја 2026. године. Предност даје сарадњи са партнерима који имају приступ дечијем говорном материјалу или конкретном апликативном контексту (нпр. образовне платформе, логопедска пракса).

R0147.title: Isidora Kovačević
R0147.text:
Isidora Kovačević (R0147): Associate Professor, Department of Management, Technical Faculty "Mihajlo Pupin" Zrenjanin, University of Novi Sad.
Fields: Management and Organization; Public Administration; Knowledge Management; Organizational Learning.
Keywords: knowledge management maturity; public sector; post-socialist transition; organizational learning; knowledge audit; institutional capacity; Serbia; Central and Eastern Europe; change management; tacit knowledge.
Bio: Isidora Kovačević diplomirala je na Fakultetu tehničkih nauka u Novom Sadu 2004. godine, a doktorsku disertaciju odbranila je 2013. na Tehničkom fakultetu „Mihajlo Pupin“ u Zrenjaninu, gde je od 2015. zaposlena u zvanju docenta, a od 2021. u zvanju vanrednog profesora. Njena istraživačka grupa bavi se merjenjem zrelosti upravljanja znanjem u javnim institucijama, sa posebnim fokusom na tranzicione ekonomije centralne i jugoistočne Evrope. Predaje predmete Menadžment znanja, Organizaciono učenje i Upravljanje promenama. U radu koristi softver za kvalitativnu analizu (ATLAS.ti) i alate za statističku obradu podataka (SPSS, R), kao i institucionalne baze podataka opština i javnih preduzeća u Vojvodini.
Open to: joint projects with technology park companies on knowledge management system design and assessment; contract research: knowledge audits and maturity assessments for companies or public institutions; consulting on organisational learning and knowledge retention for companies undergoing rapid staff growth or restructuring; industrial PhD supervision for candidates with a background in management, public administration, or organisational studies; student internships involving data collection, survey administration, or qualitative research support.
Industry experience: Kovačević je u periodu od 2015. do 2017. godine učestvovala kao ekspert-konsultant u projektu modernizacije poslovnih procesa za jedno javno komunalno preduzeće u Zrenjaninu, u okviru kojeg je sprovela dijagnostiku upravljanja znanjem i predložila plan internih obuka. Nema iskustva u privatnom sektoru van konsultantskih angažmana.
Notes: Kovačević trenutno mentoriše dva doktoranda i opterećenje nastavom je standardno za njeno zvanje; dostupna je za nove projekte počev od akademske 2025/2026. godine. Interesuje je saradnja s kompanijama u oblasti upravljanja znanjem i organizacionog razvoja, naročito ako one poseduju sopstvene podatke koje bi bilo moguće analizirati u zajedničkim istraživačkim studijama. Preferira angažmane u kojima postoji jasno definisana istraživačka komponenta, a ne isključivo primenska konsultantska uloga.

R0164.title: Sofija Mirković
R0164.text:
Sofija Mirković (R0164): Assistant Professor, Department of Computing and Control Engineering, Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad.
Fields: Computer Security; Embedded Systems; Program Analysis; Software Engineering.
Keywords: symbolic execution; dynamic taint analysis; firmware analysis; binary analysis; vulnerability discovery; embedded systems security; network-attached devices; fuzzing; static analysis; exploit development.
Bio: Sofija Mirković received her B.Sc. and M.Sc. degrees in Computer Engineering from the Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad, in 2010 and 2012 respectively, and her Ph.D. from the same institution in 2018, with a dissertation on scalable symbolic execution for vulnerability detection in stripped ARM binaries. She was a visiting researcher at TU Graz in 2016–2017. Since 2019 she has held an Assistant Professor position in the Department of Computing and Control Engineering. Her group focuses on automated bug-finding in firmware of routers, industrial gateways, and IoT devices, combining binary analysis, fuzzing, and taint tracking. She teaches courses on system security and reverse engineering. The group uses a dedicated testbed of physical embedded devices and licenses IDA Pro and Binary Ninja for disassembly work.
Open to: joint projects with companies performing security assessments of embedded or IoT products; contract research on firmware vulnerability analysis for specific device families; industrial PhD supervision for candidates employed at NTP Novi Sad companies; student internships involving binary analysis or fuzzing tool development; consulting on embedded device security architecture and secure firmware update mechanisms; equipment access to the physical device testbed and licensed disassembly tools for short-term collaborations.
Industry experience: Sofija conducted a six-month consulting engagement in 2020 with Automatika d.o.o., a Novi Sad-based industrial automation company, to assess the security of firmware running on their serial-to-Ethernet gateway product line. The engagement resulted in eight confirmed vulnerability reports and a revised secure development checklist adopted by the company.
Notes: Sofija is currently supervising two PhD students funded through FIRMSHIELD and has limited capacity for new long-term commitments until mid-2025. She has expressed a strong preference for collaborations where the company can share actual firmware images under NDA, rather than purely theoretical engagements. She is not interested in pure penetration testing work that does not involve research questions.

R0193.title: Igor Matić
R0193.text:
Igor Matić (R0193): Associate Professor, Department of Computing and Control Engineering, Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad.
Fields: embedded software; automotive systems.
Keywords: AUTOSAR; ISO 26262; functional safety; hardware-in-the-loop; model-based testing.
Bio: Igor Matić is an Associate Professor in the Department of Computing and Control Engineering at the Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad. His research focuses on embedded software engineering and automotive systems, with particular emphasis on AUTOSAR-compliant architectures, ISO 26262 functional safety standards, hardware-in-the-loop testing, and model-based testing methodologies. Before entering academia, he spent eight years as a software engineer and technical lead at an automotive software supplier in Novi Sad, gaining extensive hands-on experience with production-grade embedded control units. He actively collaborates with industry partners on safety-critical software development and supervises industrial PhD candidates working at the intersection of academic research and automotive practice.
Open to: industrial PhD supervision; joint projects.
Industry experience: Eight years with an automotive software supplier in Novi Sad.

R0206.title: Vesna Knežević
R0206.text:
Vesna Knežević (R0206): Assistant Professor, Department of Power, Electronics and Telecommunications, Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad.
Fields: Embedded Systems and IoT; Signal Processing; Machine Learning for Edge Devices; Condition Monitoring and Fault Diagnostics.
Keywords: vibration signal compression; edge inference; adaptive sampling; microcontroller deployment; neural network quantisation; rotating machinery diagnostics; compressive sensing; real-time DSP; fault detection; hardware-software co-design.
Bio: Vesna Knežević received her B.Sc. and M.Sc. degrees in Electrical Engineering from the Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad, in 2009 and 2012 respectively, and her Ph.D. from the same institution in 2018, with a thesis on adaptive data reduction for vibration monitoring in rotating machinery. She joined the Department of Power, Electronics and Telecommunications as a Teaching Assistant in 2013 and was promoted to Assistant Professor in 2019. Her group focuses on resource-constrained signal processing: compressing high-frequency vibration streams on microcontroller-class hardware, deploying quantised neural networks for fault detection without cloud offloading, and designing adaptive sampling schemes that meet latency and power budgets. She teaches courses on digital signal processing and embedded systems. The group regularly uses a Kistler piezoelectric sensor array, an oscilloscope bench with 200 MHz bandwidth, and STM32- and RISC-V-based development platforms.
Open to: joint projects with companies needing embedded condition monitoring solutions; contract research on microcontroller-based signal processing and TinyML deployment; industrial PhD supervision for candidates with embedded systems background; student internships on firmware development and sensor node prototyping; consulting on neural network quantisation and edge inference optimisation; equipment access (bearing test rigs, Kistler sensor array, STM32 and RISC-V development platforms).
Industry experience: Vesna Knežević has collaborated with two small companies at NTP Novi Sad on pilot deployments of vibration sensor nodes for conveyor and CNC applications within the EDGEVIB project, including firmware integration and on-site calibration work.
Notes: She is currently finalising the EDGEVIB project (ending late 2025) and would be well positioned to take on a new industry contract or Horizon Europe work package starting from mid-2026. She has expressed a preference for collaborations where the company can provide labelled operational data from real machinery, as the group's existing datasets are all from controlled laboratory rigs.

R0233.title: Valentina Stojanović
R0233.text:
Valentina Stojanović (R0233): Associate Professor, Department of Computing and Control Engineering, Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad.
Fields: Software Engineering and Testing; Embedded Systems; Formal Methods; Computing and Control Engineering.
Keywords: model-based testing; mutation testing; embedded firmware; automated regression testing; formal specification; test case generation; state machine models; hardware-in-the-loop testing; test adequacy criteria; control software verification.
Bio: Valentina Stojanović received her B.Sc. and M.Sc. degrees in Computer Engineering from the Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad, in 2004 and 2007 respectively, and her Ph.D. in 2012 from the same institution with a dissertation on mutation-based adequacy criteria for embedded control software. She was appointed Assistant Professor in 2013 and Associate Professor in 2018. Her group focuses on formal specification languages for firmware behaviour, automated generation of test suites from state-machine and contract-based models, and regression testing strategies for resource-constrained embedded systems. She teaches courses on software testing, formal methods, and embedded systems at both undergraduate and graduate levels. The group uses a lab equipped with JTAG debuggers, hardware-in-the-loop rigs, and several microcontroller development platforms for validation experiments.
Open to: joint projects with companies developing or testing embedded firmware; contract research on automated testing toolchain development; industrial PhD supervision for candidates from technology companies; consulting on test process improvement for embedded software teams; student internships in the testing and formal methods lab.
Industry experience: Stojanović conducted a two-year action research collaboration with a regional industrial electronics firm producing programmable logic controllers, contributing to the introduction of formal specification practices in their firmware development workflow. She has provided short-term consulting to two additional companies in the automotive electronics sector on test adequacy assessment.
Notes: Stojanović has a preference for collaborations where research access to real firmware codebases or development histories is possible; anonymised datasets are acceptable. The lab has hardware-in-the-loop rigs available for collaborative experiments. She is not seeking pure consulting arrangements but is open to industry contracts that include a research output component.

R0258.title: Zoran Vukelić
R0258.text:
Zoran Vukelić (R0258): Full Professor, Department of Serbian Language and Linguistics, Faculty of Philosophy, University of Novi Sad.
Fields: Computational Linguistics; Lexicography and Lexical Resources; Corpus Linguistics; Cross-lingual Information Retrieval.
Keywords: multilingual lexical resources; Serbian morphology; cross-lingual information retrieval; Slavic–Germanic language contact; bilingual professional corpora; finite-state morphology; wordnet construction; terminological databases; contrastive linguistics; morphologically rich languages.
Bio: Zoran Vukelić completed his undergraduate and master's studies at the Faculty of Philosophy, University of Novi Sad, and received his PhD in Linguistics from the same institution in 2003, with a dissertation on morphological encoding in Serbian–German contact lexicons. He joined the Department of Serbian Language and Linguistics as an assistant professor in 2004 and was promoted to Full Professor in 2016. His research group focuses on building multilingual lexical databases, developing morphological analyzers for inflectionally rich Slavic languages, and studying cross-lingual information retrieval in bilingual professional corpora where Serbian interacts with German or Hungarian. He teaches courses on computational lexicology, corpus linguistics, and contrastive grammar. The group regularly uses the Sketch Engine corpus platform, custom finite-state morphological tools, and a departmental annotated corpus of approximately 120 million tokens.
Open to: joint projects with companies needing multilingual text processing or terminology management; contract research on building domain-specific bilingual lexicons or morphological analyzers; consulting on cross-lingual document search and retrieval system design; student internships for computational linguistics or software engineering students; industrial PhD supervision for candidates working on Serbian NLP in professional domains.
Industry experience: During the VOITERM project, Vukelić collaborated directly with the translation unit of the Provincial Secretariat and with two manufacturing companies from the NTP Novi Sad area to collect and validate domain terminology. He has provided informal consulting on text search systems to a Novi Sad-based software company developing document management tools for Serbian public institutions.
Notes: Vukelić is currently in the final year of CROSSLEX and has capacity for one new collaboration starting in late 2025 or 2026. He prefers engagements where linguistic expertise is genuinely central rather than peripheral. He is not equipped for speech processing or acoustic work; his group's tools and data are text-only.

R0265.title: Emilija Kapor
R0265.text:
Emilija Kapor (R0265): PhD student, Department of Computing and Control Engineering, Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad.
Fields: Speech and Language Technology; Signal Processing; Machine Learning; Human–Computer Interaction.
Keywords: automatic speech recognition; Serbian language; telephone speech; noisy channel ASR; acoustic modelling; Kaldi; low-resource ASR; noise robustness; end-to-end ASR; speech corpus.
Bio: Emilija Kapor received her Bachelor's degree in Electrical and Computer Engineering from the Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad in 2021, and her Master's degree from the same institution in 2022, where she is currently a third-year PhD student in the Department of Computing and Control Engineering. Her doctoral research focuses on automatic speech recognition (ASR) for Serbian spoken over telephone channels, with particular attention to noise robustness and low-resource acoustic modelling. She works within the Speech and Language Technologies Laboratory under the supervision of Associate Professor Dragan Vukić, a group that maintains corpora of Serbian telephone speech and uses Kaldi and ESPnet toolkits on GPU clusters. She assists in teaching the undergraduate course on Digital Signal Processing.
Open to: joint projects on speech technology for Serbian or regional languages; contract research on call-centre speech analytics or voice-based customer service automation; student internships in speech data annotation or ASR system evaluation; access to TelSrp-100 corpus under data-sharing agreement.
Industry experience: During summer 2022, Emilija worked for three months as a data annotation contractor for a Belgrade-based voice analytics startup, where she labelled and quality-checked transcriptions of customer-service call recordings.
Notes: Currently in the third year of her PhD with an expected defence in late 2026 or early 2027; available for collaboration that aligns with her doctoral timeline. Prefers projects where Serbian-language data or telephone channel conditions are relevant, as this overlaps directly with her dissertation work.

R0286.title: Ana Rajić
R0286.text:
Ana Rajić (R0286): Full Professor, Department of Power, Electronics and Telecommunications, Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad.
Fields: Телекомуникације и бежичне мреже; Безбедност уграђених система; Индустријска информатика и теlemетрија; Криптографски протоколи.
Keywords: firmware update protocols; LPWAN; industrial telemetry; authenticated firmware delivery; intermittent wireless links; low-bandwidth networks; SCADA security; LoRaWAN; delta patching; cryptographic authentication.
Bio: Ана Рајић је редовни професор на Катедри за енергетику, електронику и телекомуникације Факултета техничких наука Универзитета у Новом Саду. Дипломирала је 2001. и докторирала 2009. године на истом факултету, са тезом о протоколима за безбедну дистрибуцију фирмвера у индустријским мрежама са ограниченим пропусним опсегом. Њена истраживачка група бави се аутентификацијом и интегритетом фирмвера у телеметријским системима са прекидном бежичном везом, укључујући LPWAN технологије и индустријске SCADA окружења. Предаје курсеве из безбедности уграђених система и протокола бежичних мрежа. Лабораторија располаже опремом за емулацију деградираних канала, LoRaWAN и Zigbee развојним платформама, као и алатима за формалну верификацију криптографских протокола.
Open to: joint projects with industry on firmware security for industrial IoT deployments; contract research on protocol design and evaluation for OTA update systems; industrial PhD supervision for candidates with embedded systems background; consulting on IEC 62443 firmware security compliance; equipment access: LoRaWAN testbed, Zigbee development platforms, channel emulator.
Industry experience: Сарађивала је са домаћим произвођачем система за даљинско очитавање бројила (AMI) на пројекту испоруке фирмвера преко PLC-а и бежичних веза у дистрибутивној мрежи у периоду 2016–2018. године. Поред тога, учествовала је као технички саветник у пројекту надоградње SCADA телеметријског система за водопривредно предузеће.
Notes: Тренутно надгледа четири докторанда и активно тражи индустријске партнере за примену резултата пројекта SAFELINK. Заинтересована искључиво за сарадњу у домену индустријске безбедности уграђених система; не прихвата консалтинг изван овог домена.

R0288.title: Katarina Nikolić
R0288.text:
Katarina Nikolić (R0288): Associate Professor, Department of Serbian Language and Linguistics, Faculty of Philosophy, University of Novi Sad.
Fields: corpus linguistics; morphology.
Keywords: Serbian morphology; lemmatization; corpora; inflection; spelling variants.
Bio: Katarina Nikolić is an Associate Professor in the Department of Serbian Language and Linguistics at the Faculty of Philosophy, University of Novi Sad. Her research focuses on corpus linguistics and morphology, with particular emphasis on Serbian inflectional paradigms, lemmatization, spelling variants, and the construction of large-scale reference corpora. She is the principal investigator of KORPUS-NS, a flagship project aiming to build a comprehensive reference corpus of contemporary Serbian. Professor Nikolić has contributed extensively to the development of language processing tools tailored to the morphological complexity of Serbian, and her work bridges theoretical linguistics with practical computational applications relevant to industry and digital humanities.
Open to: industrial PhD supervision; joint projects.

R0341.title: Milana Bošković
R0341.text:
Milana Bošković (R0341): Assistant Professor, Department of Computing and Control Engineering, Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad.
Fields: Software Engineering; Formal Methods; Enterprise Systems Integration; Model-Driven Engineering.
Keywords: model-driven engineering; enterprise integration patterns; formal specification; interface adaptation; metamodeling; ATL transformations; architectural conformance; message routing; protocol mediation; Alloy.
Bio: Milana Bošković received her B.Sc. and M.Sc. degrees in Computer Engineering from the Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad, in 2008 and 2010, respectively, and her Ph.D. in Computer Science from the same institution in 2016, with a thesis on formal verification of enterprise integration pattern compositions. She held a postdoctoral position at the University of Ljubljana from 2017 to 2019 before returning to Novi Sad as an Assistant Professor. Her research group works on model-driven engineering approaches to software architecture, with a particular focus on formalising enterprise integration patterns and automating the adaptation of system interfaces under evolving integration constraints. She teaches courses on software architecture, formal methods, and middleware design. The group regularly uses the Eclipse Modeling Framework, Alloy Analyzer, and an in-house model transformation toolchain built on ATL.
Open to: joint projects with companies needing formal specification or automated adapter generation; contract research on integration architecture assessment; industrial PhD supervision for candidates embedded in companies with integration-heavy systems; student internships on toolchain development or case-study evaluation; consulting on enterprise integration architecture and API design.
Industry experience: During the FORMIGA project Bošković worked directly with two Vojvodina manufacturing companies to apply the adapter generation toolchain to their ERP–MES integration problems, including on-site requirements elicitation and iteration on generated artefacts. She also provided paid consulting to a regional logistics company in 2022 on the architectural restructuring of their message-broker configuration.
Notes: Bošković is on leave until September 2026 and is available for new project discussions and contract negotiations from that point onward; she remains reachable by email and can participate in online meetings during the leave period.

R0349.title: Stefan Dragić
R0349.text:
Stefan Dragić (R0349): Full Professor, Department of Mathematics and Informatics, Faculty of Sciences, University of Novi Sad.
Fields: Information Retrieval; Natural Language Processing; Text Mining; Computational Linguistics.
Keywords: information retrieval; script normalization; transliteration; Serbian text; mixed-script indexing; Cyrillic-Latin; inverted index; query expansion; morphological analysis; corpus linguistics.
Bio: Stefan Dragić je diplomirao matematiku na Prirodno-matematičkom fakultetu Univerziteta u Novom Sadu 2001. godine, a doktorirao je 2008. na istom fakultetu, s tezom o indeksiranju višeskriptnih tekstualnih korpusa. Nakon postdoktorskog boravka na Univerzitetu u Beču (2009–2010), vratio se na Departman za matematiku i informatiku, gde je 2019. izabran u zvanje redovnog profesora. Njegova istraživačka grupa bavi se pronalaženjem informacija u dokumentima koji sadrže mešovito ćirilično-latinično srpsko pismo, normalizacijom skripte, transliteracijom kao korakom u pretprocesiranju i izgradnjom invertovanih indeksa otpornih na varijacije pisma. Predaje kurseve iz upravljanja bazama podataka i rudarenja teksta. Laboratorija koristi sopstvene korpuse pravnih i novinarskih tekstova.
Open to: joint projects with companies that manage large Serbian-language document collections; contract research on internal search engine customization; consulting on script normalization and multilingual indexing; industrial PhD supervision for candidates with a software background; student internships (master's level) focused on NLP pipeline development.
Industry experience: U periodu 2022–2023. sarađivao je s jednim novosadskim startapom iz oblasti legaltech-a na prilagođavanju pretražnog modula za srpske sudske odluke, u okviru ugovornog istraživanja trajanja 18 meseci.
Notes: Dragić preferira saradnju s kompanijama koje imaju jasno definisan i dovoljno veliki tekstualni korpus na srpskom jeziku; nije zainteresovan za opšte projekte razvoja softvera bez istraživačke komponente. Trenutno je angažovan na dva aktivna projekta, ali ima kapaciteta za jedan manji industrijski ugovor ili konsultantski angažman.

R0356.title: Darko Ninkov
R0356.text:
Darko Ninkov (R0356): Senior Research Associate, Department of Mechatronics, Robotics and Automation, Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad.
Fields: Mechatronics and Embedded Systems; Automotive Electronics and ECU Testing; Real-Time and FPGA-Based Control; Hardware-in-the-Loop Simulation.
Keywords: hardware-in-the-loop; ECU validation; FPGA I/O emulation; real-time simulation; open-source real-time target; CAN bus; automotive embedded systems; fault injection; rapid control prototyping; low-cost test bench.
Bio: Darko Ninkov received his B.Sc. and M.Sc. degrees in Mechatronics Engineering from the Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad, in 2005 and 2008 respectively, and his Ph.D. in Electrical and Computer Engineering from the same institution in 2013. He joined the Department of Mechatronics, Robotics and Automation as a Research Associate in 2013 and was promoted to Senior Research Associate in 2019. His group focuses on hardware-in-the-loop simulation, real-time control platforms, and FPGA-based I/O emulation primarily for automotive ECU testing. He teaches courses on embedded systems and real-time programming at undergraduate and master levels. The laboratory operates several open-source real-time targets based on ARM and x86 architectures, a suite of Xilinx-family FPGA boards, CAN/LIN/FlexRay bus interfaces, and bench-level power supply and fault-injection hardware.
Open to: contract research on ECU test bench development; joint projects with automotive ECU suppliers or Tier-1 companies; industrial PhD supervision in real-time systems and FPGA-based I/O emulation; student internships on FPGA board bring-up and Linux real-time configuration; equipment access for FPGA development boards and CAN/FlexRay bus analysers; consulting on selecting and configuring open-source real-time platforms.
Industry experience: Ninkov collaborated with two regional automotive ECU suppliers under non-disclosure agreements during the HILVOP project, providing bench design support and test case development. He has also delivered short technical training sessions for engineering teams at a Novi Sad-based electronics manufacturing company.
Notes: Prefers projects where at least part of the results can be published; willing to negotiate publication embargoes of up to 18 months for industry contracts. Currently supervising two doctoral students, so capacity for new long-term commitments is limited until mid-2027.

R0386.title: Ognjen Ninkov
R0386.text:
Ognjen Ninkov (R0386): Research Associate, Department of Psychology, Faculty of Philosophy, University of Novi Sad.
Fields: Organisational Psychology; Educational Psychology; Cognitive Psychology; Human Factors.
Keywords: knowledge transfer; workplace learning; onboarding; cognitive load theory; situated learning; learning curves; instructional design; time-to-competency; training effectiveness; experience sampling.
Bio: Ognjen Ninkov completed his undergraduate and master's studies in psychology at the University of Novi Sad, Faculty of Philosophy, graduating in 2009 and 2012 respectively. He received his PhD from the same institution in 2018, with a dissertation examining cognitive load as a predictor of time-to-competency in structured workplace onboarding programmes. He joined the Department of Psychology as a Research Associate in 2019. His work focuses on how new employees acquire job-relevant knowledge, with particular attention to instructional design, the sequencing of training materials, and the role of prior knowledge in learning efficiency. He teaches courses in work and organisational psychology and research methods. The group uses eye-tracking equipment and experience-sampling software for data collection, and collaborates regularly with the department's applied cognitive lab.
Open to: joint projects; contract research; student internships; consulting; equipment access (eye-tracking lab).
Industry experience: Ninkov has carried out two short consulting engagements for companies in the Novi Sad area, advising on the redesign of their formal induction programmes based on cognitive load principles. He has maintained ongoing data-collection partnerships with three companies participating in the COGONBOARD field trial.
Notes: Ninkov is currently mid-way through the COGONBOARD project and has limited capacity for large new commitments until mid-2026. He is particularly interested in collaborations with technology or logistics companies at NTP Novi Sad that could serve as field sites. Access to the department's eye-tracking lab can be arranged for joint projects with prior agreement.

R0564.title: Árpád Nagy
R0564.text:
Árpád Nagy (R0564): Full Professor, Department of Computing and Control Engineering, Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad.
Fields: Network Security; Autonomous and Multi-Agent Systems; Graph Theory and Applied Algorithms; Distributed Systems.
Keywords: network reconnaissance; vulnerability enumeration; attack surface modelling; agent-based scanning; graph-based security models; software-defined networking; penetration testing automation; cyber-physical systems security; topology discovery; exploit path analysis.
Bio: Árpád Nagy received his B.Sc. and M.Sc. degrees in Computer Engineering from the Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad, in 2001 and 2003 respectively, and his Ph.D. in Computer Science from the same institution in 2008, with a dissertation on automated topology discovery in heterogeneous networks. After a postdoctoral period at the University of Ljubljana (2009–2011), he returned to Novi Sad as Assistant Professor and was promoted to Full Professor in 2021. His group investigates automated network reconnaissance, vulnerability enumeration, and attack-surface modelling using intelligent agent-based scanning pipelines and graph-theoretic representations of network state. He teaches courses on network security, distributed systems, and autonomous agents. The group maintains a dedicated network-emulation laboratory equipped with reconfigurable VLAN hardware, a cluster of software-defined networking switches, and licensed vulnerability-management platforms.
Open to: joint projects with NTP companies on internal network security assessment; contract research on vulnerability scanning pipeline development; industrial PhD supervision for candidates from NTP companies; consulting on attack surface modelling and penetration testing automation; student internships in the network-emulation laboratory; equipment access for external researchers requiring VLAN testbed or SDN infrastructure.
Industry experience: Between 2014 and 2016 Nagy provided part-time consulting to a regional managed security services provider, reviewing their automated scanning workflows and contributing to toolchain integration. He has also conducted paid pilot assessments for two technology companies at NTP Novi Sad under the GRAPHSEC project.
Notes: Nagy has indicated a preference for collaborations that involve access to real network environments rather than purely synthetic data, as his group's tooling is at a maturity level where production-grade evaluation would be valuable. He has no current sabbatical plans and takes on a moderate teaching load, leaving capacity for one new significant collaboration per year.

R0641.title: Branislav Stojanović
R0641.text:
Branislav Stojanović (R0641): Full Professor, Department of Computing and Control Engineering, Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad.
Fields: Embedded Systems and IoT; Signal Processing; Data Compression; Computer Engineering.
Keywords: edge computing; lossy compression; adaptive sampling; anomaly detection; resource-constrained devices; IoT sensor nodes; on-device processing; microcontroller; vibration monitoring; energy-efficient algorithms.
Bio: Branislav Stojanović received his Dipl.Ing. degree in computer engineering from the Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad in 2001, followed by an M.Sc. in 2004 and a Ph.D. in 2009 from the same institution. He joined the Department of Computing and Control Engineering as an assistant professor in 2010 and was promoted to full professor in 2021. His research group focuses on signal processing algorithms designed to operate within the severe memory, compute, and energy budgets of microcontroller-class hardware, with particular emphasis on lossy compression schemes that preserve anomaly signatures in sensor streams. He teaches courses on embedded systems, digital signal processing, and real-time operating systems. The group maintains a laboratory equipped with mixed-signal oscilloscopes, logic analysers, a range of ARM Cortex-M and RISC-V development boards, and a small anechoic test chamber for acoustic sensing experiments.
Open to: joint projects; contract research; industrial PhD supervision; consulting; equipment access; student internships.
Industry experience: Stojanović served as a technical consultant to StruktoSens d.o.o. between 2022 and 2024, advising on embedded firmware architecture for their wireless structural monitoring product line. He has also provided paid consultancy on LoRaWAN payload optimisation to two regional agricultural technology startups.
Notes: Stojanović is particularly interested in collaboration with companies working on predictive maintenance, structural monitoring, precision agriculture, or wearable health devices where embedded data reduction is a bottleneck. He is open to co-supervising engineering students placed at NTP companies. His laboratory has spare board-bring-up capacity and can run short contracted benchmarking studies on new microcontroller families.

R0754.title: Žarko Jakovljević
R0754.text:
Žarko Jakovljević (R0754): Research Associate, Sensors and Microsystems Group, BioSense Institute, University of Novi Sad.
Fields: Embedded Systems and IoT; Wireless Sensor Networks; Signal Processing and Data Quality; Telecommunications.
Keywords: fault-tolerant sensor nodes; edge diagnostics; low-power wide-area networks; data quality; heterogeneous cellular networks; sensor degradation detection; NB-IoT; remote monitoring; energy harvesting; embedded firmware.
Bio: Žarko Jakovljević received his B.Sc. in Electrical Engineering from the University of Novi Sad in 2011 and his Ph.D. in Technical Sciences from the same university in 2018, with a dissertation on fault detection architectures for resource-constrained wireless sensor nodes. Since 2019 he has been a Research Associate in the Sensors and Microsystems Group at the BioSense Institute, where the group develops precision sensing systems for agricultural, environmental, and infrastructure monitoring. His work focuses on hardware and firmware strategies for maintaining data integrity in IoT deployments subject to intermittent cellular connectivity, power fluctuations, and sensor degradation. He contributes to practical courses in embedded systems at the Faculty of Technical Sciences. His primary laboratory tools include network emulation rigs, low-power microcontroller evaluation boards, vector network analysers, and a multi-channel climate chamber for accelerated sensor ageing tests.
Open to: joint projects; contract research; consulting; student internships; equipment access (climate chamber, network emulation rig).
Industry experience: Jakovljević completed a three-month technical secondment in 2022 at Telemetrija d.o.o., a Novi Sad-based company producing remote water-level monitoring systems, where he assisted with NB-IoT modem integration and on-device diagnostic firmware. He has also provided informal consulting to two agricultural technology startups on sensor selection and data validation pipelines.
Notes: Currently principal investigator on an active PROMIS project (DIAQUAL, ending 2026), so capacity for entirely new large-scale commitments is limited until mid-2026; smaller consulting engagements and student co-supervision are feasible. Has expressed interest in working with companies that have existing IoT hardware deployments generating data quality problems, particularly in utilities or infrastructure monitoring, where his diagnostic methods could be adapted beyond agriculture.

R0773.title: Branislava Ostojić
R0773.text:
Branislava Ostojić (R0773): Full Professor, Department of Computing and Control Engineering, Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad.
Fields: Statistical Process Control; Machine Learning; Industrial Cyber-Physical Systems; Time Series Analysis.
Keywords: multivariate statistical process control; change-point detection; non-stationary time series; adaptive thresholding; unsupervised anomaly detection; cyber-physical systems; online learning; control charts; kernel methods; industrial monitoring.
Bio: Branislava Ostojić received her Dipl.Ing. in Computer Engineering from the Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad in 2000, followed by an M.Sc. in 2003 and a Ph.D. in 2009, both from the same institution. She was appointed Assistant Professor in 2010, Associate Professor in 2016, and Full Professor in 2022. Her research group focuses on statistical process control for industrial systems, combining multivariate time-series analysis with machine learning methods such as kernel-based change-point detection, online anomaly scoring, and adaptive control-chart thresholds for non-stationary signals. She teaches courses in Stochastic Systems, Applied Statistics for Engineers, and Industrial Data Analysis. The group operates within the Laboratory for Intelligent Measurement and Control Systems at FTN, using a real-time data acquisition testbed with programmable logic controllers, vibration sensors, and a shared high-memory compute server for streaming-data experiments.
Open to: joint research projects with companies operating sensor-instrumented production equipment; contract research on anomaly detection and SPC system design; industrial PhD supervision for candidates employed in manufacturing or automation companies; consulting on deployment and calibration of statistical monitoring systems; student internships focused on data collection and algorithm prototyping; equipment access (laboratory testbed with PLC, vibration, pressure, and temperature acquisition).
Industry experience: Ostojić has carried out paid consultancy engagements for two manufacturers in the Vojvodina region, advising on the replacement of rule-based alarm systems with data-driven SPC methods and on the design of operator dashboards for process monitoring. Both engagements ran for approximately six months each.
Notes: Ostojić is particularly interested in collaborators who can provide access to labelled or time-stamped operational data from real production systems, as clean annotated industrial datasets are the main bottleneck for her group's current research. She is not in a position to take on projects requiring extensive hardware integration or embedded firmware development beyond lightweight deployment of pre-trained models.

R0802.title: Luka Knežević
R0802.text:
Luka Knežević (R0802): Assistant Professor, Department of Computing and Control Engineering, Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad.
Fields: Compiler Design and Code Generation; Computer Architecture; High-Performance Computing; Domain-Specific Hardware Acceleration.
Keywords: intermediate representation; register allocation; sparse tensor operations; domain-specific accelerators; LLVM; compiler back-end; FPGA; dataflow graphs; sparsity-aware compilation; hardware-software co-design.
Open to: joint projects with companies developing custom silicon or FPGA accelerators; contract research on compiler back-end development for domain-specific hardware; industrial PhD supervision for candidates working on hardware-compiler co-design; student internships in compiler engineering and FPGA benchmarking; consulting on LLVM back-end customisation and sparse workload profiling.
Industry experience: During his postdoctoral period at TU Dresden, Knežević participated in a six-month consulting engagement with a Dresden-based embedded systems company, assisting in porting their proprietary DSP compiler back-end to an updated instruction set. He has since maintained an informal collaboration with a Novi Sad FPGA design house that provides hardware access for benchmarking in the SPARC-IR project.
Notes: Knežević is actively looking for industry partners who can provide access to proprietary accelerator specifications or silicon under NDA, as academic FPGA emulation covers only part of the relevant design space. He prefers collaborations with a clear compiler or toolchain component rather than pure hardware design engagements.

R0826.title: Vuk Bačić
R0826.text:
Vuk Bačić (R0826): Research Associate, Department of Power, Electronics and Telecommunications, Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad.
Fields: Electrical Engineering; Energy Storage and Power Electronics; Embedded Systems; Wireless Sensor Networks.
Keywords: primary lithium cells; pulsed-load discharge; electrochemical impedance spectroscopy; battery lifetime estimation; wireless sensor networks; low-power embedded systems; energy modelling; parametric degradation; capacity fade; WSN energy budgeting.
Bio: Vuk Bačić received his B.Sc. and M.Sc. degrees in Electrical Engineering from the Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad, in 2012 and 2014 respectively, and completed his Ph.D. at the same institution in 2020, with a dissertation on electrochemical characterisation of primary lithium cells under pulsed-load conditions. He has been a Research Associate in the Department of Power, Electronics and Telecommunications since 2021. His group focuses on energy budgeting and lifetime prediction for battery-powered wireless sensor nodes, combining empirical cell testing with parametric degradation models. He teaches laboratory courses in analogue electronics and embedded systems. He regularly uses the department's battery cycling test bench, a Gamry impedance analyser, and a custom pulsed-load board developed in-house for WSN emulation.
Open to: joint projects with companies deploying battery-powered IoT or wireless sensor devices; contract research on primary-cell selection and sizing for specific application profiles; equipment access — battery cycling test bench, Gamry impedance analyser, pulsed-load emulation hardware; student internships in embedded hardware design or electrochemical testing; consulting on LoRaWAN and low-power wireless node energy budgeting.
Industry experience: Bačić carried out a short consultancy engagement in 2023 for a precision-agriculture startup based in Novi Sad, reviewing their WSN node power architecture and recommending a cell type change that extended projected node lifetime by approximately 40 %. He has no other formal industry experience outside academia.
Notes: Bačić is finishing the main experimental phase of the SENWATT project in 2025 and expects capacity for a new collaboration from early 2026. He is particularly interested in partners who can provide real deployment data or access to application-specific load profiles, which are the main bottleneck for model validation. He prefers applied collaborations with a concrete measurement or characterisation component over purely computational work.

R0905.title: Filip Mijatović
R0905.text:
Filip Mijatović (R0905): Assistant Professor, Department of Power, Electronics and Telecommunications, Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad.
Fields: Microelectronics and mixed-signal circuit design; Wireless sensor networks and embedded systems; Biomedical instrumentation; Low-power communication protocols.
Keywords: ultra-low-power design; body-area networks; mixed-signal CMOS; biopotential acquisition; duty-cycled MAC; energy harvesting; sub-threshold circuits; wireless health monitoring; impedance spectroscopy; biomedical sampling constraints.
Bio: Filip Mijatović received his B.Sc. and M.Sc. degrees in Electronics and Telecommunications from the Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad, in 2009 and 2012 respectively, and his Ph.D. from the same institution in 2018, with a thesis on duty-cycled MAC protocols for implantable sensor nodes. He spent fourteen months as a visiting researcher at the Graz University of Technology between 2016 and 2017. Since 2019 he has held an Assistant Professor position in the Department of Power, Electronics and Telecommunications. His group focuses on mixed-signal front-end circuits operating below 1 µA average current, low-noise amplifier topologies for biopotential acquisition, and link-layer scheduling algorithms that respect biomedical sampling timing constraints. He teaches undergraduate analogue electronics and graduate wireless sensor systems. The group uses a Cadence Virtuoso IC design suite, a Keysight parametric analyser, and a small anechoic chamber shared with the antenna laboratory.
Open to: joint projects with medical device companies; contract research on mixed-signal front-end design; industrial PhD supervision; student internships (M.Sc. level, hardware-oriented); consulting on BLE and 802.15.4 protocol configuration for biomedical products; access to Cadence Virtuoso design suite for short collaborative visits.
Industry experience: Between 2012 and 2014, Mijatović worked part-time as a hardware design consultant for a Novi Sad-based startup developing Bluetooth-connected pulse oximetry accessories, contributing to the analogue signal chain and firmware of their first product revision.
Notes: Mijatović is currently supervising two doctoral candidates and has limited bandwidth for large new commitments before mid-2025. He has expressed interest in applied problems from companies developing wearable or implantable devices, particularly where circuit-level co-design with protocol optimisation is relevant. He is cautious about projects requiring significant regulatory or clinical-trial management, which is outside his team's expertise.

R0906.title: Maja Popović
R0906.text:
Maja Popović (R0906): Associate Professor, Department of Biomedical Engineering, Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad.
Fields: biomedical signal processing; wearables.
Keywords: ECG; atrial fibrillation; arrhythmia detection; false alarms; accelerometer.
Bio: Maja Popović is an Associate Professor in the Department of Biomedical Engineering at the Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad. Her research focuses on biomedical signal processing and wearable sensing systems, with a particular emphasis on cardiac monitoring, arrhythmia detection, and the reduction of false alarms in ambulatory ECG devices. She develops embedded signal-processing algorithms suitable for deployment on resource-constrained microcontrollers and wearable patch sensors. Professor Popović leads the HEARTWATCH project, which investigates remote cardiac monitoring solutions for long-term atrial fibrillation screening. She has authored multiple peer-reviewed publications on ECG classification, motion-artifact suppression, and accelerometer-based activity recognition. She is actively seeking industrial PhD co-supervision arrangements and joint applied research projects with technology companies.
Open to: industrial PhD supervision; joint projects.

R0919.title: Martina Lačoková
R0919.text:
Martina Lačoková (R0919): Senior Research Associate, Department of Computing and Control Engineering, Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad.
Fields: Software Engineering and Testing; Embedded and Real-Time Systems; Formal Methods and Verification; Automotive and Industrial Control.
Keywords: combinatorial interaction testing; t-way test generation; interface contract specification; compositional verification; CAN bus; multi-supplier integration; runtime assertion monitoring; covering arrays; constraint solving; embedded software.
Bio: Martina Lačoková received her B.Sc. and M.Sc. degrees in Computing and Control Engineering from the Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad, in 2006 and 2009 respectively, and her Ph.D. from the same institution in 2014, with a thesis on combinatorial test generation for automotive communication middleware. Since 2015 she has held a Senior Research Associate position in the Department of Computing and Control Engineering. Her group focuses on test adequacy and compositional verification for embedded software assembled from components supplied by multiple vendors, with particular emphasis on CAN-based automotive and industrial networks. She teaches graduate courses on software testing and formal methods. The group maintains a CAN/LIN bus laboratory with vector hardware interfaces and a small cluster for constraint-solving workloads.
Open to: joint projects with companies integrating multi-supplier embedded components; contract research on CAN/CAN FD integration testing methodology; industrial PhD supervision for candidates from embedded systems companies; student internships in the CAN bus laboratory; consulting on AUTOSAR integration test strategy; equipment access to CAN/LIN hardware interfaces and HIL test rig.
Industry experience: Lačoková conducted a six-month placement at a Novi Sad-based automation equipment company in 2012–2013, contributing to integration test planning for a CAN-networked motor-drive product line. She has since maintained informal advisory relationships with two Serbian companies that participated in the CONTRACE project.
Notes: Lačoková is currently supervising two doctoral students expected to defend in 2026 and 2027, which limits availability for new long-term commitments before mid-2026. She has expressed interest in collaborations that include access to real integration fault records from industry, as this remains the main bottleneck for empirical validation work.

R0925.title: Milan Petrović
R0925.text:
Milan Petrović (R0925): Assistant Professor, Department of Computing and Control Engineering, Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad.
Fields: natural language processing; machine learning.
Keywords: transformer models; Serbian language; retrieval; embeddings; question answering.
Bio: Milan Petrović is an Assistant Professor at the Department of Computing and Control Engineering, Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad. His research focuses on natural language processing and machine learning, with a particular emphasis on transformer-based language models and low-resource NLP for Serbian. He works on building open language resources for Serbian, including pre-trained models, annotated corpora, and evaluation benchmarks. His recent work addresses dense retrieval, question answering, and the challenges of processing text in both Latin and Cyrillic scripts within a unified embedding space. He collaborates with regional and international partners and is actively involved in the SRB-NLP initiative under the Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia. He is open to industrial PhD supervision and joint research projects with companies seeking NLP solutions.
Open to: industrial PhD supervision; joint projects.

R0948.title: Mirjana Vidaković
R0948.text:
Mirjana Vidaković (R0948): Full Professor, Department of Computing and Control Engineering, Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad.
Fields: Model-Driven Engineering; Embedded Systems Software; Software Architecture; Automotive Software Engineering.
Keywords: AUTOSAR; model-driven engineering; metamodel transformation; code generation; ARXML; domain-specific language; template-based synthesis; Eclipse Modeling Framework; real-time embedded systems; toolchain integration.
Bio: Mirjana Vidaković received her Dipl.Ing. degree in computer engineering from the Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad in 2001, her M.Sc. in 2005, and her Ph.D. in 2011, with a dissertation on metamodel-driven generation of AUTOSAR software component descriptors. She joined the Department of Computing and Control Engineering as an assistant professor in 2012 and was promoted to full professor in 2022. Her research group focuses on model-driven engineering (MDE) for safety-relevant embedded systems, with particular emphasis on AUTOSAR-compliant architectures, ARXML artefact manipulation, template-based code synthesis, and toolchain integration. She teaches courses on embedded systems software, domain-specific languages, and software architectures for real-time systems. The group uses Eclipse Modeling Framework, Ecore-based metamodeling tools, AUTOSAR authoring environments, and hardware-in-the-loop test benches available in the Faculty's Embedded Systems Laboratory.
Open to: joint projects with companies on AUTOSAR toolchain development or customisation; contract research on ARXML artefact processing and model transformation; industrial PhD supervision for candidates from automotive or embedded-software companies; student internships in the Embedded Systems Laboratory; consulting on MDE toolchain architecture and AUTOSAR workflow design.
Industry experience: Vidaković has served as a technical consultant to Embron d.o.o., a Novi Sad-based embedded-software company, on AUTOSAR toolchain architecture over three separate engagements between 2015 and 2022. She also participated in a four-month knowledge-transfer engagement with a regional automotive Tier-1 supplier in 2018 focused on introducing MDE practices into their ECU development workflow.
Notes: Vidaković is currently supervising three doctoral students, which limits capacity for new long-term commitments before mid-2026. She has expressed preference for collaborations that involve access to realistic industrial AUTOSAR model corpora, as the Faculty's internal model library covers only a narrow range of ECU domains. Short-term consulting or focused contract research engagements are feasible at any time.

R0983.title: Andrea Jovanović
R0983.text:
Andrea Jovanović (R0983): Assistant Professor, Department of Computing and Control Engineering, Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad.
Fields: Software Engineering; Automated Testing; Cloud Computing; Search-Based Software Engineering.
Keywords: automated test generation; coverage-guided fuzzing; search-based testing; legacy system migration; cloud-native applications; mutation testing; microservices testing; code coverage; regression testing; containerisation.
Open to: joint projects with companies performing legacy-to-cloud migrations; contract research on test automation tooling and methodology; industrial PhD supervision for software engineers working on migration projects; student internships at companies using automated testing in CI/CD pipelines; consulting on fuzzing tool selection and integration; access to the group's containerised legacy application testbed for joint experiments.
Industry experience: Between 2012 and 2013 Jovanović worked part-time as a QA engineer at a Novi Sad software consultancy, where she introduced automated regression testing for a client's Java EE payroll system. She has since maintained informal advisory relationships with two local software companies involved in cloud migration projects.
Notes: Jovanović is currently finalising supervision of two PhD students expected to defend in 2026–2027, so her capacity for new large-scale commitments is limited until mid-2026. She is particularly interested in partnerships that provide access to real legacy codebases and migration artefacts under research-use agreements, as such datasets are difficult to obtain through open sources alone.

R0995.title: Veljko Pantelić
R0995.text:
Veljko Pantelić (R0995): Assistant Professor, Department of Computing and Control Engineering, Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad.
Fields: Software Engineering; Industrial Automation; Model-Driven Engineering; Programming Languages and Compilers.
Keywords: IEC 61131-3; model-driven engineering; software product lines; domain-specific languages; code generation; PLC programming; metamodeling; feature models; model transformation; Structured Text.
Bio: Veljko Pantelić received his B.Sc. and M.Sc. degrees in Computing and Control Engineering from the Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad, in 2010 and 2013 respectively, and his Ph.D. from the same institution in 2019. His doctoral work focused on metamodel-driven code generation pipelines targeting IEC 61131-3 Structured Text for programmable logic controllers. Since 2020 he has held an Assistant Professor position in the Department of Computing and Control Engineering. His research group investigates domain-specific language design, model transformation chains, and software product-line variability management for industrial automation software. He teaches courses in software engineering, formal languages, and industrial programming. The group uses Eclipse Modeling Framework, Xtext, Sirius, and a small PLC laboratory equipped with several Wago and Beckhoff controllers for validation experiments.
Open to: joint projects with automation software companies; contract research on PLC code generation tooling; industrial PhD supervision; student internships in PLC software tooling development; consulting on DSL design for industrial automation; equipment access to PLC laboratory for partner validation experiments.
Industry experience: During 2013–2015 Pantelić worked part-time as a software engineer at a Novi Sad-based automation integrator, where he developed IEC 61131-3 programs for conveyor and palletiser systems; this experience directly motivated his research focus on maintainability and variability in PLC codebases.
Notes: Pantelić is particularly interested in partnerships with NTP companies developing configurable or product-line-structured automation equipment, especially where legacy code migration is a concern. He has limited availability for consulting engagements during the spring semester due to teaching load but is flexible in summer and autumn.

R1008.title: Krisztina Kiss
R1008.text:
Krisztina Kiss (R1008): Full Professor, Department of Computing and Control Engineering, Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad.
Fields: Industrial cybersecurity; Network traffic analysis; Machine learning and statistical modelling; Industrial control systems.
Keywords: anomaly detection; one-class classification; industrial control systems; SCADA security; statistical baseline modelling; Modbus; DNP3; unsupervised learning; network intrusion detection; protocol traffic analysis.
Bio: Krisztina Kiss received her Dipl.Ing. degree in computer engineering from the University of Novi Sad in 2001 and her PhD in electrical and computer engineering from the same institution in 2008, with a dissertation on statistical traffic profiling in industrial Ethernet networks. She joined the Department of Computing and Control Engineering as an assistant professor in 2009 and was promoted to full professor in 2020. Her research group focuses on unsupervised anomaly detection and one-class classification for industrial control system protocol traffic, using statistical baseline modelling, kernel methods, and lightweight online learning algorithms suited to constrained embedded environments. She teaches courses on network security, operating systems, and industrial communication protocols. The group operates a dedicated ICS testbed equipped with Siemens-compatible PLCs, Modbus/TCP and DNP3 traffic generators, and packet capture infrastructure for long-term dataset collection.
Open to: joint projects with companies deploying ICS monitoring solutions; contract research on protocol traffic analysis and anomaly detection deployment; industrial PhD supervision for candidates from companies in automation and critical infrastructure; student internships on ICS testbed experiments and dataset collection; consulting on detector calibration, evaluation methodology, and deployment architecture for industrial networks; access to ICS testbed and long-term traffic capture infrastructure for collaborative experiments.
Industry experience: Kiss has collaborated with a regional energy distributor and a water utility as monitoring data partners on two funded projects, providing practical validation of research methods on operational infrastructure. She has carried out paid consulting for a mid-size automation integrator on specifying anomaly detection requirements for a SCADA upgrade project.
Notes: Kiss prefers applied collaborations that result in deployment on real infrastructure rather than purely synthetic experiments. Her group's testbed capacity is available to industrial partners under a data-sharing agreement. She is particularly interested in partners dealing with proprietary or undocumented ICS protocols, which represent a gap in her current work.

R1015.title: Vuk Đukić
R1015.text:
Vuk Đukić (R1015): Associate Professor, Department of Computing and Control Engineering, Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad.
Fields: cybersecurity; network security.
Keywords: intrusion detection; industrial control systems; anomaly detection; IoT security; threat modelling.
Bio: Vuk Đukić is an Associate Professor at the Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad, within the Department of Computing and Control Engineering. His research focuses on cybersecurity and network security, with particular emphasis on intrusion detection, anomaly detection in industrial control systems, IoT security, and threat modelling. He has led and contributed to multiple national and international research initiatives aimed at securing critical infrastructure and smart environments. Professor Đukić has published in reputable journals and conferences and is actively involved in interdisciplinary collaboration with industry. He is open to supervising industrial PhD students and engaging in joint research projects with technology companies seeking expertise in operational technology security and advanced threat analysis.
Open to: industrial PhD supervision; joint projects.

R1027.title: Tanja Simić
R1027.text:
Tanja Simić (R1027): Research Associate, Department of Pedagogy, Faculty of Philosophy, University of Novi Sad.
Fields: Educational Sciences; Adult and Continuing Education; Curriculum Development; Human Resources Development.
Keywords: instructional design; competency-based education; adult technical learners; knowledge transfer assessment; curriculum development; learning outcomes; vocational training; e-learning; workplace learning.
Bio: Tanja Simić completed her Bachelor's and Master's degrees in Pedagogy at the Faculty of Philosophy, University of Novi Sad, and defended her doctoral dissertation on competency-based curriculum models for technical vocational education in 2017 at the same institution. She joined the Department of Pedagogy as a Research Associate in 2018. Her work focuses on instructional design for adult learners in technical and engineering contexts, with particular attention to how learning objectives can be operationalised into measurable competency outcomes. She participates in undergraduate and graduate teaching in curriculum theory and adult education methodology. Her research group uses learning management system log data, structured competency rubrics, and pre/post knowledge transfer assessments; analytical work is carried out using SPSS and R.
Open to: joint projects; contract research; consulting on competency framework design and curriculum alignment; student internships in training evaluation and instructional design; co-supervision of master's theses with industry partners.
Industry experience: Tanja Simić has provided consulting to two training departments in the Vojvodina manufacturing sector on redesigning their internal onboarding and upskilling curricula between 2019 and 2021. She collaborated directly with HR and operations staff to translate job task analyses into structured learning modules.
Notes: Tanja Simić is primarily interested in working with companies that run or are planning to build structured internal training programmes and want to improve how they define, deliver, and evaluate employee learning. She is less interested in purely technology-development partnerships without a training or assessment component. The KOMPAS project runs until mid-2026 and represents her main workload commitment at present.

SYN-PAT-009.title: Method and Device for Anomaly-Preserving Adaptive Bit Allocation in Compressed Sensor Data Streams
SYN-PAT-009.text:
Method and Device for Anomaly-Preserving Adaptive Bit Allocation in Compressed Sensor Data Streams (2023, pending).
Inventors: Branislav Stojanović (R0641).
A method for compressing sensor data streams on resource-constrained embedded processors wherein a CUSUM-based detector flags anomalous signal segments in real time and a bit allocator redistributes the saved bits from normal segments to flagged segments within a fixed per-frame bit budget. The device comprises a microcontroller executing the detector and allocator in under 15 CPU cycles per sample and a non-volatile memory unit storing compressed output. The method preserves signal peaks associated with mechanical fault events at compression ratios where conventional uniform-bit-rate coders suppress such peaks below detection threshold.

SYN-PAT-018.title: Circuit and method for electrode-offset cancellation in a capacitively coupled biopotential amplifier with sub-nanoampere DC servo current
SYN-PAT-018.text:
Circuit and method for electrode-offset cancellation in a capacitively coupled biopotential amplifier with sub-nanoampere DC servo current (2022, granted).
Inventors: Filip Mijatović (R0905).
The invention covers a DC servo loop architecture for use in capacitively coupled instrumentation amplifiers intended for wearable biopotential acquisition. The loop uses a switched-capacitor integrator clocked at 8 Hz to sense residual offset at the output and apply a correction current at the input through a high-impedance current DAC, keeping total servo current below 20 nA. The approach tolerates electrode polarisation offsets up to ±400 mV without saturating the main amplifier chain. The patent was filed in Serbia through the Intellectual Property Office and subsequently extended via PCT.

SYN-PAT-043.title: Reconfigurable Fault Injection Board for Automotive ECU I/O Lines with Solid-State Relay Matrix and Microcontroller Interface
SYN-PAT-043.text:
Reconfigurable Fault Injection Board for Automotive ECU I/O Lines with Solid-State Relay Matrix and Microcontroller Interface (2020, granted).
Inventors: Darko Ninkov (R0356).
A hardware board comprising a matrix of solid-state relays arranged to selectively connect any of up to 32 ECU I/O lines to open-circuit, battery voltage, or ground conditions under software control. A microcontroller receives fault commands over a standard serial interface and drives the relay gates within a guaranteed 2 ms switching latency. The board includes overcurrent protection on each channel and a watchdog that returns all channels to a safe default state if the host controller fails to send a heartbeat within a configurable timeout. The design targets low-cost laboratory HiL bench applications.

SYN-PAT-044.title: Method and Circuit Arrangement for Adaptive Threshold-Triggered Vibration Data Acquisition on Low-Power Microcontroller Platforms
SYN-PAT-044.text:
Method and Circuit Arrangement for Adaptive Threshold-Triggered Vibration Data Acquisition on Low-Power Microcontroller Platforms (2022, granted).
Inventors: Vesna Knežević (R0206).
The patent covers a hardware-software method in which an analogue comparator on a microcontroller's input pin monitors a running RMS estimate of an accelerometer signal and triggers a DMA burst acquisition only when the estimate exceeds a configurable threshold stored in non-volatile memory. The threshold may be updated by a host application over UART or BLE without reflashing firmware. The arrangement reduces idle current draw by 55–70% compared to continuous DMA acquisition in laboratory measurements on an STM32L4 platform. The patent is assigned to the University of Novi Sad.

SYN-PRJ-0009.title: SRB-NLP: open language resources for Serbian
SYN-PRJ-0009.text:
SRB-NLP: open language resources for Serbian (Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia, 2023–2026).
Participants: R0925 researcher.
The SRB-NLP project aims to build a comprehensive suite of open language resources for Serbian, addressing a long-standing gap in the NLP ecosystem for South Slavic languages. The project encompasses the creation of large pre-training corpora, fine-tuning datasets for core NLP tasks including named entity recognition, question answering, semantic similarity, and intent detection, as well as the training and public release of transformer-based language models tailored to Serbian. A central objective is ensuring that all resources support both Latin and Cyrillic scripts on equal footing. The project also includes the design and dissemination of standardised evaluation benchmarks to enable reproducible comparison of future Serbian NLP systems. Running from 2023 to 2026 with funding from the Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia, the project involves collaboration between linguists and computer scientists and is committed to open science through the public release of all data, model weights, and code.

SYN-PRJ-0013.title: KORPUS-NS: a reference corpus of contemporary Serbian
SYN-PRJ-0013.text:
KORPUS-NS: a reference corpus of contemporary Serbian (Ministry of Science, 2020–2024).
Participants: R0288 principal investigator.
KORPUS-NS aims to create a 500-million-token reference corpus of contemporary Serbian serving as the primary large-scale resource for linguistic research, lexicography and natural language processing in Serbia. Led by Professor Nikolić as principal investigator, the project encompasses text collection from journalism, literature, academic writing, legal texts, social media and transcribed speech, as well as the development of a full annotation pipeline covering tokenisation, lemmatisation, part-of-speech tagging and morphosyntactic description. A custom morphological lexicon, a web concordancer, and open-source processing tools are being released progressively throughout the project period. KORPUS-NS is expected to become the standard empirical reference for Serbian linguistics and to supply training and evaluation data for downstream computational applications in industry and academia.

SYN-PRJ-0014.title: HEARTWATCH: remote cardiac monitoring
SYN-PRJ-0014.text:
HEARTWATCH: remote cardiac monitoring (Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia, 2022–2025).
Participants: R0906 principal investigator.
HEARTWATCH is a three-year research project funded by the Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia, running from 2022 to 2025, with Associate Professor Maja Popović serving as principal investigator. The project addresses the clinical need for reliable, long-term remote cardiac monitoring outside hospital settings, targeting particularly the early detection of atrial fibrillation in high-risk populations. The core technical objective is the development of a complete algorithmic stack—spanning signal quality assessment, motion-artifact suppression, real-time arrhythmia classification, and adaptive false-alarm reduction—capable of executing on a low-power wearable ECG patch. A secondary objective is the creation of a clinically annotated benchmark dataset in partnership with the Clinical Centre of Vojvodina. By project completion, HEARTWATCH aims to deliver open-source firmware validated in a prospective pilot study involving at least 120 participants, providing a translational foundation for commercialization through collaboration with medical device companies.

SYN-PRJ-0017.title: SECURE-ICS: security monitoring for factories
SYN-PRJ-0017.text:
SECURE-ICS: security monitoring for factories (Innovation Fund, 2023–2025).
Participants: R1015 academic partner.
SECURE-ICS addresses the growing need for robust cybersecurity monitoring in industrial manufacturing environments. The project develops an integrated security monitoring platform tailored specifically to factory automation systems, encompassing network traffic analysis, anomaly detection, and real-time alerting for operational technology networks. As academic partner, the University of Novi Sad team led by Professor Đukić contributes expertise in intrusion detection algorithm design, threat modelling for ICS environments, and evaluation methodology. The platform targets Modbus, PROFINET, and EtherNet/IP protocol stacks commonly found in Serbian manufacturing facilities. Deliverables include a deployable monitoring agent, a validated anomaly detection model trained on representative factory traffic, and a set of security assessment guidelines for small and medium enterprises in the industrial sector. The project runs from 2023 to 2025 under the Innovation Fund programme.

SYN-PRJ-0019.title: Formal Model-Driven Interface Generation and Adaptation for Heterogeneous Enterprise Systems
SYN-PRJ-0019.text:
FORMIGA: Formal Model-Driven Interface Generation and Adaptation for Heterogeneous Enterprise Systems (Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma), 2021–2024).
Participants: R0341 principal investigator.
Partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad; Mathematical Institute, Serbian Academy of Sciences and Arts.
FORMIGA developed a toolchain for specifying enterprise integration architectures in a formal DSL and automatically generating executable interface adapters from detected mismatches. The project produced three tool components: a metamodel editor built on Eclipse EMF, a mismatch analyser using constraint solving, and an ATL-based code generator targeting Apache Camel. Validation was carried out with two companies in the Vojvodina region operating heterogeneous ERP and MES systems. The project trained two PhD students and produced seven peer-reviewed publications. A public repository containing the toolchain and all benchmark models was released under an open-source licence at project completion.

SYN-PRJ-0020.title: Integration Middleware for Edge-Cloud Continuum in Smart Manufacturing
SYN-PRJ-0020.text:
INTEDGE: Integration Middleware for Edge-Cloud Continuum in Smart Manufacturing (Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia, 2023–2026).
Participants: R0341 work package leader.
Partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad; Bay Zoltán Nonprofit Ltd. for Applied Research, Miskolc; Vojvodina ICT Cluster, Novi Sad; Chamber of Commerce and Industry of Csongrád-Csanád County.
INTEDGE addresses the challenge of integrating edge computing nodes with cloud-hosted enterprise systems in small and medium manufacturing enterprises along the Hungarian–Serbian border region. Bošković leads the work package on formal interface specification and automated adapter generation for edge device protocols. The project involves four partners across two countries and targets deployment pilots in two manufacturing SMEs. The formal methods component builds directly on the adapter generation framework from earlier research, extending it with resource-constrained runtime profiles suitable for edge hardware. Expected outputs include a reusable pattern library for edge-cloud integration and two pilot deployments.

SYN-PRJ-0023.title: Cloud Testing and Service Reliability for Regional Digital Infrastructure
SYN-PRJ-0023.text:
CLOTSER: Cloud Testing and Service Reliability for Regional Digital Infrastructure (Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia, 2022–2025).
Participants: R0983 work package leader.
Partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad; Pannon Institute of Technology, Pécs (invented); Chamber of Commerce of Vojvodina (associated partner).
CLOTSER is a cross-border cooperation project addressing software testing capacity in the Hungary–Serbia border region, where a growing number of small software companies lack access to automated testing expertise and tooling for cloud deployments. The project establishes a shared testing competence centre with nodes at the Faculty of Technical Sciences in Novi Sad and a Hungarian technical college, provides training workshops to regional SMEs, and funds applied research into lightweight test automation suitable for small development teams. Andrea Jovanović leads Work Package 3, which covers the technical research component on coverage measurement and fuzzing for SME-scale cloud services. Two joint pilot deployments with regional software companies are planned for the final project year.

SYN-PRJ-0050.title: Bridging Formal and Informal Learning Pathways in SME Onboarding Across the Hungary–Serbia Border Region
SYN-PRJ-0050.text:
LEARNBRIDGE: Bridging Formal and Informal Learning Pathways in SME Onboarding Across the Hungary–Serbia Border Region (Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia, 2021–2023).
Participants: R0386 work package leader.
Partners: Faculty of Philosophy, University of Novi Sad; Chamber of Commerce and Industry of Vojvodina; Faculty of Business and Economics, University of Pécs; Regional Development Agency of Southern Transdanubia.
