The project examined differences and commonalities in how small and medium-sized enterprises in the Vojvodina–southern Hungary border region structure their employee onboarding programmes, with a focus on the balance between formal instruction and informal workplace learning. Ninkov led the work package responsible for field data collection in Serbian partner organisations, coordinating structured observations and employee surveys across seven SMEs. The project produced a comparative report, a set of practitioner guidelines for SME HR managers, and a short online training module for onboarding coordinators. Three joint workshops were held across the two countries. Final outputs were disseminated in both Serbian and Hungarian.

SYN-PRJ-0051.title: Cognitive Load Profiling as a Tool for Adaptive Onboarding Programme Design in Technology Companies
SYN-PRJ-0051.text:
COGONBOARD: Cognitive Load Profiling as a Tool for Adaptive Onboarding Programme Design in Technology Companies (Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma), 2023–2026).
Participants: R0386 principal investigator; R0291 team member.
Partners: Department of Psychology, University of Novi Sad; Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad; Science Technology Park Novi Sad.
This project develops and tests a practical methodology for using real-time and retrospective cognitive load indicators to inform the adaptive sequencing of onboarding content in technology sector companies. The core activities include laboratory studies using eye-tracking and secondary task measures to build a cognitive load profile of representative onboarding task families, followed by a field trial in three technology companies based at the Science Technology Park Novi Sad. The field trial tests whether training coordinators who receive cognitive load feedback reports adjust their programmes in ways that improve time-to-competency outcomes. A freely available diagnostic toolkit will be produced at the project's conclusion, alongside peer-reviewed publications and a doctoral thesis co-supervised under the project.

SYN-PRJ-0054.title: Terminological Infrastructure for Vojvodina's Bilingual Administrative and Professional Communication
SYN-PRJ-0054.text:
VOITERM: Terminological Infrastructure for Vojvodina's Bilingual Administrative and Professional Communication (Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research, 2018–2021).
Participants: R0258 principal investigator.
Partners: Provincial Secretariat for Administration, Regulation and National Minorities, Novi Sad; Faculty of Agriculture, University of Novi Sad; Faculty of Humanities, University of Pécs.
The project built a publicly accessible bilingual Serbian–Hungarian terminological database covering the administrative, agricultural, and light manufacturing sectors active in Vojvodina. The database was populated from a 28-million-token corpus of administrative documents, agricultural extension bulletins, and industrial catalogs collected from provincial institutions and companies. Terminology extraction combined rule-based and statistical methods with expert post-editing. The final resource contains 34,000 verified term pairs with inflectional class and domain metadata. A web search interface was deployed on Faculty of Philosophy servers and has been used by the Provincial Secretariat's translation unit since 2021. The project employed two research assistants and supported one doctoral dissertation.

SYN-PRJ-0119.title: Edge-Deployable Streaming Analytics for Smart Manufacturing in the Danube Region
SYN-PRJ-0119.text:
STREAMWISE: Edge-Deployable Streaming Analytics for Smart Manufacturing in the Danube Region (Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia, 2023–2026).
Participants: R0071 work package leader.
Partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad; Bay Zoltán Alkalmazott Kutatási Közhasznú Nonprofit Kft. (fictional); Precizna Automatika d.o.o. Subotica (fictional); Pannon Ipar Klaszter (fictional); NTP Novi Sad – Science Technology Park Novi Sad (fictional).
STREAMWISE is a cross-border cooperation project targeting the deployment of data stream analytics in small and medium enterprises in the Hungarian–Serbian border region. Olivera Rakić leads the work package on model compression and edge deployment, responsible for adapting anomaly detection and classification pipelines to resource-constrained hardware installed in partner SME facilities. The work package produces deployment-ready software containers, an evaluation report comparing accuracy–latency trade-offs across hardware tiers, and a training curriculum for engineers at partner companies. The project is coordinated by the Hungarian partner and involves three Serbian and two Hungarian organisations.

SYN-PRJ-0150.title: Anomaly-Preserving Compression Architectures for Dense Structural Health Monitoring Networks
SYN-PRJ-0150.text:
COMPRESS-SHM: Anomaly-Preserving Compression Architectures for Dense Structural Health Monitoring Networks (Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma), 2021–2024).
Participants: R0641 principal investigator.
Partners: Faculty of Civil Engineering, University of Novi Sad; StruktoSens d.o.o., Novi Sad.
The project investigated how lossy compression can be designed to maintain the diagnostic information content relevant for structural damage localisation while still achieving practically useful compression ratios on microcontroller-class hardware. Work packages covered theoretical distortion bounds for guided-wave signals, implementation of anomaly-preserving codecs on RISC-V and ARM platforms, and a full-scale validation on a pedestrian bridge. The project funded the procurement of a 32-channel wireless sensor array, a vibration shaker for lab excitation experiments, and two postgraduate students. Results were disseminated through four journal papers and contributed to one patent application. Partners included the Faculty of Civil Engineering in Novi Sad and a structural monitoring consultancy.

SYN-PRJ-0151.title: Edge Processing and Compressed Sensing for Precision Agriculture IoT Deployments in Cross-Border Regions
SYN-PRJ-0151.text:
IOTEDGE-AG: Edge Processing and Compressed Sensing for Precision Agriculture IoT Deployments in Cross-Border Regions (Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia, 2019–2022).
Participants: R0641 work package leader.
Partners: University of Szeged, Faculty of Engineering, Hungary; BioSense Institute, Novi Sad; Vojvodinašume JP, Petrovaradin.
A cross-border cooperation project aiming to deploy low-cost LoRaWAN-connected soil and microclimate sensor nodes across agricultural holdings in Bács-Kiskun County (Hungary) and South Bačka District (Serbia). Stojanović led the work package on on-device data reduction, contributing dictionary coding and adaptive sampling methods validated in the field. The project produced a common hardware reference design and an open-source firmware library for payload compression. Field trials involved 140 sensor nodes over two growing seasons monitoring maize, sunflower, and soybean plots. The project also organised two joint student workshops on embedded IoT programming attended by 34 students from both countries.

SYN-PRJ-0211.title: Sub-microwatt Sensor Front-ends for Secure Continuous Cardiac Monitoring
SYN-PRJ-0211.text:
SENSEC: Sub-microwatt Sensor Front-ends for Secure Continuous Cardiac Monitoring (Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma), 2021–2024).
Participants: R0905 principal investigator.
Partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad; Clinical Centre of Vojvodina, Novi Sad; Institute of Biosensing Technologies, Ljubljana.
SENSEC addressed the power and security gap in wearable cardiac monitoring by developing analogue front-end circuits consuming below 1 µW alongside a lightweight authenticated wake-up protocol that prevents replay attacks on the wireless link. The project combined CMOS IC design in 130 nm and 65 nm processes with protocol-level work implemented on nRF5340 and STM32L4 platforms. Clinical relevance was established through a pilot recording campaign at a partner hospital cardiology ward involving 22 volunteer subjects. Deliverables included two fabricated prototypes, open-source firmware, and a dataset of annotated ECG recordings. The project funded one doctoral student who completed her thesis in 2024.

SYN-PRJ-0213.title: Physiological Signal Compression for Low-Power Telemetry in Remote Patient Monitoring
SYN-PRJ-0213.text:
PHYCOMP: Physiological Signal Compression for Low-Power Telemetry in Remote Patient Monitoring (Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma), 2022–2025).
Participants: R0057 principal investigator.
Partners: Clinical Centre of Vojvodina; Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad.
The project investigates compression algorithms suitable for deployment on low-power microcontrollers in wearable and implantable patient monitoring devices. Work packages cover beat-synchronous transform coding, sparse dictionary methods, and lightweight learned entropy models with a shared emphasis on keeping encoder complexity below 10 mJ per minute of single-lead ECG. The project includes a clinical validation component in collaboration with the Clinical Centre of Vojvodina, where compressed and reconstructed signals are assessed for diagnostic equivalence by cardiologists. A reference software library with documented APIs is being developed for use by regional medical-device developers. The project funds two PhD students and one postdoctoral researcher.

SYN-PRJ-0214.title: Cross-Border Telemedicine Data Infrastructure for Cardiac Monitoring
SYN-PRJ-0214.text:
CROTIMED: Cross-Border Telemedicine Data Infrastructure for Cardiac Monitoring (Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia, 2021–2023).
Participants: R0057 work package leader; R0653 team member; R0019 team member.
Partners: Somogy County Health Authority, Kaposvár; General Hospital Subotica; Mediconn d.o.o., Novi Sad.
A cross-border infrastructure project aiming to establish shared telemedicine data pipelines between partner hospitals in southern Hungary and the Vojvodina region. Šarić leads the work package on signal compression and transmission standards, contributing ECG and PPG codec implementations compliant with the SCP-ECG data standard. The work package also produces interoperability guidelines for compressed signal exchange between different hospital information systems used on the two sides of the border. Deliverables include a compression middleware component integrated into the project's shared telemedicine platform and a joint training session for clinical IT staff at both partner sites.

SYN-PRJ-0286.title: Voice-Enabled Educational Tools for Bilingual Primary Schools in the Serbia–Hungary Cross-Border Region
SYN-PRJ-0286.text:
EduVoice-RS-HU: Voice-Enabled Educational Tools for Bilingual Primary Schools in the Serbia–Hungary Cross-Border Region (Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia, 2023–2026).
Participants: R0131 work package leader.
Partners: Department of Telecommunications and Media Informatics, Budapest University of Technology; Завод за унапређивање образовања и васпитања, Београд; Oktatáskutató és Fejlesztő Intézet, Budapest.
EduVoice-RS-HU развија прототипове образовних апликација са гласовним интерфејсом намењених ученицима у двојезичним основним школама у прекограничном региону Србија–Мађарска. Задатак новосадске групе обухвата прилагођавање акустичких и језичких модела за двојезичне говорнике српског и мађарског, уз израду смерница за педагошку употребу гласовних технологија. Мађарска страна обезбеђује паралелни рад на препознавању мађарског говора деце. Крајњи корисници су наставници и ученици у 12 основних школа. Пројекат укључује теренска тестирања у школама и итеративно побољшање система на основу повратних информација.

SYN-PRJ-0340.title: Self-Diagnosing Sensor Networks for Autonomous Precision Agriculture in the Pannonian Region
SYN-PRJ-0340.text:
SENSORNET-AP: Self-Diagnosing Sensor Networks for Autonomous Precision Agriculture in the Pannonian Region (Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia, 2020–2023).
Participants: R0754 work package leader.
Partners: BioSense Institute, University of Novi Sad; Faculty of Agricultural and Food Sciences, University of Pécs, Hungary; Provincial Institute for Agriculture Novi Sad; AgroData Solutions Kft., Pécs, Hungary.
The project deployed and evaluated a cross-border agricultural sensor network spanning eight farm sites in Hungary and Serbia. Žarko Jakovljević led the work package responsible for node-level fault detection firmware and gateway-side data quality validation. The work package produced a reference firmware architecture supporting three diagnostic modules (drift detection, connectivity health scoring, and battery state estimation) and a validation protocol used to certify sensor data before ingestion into partner farm management systems. Field trials covered approximately 1,100 hectares of maize, sunflower, and wheat. The project produced two open datasets published through the Pannonian Environmental Data Repository and contributed results to two of the journal publications listed in this profile.

SYN-PRJ-0372.title: Sensor Node Energy Autonomy Through Accurate Cell Lifetime Modelling
SYN-PRJ-0372.text:
SENWATT: Sensor Node Energy Autonomy Through Accurate Cell Lifetime Modelling (Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma), 2022–2025).
Participants: R0826 principal investigator.
Partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad; Institute of Chemistry, Technology and Metallurgy, Belgrade.
SENWATT aims to replace empirical rules of thumb for primary-cell sizing in long-lived IoT deployments with physics-informed parametric models calibrated on systematic laboratory ageing data. The project involves construction of an automated 48-channel pulse-load cycling station, a three-year ageing experiment on Li/SOCl₂ and Li/MnO₂ cells under nine IoT traffic profiles, and development of an open-source lifetime estimation library targeting resource-constrained microcontrollers. Validation deployments are planned in agricultural and hydrological monitoring networks in Vojvodina. A secondary objective is a public dataset of cell impedance and capacity data to support reproducible research in the field.

SYN-PRJ-0373.title: Danube Basin Environmental Sensor Infrastructure for Water-Quality and Flood Early Warning
SYN-PRJ-0373.text:
DANUBESENS: Danube Basin Environmental Sensor Infrastructure for Water-Quality and Flood Early Warning (Interreg IPA Romania–Serbia, 2021–2023).
Participants: R0826 team member; R0182 team member.
Partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad; Politehnica University of Timișoara, Romania; Institute for Water Management Jaroslav Černi, Belgrade; National Institute of Hydrology and Water Management, Bucharest.
DANUBESENS deployed a cross-border network of 120 water-quality and river-level sensor nodes along the Serbian and Romanian stretches of the Danube. Vuk Bačić contributed to the power-systems work package, responsible for specifying primary-cell types and sizes for each node class, defining adaptive duty-cycle policies to extend cell life in high-traffic alarm conditions, and conducting post-deployment energy audits using the embedded energy meters developed in his group. The project delivered 18 months of continuous monitoring data and a maintenance protocol for battery replacement scheduling.

SYN-PRJ-0390.title: Product-Line Code Generation Infrastructure for Configurable PLC Software
SYN-PRJ-0390.text:
PLCGEN: Product-Line Code Generation Infrastructure for Configurable PLC Software (Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma), 2021–2024).
Participants: R0995 principal investigator.
Partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad; Politehnica University of Timișoara, Romania.
The PLCGEN project developed an end-to-end toolchain for model-driven software product-line engineering targeting IEC 61131-3 Structured Text. Work packages covered metamodel design, feature model integration, incremental generation, and round-trip recovery of variation points from legacy code. The project delivered an Eclipse-based IDE plugin, a library of reusable transformation modules, and the benchmark suite reported in the 2026 journal paper. Two Ph.D. students were funded through the project. Industry validation was carried out with one automation equipment manufacturer in Novi Sad and one in Subotica under non-disclosure agreements. The project produced nine peer-reviewed publications and one master thesis.

SYN-PRJ-0391.title: Safety-Aware Product-Line Modelling for Certified Automation Software
SYN-PRJ-0391.text:
SAFEPLL: Safety-Aware Product-Line Modelling for Certified Automation Software (Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia, 2022–2024).
Participants: R0995 work package leader; R0749 team member.
Partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad; Budapest University of Technology and Economics, Hungary; Automatika-Pro d.o.o., Novi Sad; RoboSystems Kft., Pécs, Hungary.
SAFEPLL addressed the integration of functional safety requirements into model-driven PLC product-line workflows, targeting IEC 62061 SIL 1 and SIL 2 certified applications. The project brought together researchers from Novi Sad and Budapest with two SME automation integrators. Veljko Pantelić led the work package on traceability from HAZOP artefacts to generated code, contributing the SysML parametric diagram transformation described in the 2021 conference paper. The project produced a methodology document adopted by both industrial partners as an internal development guideline, and delivered training workshops for engineering staff at both companies.

SYN-PRJ-0416.title: Hardware-in-the-Loop Validation on Open Platforms for Regional Automotive Suppliers
SYN-PRJ-0416.text:
HILVOP: Hardware-in-the-Loop Validation on Open Platforms for Regional Automotive Suppliers (Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma), 2020–2023).
Participants: R0356 principal investigator; R0531 team member; R0174 team member.
Partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad; Institute for Automotive Engineering Vojvodina (fictional); Politehnica University of Timișoara, Romania.
The project aimed to develop and validate a complete open-source HiL framework—comprising real-time kernel configurations, FPGA I/O boards, fault injection hardware, and test automation scripts—targeting small and medium-sized automotive ECU suppliers in the Vojvodina region who cannot afford commercial HiL systems. Three reference bench configurations were developed and documented, covering powertrain, body, and chassis domains. The framework was tested in collaboration with two regional suppliers under non-disclosure agreements. Deliverables include hardware design files, kernel build scripts, and a test case library with over 400 parametric test vectors. A graduate-level course module on open-source HiL was developed as a secondary outcome.

SYN-PRJ-0427.title: Energy-Efficient Edge Vibration Monitoring for Smart Manufacturing
SYN-PRJ-0427.text:
EDGEVIB: Energy-Efficient Edge Vibration Monitoring for Smart Manufacturing (Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research, 2023–2025).
Participants: R0206 principal investigator.
Partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad; Automat d.o.o. Novi Sad (fictional industrial partner); SensoraTech d.o.o. Novi Sad (fictional industrial partner).
EDGEVIB focuses on the integration of adaptive sampling, lightweight data compression, and on-device neural inference within a single firmware stack targeting coin-cell-powered BLE sensor nodes. The project collaborates with two companies at NTP Novi Sad for pilot deployments on conveyor drive motors and CNC spindle units. Key research questions concern the trade-off between inference duty cycle and battery longevity, the robustness of int8 models after incremental over-the-air updates, and the minimum sensor bandwidth needed to detect early-stage bearing faults. A secondary outcome is a teaching module on TinyML incorporated into the embedded systems curriculum at the Faculty of Technical Sciences.

SYN-PRJ-0432.title: Model-Driven Engineering Methods for Verified Automotive Embedded Software
SYN-PRJ-0432.text:
MDEVS: Model-Driven Engineering Methods for Verified Automotive Embedded Software (Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma), 2021–2024).
Participants: R0948 principal investigator; R0054 team member.
Partners: Faculty of Electronic Engineering, University of Niš; Slovak University of Technology in Bratislava; Embron d.o.o., Novi Sad.
The project investigates formal and semi-formal methods for verifying the correctness of model transformations used in AUTOSAR toolchains. Activities include: formalising ATL transformation semantics in a subset of Z notation, developing a property-based test generation framework for Ecore-based transformations, and building a prototype transformation verification tool integrated into the Eclipse ecosystem. The project collaborates with the Faculty of Electronic Engineering in Niš and the Slovak University of Technology in Bratislava. Industrial relevance is maintained through a liaison with a regional embedded-software consultancy that provides representative AUTOSAR model corpora for evaluation. The project supports two doctoral students and targets six journal publications over its four-year duration.

SYN-PRJ-0433.title: Toolchain Support for AUTOSAR Adaptive Platform Adoption in the Western Balkan Automotive Supply Chain
SYN-PRJ-0433.text:
AUTOCHAIN-AP: Toolchain Support for AUTOSAR Adaptive Platform Adoption in the Western Balkan Automotive Supply Chain (Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia, 2023–2025).
Participants: R0948 work package leader.
Partners: Faculty of Informatics, University of Debrecen; Pannonia Automotive Technologies Zrt., Győr; Embron d.o.o., Novi Sad; Vojvođanski Institut za Automobilske Tehnologije, Novi Sad.
AUTOCHAIN-AP addresses the limited readiness of small and medium-sized automotive suppliers in Hungary and Serbia to adopt the AUTOSAR Adaptive Platform. The Faculty of Technical Sciences leads the work package on toolchain adaptation, developing open-source Eclipse-based tools for service architecture modelling, SIM generation, and AP-specific consistency checking. The Hungarian partner contributes expertise in functional safety assessment. An associated training programme targets engineering staff at three participating supplier companies. The project includes a shared model repository and a joint evaluation campaign using industrial-grade AP reference implementations. Expected outputs include two open-source Eclipse plug-ins, four technical reports, and a practitioner training curriculum.

SYN-PRJ-0507.title: Graph-Based Attack Surface Management for Heterogeneous Enterprise and Industrial Networks
SYN-PRJ-0507.text:
GRAPHSEC: Graph-Based Attack Surface Management for Heterogeneous Enterprise and Industrial Networks (Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma), 2021–2024).
Participants: R0564 principal investigator.
Partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad; Faculty of Electronic Engineering, University of Niš; Cerberus Systems d.o.o., Novi Sad.
GRAPHSEC developed a unified framework for constructing, maintaining, and querying attack surface graphs that span both enterprise IT and operational technology network segments. The project produced an ontology for cross-domain vulnerability data normalisation, incremental graph-update algorithms validated on synthetic benchmarks, and a prototype scanning pipeline with Kubernetes awareness. Research outputs include six journal articles and four conference papers. The project also delivered an open-source toolchain released under the EUPL licence, and provided two industry partners from the Novi Sad technology sector with pilot assessments of their internal networks. Two doctoral students were trained under the project, one of whom defended in 2024.

SYN-PRJ-0509.title: Retraining Pathways for Adults in the Pannonian Region: Curriculum Models and Assessment Tools
SYN-PRJ-0509.text:
RETRAIN-AP: Retraining Pathways for Adults in the Pannonian Region: Curriculum Models and Assessment Tools (Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia, 2021–2023).
Participants: R1027 work package leader.
Partners: Faculty of Education, University of Szeged, Hungary; Regional Development Agency Vojvodina Nord, Subotica; Vocational Training Centre Novi Sad; South Transdanubia Training Institute, Pécs, Hungary.
RETRAIN-AP addressed the shortage of portable, recognised retraining programmes for adults affected by industrial restructuring in the Vojvodina–Southern Great Plain cross-border region. The project brought together two universities, one regional development agency, and two vocational training centres. Tanja Simić led the work package responsible for developing and piloting competency-based curriculum templates and the corresponding assessment tools across four occupational domains. The project produced a shared curriculum repository of twelve retraining modules, a multilingual assessor training package, and a policy brief submitted to the relevant ministries in both countries. Approximately 340 adults participated in piloted programmes over the project period.

SYN-PRJ-0510.title: Competency-Based Assessment Practices in Serbian Adult Technical Education
SYN-PRJ-0510.text:
KOMPAS: Competency-Based Assessment Practices in Serbian Adult Technical Education (Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma), 2023–2026).
Participants: R1027 principal investigator; R0367 team member; R0077 team member.
Partners: Institute for Educational Research, Belgrade; Faculty of Philosophy, University of Novi Sad.
KOMPAS investigates the gap between formally declared competency-based assessment practices in Serbian adult technical education and the assessment instruments and grading behaviours actually used by trainers. The project combines a national survey of 120 accredited training centres, qualitative case studies in eight centres, and a randomised rubric-training intervention with trainer cohorts. Primary outcomes include a diagnostic instrument for assessing assessment quality in training centres, an evidence base on the factors that support or hinder consistent competency assessment, and a trainer development module. The project is hosted at the Faculty of Philosophy, University of Novi Sad, with collaboration from the Institute for Educational Research in Belgrade.

SYN-PRJ-0511.title: Incremental and Calibrated Anomaly Recognition for Operational SCADA Systems
SYN-PRJ-0511.text:
ICAROS: Incremental and Calibrated Anomaly Recognition for Operational SCADA Systems (Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma), 2021–2024).
Participants: R1008 principal investigator; R0564 team member; R0043 team member.
Partners: Elektrodistribucija Bačka d.o.o., Novi Sad (fictional regional energy distributor); Faculty of Electronic Engineering, University of Niš.
ICAROS addressed the calibration and incremental update of unsupervised anomaly detectors deployed on live SCADA networks. The project developed threshold calibration procedures for detectors operating without labelled attack data, incremental Gaussian mixture and autoencoder update algorithms suited to concept drift induced by planned process changes, and a set of evaluation protocols for comparing detectors across different ICS protocol environments. A labelled Modbus/TCP and DNP3 benchmark dataset was produced and released. Partners included a regional energy distributor that provided controlled access to a monitoring mirror port on an operational substation network, enabling validation under real traffic conditions. The project supported two doctoral candidates and produced nine peer-reviewed publications.

SYN-PRJ-0512.title: Federated Anomaly Detection Across Distributed Industrial Control System Sites
SYN-PRJ-0512.text:
FEDICS: Federated Anomaly Detection Across Distributed Industrial Control System Sites (Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia, 2022–2025).
Participants: R1008 coordinator.
Partners: Department of Automation and Applied Informatics, Budapest University of Technology; Faculty of Informatics, University of Debrecen; Vodovod Vojvodina d.o.o., Novi Sad (fictional regional water utility).
FEDICS developed federated learning protocols enabling anomaly detection models trained at geographically distributed ICS sites to be aggregated without exchanging raw network traffic. The project addressed privacy constraints common in critical infrastructure contexts and evaluated ensemble aggregation strategies for combining site-level one-class classifiers. Pilot deployments were conducted at two water utility control centres and two district heating substations across the Hungarian–Serbian border region. The project also produced a joint curriculum module on ICS cybersecurity delivered at partner universities. Key deliverables included open-source federated aggregation software, two datasets, and six joint publications by the consortium.

SYN-PRJ-0513.title: Secure and Authenticated Firmware Lifecycle Management for Low-Power Industrial Wireless Networks
SYN-PRJ-0513.text:
SAFELINK: Secure and Authenticated Firmware Lifecycle Management for Low-Power Industrial Wireless Networks (Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma), 2021–2024).
Participants: R0286 principal investigator.
Partners: Електротехнички факултет, Универзитет у Београду; Faculty of Electrical Engineering and Computing, University of Zagreb.
Пројекат SAFELINK бави се дизајном, формалном анализом и практичном имплементацијом протокола за управљање животним циклусом фирмвера у индустријским бежичним мрежама са малом потрошњом енергије. Обухвата три главна правца: развој протокола за аутентификовану испоруку фирмвера усклађених са ограничењима LPWAN технологија, процену примењивости пост-квантних потписних схема на уређајима класе 1 и класе 2, и методологију за верификацију усклађености са индустријским безбедносним стандардима. Пројекат укључује лабораторијско тестирање на тестбеду са 40 чворова и сарадњу са два партнерска универзитета из региона. Планирани резултати укључују шест журналских радова, отворени репозиторијум имплементације протокола и нацрт техничке препоруке за индустријске кориснике.

SYN-PRJ-0514.title: Cross-Border Deployment of Secure LPWAN Telemetry Infrastructure for Environmental and Industrial Monitoring
SYN-PRJ-0514.text:
TRANS-LPWAN: Cross-Border Deployment of Secure LPWAN Telemetry Infrastructure for Environmental and Industrial Monitoring (Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia, 2022–2025).
Participants: R0286 work package leader.
Partners: University of Pécs, Faculty of Engineering and Information Technology, Hungary; ЈВП Воде Војводине, Нови Сад; Tiszamenti Vízügyi Igazgatóság, Szolnok, Hungary.
TRANS-LPWAN је прекогранични пројекат који развија заједничку инфраструктуру за телеметријски мониторинг животне средине и индустријских постројења у пограничном подручју Србије и Мађарске. Главни технички допринос тима са Факултета техничких наука односи се на безбедносни слој: дефинисање протокола за аутентификовану испоруку фирмвера на уређајима расположеним дуж прекограничних руских обала Тисе, управљање кључевима у административно хетерогеном окружењу са два различита национална оператора мреже, и успостављање процедуре за безбедну даљинску надоградњу уређаја без физичког приступа. Пројекат подразумева пилот-инсталацију на 35 теренских чворова.

SYN-PRJ-0517.title: Formal Regression Methods for Testing Embedded Control Firmware
SYN-PRJ-0517.text:
FRMTEST: Formal Regression Methods for Testing Embedded Control Firmware (Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma), 2021–2024).
Participants: R0233 principal investigator.
Partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad; Faculty of Electronic Engineering, University of Niš.
The project developed a coherent toolchain for specification-driven regression testing of embedded firmware, covering model authoring in a constrained EFA dialect, automated test case generation, hardware-in-the-loop execution adapters for STM32 and NXP platforms, and mutation-based suite adequacy assessment. Research activities included empirical studies on maintenance cost across firmware release histories and the development of the SpecMutate framework. The project funded two PhD students and one postdoctoral researcher and resulted in six peer-reviewed publications. Dissemination included a publicly released open-source toolchain prototype and a two-day industrial workshop held in Novi Sad attended by engineers from three regional firms.

SYN-PRJ-0518.title: Hardware-in-the-Loop Test Oracle Synthesis from Temporal Specifications
SYN-PRJ-0518.text:
HILSPEC: Hardware-in-the-Loop Test Oracle Synthesis from Temporal Specifications (bilateral, 2019–2021).
Participants: R0233 principal investigator.
Partners: INESC-ID, Instituto Superior Técnico, Lisbon, Portugal.
A bilateral collaboration with Instituto Superior Técnico, Lisbon, focusing on the automated construction of test oracles for HIL test environments using Signal Temporal Logic. The project combined expertise in temporal logic parameter synthesis from the Lisbon group with embedded testing infrastructure in Novi Sad. Joint work produced the STL oracle mining approach published in a journal article and a shared experimental dataset of motor control and temperature regulation firmware traces. Researcher exchanges included two short-term visits to Lisbon and one visit to Novi Sad by Portuguese collaborators.

SYN-PRJ-0546.title: Mixed-Script Information Retrieval for South Slavic Administrative and Legal Documents
SYN-PRJ-0546.text:
MixIR: Mixed-Script Information Retrieval for South Slavic Administrative and Legal Documents (Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma), 2021–2024).
Participants: R0349 principal investigator.
Partners: Pravni fakultet, Univerzitet u Novom Sadu; Opštinska uprava Novi Sad — Služba za informatiku; Viši sud u Novom Sadu.
Projekat MixIR bavio se izgradnjom pretražnih sistema prilagođenih srpskim administrativnim i pravnim dokumentima koji sadrže mešovito pismo. Cilj je bio razvoj metodoloških osnova i softverskih alata za normalizaciju pisma, transliteraciju i rangiranje koji se mogu primeniti u javnom sektoru. U okviru projekta izgrađen je anotiran korpus od 150 000 dokumenata, razvijen je open-source modul za normalizaciju pisma kompatibilan s popularnim okvirima za pretragu, i sprovedene su tri pilot implementacije u saradnji s jednom opštinskom upravom i jednim regionalnim sudom. Rezultati su objavljeni u sedam naučnih radova i prezentovani na tri međunarodne konferencije.

SYN-PRJ-0671.title: Interoperable Monitoring Middleware for Industrial IoT with Embedded Statistical Quality Control
SYN-PRJ-0671.text:
IIoTMON: Interoperable Monitoring Middleware for Industrial IoT with Embedded Statistical Quality Control (Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia, 2022–2025).
Participants: R0773 work package leader.
Partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad; Faculty of Information Technology and Bionics, Pázmány Péter Catholic University, Budapest; Regional Chamber of Commerce Subotica; Chamber of Industry and Commerce Bács-Kiskun County, Kecskemét.
This cross-border project addressed the integration of statistical process control logic into IoT middleware platforms used by small and medium-sized manufacturers in the Hungary–Serbia border region. The Novi Sad team led the work package on SPC algorithm design and embedded deployment, contributing drift-robust anomaly scoring modules certified to run on Cortex-M class microcontrollers. The Hungarian partner coordinated middleware architecture and communication protocols, while a regional chamber of commerce facilitated access to pilot companies. Three pilot deployments were completed: a food-packaging line, a metal-pressing workshop, and a grain-drying facility. Evaluation covered detection latency, energy consumption, and false-alarm frequency over 12-month monitoring periods.

SYN-PRJ-0744.title: Scalable Taint-Guided Fuzzing for Security Assessment of Industrial IoT Firmware
SYN-PRJ-0744.text:
FIRMSHIELD: Scalable Taint-Guided Fuzzing for Security Assessment of Industrial IoT Firmware (Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma), 2022–2025).
Participants: R0164 principal investigator.
Partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad; Mathematical Institute of the Serbian Academy of Sciences and Arts, Belgrade; Automatika d.o.o., Novi Sad.
FIRMSHIELD develops automated tooling for security assessment of firmware used in industrial IoT gateways and network-attached sensors deployed in Serbian manufacturing facilities. The project combines offline binary analysis—control-flow recovery and protocol grammar extraction—with online dynamic taint analysis to guide a grey-box fuzzer toward inputs that reach memory-unsafe code paths. A corpus of firmware images from cooperating industrial partners is maintained under a data-sharing agreement. The project funds two PhD students and one postdoctoral researcher, and supports a hardware testbed of 40 physical embedded devices across four CPU architectures. Results are published as open-source tooling and peer-reviewed papers.

SYN-PRJ-0799.title: Sparsity-Aware Intermediate Representations and Code Generation for Reconfigurable Compute Fabrics
SYN-PRJ-0799.text:
SPARC-IR: Sparsity-Aware Intermediate Representations and Code Generation for Reconfigurable Compute Fabrics (Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma), 2021–2024).
Participants: R0802 principal investigator; R1002 team member; R0071 team member.
Partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad; Faculty of Electronic Engineering, University of Niš; Vektron FPGA Design d.o.o., Novi Sad.
The project develops a compiler infrastructure centred on a typed intermediate representation that carries sparsity annotations as first-class attributes alongside standard SSA constructs. The main deliverables are: a formal semantics for the sparse-annotated IR, a suite of analysis and transformation passes implemented in LLVM, and an evaluation methodology based on reproducible benchmarks compiled to FPGA-emulated accelerator targets. The project involves three researchers from the Faculty of Technical Sciences and one from the Faculty of Electronic Engineering in Niš. Industrial relevance is validated through collaboration with a local FPGA design house that provides access to proprietary accelerator models under a non-disclosure agreement. Results are published in open access venues wherever journal policy permits.

SYN-PRJ-0800.title: Register Allocation Strategies for Heterogeneous Tensor Processing Units
SYN-PRJ-0800.text:
REGOPT: Register Allocation Strategies for Heterogeneous Tensor Processing Units (Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research, 2023–2025).
Participants: R0802 principal investigator; R0575 team member.
Partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad; Karlsruhe Institute of Technology, Germany.
This project investigates register allocation algorithms tailored to tensor processing units that expose multiple register files of different widths. The core research questions concern how to extend classical interference-graph methods to heterogeneous file configurations and how to integrate format-selection decisions into the allocation phase. The project funds one doctoral student and supports collaboration with the Karlsruhe Institute of Technology through short-term researcher exchanges. A secondary objective is to produce open-source LLVM passes that can be reused by other groups working on domain-specific accelerators. Project outputs include at least two journal publications and participation in one international compiler workshop.

SYN-PRJ-1580.title: Readiness Assessment Framework for ERP Adoption in SMEs of the Hungary–Serbia Cross-Border Region
SYN-PRJ-1580.text:
READY4ERP: Readiness Assessment Framework for ERP Adoption in SMEs of the Hungary–Serbia Cross-Border Region (Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia, 2019–2022).
Participants: R0064 coordinator.
Partners: Chamber of Commerce and Industry of Vojvodina (Novi Sad); West Pannonia Regional Development Agency (Győr); Faculty of Economics in Subotica, University of Novi Sad; University of Pécs, Faculty of Business and Economics.
The project developed and piloted a bilingual (Hungarian and Serbian) change readiness assessment toolkit tailored to SMEs operating in the Hungary–Serbia cross-border region. The toolkit comprised a validated 32-item diagnostic questionnaire, a facilitated workshop protocol, and an interpretation guide for use by business consultants without academic backgrounds. The toolkit was piloted in 22 SMEs across both countries, with paired pre- and post-pilot data collected to assess usability and predictive validity against six-month implementation progress markers. Training sessions for regional business support organisations were conducted on both sides of the border. All materials were released as open-access resources in both languages.

SYN-PRJ-1581.title: Post-Implementation Knowledge Retention in ERP-Dependent SMEs: Mechanisms, Measurement, and Intervention Design
SYN-PRJ-1581.text:
ERPKNOW: Post-Implementation Knowledge Retention in ERP-Dependent SMEs: Mechanisms, Measurement, and Intervention Design (Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma), 2022–2025).
Participants: R0064 principal investigator.
Partners: Faculty of Economics in Subotica, University of Novi Sad; Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad; Serbian Chamber of Commerce – Directorate for SMEs.
This project addresses the systematic erosion of ERP system knowledge that occurs in SMEs in the years following implementation, a phenomenon that limits long-term return on investment and drives costly re-implementation cycles. The project combines longitudinal competency measurement across a cohort of 30 Serbian SMEs, development and testing of a low-burden knowledge retention protocol, and construction of an open benchmark dataset. A key deliverable is a diagnostic instrument enabling SME managers to estimate their current knowledge retention risk without engaging external consultants. The project also funds two doctoral researchers and includes a policy brief directed at the Serbian government's digitalisation support programmes.

SYN-PRJ-1818.title: Telephone Speech Resources and Processing for Under-Resourced South Slavic Languages
SYN-PRJ-1818.text:
TELSRP: Telephone Speech Resources and Processing for Under-Resourced South Slavic Languages (Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma), 2023–2025).
Participants: R0265 team member.
Partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad; Faculty of Electrical Engineering, University of Sarajevo; Institute for Serbian Language, Serbian Academy of Sciences and Arts, Belgrade.
The project targets the creation of annotated telephone speech resources and the development of robust ASR components for Serbian and related South Slavic languages with limited existing data. Activities include corpus collection from call-centre partners in Serbia and Bosnia-Herzegovina, annotation toolchain development, and acoustic model training and evaluation. The project also covers dialect variation analysis and prepares data in formats compatible with CLARIN and META-SHARE infrastructures. Emilija Kapor contributes to corpus design, data collection coordination, and acoustic modelling experiments, and her doctoral research on noisy-channel ASR is embedded within the project's technical workplan.

SYN-PUB-00225.title: Uticaj morfološke redukcije na preciznost pretrage srpskih višeskriptnih dokumenata
SYN-PUB-00225.text:
Uticaj morfološke redukcije na preciznost pretrage srpskih višeskriptnih dokumenata (2013, journal, Infoteka: Časopis za informatiku i bibliotekarstvo).
Authors: Stefan Dragić (R0349); Jovana Ilić (outside co-author); Jasmina Arsić (R0664); Petar Hadžić (R0019).
Keywords: morfološka analiza; stemovanje; višeskriptni tekst; srpski jezik; rangiranje.
Srpski jezik je morfološki bogat, što znači da ista leksema može imati nekoliko desetina flektivnih oblika. U ovom radu ispitujemo kako stemovanje i lematizacija interaguju s postupkom normalizacije skripte pri izgradnji pretražnog indeksa. Koristimo tri stemera dostupna za srpski jezik — dva pravilo-zasnovana i jedan statistički — i kombinujemo ih s fonemskim kanonizacionim korakom opisanim u prethodnim radovima. Evaluacija je sprovedena na podskupu CLEF 2012 kolekcije koji sadrži dokumente u oba pisma. Rezultati pokazuju da redosled operacija (stemovanje pre ili posle normalizacije skripte) utiče na odziv, pri čemu stemovanje posle normalizacije daje konzistentno bolje rezultate za sve tri kombinacije (poboljšanje od 4 do 9 procentnih poena u MAP). Rad daje i analizu grešaka za 50 ručno pregledanih upita.

SYN-PUB-00336.title: Quantisation Effects on Convolutional Neural Networks for Vibration-Based Fault Detection Deployed on Cortex-M7
SYN-PUB-00336.text:
Quantisation Effects on Convolutional Neural Networks for Vibration-Based Fault Detection Deployed on Cortex-M7 (2020, journal, Microprocessors and Embedded Computing).
Authors: Vesna Knežević (R0206); Stefan Radovanović (outside co-author); Aleksandar Jeremić (R0696); Olivera Kuzmanović (R0028); Claudia Bauer (outside co-author).
Keywords: post-training quantisation; 1-D CNN; Cortex-M7; fault detection; mixed precision.
Post-training quantisation (PTQ) of floating-point convolutional neural networks to 8-bit fixed-point is a standard step for microcontroller deployment, but its effect on detection sensitivity for subtle bearing faults is not well characterised. This paper trains a small five-layer 1-D CNN on 30000 vibration segments (2048 samples each, 25.6 kHz) covering five fault categories and a healthy class, then applies symmetric and asymmetric per-layer and per-channel PTQ schemes. Accuracy degradation from float32 to int8 ranged from 0.4% (per-channel asymmetric) to 3.8% (per-layer symmetric) on the test set. Flash footprint dropped from 187 kB to 51 kB, and inference on an STM32H743 at 480 MHz required 4.1 ms, fitting comfortably within a 10 ms real-time budget. An ablation study shows that quantisation of the first convolutional layer accounts for 60–70% of total accuracy loss, suggesting a mixed-precision strategy where only that layer remains in float16.

SYN-PUB-00405.title: Calibration of a Battery Cell Emulator for BMS ECU Validation on a Low-Cost HiL Platform
SYN-PUB-00405.text:
Calibration of a Battery Cell Emulator for BMS ECU Validation on a Low-Cost HiL Platform (2023, conference, Proceedings of the 15th European Conference on Power Electronics and Embedded Control (EPEC)).
Authors: Darko Ninkov (R0356); Stefan Radovanović (outside co-author); Žarko Gavrilović (R0033); Cristian Morariu (outside co-author); Aleksandar Petrović (outside co-author).
Keywords: battery cell emulator; BMS ECU; Zynq SoC; impedance emulation; HiL calibration.
Battery management system (BMS) ECUs require accurate emulation of cell voltages, temperatures, and internal impedances during validation testing. This paper describes the design and calibration of a 12-cell emulator board built from precision voltage references, operational amplifier buffers, and a digitally programmable resistor network to model ohmic and diffusion impedances. The board interfaces to a Zynq-7020 SoC running the simulation host and updates cell parameters at 10 ms intervals via SPI. Calibration was performed against a reference Keithley source-measure unit across the 2.5–4.2 V operating range; voltage accuracy after calibration was ±2.1 mV at 25 °C and ±4.8 mV over the −20 °C to 60 °C range. A lithium iron phosphate cell model with 18 parameters was validated against 12 published drive-cycle datasets. A commercial BMS ECU was tested using 88 scripted test cases including cell balancing activation, state-of-charge estimation accuracy, and over-voltage protection response time. The total bill of materials for the emulator board was 280 EUR.

SYN-PUB-00491.title: Automated Adapter Generation from Mismatched Interface Specifications
SYN-PUB-00491.text:
Automated Adapter Generation from Mismatched Interface Specifications (2018, conference, Proceedings of the International Conference on Model-Driven Engineering and Software Systems (MODELS-SD)).
Authors: Milana Bošković (R0341); Nemanja Vukić (outside co-author); Petra Novak (outside co-author); Aleksandar Ivković (R0039); Boštjan Žagar (outside co-author).
Keywords: adapter generation; protocol mismatch; ATL; Apache Camel; finite-state machine.
When two systems must be integrated but their interface specifications describe incompatible message structures or interaction protocols, a protocol adapter is required. Manual adapter coding is error-prone and difficult to maintain. This paper presents a model-driven method in which both interfaces are described as finite-state machines annotated with typed message vocabularies; the mismatch is characterised as a set of transformation rules derived automatically by a constraint solver, and ATL templates then generate executable Apache Camel routes that implement the adapter. The method was applied to 22 real interface pairs collected from three companies in the manufacturing sector in Vojvodina. Fully automated generation succeeded in 16 cases; the remaining six required on average 2.3 hours of manual refinement. Generated adapters passed all supplied regression tests.

SYN-PUB-00492.title: Incremental Gaussian Mixture Models for Online Anomaly Detection in Continuous ICS Traffic Streams
SYN-PUB-00492.text:
Incremental Gaussian Mixture Models for Online Anomaly Detection in Continuous ICS Traffic Streams (2018, journal, Control Engineering Practice).
Authors: Jelena Kovačević (outside co-author); Aleksandar Ivković (R0039); Péter Horváth (outside co-author); Krisztina Kiss (R1008).
Keywords: incremental learning; Gaussian mixture model; online detection; concept drift; district heating.
This paper proposes an incremental variant of Gaussian mixture modelling (iGMM) for online anomaly detection in ICS traffic without the need for periodic full retraining. The algorithm maintains a fixed number of Gaussian components (K = 5 to 20 evaluated) and uses a Bayesian update rule to adjust component means, covariances, and weights with each arriving window of observations. Feature vectors are 32-dimensional, derived from 10-second traffic windows. The method was evaluated on a 180-day Modbus/TCP capture from a district heating control network and compared with a static GMM retrained every 24 hours. The iGMM maintained an F1 score within 0.03 of the periodically retrained model while reducing retraining compute cost by 94%. Concept drift induced by a planned process reconfiguration was detected as a persistent anomaly episode; a supervised reset mechanism based on operator acknowledgement was proposed and tested. Memory footprint per detector instance was under 120 KB.

SYN-PUB-00722.title: Detecting Stealthy Coil-Write Injection in Modbus Networks Using Temporal Autoencoder Ensembles
SYN-PUB-00722.text:
Detecting Stealthy Coil-Write Injection in Modbus Networks Using Temporal Autoencoder Ensembles (2023, journal, IEEE Transactions on Industrial Informatics).
Authors: Mirjana Stošić (outside co-author); Veljko Pantelić (R0995); Marek Novotný (outside co-author); Krisztina Kiss (R1008); Nina Dimitrijević (R0054).
Keywords: stealthy attacks; autoencoder ensemble; coil-write injection; Modbus; temporal features.
Stealthy coil-write injection attacks modify a small number of PLC output coils at irregular intervals designed to evade detectors sensitive only to rate or volume changes. This paper evaluates temporal autoencoder ensembles—ten autoencoders trained on temporally shuffled subsets of a 60-day Modbus/TCP capture—for detecting such attacks. Each autoencoder receives a 30-dimensional feature vector derived from 5-second windows including coil change frequency, write-to-read ratio per coil address, and inter-write interval statistics. Anomaly scores from ensemble members are aggregated by the maximum rule. Against 240 injected stealthy attack episodes of varying intensity (1 to 8 modified coils per window), the ensemble achieved recall of 0.89 at a false positive rate of 0.8 per hour, compared with 0.64 for a single autoencoder and 0.58 for a static threshold detector. Computational cost of the ensemble was 2.3× that of a single autoencoder, remaining feasible on edge hardware.

SYN-PUB-00755.title: Beat-Synchronous DCT Coding of Long-Term ECG Recordings
SYN-PUB-00755.text:
Beat-Synchronous DCT Coding of Long-Term ECG Recordings (2015, conference, Proceedings of the International Symposium on Biomedical Engineering and Medical Informatics (SBEMI)).
Authors: Milena Vuković (outside co-author); Lazar Šarić (R0057); Ana Nikolić (outside co-author).
Keywords: Holter ECG; DCT; beat segmentation; compression ratio; PRD.
Long-term (Holter) ECG recordings present compression challenges because gradual heart-rate drift shifts beat boundaries relative to fixed analysis windows. This work proposes a beat-synchronous discrete cosine transform (DCT) coder in which each beat is individually segmented using a Pan-Tompkins R-peak detector, zero-padded or truncated to a uniform 512-sample frame, and transformed to the DCT domain. Coefficient quantisation thresholds are derived per lead from a short training segment of the same recording, adapting to inter-patient variability. Tested on 18 two-lead 24-hour recordings at 250 Hz sampled at the Clinical Centre of Vojvodina, the coder achieves a mean compression ratio of 9.3:1 at a percentage root-mean-square difference (PRD) of 1.8%, with diagnostic quality preserved as assessed by two cardiologists. The encoding latency per beat averages 0.4 ms on a standard laptop CPU, confirming real-time feasibility.

SYN-PUB-00756.title: Wavelet Packet Decomposition for Compression of Neonatal EEG with Burst-Suppression Patterns
SYN-PUB-00756.text:
Wavelet Packet Decomposition for Compression of Neonatal EEG with Burst-Suppression Patterns (2016, journal, Signal, Image and Data Compression Letters).
Authors: Lazar Šarić (R0057); Tibor Farkaš (outside co-author); Jelena Graovac (outside co-author); Klaus Binder (outside co-author).
Keywords: EEG compression; burst-suppression; wavelet packet; best-basis; neonatal.
Neonatal EEG with burst-suppression (BS) patterns has highly non-stationary quasi-periodicity that challenges standard EEG compressors tuned to adult signals. This study applies wavelet packet decomposition with adaptive basis selection via the best-basis algorithm, followed by run-length and Huffman coding of thresholded coefficients. The degree of non-stationarity is quantified by a burst-ratio metric computed over 10-second epochs, and the decomposition depth is adjusted accordingly. A dataset of 22 neonatal eight-channel recordings (duration 2–4 hours each, sampled at 256 Hz) was provided by the Institute for Child and Youth Health Care of Vojvodina. At a reconstruction SNR of 30 dB, the adaptive scheme achieves a compression ratio of 6.8:1 compared to 4.9:1 for a fixed-depth packet transform, a gain attributed primarily to more efficient representation of suppression epochs. No statistically significant difference in burst detection sensitivity was found between original and reconstructed signals using an automated BS detector.

SYN-PUB-00757.title: Exploiting Inter-Beat Redundancy in ECG Compression via Differential Pulse-Code Modulation of DCT Coefficients
SYN-PUB-00757.text:
Exploiting Inter-Beat Redundancy in ECG Compression via Differential Pulse-Code Modulation of DCT Coefficients (2018, journal, IEEE Transactions on Biomedical Coding and Compression).
Authors: Klaus Binder (outside co-author); Lazar Šarić (R0057); Dragan Petković (outside co-author).
Keywords: inter-beat redundancy; DPCM; DCT; arithmetic coding; atrial fibrillation.
Consecutive cardiac beats in sinus rhythm show high morphological similarity, so their DCT coefficient sequences are strongly correlated across time. This paper models each lead's DCT coefficient track as a first-order autoregressive process and applies differential pulse-code modulation (DPCM) along the beat index rather than within a single beat. A predictor is trained on the first 30 seconds of each record and updated every 60 seconds to track slow morphological drift. Arithmetic coding is applied to the residual with a Laplacian model for the dominant low-frequency coefficients and a Cauchy model for higher-frequency ones. On a corpus of 48 single-lead records at 500 Hz, mean PRD is 1.4% at a compression ratio of 12.7:1, compared to 9.3:1 for independent per-beat DCT coding at matched PRD. The improvement degrades gracefully to 10.1:1 in the presence of atrial fibrillation, where inter-beat morphology is less predictable.

SYN-PUB-00758.title: Sparse Coding of PPG Signals Using a Learned Overcomplete Dictionary
SYN-PUB-00758.text:
Sparse Coding of PPG Signals Using a Learned Overcomplete Dictionary (2019, conference, Biomedical Compression and Coding Workshop (BCCW), Ljubljana).
Authors: Lazar Šarić (R0057); Marek Kowalski (outside co-author); Milena Vuković (outside co-author).
Keywords: PPG; sparse coding; K-SVD; overcomplete dictionary; matching pursuit.
Photoplethysmography (PPG) signals share quasi-periodic pulse structure but exhibit waveform variation due to respiratory modulation and motion artefact. This work trains a 256-atom overcomplete dictionary on a 10,000-pulse corpus using the K-SVD algorithm, then encodes each 200-sample pulse segment as a sparse combination of at most eight atoms, with atom indices and coefficients quantised to 8 and 16 bits respectively. A greedy matching pursuit selects atoms sequentially. On a held-out test set of 3,200 pulses from 16 subjects collected with a finger oximeter at 100 Hz, the method achieves a mean reconstruction error of 0.6% PRD at 3.2 bits per sample, compared to 4.1 bits per sample for a 12-coefficient per-pulse DCT coder at the same PRD. Dictionary generalisation across subjects is evaluated; inter-subject PRD increase is 0.3 percentage points on average, suggesting moderate portability without per-subject retraining.

SYN-PUB-00759.title: Compression of Multi-Lead ECG Using Joint Sparsity Across Leads
SYN-PUB-00759.text:
Compression of Multi-Lead ECG Using Joint Sparsity Across Leads (2020, journal, Journal of Biomedical Signal Analysis).
Authors: Lazar Šarić (R0057); Jelena Graovac (outside co-author); Sorin Moldovan (outside co-author).
Keywords: 12-lead ECG; joint sparsity; multi-lead compression; dictionary learning.
(no abstract)

SYN-PUB-00760.title: Rate-Distortion Analysis of Beat-Aligned Versus Free-Running Frames for ECG Entropy Coding
SYN-PUB-00760.text:
Rate-Distortion Analysis of Beat-Aligned Versus Free-Running Frames for ECG Entropy Coding (2021, journal, Signal Processing: Biomedical Applications).
Authors: Lazar Šarić (R0057); Dragan Petković (outside co-author).
Keywords: rate-distortion; ECG framing; entropy coding; context-adaptive arithmetic coding.
A systematic rate-distortion (R-D) comparison is made between two framing strategies for ECG entropy coding: beat-aligned frames that follow R-peak detection and free-running fixed-length frames of equivalent average duration. For each strategy, DCT coefficients are entropy coded with a context-adaptive arithmetic coder using three coefficient-magnitude context classes. R-D curves are computed at PRD values of 0.5%, 1%, 2%, 4%, and 8% across 60 single-lead records spanning normal sinus rhythm, sinus tachycardia, and first-degree AV block. Beat-aligned framing provides lower bit rates at PRD below 2%—a mean advantage of 0.4 bits per sample—while free-running framing is competitive at higher distortion where the frame-synchronisation overhead of beat detection is not amortised. The crossover PRD and its dependence on heart rate are characterised analytically. The results inform codec design choices in constrained implantable device scenarios.

SYN-PUB-00761.title: Learned Entropy Models for ECG Compression Using Recurrent Context Prediction
SYN-PUB-00761.text:
Learned Entropy Models for ECG Compression Using Recurrent Context Prediction (2023, conference, Proceedings of the European Conference on Signal and Image Processing (ECSIP), Vienna).
Authors: Lazar Šarić (R0057); Valentina Risso (outside co-author); Milena Vuković (outside co-author); Stefan Horvat (outside co-author).
Keywords: learned compression; entropy model; GRU; ECG; neural codec.
Recent learned image compression methods use neural networks to model the entropy of quantised latent representations. This paper adapts that paradigm to single-lead ECG by replacing the standard spatial entropy model with a small gated recurrent unit (GRU) that predicts the probability distribution of each DCT coefficient from the previous 16 coefficients in the same beat and from the corresponding coefficient in the preceding beat, capturing both intra-beat spectral structure and inter-beat temporal redundancy. The GRU has 64 hidden units and is trained jointly with a scalar quantiser on 120 hours of ECG drawn from publicly available databases. At a target PRD of 1.5%, the learned model uses 1.6 bits per sample compared to 2.1 bits per sample for a hand-designed Laplacian arithmetic coder, a 24% reduction. Model size is 48 kB, and decoding runs at 180× real time on a laptop CPU. The paper also analyses failure modes on arrhythmic beats.

SYN-PUB-00762.title: Embedded Coding of Physiological Signals: A Survey of Transform, Sparse, and Learned Approaches
SYN-PUB-00762.text:
Embedded Coding of Physiological Signals: A Survey of Transform, Sparse, and Learned Approaches (2024, book chapter, Advances in Biomedical Data Processing, Vol. 4 (Springer)).
Authors: Klaus Binder (outside co-author); Sorin Moldovan (outside co-author); Lazar Šarić (R0057); Jelena Graovac (outside co-author).
Keywords: survey; ECG; EEG; PPG; transform coding; sparse representation; learned compression.
This chapter surveys compression techniques for ECG, EEG, and PPG signals with emphasis on methods that exploit quasi-periodic structure. The first part covers classical transform-based approaches—DCT, wavelet, and wavelet packet—and their adaptation to beat-aligned or epoch-aligned frames. The second part reviews sparse representation methods, including structured dictionaries and joint multi-channel sparsity. The third part covers learned approaches: variational autoencoders, recurrent entropy models, and hybrid transform-neural architectures published up to early 2024. For each family, representative methods are compared on standardised datasets where available, and compression ratio, PRD, and encoder complexity are tabulated. The chapter also discusses application constraints: energy budgets in implantable devices, latency in real-time telemetry, and regulatory considerations for diagnostic-grade reconstruction. Open problems, including compression under non-stationary arrhythmic conditions and the lack of unified evaluation benchmarks, are identified.

SYN-PUB-00763.title: Variable-Rate Learned ECG Compression with a Single Model via Conditional Quantisation Noise
SYN-PUB-00763.text:
Variable-Rate Learned ECG Compression with a Single Model via Conditional Quantisation Noise (2026, preprint, arXiv preprint).
Authors: Lazar Šarić (R0057); Stefan Horvat (outside co-author); Valentina Risso (outside co-author).
Keywords: variable-rate compression; conditional quantisation; learned codec; ECG; single model.
Most learned compression models are trained at a fixed rate-distortion tradeoff, requiring separate models per operating point. This preprint proposes a single-model variable-rate ECG codec in which the quantisation noise level is fed as a scalar condition to both the GRU entropy model and a lightweight convolutional synthesis network. The condition scalar is drawn from a uniform grid of 16 values covering PRD targets from 0.5% to 8%. Training uses a weighted sum of rate and distortion losses with the condition scalar randomised each mini-batch. On a held-out test set of 48 single-lead records, the single conditioned model matches or slightly exceeds per-target trained models at all 16 operating points, with a maximum PRD deviation of 0.12 percentage points. Total model footprint is 61 kB, only 27% larger than a single fixed-rate model. Ablations confirm that conditioning the synthesis network is necessary; conditioning only the entropy model reduces the gain by roughly half.

SYN-PUB-00803.title: Kalman-filter-based plausibility checking for soil temperature sensor arrays with heterogeneous failure modes
SYN-PUB-00803.text:
Kalman-filter-based plausibility checking for soil temperature sensor arrays with heterogeneous failure modes (2024, journal, Measurement Science and Sensor Diagnostics).
Authors: Tijana Ostojić (outside co-author); Dragana Vukić (outside co-author); Jana Novotná (outside co-author); Vladan Nedić (R0060); Žarko Ivanović (R0630); Žarko Jakovljević (R0754).
Keywords: Kalman filter; soil temperature; sensor fault isolation; heat diffusion model; edge computation.
Soil temperature arrays deployed at multiple depths are subject to at least four distinct failure modes: complete open-circuit failure, partial short inducing constant-low readings, slow drift from burial-induced mechanical stress on thermistor leads, and intermittent noise injection from nearby electric fence controllers. This paper applies an ensemble Kalman filter to a seven-sensor vertical array, using a one-dimensional heat diffusion model as the process model parameterised with local soil thermal diffusivity estimates. The filter's innovation sequence is monitored with a chi-squared test to isolate faulty sensors without discarding the ensemble. In a 14-month field deployment at two sites in the Banat region, the method identified all 9 sensor faults confirmed by physical inspection, correctly attributed failure mode in 7 of those cases, and continued providing usable profile estimates from the remaining functional sensors throughout each fault episode. The paper also examines computational feasibility on a Cortex-M4 at 80 MHz, where the 7-state filter update completes in 3.8 ms, making edge execution practical with 30-minute sampling.

SYN-PUB-00857.title: Change Readiness as a Predictor of ERP Implementation Outcome in Serbian Manufacturing SMEs
SYN-PUB-00857.text:
Change Readiness as a Predictor of ERP Implementation Outcome in Serbian Manufacturing SMEs (2010, journal, Journal of Business Information Systems in Emerging Economies).
Authors: Zsuzsanna Molnár (R0064); Szabolcs Fehér (R0494); Petar Krstić (R0333); Árpád Fehér (outside co-author).
Keywords: change readiness; ERP implementation; SME; logistic regression; Vojvodina.
This paper examines the relationship between pre-implementation change readiness scores and project outcome in a sample of 47 manufacturing SMEs in the Vojvodina region that adopted ERP systems between 2005 and 2009. Change readiness was operationalised through a 24-item questionnaire adapted from Armenakis's readiness model, administered to top and middle management six months prior to go-live. Implementation outcome was assessed using a composite index combining schedule adherence, budget deviation, and user satisfaction measured twelve months post-go-live. Ordinal logistic regression revealed that change readiness scores explained 31% of the variance in outcome, with the subscale capturing management commitment showing the strongest individual effect. Firms with readiness scores in the lowest quartile were 4.2 times more likely to report failed or severely delayed implementations. The findings suggest that readiness diagnostic tools should be embedded in vendor pre-sales processes rather than treated as optional consulting add-ons.

SYN-PUB-00859.title: Post-Go-Live Knowledge Erosion in Small Enterprises: A Longitudinal Perspective
SYN-PUB-00859.text:
Post-Go-Live Knowledge Erosion in Small Enterprises: A Longitudinal Perspective (2014, journal, Information Systems Management Practice).
Authors: Dragana Savić (outside co-author); Zsuzsanna Molnár (R0064).
Keywords: knowledge erosion; post-go-live; SME; longitudinal study; competency testing.
This study tracks documented system knowledge among key users and IT staff at eleven small enterprises in Serbia's wholesale trade sector at three time points: immediately after go-live, twelve months later, and twenty-four months later. Knowledge was assessed through structured competency tests covering module-specific functionality and through analysis of internal support ticket logs. Mean competency test scores declined by 18% at month twelve and by 34% at month twenty-four relative to the post-training baseline. Support ticket volume increased correspondingly, peaking at month eighteen. Semi-structured interviews with general managers revealed that only two of the eleven firms maintained a formal knowledge retention plan; neither had experienced statistically significant test score declines. The paper discusses the role of staff turnover, vendor disengagement, and absence of internal documentation standards in accelerating knowledge loss. A simple retention index is proposed for SME use without specialist HR infrastructure.

SYN-PUB-00860.title: Measuring ERP Implementation Failure: Towards a Consistent Definition and Taxonomy for SME Research
SYN-PUB-00860.text:
Measuring ERP Implementation Failure: Towards a Consistent Definition and Taxonomy for SME Research (2015, journal, Balkan Journal of Information and Management Sciences).
Authors: Zsuzsanna Molnár (R0064).
Keywords: ERP failure taxonomy; measurement; literature review; SME; reporting standards.
The ERP implementation literature applies the term 'failure' inconsistently, making cross-study comparison unreliable. This conceptual paper reviews 94 empirical studies published between 1995 and 2013 and identifies six distinct operationalisations of failure ranging from project abandonment to long-term underutilisation. A taxonomy is proposed that separates project-level failure (budget, schedule) from adoption-level failure (utilisation, benefit realisation) and organisational failure (strategic misalignment). The taxonomy is applied retrospectively to the reviewed studies, and it is shown that 38% of results reported as contradictory become consistent when the failure type is held constant. The paper concludes with a minimum reporting standard recommended for researchers studying SME ERP outcomes, including required variables and suggested measurement intervals. The framework is intended to be practically applicable without requiring large-scale survey infrastructure.

SYN-PUB-00861.title: The Role of Middle Management in ERP Resistance Diffusion: Insights from the Serbian Retail Sector
SYN-PUB-00861.text:
The Role of Middle Management in ERP Resistance Diffusion: Insights from the Serbian Retail Sector (2016, conference, Proceedings of the South-East European Conference on Information Systems).
Authors: Miroslav Đorđević (outside co-author); Petra Kowalczyk (outside co-author); Zsuzsanna Molnár (R0064).
Keywords: middle management; resistance diffusion; SEM; retail; role threat.
Middle managers occupy a structurally ambiguous position during ERP implementations: they are expected to champion change while often feeling their own roles are threatened by system transparency. This mixed-methods study surveyed 112 middle managers at 29 retail companies in Serbia and conducted follow-up interviews with 18 of them. Quantitative analysis using structural equation modelling found that perceived role threat fully mediated the relationship between ERP transparency features and resistance behaviour, explaining 44% of the variance in resistance scores. The qualitative component revealed four distinct coping strategies: constructive engagement, passive compliance, covert obstruction, and overt refusal. Companies that involved middle managers in module configuration decisions reported lower resistance diffusion to their subordinates. Findings underscore that implementation success depends on explicitly addressing the middle-management layer rather than focusing change communication solely on executive sponsors and frontline users.

SYN-PUB-00863.title: Organisational Change Readiness Assessment Tools for ERP Projects: A Comparative Evaluation
SYN-PUB-00863.text:
Organisational Change Readiness Assessment Tools for ERP Projects: A Comparative Evaluation (2018, book chapter, Handbook of Enterprise Systems Implementation in Developing and Transitional Economies (Springer)).
Authors: Renáta Csordás (outside co-author); Björn Lindström (outside co-author); Zsuzsanna Molnár (R0064); Ivona Pejić (R0273).
Keywords: readiness assessment; instrument evaluation; ERP; SME; psychometric validation.
This book chapter reviews and comparatively evaluates six readiness assessment instruments available to organisations planning ERP implementations, including both commercially available diagnostic surveys and instruments proposed in academic literature. Each instrument is assessed against eight criteria: theoretical grounding, psychometric validation evidence, applicability to SMEs, coverage of structural versus attitudinal readiness, administration burden, cost, availability of normative benchmarks, and track record in published studies. Instruments developed primarily in North American large-enterprise contexts showed systematic weaknesses when applied to the SME setting: they underweighted resource scarcity and overweighted IT governance maturity. A composite checklist is provided that practitioners can adapt for organisations with fewer than 250 employees. The chapter also identifies gaps in instrument design, particularly the absence of tools that assess readiness dynamically across the implementation lifecycle rather than at a single pre-project snapshot.

SYN-PUB-00864.title: Turnover-Triggered Knowledge Loss After ERP Go-Live: Patterns from Twelve Vojvodina SMEs
SYN-PUB-00864.text:
Turnover-Triggered Knowledge Loss After ERP Go-Live: Patterns from Twelve Vojvodina SMEs (2019, journal, Balkan Journal of Information and Management Sciences).
Authors: Nataša Petrović (outside co-author); Branislava Erić (R0816); Szabolcs Fehér (R0494); Zsuzsanna Molnár (R0064).
Keywords: staff turnover; knowledge loss; ERP; SME; handover protocol.
(no abstract)

SYN-PUB-00865.title: Process Mining as a Diagnostic Tool for Post-Go-Live ERP Underutilisation
SYN-PUB-00865.text:
Process Mining as a Diagnostic Tool for Post-Go-Live ERP Underutilisation (2020, conference, Proceedings of the International Conference on Enterprise Systems and Digital Transformation).
Authors: Gábor Fekete (outside co-author); Zsuzsanna Molnár (R0064); Ana Luković (outside co-author).
Keywords: process mining; conformance checking; ERP underutilisation; post-go-live audit; Celonis.
(no abstract)

SYN-PUB-00866.title: ERP Implementation Failure Rates in the Western Balkans: A Structured Survey of 140 SMEs
SYN-PUB-00866.text:
ERP Implementation Failure Rates in the Western Balkans: A Structured Survey of 140 SMEs (2021, journal, Southeast European Journal of Information Systems and Digital Economy).
Authors: Samir Husić (outside co-author); Biljana Ilić (outside co-author); Árpád Fehér (outside co-author); Zsuzsanna Molnár (R0064).
Keywords: ERP failure rates; Western Balkans; SME survey; adoption failure; cross-country comparison.
Despite the importance of SME digitalisation to regional economic development, systematic data on ERP implementation outcomes in the Western Balkans are lacking. This paper reports results from a structured questionnaire survey administered to 140 SMEs in Serbia, Bosnia and Herzegovina, and North Macedonia that completed an ERP implementation between 2014 and 2019. Failure was operationalised using the taxonomy proposed in the author's 2015 work, allowing separate analysis of project-level and adoption-level failure. Project-level failure rates were 29% in Serbia, 34% in Bosnia and Herzegovina, and 31% in North Macedonia. Adoption-level failure rates were substantially higher: 52%, 58%, and 55% respectively. Logistic regression identified absence of a dedicated internal project manager, implementation duration exceeding eighteen months, and use of heavily customised deployments as the strongest predictors of both failure types. The data are made available as a supplementary dataset to encourage replication.

SYN-PUB-00868.title: Knowledge Transfer Mechanisms in ERP Transitions Between Incumbent and Successor Systems: Evidence from SME Upgrades
SYN-PUB-00868.text:
Knowledge Transfer Mechanisms in ERP Transitions Between Incumbent and Successor Systems: Evidence from SME Upgrades (2023, conference, Proceedings of the Danube Region Conference on Business Informatics).
Authors: Gábor Fekete (outside co-author); Zsuzsanna Molnár (R0064); Éva Sándor-Pintér (outside co-author).
Keywords: knowledge transfer; ERP replacement; system succession; tacit knowledge; SME.
When an SME replaces one ERP system with another, it faces a compound knowledge transfer challenge: institutional knowledge embedded in the old system must be surfaced and re-contextualised for the new platform while new functionality is simultaneously introduced. This study examines twelve such system replacement projects in Serbian and Hungarian SMEs using a retrospective interview and document analysis approach. Data sources included project documentation, training records, and interviews with key users and managers conducted six months after go-live on the successor system. Analysis identified three knowledge transfer modes: tacit-to-tacit (mentoring), explicit-to-explicit (document migration), and mixed (facilitated workshops). Companies relying primarily on the tacit-to-tacit mode reported significantly higher user satisfaction but were more vulnerable to knowledge loss when key informants departed. The paper proposes a sequencing model for ERP replacement projects that prioritises explicit documentation of business-critical workarounds before decommissioning the incumbent system.

SYN-PUB-00870.title: Benchmarking Post-Go-Live Support Structures in Serbian SMEs: Findings from a Mixed-Methods Study
SYN-PUB-00870.text:
Benchmarking Post-Go-Live Support Structures in Serbian SMEs: Findings from a Mixed-Methods Study (2026, preprint, SSRN Working Papers in Business Informatics).
Authors: Ana Luković (outside co-author); Dario Marinković (outside co-author); Zsuzsanna Molnár (R0064).
Keywords: post-go-live support; vendor support; adoption quality; SME; utilisation coverage.
This preprint reports preliminary findings from an ongoing study examining the formal and informal support structures that SMEs maintain after ERP go-live, and their relationship to long-term adoption quality. Survey data were collected from 96 SMEs in Serbia across manufacturing, retail, and logistics sectors in 2024 and 2025. Support structures were categorised along three dimensions: contractual vendor support, internal first-line support capacity, and peer or community-based support.
