Only 21% of firms maintained all three categories; 38% relied exclusively on vendor contracts, which were typically activated reactively. Adoption quality, measured via a utilisation coverage index and a reported benefit realisation score, was significantly higher in firms with internal first-line support capacity than in those without (mean utilisation coverage 74% vs 51%). Qualitative interviews with 24 managers from the sample are ongoing; preliminary themes suggest that cost sensitivity and lack of awareness of alternatives rather than disinterest in training drive low internal support investment.

SYN-PUB-00958.title: Threshold Selection Strategies for Binary Classifiers Trained on Severely Imbalanced Sensor Data
SYN-PUB-00958.text:
Threshold Selection Strategies for Binary Classifiers Trained on Severely Imbalanced Sensor Data (2013, journal, Journal of Applied Signal Processing and Machine Intelligence).
Authors: Olivera Rakić (R0071); Dunja Erić (R0890); Dragan Vuković (outside co-author).
Keywords: class imbalance; threshold selection; fault detection; sensor data; classification.
Operational sensor logs from industrial machinery frequently exhibit class imbalance ratios exceeding 1:500 between fault and normal states. Standard classifiers trained on such data learn to minimise overall loss by almost entirely ignoring the minority class. This paper evaluates seven threshold-moving strategies—including cost-sensitive calibration, F-beta optimisation, and precision-recall break-even—on four publicly available and two proprietary vibration datasets with imbalance ratios between 1:200 and 1:1200. Experiments use three base classifiers: logistic regression, a gradient-boosted tree, and a one-dimensional convolutional network. Results show that threshold strategies interacting with the base classifier type produce large performance variation: no single strategy dominates across all settings. For the convolutional model, precision-recall break-even consistently achieves the best G-mean scores, while cost-sensitive calibration favours recall at an unacceptable precision cost on the most extreme imbalance cases. Recommendations are given as a decision guide indexed by imbalance ratio and acceptable false-positive rate.

SYN-PUB-00959.title: Comparative Evaluation of Oversampling Techniques for Multivariate Time-Series Fault Classification
SYN-PUB-00959.text:
Comparative Evaluation of Oversampling Techniques for Multivariate Time-Series Fault Classification (2015, conference, Proceedings of the Balkan Conference on Intelligent Systems (BCIS)).
Authors: Olivera Rakić (R0071); Miroslav Stanić (outside co-author); Ana Horvat (outside co-author).
Keywords: oversampling; SMOTE; multivariate time-series; fault classification; AUPRC.
Synthetic minority oversampling (SMOTE) and its variants were originally designed for tabular data and do not respect temporal dependencies present in multivariate sensor streams. This paper compares six oversampling methods—SMOTE, Borderline-SMOTE, ADASYN, TimeGAN-based synthesis, DTW-barycentric averaging, and a simple window-jitter baseline—on three industrial datasets: hydraulic pump telemetry, CNC spindle vibration, and electrical substation load measurements. Each dataset is split chronologically to avoid leakage, and ten-fold cross-validation is applied within the training segment. Evaluation uses area under the precision-recall curve (AUPRC) and macro F1. DTW-barycentric averaging achieves the highest AUPRC on the two vibration datasets (0.84 and 0.79 respectively) but underperforms TimeGAN on the load dataset. Window jitter, despite its simplicity, ranks third overall and substantially outperforms standard SMOTE in all tested settings, suggesting that temporal coherence is more important than interpolation sophistication for most fault types.

SYN-PUB-00960.title: A Semi-Supervised One-Class SVM Framework for Rare-Event Detection with Partial Label Information
SYN-PUB-00960.text:
A Semi-Supervised One-Class SVM Framework for Rare-Event Detection with Partial Label Information (2018, journal, Pattern Recognition and Data Analysis).
Authors: Olivera Rakić (R0071); Bojana Filipović (outside co-author); Tomáš Novotný (outside co-author).
Keywords: one-class SVM; semi-supervised learning; anomaly detection; partial labels; constraint optimisation.
In many industrial monitoring scenarios, operators can label a small fraction of anomalous events while the majority of the data stream remains unlabelled. Standard one-class SVM (OC-SVM) ignores partial labels entirely; this paper proposes a constrained OC-SVM variant that incorporates labelled anomalies as must-outside constraints during kernel optimisation. The method is evaluated on four datasets: bearing degradation signals, network intrusion logs, medical ECG records with annotated arrhythmia bursts, and a synthetic benchmark with controlled sparsity of positive labels (1%, 5%, 10%, 20%). At 5% label density, the constrained OC-SVM reduces false-negative rate by 18 percentage points relative to the unconstrained baseline without statistically significant change in false-positive rate. The framework adds a single hyperparameter controlling constraint weight and remains tractable for datasets up to 500,000 samples with an RBF kernel. Ablation studies confirm that gains diminish beyond 15% label density, at which point a supervised SVM becomes preferable.

SYN-PUB-00961.title: Detecting Concept Drift in Streaming Fault Data Using Adaptive Windowing and Classifier Ensemble Voting
SYN-PUB-00961.text:
Detecting Concept Drift in Streaming Fault Data Using Adaptive Windowing and Classifier Ensemble Voting (2019, journal, IEEE Transactions on Industrial Data Streams).
Authors: Dragan Vuković (outside co-author); Olivera Rakić (R0071); Katarina Jovanović (outside co-author); Lukas Bauer (outside co-author).
Keywords: concept drift; ADWIN; ensemble learning; streaming data; gas compressor monitoring.
Industrial processes evolve over time due to wear, seasonal variation, and deliberate operational changes, causing the statistical properties of sensor streams to shift. Classifiers trained on historical data degrade silently when such drift occurs. This work applies ADWIN-based adaptive windowing to trigger retraining of a rotating ensemble of gradient-boosted classifiers on a gas compressor monitoring stream collected over 26 months. Three types of artificial concept drift—sudden, gradual, and recurrent—are injected into a held-out test segment and detection latency is measured. ADWIN combined with ensemble voting detects sudden drift with a median latency of 47 samples and gradual drift with a latency of 190 samples, compared to 620 samples for a non-adaptive baseline. Memory overhead is bounded by retaining at most five ensemble members. The study also documents four naturally occurring drifts identified in the real 26-month log, correlating two of them with documented maintenance events.

SYN-PUB-00962.title: Self-Training with Uncertainty Filtering for Semi-Supervised Anomaly Detection in High-Dimensional Process Data
SYN-PUB-00962.text:
Self-Training with Uncertainty Filtering for Semi-Supervised Anomaly Detection in High-Dimensional Process Data (2021, journal, Expert Systems with Applications and Engineering).
Authors: Miroslav Stanić (outside co-author); Sanja Kovačević (outside co-author); Olivera Rakić (R0071).
Keywords: self-training; pseudo-labelling; Monte Carlo dropout; uncertainty estimation; semi-supervised learning.
Self-training iteratively assigns pseudo-labels to unlabelled samples and retrains a classifier, but in highly imbalanced settings pseudo-label noise disproportionately corrupts the minority class. This paper introduces an uncertainty filter based on prediction entropy estimated through Monte Carlo dropout: only samples whose entropy falls below a calibrated threshold enter the pseudo-labelled pool. The method is tested on three high-dimensional datasets (128 to 512 features) derived from chemical reactor sensors, semiconductor fabrication metrology, and server performance counters, all with imbalance ratios above 1:300. Starting from 2% labelled data, the filtered self-training approach reaches 91% of fully supervised F1 performance on the chemical reactor dataset, compared to 74% for standard self-training. Runtime scales linearly in dataset size and does not require architectural changes beyond enabling dropout at inference time. A sensitivity analysis over the entropy threshold is provided.

SYN-PUB-00963.title: Benchmarking Real-Time Anomaly Detection Pipelines on Edge Hardware Under Memory and Latency Constraints
SYN-PUB-00963.text:
Benchmarking Real-Time Anomaly Detection Pipelines on Edge Hardware Under Memory and Latency Constraints (2022, conference, Proceedings of the European Workshop on Embedded Machine Learning (EWEML)).
Authors: Olivera Rakić (R0071); Nikola Đurić (outside co-author); María Ortega Blanco (outside co-author); Petar Stevanović (R0833).
Keywords: edge inference; real-time anomaly detection; model quantisation; FPGA; SCADA.
Deploying anomaly detection at the network edge requires balancing model accuracy against strict memory budgets and latency targets. This paper profiles eight detection pipelines—including isolation forest, lightweight autoencoder, quantised convolutional network, and random forest with feature hashing—on three edge boards (an ARM Cortex-A72 single-board computer, a microcontroller-class device with 256 KB RAM, and an FPGA soft-processor). Workloads are drawn from wind turbine SCADA signals and smart meter load profiles sampled at 10 Hz and 1 Hz respectively. The quantised convolutional network fits within 200 KB and achieves 97% of its full-precision AUPRC while meeting a 5 ms per-window latency budget on the ARM board. On the microcontroller, only isolation forest and feature-hashed random forest are deployable; the latter achieves the better AUPRC (0.71 vs. 0.63). All profiling code and configuration files are released under an open licence.

SYN-PUB-00964.title: Imbalanced Learning for Industrial Time-Series: A Structured Review of Methods and Evaluation Practices
SYN-PUB-00964.text:
Imbalanced Learning for Industrial Time-Series: A Structured Review of Methods and Evaluation Practices (2023, book chapter, Advances in Machine Learning for Industrial Applications (Springer series)).
Authors: Bojana Filipović (outside co-author); Tomáš Novotný (outside co-author); Olivera Rakić (R0071); Sonja Bošković (R0923); Ivana Petrović (outside co-author); Krisztina Kiss (R1008).
Keywords: survey; imbalanced learning; industrial time-series; evaluation metrics; concept drift.
This chapter surveys the literature on learning from imbalanced industrial time-series data published between 2010 and 2022, covering approximately 160 papers. The chapter is organised around five methodological families: resampling, cost-sensitive training, anomaly-detection-based approaches, threshold adjustment, and ensemble methods. For each family, representative algorithms are described, and reported evaluation metrics are tabulated. A recurring finding is that many papers report only accuracy or AUC-ROC despite these being insensitive to minority-class performance at high imbalance ratios; the chapter argues for systematic reporting of AUPRC and G-mean alongside domain-relevant cost measures. A taxonomy of evaluation pitfalls specific to temporal data—including label leakage across temporal folds and inappropriate use of stratified k-fold on non-stationary streams—is presented. The chapter concludes with a structured list of open problems, including the combination of concept drift adaptation with imbalanced learning and the lack of standardised public benchmarks for industrial fault streams.

SYN-PUB-00965.title: Active Learning with Query-by-Committee for Labelling Efficiency in Imbalanced Fault Streams
SYN-PUB-00965.text:
Active Learning with Query-by-Committee for Labelling Efficiency in Imbalanced Fault Streams (2024, journal, Machine Learning for Industrial Systems).
Authors: Olivera Rakić (R0071); Sanja Kovačević (outside co-author); Lukas Bauer (outside co-author); Milica Nikolić (R0503).
Keywords: active learning; query by committee; labelling cost; minority class; fault streams.
Obtaining labelled fault examples is expensive in industrial settings because it requires expert inspection. Active learning selects the most informative unlabelled samples for expert annotation, potentially reducing labelling cost. This paper applies query-by-committee (QBC) using a committee of five classifiers—two gradient-boosted trees, two SVMs with different kernels, and a shallow neural network—to three simulated fault streams with imbalance ratios of 1:100, 1:500, and 1:2000. A disagreement-weighted sampling strategy biased toward minority-class candidates is introduced to counteract the tendency of standard QBC to query near the decision boundary in the majority class region. The biased strategy reaches 90% of fully labelled F1 using only 12% of available labels at 1:500 imbalance, compared to 21% for unbiased QBC and 31% for random sampling. Latency until the first useful model (F1 > 0.5) is reduced from 840 queries to 310 queries under the biased strategy.

SYN-PUB-00967.title: Embedded Predictive Coding for Inertial Measurement Unit Streams in Vehicle Telematics
SYN-PUB-00967.text:
Embedded Predictive Coding for Inertial Measurement Unit Streams in Vehicle Telematics (2020, journal, Vehicular Communications).
Authors: Uroš Filipović (outside co-author); Jovanka Đorđević (outside co-author); Olivera Rakić (R0071); Branislav Stojanović (R0641); Ksenija Mitrović (R0552).
Keywords: predictive coding; IMU; vehicle telematics; recursive least squares; Cortex-M7; event retention.
Fleet telematics units generate high-volume 6-axis IMU data at 100 Hz used for driver behaviour scoring and road surface classification. This paper describes a predictive coder for IMU streams that uses second-order linear prediction with coefficients updated per frame via a recursive least-squares routine fitting within 2 kB of working memory on a Cortex-M7 at 216 MHz. Residuals are quantised with a non-uniform scalar quantiser whose levels are adapted to a Laplacian residual distribution. Across 480 km of mixed urban, motorway, and rural driving logged with an instrumented vehicle, the coder achieves a mean compression ratio of 5.2:1 at 3.1% root-mean-square normalised distortion. Hard braking and pothole events, identified by a reference classifier, were preserved with 96.4% event retention versus 78.1% for a non-adaptive arithmetic coder at the same bit rate. Computational load was 1.4% of CPU capacity, leaving ample headroom for concurrent GNSS and CAN processing.

SYN-PUB-00990.title: Characterising packet loss patterns in NB-IoT deployments across mixed urban and agricultural terrain in Vojvodina
SYN-PUB-00990.text:
Characterising packet loss patterns in NB-IoT deployments across mixed urban and agricultural terrain in Vojvodina (2016, conference, Proceedings of the Central European Wireless Sensor Networks Workshop (CEWSNW)).
Authors: Žarko Jakovljević (R0754); Luka Horvatović (outside co-author); Lidija Arsić (R0073); Anita Fekete (outside co-author); Siniša Ranković (outside co-author).
Keywords: NB-IoT; packet loss; link characterisation; Vojvodina; Markov chain.
This paper reports an empirical measurement campaign assessing NB-IoT link behaviour at 29 fixed sites across a 2,400 km² area in the Vojvodina region, covering densely built township centres, sparse rural roads, and open crop fields. Uplink and downlink packets were transmitted at 5-minute intervals over 60 consecutive days using commercial SIM7020 modules attached to custom data loggers. The dataset comprises approximately 1.2 million transmission attempts per direction. Results show that packet loss rate is strongly bimodal: median loss of 1.3 percent at sites within 4 km of a base station versus 18.7 percent at sites beyond 12 km. Burst loss episodes lasting more than 30 minutes were observed predominantly between 05:00 and 08:00 local time, correlated with agricultural machinery interference signatures identified via received signal strength indicators. A Markov chain model fitted to the burst statistics achieves a Kolmogorov–Smirnov distance of 0.04 against the measured distribution. The characterisation informs retransmission and local buffering policies discussed in a companion study.

SYN-PUB-01006.title: Eye-Tracking Evidence for Cognitive Overload During Complex Multi-Screen Induction Tasks
SYN-PUB-01006.text:
Eye-Tracking Evidence for Cognitive Overload During Complex Multi-Screen Induction Tasks (2021, conference, Proceedings of the Central European Conference on Human Factors in Work and Technology).
Authors: Ognjen Ninkov (R0386); Emilija Jokić (R0074); Miloš Stanković (outside co-author); Zlata Ristić (R0291); Eva Horváth (outside co-author).
Keywords: eye-tracking; cognitive overload; dual-screen; induction; learning efficiency.
Twenty-eight participants with no prior experience in a target administrative task completed a simulated induction exercise across either a single-screen or dual-screen workstation setup. Eye-tracking data were recorded throughout using a desktop-mounted Tobii TX300 system. Dependent measures included fixation duration, saccade length, dwell time on instructional versus task areas, and a secondary task reaction time used as an online cognitive load indicator. Participants in the single-screen condition showed longer average fixation durations on instructional text (391 ms vs. 312 ms) and more frequent regressions, suggesting greater processing difficulty despite—or because of—the reduced spatial separation of information sources. Dual-screen participants completed the task 18% faster on average but scored 11% lower on a subsequent unannounced retention test. The results partially support a distinction between performance efficiency and learning efficiency and have direct implications for workstation design during early-tenure onboarding.

SYN-PUB-01116.title: Noise-robust Serbian speech recognition for telephone audio
SYN-PUB-01116.text:
Noise-robust Serbian speech recognition for telephone audio (2024, journal, Speech Technology Journal).
Authors: Dušan Milošević (R0083); Jelena Vuković (outside co-author); Marko Đorđević (outside co-author); Petra Halász (outside co-author).
Automatic speech recognition (ASR) systems deployed in telephone call centres routinely encounter background noise, channel distortions, and codec artefacts that degrade recognition accuracy. This paper presents a noise-robust ASR framework specifically designed for Serbian telephone audio. We compile a new evaluation benchmark drawn from real call-centre recordings and augment an existing Serbian speech corpus with synthetically degraded samples covering eight noise categories at signal-to-noise ratios between 0 dB and 20 dB. Acoustic models based on a hybrid TDNN-HMM architecture are trained with multi-condition augmentation, and we further investigate the effectiveness of spectral mapping and feature normalisation as front-end compensations. Results show that our best system achieves a 17.3% relative word-error-rate reduction over a clean-trained baseline on the noisy telephone benchmark while retaining competitive performance on clean read speech. We additionally evaluate domain adaptation using a small set of in-domain transcribed calls, demonstrating that even 30 minutes of labelled telephone data yields measurable gains. The released models and benchmark encourage reproducible research on under-resourced Slavic languages in noisy telephony conditions.

SYN-PUB-01117.title: A Serbian text-to-speech voice built from 20 hours of audio
SYN-PUB-01117.text:
A Serbian text-to-speech voice built from 20 hours of audio (2022, conference, Interspeech-style Workshop on Low-Resource Speech).
Authors: Dušan Milošević (R0083); Svetlana Ristić (outside co-author); Tomáš Novák (outside co-author).
High-quality text-to-speech (TTS) synthesis for low-resource languages typically demands hundreds of hours of professionally recorded audio, an impractical requirement for Serbian. This paper describes the construction of a natural-sounding Serbian TTS voice trained from only 20 hours of studio-quality recordings produced by a single female speaker. We adopt a Tacotron-2-style sequence-to-sequence acoustic model combined with a flow-based neural vocoder and investigate several data-efficiency techniques including transfer learning from a related Slavic language, phoneme-level duration modelling, and prosody embedding. Objective evaluations using mel-cepstral distortion and voiced/unvoiced decision rates confirm the viability of the approach, while a listening test with 42 native Serbian speakers yields a mean opinion score of 4.01, competitive with systems trained on substantially larger corpora. We publicly release the trained model weights and the pronunciation lexicon developed during the project. The work establishes a reproducible pipeline for building decent-quality TTS voices for other South Slavic languages that currently lack such resources.

SYN-PUB-01118.title: Building a telephone speech corpus for Serbian: collection, annotation, and baseline ASR results
SYN-PUB-01118.text:
Building a telephone speech corpus for Serbian: collection, annotation, and baseline ASR results (2023, conference, Language Resources and Evaluation Conference (LREC-style)).
Authors: Marko Đorđević (outside co-author); Ivana Petrović (outside co-author); Dušan Milošević (R0083); Zoran Nikolić (outside co-author).
Keywords: Serbian; speech corpus; telephone speech; automatic speech recognition; dialect.
Scarcity of annotated telephone-quality speech data is a primary obstacle to advancing automatic speech recognition for Serbian. This paper describes the design and construction of TeleSrp-300, a 300-hour corpus of simulated and real telephone conversations in Serbian, collected from 180 speakers across three dialect regions. Recordings were captured over both VoIP and PSTN channels, then manually transcribed and annotated for speaker identity, channel type, and background noise level. We describe the annotation workflow, quality-control procedures, and the resulting inter-annotator agreement scores. Baseline ASR experiments using a Kaldi-based recipe establish word error rates that serve as reproducible reference points for the community. Comparative analysis across dialect sub-sets reveals that non-standard dialectal pronunciations account for approximately 34% of substitution errors in the baseline model. The corpus and associated tools are made freely available for academic use, and we outline a roadmap for extending coverage to spontaneous conversational speech and code-switching scenarios common in Serbian urban environments.

SYN-PUB-01119.title: End-to-end speech recognition for Serbian using transformer architectures with limited training data
SYN-PUB-01119.text:
End-to-end speech recognition for Serbian using transformer architectures with limited training data (2023, conference, Proceedings of the Annual Conference of the International Speech Communication Association (INTERSPEECH-style)).
Authors: Jelena Vuković (outside co-author); Ana Lukić (outside co-author); Dušan Milošević (R0083).
Keywords: automatic speech recognition; transformer; Conformer; low-resource; Serbian; fine-tuning.
End-to-end models have largely supplanted hybrid systems in high-resource speech recognition, yet their appetite for labelled data makes direct application to low-resource languages such as Serbian challenging. This paper investigates how transformer-based end-to-end architectures—specifically Conformer CTC/Attention and Whisper fine-tuning—perform when training data is limited to under 100 hours of Serbian speech. We systematically compare three data augmentation regimes (SpecAugment, speed perturbation, and room-impulse-response simulation) and two cross-lingual initialisation strategies (from Croatian and from a massively multilingual model). Experiments on three test sets of varying acoustic conditions show that fine-tuning a multilingual pre-trained checkpoint with aggressive augmentation outperforms all from-scratch baselines, achieving a word error rate of 9.4% on read speech and 22.1% on spontaneous telephone conversations. We also quantify the effect of vocabulary size and subword unit type for Serbian's inflectional morphology, finding that character-level models are surprisingly competitive with byte-pair-encoding variants when training data is scarce.

SYN-PUB-01120.title: Pronunciation lexicon construction for Serbian TTS: a rule-based and data-driven hybrid approach
SYN-PUB-01120.text:
Pronunciation lexicon construction for Serbian TTS: a rule-based and data-driven hybrid approach (2021, journal, Speech and Language Technology Journal).
Authors: Dušan Milošević (R0083); Svetlana Ristić (outside co-author); Miloš Filipović (outside co-author).
Keywords: pronunciation lexicon; grapheme-to-phoneme; Serbian; speech synthesis; text-to-speech.
A high-coverage pronunciation lexicon is a fundamental component of both speech synthesis and recognition systems, yet no publicly available standardised lexicon exists for Serbian. This paper presents a methodology for constructing such a lexicon by combining hand-crafted grapheme-to-phoneme rules derived from Serbian orthographic conventions with a sequence-to-sequence neural model trained on 28,000 manually verified word–phoneme pairs. We introduce a novel hybrid decoding strategy that applies the rule-based system as a constraint over the neural model's beam search, reducing the phoneme error rate on a held-out test set to 2.1%, compared with 4.7% for the neural-only baseline. The resulting lexicon covers 210,000 headwords including inflected forms, proper nouns, and foreign loanwords common in contemporary Serbian media. Integration experiments within the TTS pipeline described in our earlier work confirm that the improved lexicon raises the mean opinion score by 0.13 points. The lexicon is released under an open licence to facilitate reproducibility.

SYN-PUB-01121.title: Speaker adaptation for call-centre ASR: few-shot techniques for Serbian conversational speech
SYN-PUB-01121.text:
Speaker adaptation for call-centre ASR: few-shot techniques for Serbian conversational speech (2022, journal, Journal of Speech Processing and Communication).
Authors: Dušan Milošević (R0083); Marko Đorđević (outside co-author); Branimir Kovačević (outside co-author).
Keywords: speaker adaptation; call centres; automatic speech recognition; Serbian; x-vectors; few-shot.
In deployed call-centre environments, ASR systems routinely encounter a wide diversity of speakers whose vocal characteristics differ substantially from the training population. This paper examines speaker adaptation strategies for a Serbian call-centre ASR system, focusing on the practically important scenario where only a small amount of unlabelled or weakly labelled speech from a new speaker is available at inference time. We compare i-vector and x-vector speaker representations as conditioning inputs, test model-agnostic meta-learning initialisation for rapid fine-tuning, and evaluate unsupervised hypothesis-driven adaptation using N-best list rescoring. Experiments conducted on 50 held-out speaker profiles from a real call-centre deployment show that x-vector conditioning combined with two-pass decoding reduces word error rate by 11.8% relative compared with the unadapted baseline using only 60 seconds of unlabelled target-speaker audio. We discuss practical deployment constraints—latency, memory footprint, and privacy—that influence the choice of adaptation method in production systems.

SYN-PUB-01122.title: Noise robustness benchmarks for South Slavic speech recognition: a comparative study
SYN-PUB-01122.text:
Noise robustness benchmarks for South Slavic speech recognition: a comparative study (2024, conference, Proceedings of the Workshop on Slavic Language Technologies (SlavicNLP-style)).
Authors: Dušan Milošević (R0083); Tomáš Novák (outside co-author); Petra Halász (outside co-author); Jelena Vuković (outside co-author).
Keywords: noise robustness; Serbian; Croatian; Bosnian; benchmarking; automatic speech recognition.
Despite the linguistic proximity of the South Slavic language cluster, automatic speech recognition systems for these languages have been evaluated on inconsistent benchmarks, making cross-language comparison difficult. This paper introduces a unified noise robustness benchmark suite covering Serbian, Croatian, and Bosnian, comprising read speech, spontaneous speech, and telephone-channel recordings, each degraded with eight standardised noise types at five SNR levels. We evaluate five published ASR systems for each language under identical conditions and report word error rates alongside a newly proposed noise-robustness index (NRI) that summarises performance across conditions in a single comparable scalar. Results reveal that Serbian models lag Croatian counterparts by 4–7 absolute WER points on noisy telephone conditions, largely attributable to corpus size differences. The benchmark suite and evaluation scripts are released openly, and we propose a shared task at the next relevant workshop to stimulate community participation in improving robustness for all three languages.

SYN-PUB-01123.title: Prosody modelling for expressive Serbian speech synthesis
SYN-PUB-01123.text:
Prosody modelling for expressive Serbian speech synthesis (2023, conference, Proceedings of the European Conference on Speech Communication and Technology (Eurospeech-style)).
Authors: Dušan Milošević (R0083); Svetlana Ristić (outside co-author); Dragana Simić (outside co-author).
Keywords: prosody; text-to-speech; speech synthesis; Serbian; intonation; neural TTS.
Monotone prosody is a well-documented limitation of neural text-to-speech systems trained on neutral read speech, and Serbian is no exception. This paper investigates explicit prosody modelling techniques aimed at producing more natural-sounding Serbian synthesis. We propose a hierarchical prosody encoder that operates at word, phrase, and utterance level, extracting latent pitch and energy representations from reference audio at training time and predicting them from text alone at inference. The model is trained on the same 20-hour corpus used in our prior TTS work, supplemented with 3 hours of expressive radio-broadcast speech to enrich prosodic variety. Subjective evaluation via a 5-point naturalness test with 55 Serbian listeners shows a mean opinion score of 4.18, an improvement of 0.17 over the baseline flat-prosody system. Acoustic analysis confirms that the proposed model reproduces interrogative and emphatic intonation patterns with significantly higher fidelity. We release model checkpoints and audio samples alongside the paper.

SYN-PUB-01124.title: Speech technology for interactive voice response systems: lessons from deploying Serbian ASR and TTS in a call-centre environment
SYN-PUB-01124.text:
Speech technology for interactive voice response systems: lessons from deploying Serbian ASR and TTS in a call-centre environment (2022, book chapter, Advances in Speech Technology for Under-Resourced Languages (Edited Volume, Springer-style)).
Authors: Branimir Kovačević (outside co-author); Marko Đorđević (outside co-author); Dušan Milošević (R0083).
Keywords: call centres; interactive voice response; Serbian; automatic speech recognition; speech synthesis; deployment.
Interactive voice response (IVR) systems are among the most commercially significant applications of speech technology, yet practical accounts of deploying such systems for morphologically complex languages like Serbian remain scarce in the academic literature. This book chapter describes the architectural and linguistic engineering decisions made during the 2018–2021 deployment of a Serbian-language speech pipeline within a commercial call-centre product. We discuss corpus collection under operational constraints, the iterative design of the pronunciation lexicon and language model for the telephony domain, acoustic model training and re-training schedules triggered by production feedback, and the integration of a neural TTS component for dynamic prompt generation. Key challenges including dialectal variation, spontaneous disfluencies, and DTMF interference are examined alongside the practical solutions adopted. The chapter concludes with a retrospective analysis of performance metrics tracked over three years of live deployment and identifies open research problems that motivated subsequent academic work by the authors.

SYN-PUB-01243.title: Knowledge Management Maturity Across Post-Socialist Local Governments: A Comparative Survey in Serbia and Croatia
SYN-PUB-01243.text:
Knowledge Management Maturity Across Post-Socialist Local Governments: A Comparative Survey in Serbia and Croatia (2016, journal, Croatian and Comparative Public Administration).
Authors: Isidora Kovačević (R0147); Nikola Grbić (R0092); Ivana Šimić Banović (outside co-author); Natalija Despotović (R0935); Dragan Milošević (outside co-author).
Keywords: knowledge management maturity; comparative study; local government; Serbia; Croatia; post-socialism.
Using the six-dimension instrument developed in earlier work, this study compares knowledge management maturity levels across 28 local governments in Serbia and 19 in Croatia. Data were collected via self-administered questionnaires completed by department heads (N = 412) during 2014–2015. Descriptive statistics and Mann–Whitney U tests were applied to detect cross-country and size-related differences. Results show that average maturity scores in both countries fall in the second of five levels ('reactive'), with technology and measurement dimensions scoring consistently lowest. Croatian municipalities score marginally higher on the strategy dimension, a difference that is statistically significant (p < 0.05) but modest in effect size (r = 0.17). Institution size correlates positively with maturity on the process dimension (ρ = 0.41, p < 0.001). The paper discusses how shared administrative legacies coexist with divergent post-1990 reform trajectories to produce partially overlapping maturity profiles.

SYN-PUB-01245.title: Procena zrelosti upravljanja znanjem u zdravstvenim ustanovama: prilagođavanje okvira za upotrebu u domovima zdravlja u Vojvodini
SYN-PUB-01245.text:
Procena zrelosti upravljanja znanjem u zdravstvenim ustanovama: prilagođavanje okvira za upotrebu u domovima zdravlja u Vojvodini (2024, journal, Zdravstvena zaštita: stručno-naučni časopis).
Authors: Isidora Kovačević (R0147); Aleksandar Pupovac (outside co-author); Jelena Stević (outside co-author); Nikola Grbić (R0092); Natalija Despotović (R0935).
Keywords: knowledge management maturity; primary healthcare; Vojvodina; instrument adaptation; health sector.
Istraživanje ispituje mogućnost primene šestodimenzionalnog okvira zrelosti upravljanja znanjem u primarnoj zdravstvenoj zaštiti, na uzorku od osam domova zdravlja u Vojvodini. Okvir je adaptiran uvođenjem zdravstveno-specifičnih indikatora u dimenzijama procesa i kulture, na osnovu kvalitativnih intervjua sa 27 koordinatora i šefova službi. Kvantitativan deo istraživanja uključivao je anketiranje 183 zaposlena. Analiza pouzdanosti i eksploratorska faktorska analiza ukazuju na potrebu za razdvajanjem dimenzije kulture na dve posebne podskale: kultura razmene znanja između stručnjaka i kultura organizacionog učenja. Prosečan nivo zrelosti u uzorku odgovara trećem stepenu petostepene skale, što je viši rezultat nego u opštinskim upravama iz ranijih studija. Identifikovani su i specifični izazovi vezani za čuvanje medicinskog znanja u uslovima visoke fluktuacije lekara.

SYN-PUB-01434.title: Integracija Balanced Scorecard pristupa u prioritizaciju R&D portfolija: studija slučaja
SYN-PUB-01434.text:
Integracija Balanced Scorecard pristupa u prioritizaciju R&D portfolija: studija slučaja (2020, journal, Tehnika – Savez inženjera i tehničara Srbije).
Authors: Marija Puzović (R0108); Isidora Kovačević (R0147).
Keywords: Balanced Scorecard; AHP; prioritizacija portfolija; studija slučaja; KPI.
Rad opisuje integraciju Balanced Scorecard (BSC) okvira s modelom prioritizacije R&D portfolija u jednom srednje velikom srpskom preduzeću iz sektora automatizacije industrijskih procesa, koje zapošljava oko 180 radnika. Studija slučaja zasnovana je na dvogodišnjoj saradnji (2017–2019) tokom koje je autorka učestvovala kao konsultant. Prikazano je kako su četiri BSC perspektive (finansijska, korisnička, interna, rast i učenje) prevedene u kvantitativne težine kriterijuma za AHP model prioritizacije. Inicijalni portfelj od 21 projektnog predloga sveden je na realizabilni skup od 12 projekata. Praćenjem realizacije tokom 18 meseci utvrđeno je da su projekti selektovani integrisanim BSC-AHP pristupom u proseku ostvarili 91% planiranih KPI vrednosti, u poređenju sa 74% kod projekata odobrenih ranije, bez formalnog modela. Rad ukazuje na vrednost iterativnih kalibracijskih sesija s menadžmentom kao ključnog faktora uspešne primene.

SYN-PUB-01440.title: Grey Relational Analysis for Ranking Vegetable Oil Suppliers Under Incomplete Information
SYN-PUB-01440.text:
Grey Relational Analysis for Ranking Vegetable Oil Suppliers Under Incomplete Information (2016, conference, Proceedings of the International Symposium on Industrial Engineering and Management (ISIEM), Subotica).
Authors: Natalija Despotović (R0935); Isidora Kovačević (R0147); Milena Savković (outside co-author); Borislav Todorović (outside co-author); Marija Puzović (R0108).
Keywords: grey relational analysis; supplier ranking; vegetable oil; incomplete data; procurement.
Supplier evaluation in the edible oil sector frequently involves incomplete or imprecise data, particularly for small and medium-sized enterprises that lack formalised procurement systems. This study applies grey relational analysis (GRA) to rank five sunflower oil suppliers for a mid-sized processing company in southern Vojvodina. Data were gathered through structured interviews and a review of procurement records spanning three years. Eight evaluation attributes were included: cost per tonne, moisture content of raw material, contract fulfilment rate, lead time variability, traceability documentation, proximity to plant, pesticide residue compliance, and supplier financial health. Grey coefficients and relational grades were computed, and a final ranking was derived. Results indicated that traceability documentation and pesticide residue compliance emerged as the most discriminating attributes. The paper also discusses the practical conditions under which GRA offers advantages over classical weighted-sum methods when attribute data are partially missing.

SYN-PUB-01450.title: Compositional Verification of Embedded Software Stacks: Scalability Limits and Practical Workarounds
SYN-PUB-01450.text:
Compositional Verification of Embedded Software Stacks: Scalability Limits and Practical Workarounds (2018, book chapter, Advances in Formal Verification of Embedded Control Software, Springer Series on Embedded Systems).
Authors: Tatjana Davidović-Šimić (outside co-author); Jochen Wernstedt (outside co-author); Martina Lačoková (R0919); Strahinja Knežević (R0109).
Keywords: compositional verification; assume-guarantee; state-space explosion; embedded stacks; static analysis.
Compositional verification decomposes a global correctness proof into per-component proofs discharged against local assume-guarantee contracts, promising relief from state-space explosion. However, compositionality breaks down when shared global resources—interrupt controllers, DMA channels, non-preemptive schedulers—create implicit dependencies not captured in pairwise contracts. This chapter surveys three years of experience applying compositional verification to industrial embedded stacks of 5 to 23 components. We identify four recurring dependency patterns that defeat standard circular assume-guarantee reasoning and describe adaptations: dependency annotations, ordered discharge sequences and partial verification with residual simulation. Case studies are drawn from a body-control module and a motor-drive controller. The chapter concludes with a discussion of tool support and the current state of integration with commercial static analysers.

SYN-PUB-01480.title: Mapping SpGEMM onto a Reconfigurable Dataflow Fabric with a Compiled Routing Layer
SYN-PUB-01480.text:
Mapping SpGEMM onto a Reconfigurable Dataflow Fabric with a Compiled Routing Layer (2021, conference, Proceedings of the Workshop on Reconfigurable Computing and Compilation).
Authors: Luka Knežević (R0802); Nemanja Simić (outside co-author); Zoran Pekez (R0162); Dragana Kovačević (outside co-author); Vukica Vasić (R0112); Tobias Wehrle (outside co-author).
Keywords: SpGEMM; dataflow fabric; FPGA; routing; sparse compilation.
Sparse general matrix–matrix multiplication (SpGEMM) exhibits highly irregular data movement that challenges static compilation. This paper describes a compilation approach in which an intermediate dataflow graph for SpGEMM is partitioned into segments whose routing requirements can be resolved statically, while a thin runtime layer handles dynamic segment transitions. The target is a reconfigurable FPGA-based dataflow fabric with 64 processing elements and a configurable interconnect. Compilation proceeds in three phases: symbolic sparsity analysis, segment extraction and scheduling, and routing table generation. Evaluated on six matrix pairs from scientific simulation and machine-learning workloads, the compiled fabric achieves 1.4–2.1× higher throughput than a reference CPU implementation running eight threads and 1.1–1.6× over a hand-tuned GPU kernel. The paper reports configuration compilation time, routing table size, and sensitivity to input matrix density.

SYN-PUB-01686.title: Character-Level Neural Transliteration for Serbian: Training Data, Architecture Choices, and Error Analysis
SYN-PUB-01686.text:
Character-Level Neural Transliteration for Serbian: Training Data, Architecture Choices, and Error Analysis (2019, journal, Natural Language Engineering).
Authors: Stefan Dragić (R0349); Nikola Petrović (outside co-author); Emilija Tešić (R0127); Miroslav Ćirić (outside co-author); Jana Zahorecová (R0931).
Keywords: neural transliteration; sequence-to-sequence; character-level model; Serbian; error analysis.
Deterministic rule-based transliteration between Serbian Cyrillic and Latin scripts handles the majority of tokens correctly, but fails on foreign loanwords, abbreviations, and alphanumeric strings. This paper investigates whether a character-level sequence-to-sequence neural model can handle these exceptions while remaining accurate on regular tokens. We trained models on a corpus of 2.3 million aligned Cyrillic–Latin token pairs extracted from parallel editions of official gazettes, experimenting with LSTM encoder-decoder architectures with attention, as well as a character-level transformer. The transformer model achieved a character error rate of 0.4% on regular tokens and 3.1% on the exception classes, compared with 0.1% and 19.4% respectively for the deterministic baseline. We performed a detailed error analysis categorising 800 mistransliterated tokens by type. The paper concludes that a cascaded system — deterministic rules followed by the neural model for detected exceptions — outperforms either component alone, reaching a token error rate of 0.6% overall.

SYN-PUB-01727.title: Maximum Likelihood Linear Regression Adaptation of GMM-HMM Acoustic Models for Child Serbian
SYN-PUB-01727.text:
Maximum Likelihood Linear Regression Adaptation of GMM-HMM Acoustic Models for Child Serbian (2013, conference, Proceedings of the Central-European Workshop on Speech Technologies (CEWST)).
Authors: Жељко Узелац (R0131); Mirjana Popović-Radović (outside co-author); László Tóth (outside co-author).
Keywords: GMM-HMM; MLLR адаптација; говор деце; српски АСР; адаптација говорника.
Gaussian mixture model–hidden Markov model (GMM-HMM) systems trained exclusively on adult speech show substantial word error rate (WER) degradation when applied to child speakers. This paper evaluates maximum likelihood linear regression (MLLR) and constrained MLLR (CMLLR) speaker adaptation for Serbian child speech, using a newly constructed adaptation set of 340 utterances from 34 children aged 7–11. Baseline WER on an isolated-word task was 41.3% with the unadapted adult model; MLLR adaptation with ten utterances per child reduced WER to 28.7%, and CMLLR to 26.1%. The adaptation data requirement was further analysed through a leave-one-speaker-out simulation, showing diminishing returns beyond eight utterances per speaker. Experiments used an in-house trigram language model trained on a 1.2 million word Serbian news and school-text corpus. Results confirm that standard adaptation techniques transfer to Serbian child speech but that data sparsity remains the primary bottleneck for production deployment.

SYN-PUB-01728.title: Утицај шума учионице на перформансе аутоматског препознавања говора деце на српском
SYN-PUB-01728.text:
Утицај шума учионице на перформансе аутоматског препознавања говора деце на српском (2015, conference, Зборник радова Телекомуникациони форум ТЕЛФОР).
Authors: Жељко Узелац (R0131); Dragan Ivanković (outside co-author).
Keywords: шум учионице; робусно АПГ; говор деце; RASTA; SNR.
У овом раду истражује се деградација тачности аутоматског препознавања говора (АПГ) деце у условима шума карактеристичног за учионице основних школа. Снимљено је 18 часова говора у осам школа на подручју Новог Сада и Суботице употребом преносивих бинауралних рекордера. Измерени однос сигнала и шума кретао се у распону од 4 до 22 dB. Систем АПГ заснован на ДКТ особинама и тројграмском језичком моделу тестиран је без и са применом одузимања спектралног шума (spectral subtraction) и RASTA филтрације. Стопа грешака у речима порасла је са 18,4% у тихим условима на 53,7% при SNR = 6 dB без побољшања карактеристика. RASTA филтрација смањила је WER на 38,2% при истом SNR-у. Анализа грешака показује да су сугласнички скупови на почетку речи нарочито осетљиви на нискофреквентни амбијентни шум. Рад завршава препорукама за прикупљање корпуса у школским окружењима.

SYN-PUB-01729.title: Pitch Range and Speaking Rate as Confounding Factors in DNN-HMM Child ASR for Inflected Languages
SYN-PUB-01729.text:
Pitch Range and Speaking Rate as Confounding Factors in DNN-HMM Child ASR for Inflected Languages (2017, conference, Speech and Language Technology in South-Eastern Europe (SLT-SEE)).
Authors: Mirjana Popović-Radović (outside co-author); Petra Zvonařová (outside co-author); Nikola Đurić (outside co-author); Жељко Узелац (R0131).
Keywords: DNN-HMM; прозодија; говор деце; темпо говора; основна фреквенција.
Deep neural network–hidden Markov model (DNN-HMM) acoustic models are sensitive to prosodic deviations that are systematic in child speech. This study isolates the effects of elevated pitch range and reduced speaking rate on phone error rate (PER) in a DNN-HMM system trained on 60 hours of Serbian adult broadcast speech. A controlled evaluation corpus of 120 read sentences was recorded by 40 children aged 8–13, stratified by sex and age. Pitch range was estimated from autocorrelation-based F0 extraction; speaking rate was measured in syllables per second. Multiple regression analysis confirms that both variables are independently significant predictors of PER (adjusted R² = 0.43). Phone confusion matrices reveal that voiced/voiceless distinctions and affricates are disproportionately affected under high-pitch conditions. The results motivate separate acoustic models or feature normalisation strategies for different age sub-bands, and inform the design of prosody-aware front-ends for morphologically rich language ASR.

SYN-PUB-01730.title: Morphological Complexity as a Language Model Perplexity Driver in Serbian Child-Directed ASR
SYN-PUB-01730.text:
Morphological Complexity as a Language Model Perplexity Driver in Serbian Child-Directed ASR (2018, journal, Journal of Speech and Language Engineering (Eastern European Edition)).
Authors: Vuk Batranović (outside co-author); Жељко Узелац (R0131); Branislava Janković (R0811); László Tóth (outside co-author).
Keywords: језички модел; морфологија; перплексија; LSTM; српски АСР.
Serbian is a highly inflected language with seven grammatical cases and productive verb morphology, producing a large vocabulary whose coverage in child-speech language models (LMs) is constrained by available training text. This paper quantifies the contribution of morphological complexity to LM perplexity on child-produced utterances compared with adult utterances matched for topic domain. Three LMs were compared: a word-level trigram, a morpheme-level trigram after morphological segmentation with an open-source Serbian morphological analyser, and a neural LM (LSTM, two layers, 256 hidden units). Perplexity on the child test set was 312, 248, and 219 respectively; the morpheme-level model reduced out-of-vocabulary rate from 7.8% to 3.1%. Integration of the morpheme-level LM into a DNN-HMM decoder reduced WER by 4.2 percentage points absolute over the word-level baseline. Text data comprised 3.4 million words drawn from elementary school reading materials and subtitles from children's television programmes.

SYN-PUB-01731.title: Transfer Learning from Adult to Child Acoustic Models Using Bottleneck Feature Extraction
SYN-PUB-01731.text:
Transfer Learning from Adult to Child Acoustic Models Using Bottleneck Feature Extraction (2019, conference, Proceedings of Interspeech (Regional Proceedings Supplement)).
Authors: Жељко Узелац (R0131); Tamás Grósz (outside co-author); Dragan Ivanković (outside co-author).
Keywords: трансфер учење; уска грла; акустички модел; говор деце; дубоке мреже.
Training deep acoustic models from scratch for child speech is impractical due to the scarcity of transcribed child speech corpora. This paper investigates bottleneck feature (BNF) extraction as a transfer learning strategy: a DNN trained on 80 hours of adult Serbian speech is used as a fixed feature extractor, with bottleneck activations fed into a smaller DNN fine-tuned on 6 hours of child speech. Four configurations are compared: standard MFCC baseline, BNF with no fine-tuning, BNF with full fine-tuning, and BNF with layer-wise freezing. On a continuous speech test set of 40 children aged 7–12, BNF with layer-wise freezing achieves WER of 23.4%, compared to 31.7% for the MFCC baseline and 27.1% for full fine-tuning. The results suggest that lower-layer phonetic representations generalise well across speaker populations while upper layers require task-specific adjustment. Computational cost analysis shows the fine-tuning phase completes in under three hours on a single mid-range GPU.

SYN-PUB-01732.title: Regularisation Strategies for Child ASR Language Models Under Scarce In-Domain Text
SYN-PUB-01732.text:
Regularisation Strategies for Child ASR Language Models Under Scarce In-Domain Text (2020, journal, Computer Speech and Language Research Letters).
Authors: Жељко Узелац (R0131); Mirjana Popović-Radović (outside co-author); Andrej Košir (outside co-author); Nikola Đurić (outside co-author).
Keywords: регуларизација; језички модел; LSTM; говор деце; оскудност података.
Language models for child-directed ASR suffer from distributional mismatch when trained predominantly on adult text. This study examines four regularisation approaches—L2 weight decay, dropout, Bayesian interpolation with a background LM, and vocabulary pruning guided by age-of-acquisition norms—applied to an LSTM language model for Serbian. The in-domain training corpus consisted of 480,000 words extracted from primary school curricula, reading exercises, and transcribed children's radio broadcasts. Out-of-domain background data comprised 8.2 million words from web-crawled text. Evaluation was performed on a 2,000-utterance child speech test set with human-verified transcriptions. Bayesian interpolation combined with vocabulary pruning yielded the lowest perplexity (187) and the highest reduction in WER when coupled with a DNN-HMM decoder (WER 21.6% vs. 26.3% for the unregularised baseline). Age-of-acquisition pruning alone reduced the active vocabulary by 22% with only a 0.8-point WER increase, offering a viable compression strategy for embedded deployment.

SYN-PUB-01733.title: Child Speech Recognition in Educational Software: A Comparative Evaluation of Commercial and Academic ASR Back-Ends for Serbian
SYN-PUB-01733.text:
Child Speech Recognition in Educational Software: A Comparative Evaluation of Commercial and Academic ASR Back-Ends for Serbian (2021, conference, ETRAN Conference Proceedings – Telecommunications and Signal Processing).
Authors: Жељко Узелац (R0131); Sofija Marković (outside co-author); Dragan Ivanković (outside co-author).
Keywords: образовни софтвер; евалуација АСР; benchmark; говор деце; учионица.
This paper presents an independent evaluation of four ASR back-ends—two commercial cloud APIs and two academic systems built in-house—on a standardised child speech benchmark for Serbian comprising 3,600 utterances from 90 children aged 6–14. Utterances span isolated words, short phrases, and connected reading passages drawn from the national primary school curriculum. WER, sentence error rate, and latency were measured under three conditions: quiet studio, simulated classroom noise (SNR 12 dB), and real classroom recording. The best academic system outperformed the best commercial API by 6.1 WER points on the connected speech task in real classroom conditions, primarily due to language model adaptation to school vocabulary. Commercial systems performed comparably or better on isolated words, suggesting broader phone coverage from large-scale training data. The benchmark corpus and evaluation scripts are made publicly available under a Creative Commons licence to facilitate reproducibility.

SYN-PUB-01734.title: Wav2Vec 2.0 Fine-Tuning for Child Serbian: Effect of Layer Selection and Data Augmentation
SYN-PUB-01734.text:
Wav2Vec 2.0 Fine-Tuning for Child Serbian: Effect of Layer Selection and Data Augmentation (2022, conference, Proceedings of the Balkan Conference on Signal Processing and Communications (BCSPC)).
Authors: Жељко Узелац (R0131); Tamás Grósz (outside co-author); Petra Zvonařová (outside co-author); Milena Ostojić (outside co-author).
Keywords: wav2vec 2.0; самонадзирано учење; fine-tuning; аугментација; говор деце.
Self-supervised speech representations pre-trained on large adult corpora offer a potential route to high-accuracy child ASR without large labelled child datasets. This paper systematically evaluates fine-tuning of a wav2vec 2.0 base model (pre-trained on 960 hours of English and 480 hours of Croatian/Serbian broadcast data) for child Serbian. Five layer-selection strategies are compared: using only the final transformer layer, averaging the top four layers, learning layer weights, fine-tuning all layers jointly, and a frozen-encoder CTC head baseline. Data augmentation via SpecAugment and pitch-shift (±3 semitones) is applied to the 6-hour child training set. The combination of learned layer weighting and pitch-shift augmentation achieves WER of 19.1% on the child benchmark, versus 31.4% for the frozen-encoder baseline. Ablation shows pitch-shift augmentation accounts for 4.3 WER points of the improvement, directly addressing the elevated and variable F0 of child speakers.

SYN-PUB-01735.title: Annotation Consistency in Child Speech Corpora: A Study of Inter-Annotator Agreement on Spontaneous Serbian
SYN-PUB-01735.text:
Annotation Consistency in Child Speech Corpora: A Study of Inter-Annotator Agreement on Spontaneous Serbian (2023, journal, Language Resources and Evaluation for South-Slavic Languages).
Authors: Жељко Узелац (R0131); Sofija Marković (outside co-author); Vuk Batranović (outside co-author); Milena Ostojić (outside co-author).
Keywords: анотација; интер-анотаторска сагласност; корпус говора деце; спонтани говор; фонетска транскрипција.
Reliable transcription of spontaneous child speech is complicated by disfluencies, coarticulation, and non-canonical pronunciation. This paper reports an inter-annotator agreement study involving five phonetically trained annotators who independently transcribed 480 utterances from 24 children aged 7–10 recorded in a semi-structured story-retelling task. Agreement was measured at word level (WER between annotator pairs) and at phone level using Cohen's κ. Mean pairwise word-level agreement was 78.4%, with the main sources of disagreement being elision of unstressed vowels (31% of conflicts), geminate reduction (18%), and word boundary placement in cliticised sequences (27%). Phone-level κ ranged from 0.71 to 0.84 across annotator pairs, indicating substantial to near-perfect agreement for most manner classes but only moderate agreement for place distinctions in obstruent clusters. Guidelines derived from the study were used to standardise annotation of the ongoing SrpChildSpeech corpus and are released as a supplementary document.

SYN-PUB-01736.title: Дисфлуенције у читању наглас код ученика основних школа: аутоматска детекција и класификација на српском
SYN-PUB-01736.text:
Дисфлуенције у читању наглас код ученика основних школа: аутоматска детекција и класификација на српском (2025, conference, Зборник радова Телекомуникациони форум ТЕЛФОР).
Authors: Жељко Узелац (R0131); Milena Ostojić (outside co-author); Andrej Košir (outside co-author); Filip Mijatović (R0905).
Keywords: дисфлуенције; читање наглас; BiLSTM; образовни АСР; флуентност.
Дисфлуенције попут понављања речи, продужења гласова и лажних почетака значајно смањују тачност система АПГ намењених образовном контексту. У овом раду предлаже се аутоматски класификатор дисфлуенција заснован на архитектури двосмерне рекурентне мреже (BiLSTM) са улазним представама на нивоу фонемских временских оквира, извученим из унапред обученог wav2vec 2.0 модела. Систем је обучен на 4,2 сата ручно анотираних снимака читања из основних школа и тестиран на независном скупу од 1,1 сата. Постигнута је F1 мера од 0,79 за категорију понављања и 0,71 за продужења, уз укупну тачност детекције дисфлуентних оквира од 83,6%. Анализа грешака показује да систем бркa кратка продужења самогласника са нагласком у стандардном говору, указујући на потребу за прозодијски свесним особинама у будућим итерацијама. Рад укључује и квалитативну анализу повезаности аутоматски детектованих дисфлуенција са оценама читалачке флуентности коју су доделили наставници.

SYN-PUB-01737.title: On the Adequacy of Whisper-Based Transcription for Low-Resource Child Speech in Inflected Languages: Evidence from Serbian and Slovak
SYN-PUB-01737.text:
On the Adequacy of Whisper-Based Transcription for Low-Resource Child Speech in Inflected Languages: Evidence from Serbian and Slovak (2026, journal, Transactions on Spoken Language Processing).
Authors: Жељко Узелац (R0131); Petra Zvonařová (outside co-author); Milena Ostojić (outside co-author); Rastislav Sabo (outside co-author).
Keywords: Whisper; нискоресурсни АСР; говор деце; морфолошка анализа грешака; вишејезични модели.
Large multilingual ASR models such as Whisper offer zero-shot transcription for dozens of languages, but their performance on child speech in morphologically rich languages has not been systematically characterised. This study evaluates Whisper (small, medium, and large-v2 checkpoints) on standardised child speech benchmarks for Serbian and Slovak, both highly inflected Slavic languages with limited representation in Whisper's training data. Benchmarks consist of 4,800 utterances per language from children aged 6–14 in quiet and classroom-noise conditions. Zero-shot WER for Serbian ranges from 38.7% (large-v2, quiet) to 61.4% (small, noise), compared to 23.1% and 34.8% for a domain-adapted wav2vec 2.0 system. Morphological error analysis reveals that Whisper systematically produces grammatically plausible but inflectionally incorrect word forms, suggesting that its language model component does not adequately constrain morphological agreement in zero-shot conditions. Shallow fine-tuning on 10 hours of child speech reduces WER by 9–14 points absolute across checkpoints.

SYN-PUB-01739.title: Energy Budget Analysis for Always-On Vibration Monitoring on Coin-Cell-Powered Sensor Nodes: Sampling, Compression, and Inference Compared
SYN-PUB-01739.text:
Energy Budget Analysis for Always-On Vibration Monitoring on Coin-Cell-Powered Sensor Nodes: Sampling, Compression, and Inference Compared (2025, preprint, arXiv (cs.AR / eess.SP)).
Authors: Vesna Knežević (R0206); Marija Cvijić (outside co-author); Ljubomir Lekić (R1013); Claudia Bauer (outside co-author); Жељко Узелац (R0131); Stefan Radovanović (outside co-author).
Keywords: energy harvesting; coin cell; MEMS accelerometer; duty cycle; TinyML.
This preprint reports a measurement-based energy budget for three deployment configurations of a vibration monitoring node powered by a CR2032 coin cell (225 mAh): (A) continuous full-rate sampling with BLE streaming, (B) adaptive sampling with on-chip DWT compression and label transmission, and (C) configuration B plus on-device int8 CNN inference. A custom PCB was designed around the nRF52833 SoC with a MEMS accelerometer (LIS2DH12, 3.3 V, ODR 1.344 kHz). Current draw was logged at 1 ms resolution using an external shunt-based ammeter. Configuration A depleted the cell in 18 hours. Configuration B extended life to 11.4 days. Configuration C added only 4% to the average current of B, yielding 10.9 days, because inference runs in short bursts at low duty cycle. The preprint includes the PCB schematic and firmware repository link and invites community review before journal submission.

SYN-PUB-01903.title: Tacit Knowledge Retention in Serbian Municipal Administrations: An Exploratory Study
SYN-PUB-01903.text:
Tacit Knowledge Retention in Serbian Municipal Administrations: An Exploratory Study (2012, journal, Journal of Central European Public Administration).
Authors: Isidora Kovačević (R0147); Mirjana Đorđević (outside co-author); Petra Horváth (outside co-author).
Keywords: tacit knowledge; knowledge retention; municipal administration; Serbia; qualitative research.
This paper reports findings from semi-structured interviews conducted with 34 civil servants across six municipalities in Vojvodina between 2010 and 2011. The study examined how tacit knowledge held by long-serving employees is retained when those employees retire or resign, focusing on practices that were established informally during the socialist period and persist without documentation. Interviews were coded in ATLAS.ti using a grounded theory approach; 118 codes were reduced to 14 categories and four core themes. Results indicate that nearly 80 percent of knowledge-retention activity relies on informal mentoring relationships rather than codification or structured handover procedures. Smaller municipalities show higher dependence on single individuals, creating pronounced vulnerability. The paper argues that standard knowledge-transfer instruments derived from private-sector models are poorly suited to the administrative cultures observed, and proposes three context-specific retention mechanisms as starting points for further instrument development.

SYN-PUB-01904.title: Razvoj instrumenta za dijagnostiku zrelosti upravljanja znanjem u organima lokalne samouprave
SYN-PUB-01904.text:
Razvoj instrumenta za dijagnostiku zrelosti upravljanja znanjem u organima lokalne samouprave (2014, journal, Menadžment: časopis za teoriju i praksu menadžmenta).
Authors: Isidora Kovačević (R0147); Dragan Milošević (outside co-author); Natalija Despotović (R0935); Biljana Ratković (outside co-author).
Keywords: knowledge management maturity; questionnaire development; local government; CFA; Serbia.
U radu je prikazana procedura razvoja i pilot-testiranja upitničkog instrumenta za procenu zrelosti upravljanja znanjem u organima lokalne samouprave. Instrument se oslanja na petostepeni model zrelosti izveden iz Crawfordovog CMM-I okvira, prilagođenog za postsocijalistički administrativni kontekst. Upitnik sadrži 54 stavke raspoređene u šest dimenzija: strategija znanja, kultura, procesi, tehnologija, merenje i liderstvo. Pilot-testiranje je sprovedeno u deset opština u Srbiji i Severnoj Makedoniji (N = 187 ispitanika). Konfirmatornom faktorskom analizom (CFA) potvrđena je šestofaktorska struktura (CFI = 0,94; RMSEA = 0,061). Cronbachov alfa koeficijent po dimenzijama kretao se od 0,71 do 0,86. Rad sadrži preporuke za dalju primenu instrumenta u regionalnim komparativnim studijama.

SYN-PUB-01906.title: Integrating Knowledge Audit Methods into Public Sector Strategic Planning: Lessons from Two Vojvodina Pilot Projects
SYN-PUB-01906.text:
Integrating Knowledge Audit Methods into Public Sector Strategic Planning: Lessons from Two Vojvodina Pilot Projects (2018, book chapter, Upravljanje znanjem u javnom sektoru jugoistočne Evrope (ur. Nikolić, T. i Fehér, A.), Akademska knjiga, Novi Sad).
Authors: Isidora Kovačević (R0147); Tibor Fehér (outside co-author); Nataša Nikolić (outside co-author).
Keywords: knowledge audit; strategic planning; public sector; Vojvodina; implementation.
This chapter describes the design and outcomes of two pilot knowledge audits carried out in Vojvodina public institutions in 2016 and 2017 as part of a capacity-building initiative. The first pilot was conducted in a regional development agency (58 employees) and the second in a district administrative office (31 employees). Each audit combined a structured inventory of documented knowledge assets, network analysis of internal expertise flows, and individual competence mapping through a standardised card-sorting exercise. The chapter reports how findings were fed into each institution's three-year strategic plan and identifies the conditions under which audit results were actually used: senior management engagement, a dedicated knowledge coordinator role, and visible quick wins in the first six months. Conditions absent in one of the two pilots are linked to partial non-adoption of recommendations, illustrating the gap between diagnostic capacity and implementation readiness in under-resourced public bodies.

SYN-PUB-01907.title: Merenje uticaja programa obuke na transfer znanja u opštinskim upravama: pre-post studija
SYN-PUB-01907.text:
Merenje uticaja programa obuke na transfer znanja u opštinskim upravama: pre-post studija (2020, journal, Teme: časopis za društvene nauke).
Authors: Biljana Ratković (outside co-author); Isidora Kovačević (R0147); Aleksandar Pupovac (outside co-author).
Keywords: training transfer; knowledge transfer; municipal administration; Kirkpatrick model; evaluation.
Rad ispituje u kojoj meri strukturirani programi obuke dovode do merljivog transfera znanja u svakodnevnu praksu opštinskih službenika. Istraživanjem je obuhvaćeno 214 učesnika obuke u jedanaest opština u Srbiji tokom 2018. i 2019. godine. Primenom Kirkpatrickijevog četvorostepenog modela evaluacije, podaci su prikupljani na četiri tačke merenja: neposredno pre, neposredno posle, tri i šest meseci nakon završetka obuke. Instrumenti su uključivali standardizovane testove znanja, procenu nadređenih i analizu administrativnih ishoda (broj procesiranih predmeta, broj grešaka, vreme obrade). Rezultati pokazuju statistički značajan porast u znanju neposredno posle obuke (d = 0,74), ali znatan pad transfera na nivou prakse u šestomesečnom praćenju: samo 31% učesnika primenjivalo je stečene veštine. Kao ključni moderatori identifikovani su podrška neposrednog rukovodioca i prilike za primenu na radnom mestu.

SYN-PUB-01909.title: Toward a Revised Maturity Framework for Knowledge Management in Post-Socialist Public Institutions: Theoretical Grounding and Empirical Refinement
SYN-PUB-01909.text:
Toward a Revised Maturity Framework for Knowledge Management in Post-Socialist Public Institutions: Theoretical Grounding and Empirical Refinement (2023, journal, Knowledge Management Research and Practice).
Authors: Isidora Kovačević (R0147); Mirjana Đorđević (outside co-author); Andreea Moldovan (outside co-author); Bojan Leković (outside co-author).
Keywords: knowledge management maturity framework; post-socialist institutions; Delphi; multi-group CFA; public sector.
This paper presents the theoretical foundations and empirical refinement of a revised five-level knowledge management maturity framework specifically designed for public institutions in post-socialist contexts. The revision draws on three sources: a critical review of existing frameworks (n = 31); expert consultation with 18 practitioners and academics from Serbia, Slovenia, Hungary, and Romania conducted via Delphi rounds; and item-level analysis of data from 490 respondents across four countries collected between 2019 and 2022. The framework retains six dimensions but reorganises subordinate indicators to reflect characteristics documented in post-socialist institutions: high procedural formalisation coexisting with low strategic coherence; strong interpersonal knowledge networks alongside weak documentation cultures; and recurrent disruption of learning cycles by leadership turnover. Confirmatory factor analysis and multi-group invariance testing across the four national samples support the revised factor structure (CFI = 0.96, RMSEA = 0.054). Implications for benchmarking and capacity-building programmes are discussed.

SYN-PUB-01910.title: Knowledge Management Maturity and Organisational Resilience During Administrative Disruption: Evidence from Serbian Local Governments During 2020–2021
SYN-PUB-01910.text:
Knowledge Management Maturity and Organisational Resilience During Administrative Disruption: Evidence from Serbian Local Governments During 2020–2021 (2025, journal, Local Government Studies).
Authors: Isidora Kovačević (R0147); Dragan Milošević (outside co-author); Ivana Šimić Banović (outside co-author).
Keywords: knowledge management maturity; organisational resilience; local government; administrative disruption; Serbia.
This paper examines whether pre-existing knowledge management maturity moderated the organisational resilience of Serbian local governments during the administrative disruptions of 2020–2021, a period combining public health crisis responses with a cycle of local elections. Resilience was operationalised as the ability to maintain service continuity, measured through administrative output indicators drawn from municipal reporting obligations. Knowledge management maturity scores from a 2019 baseline survey (N = 310 civil servants, 38 municipalities) were matched to 2020 and 2021 service output data. Multilevel regression models indicate that municipalities scoring in the top quartile on the leadership and culture dimensions of the maturity instrument maintained statistically higher service output continuity than those in the bottom quartile (difference = 14 percentage points, p < 0.05), controlling for municipality size, budget, and region. The effect was not significant for the technology dimension. Results suggest that relational and cultural aspects of knowledge infrastructure have practical consequences for public service robustness.

SYN-PUB-02017.title: Runtime Assertion Monitoring for CAN-Based Embedded Systems Using Low-Overhead Instrumentation
SYN-PUB-02017.text:
Runtime Assertion Monitoring for CAN-Based Embedded Systems Using Low-Overhead Instrumentation (2016, conference, Proceedings of the European Conference on Dependable Embedded Systems (ECDES)).
Authors: Martina Lačoková (R0919); Branislav Tešanović (outside co-author); Miloš Vranješ (R0155); Nicolás Ferreiro-Ramos (outside co-author).
Keywords: runtime verification; assertion monitoring; CAN bus; observer tasks; hardware-in-the-loop.
Runtime verification of distributed embedded systems must contend with strict memory and timing budgets. We describe a monitoring approach that compiles CAN-CL contracts into observer tasks co-located on existing ECU spare capacity, inserting checks at message reception and prior to message transmission. The observer code is generated automatically from contract annotations and requires no changes to application logic. On a target hardware platform (32-bit microcontroller at 80 MHz, 256 KB flash), monitoring a 9-message contract set adds at most 3.1% CPU overhead and 11 KB of code. Experiments on a hardware-in-the-loop rig injected 120 fault scenarios representing timing drift, signal corruption and missing messages; the monitors detected 108 of these within one CAN frame period of occurrence. False positive rate across 48 hours of fault-free operation was zero.

SYN-PUB-02134.title: Identifying Stack Buffer Overflows in MIPS Router Firmware Through Bounded Symbolic Execution
SYN-PUB-02134.text:
Identifying Stack Buffer Overflows in MIPS Router Firmware Through Bounded Symbolic Execution (2014, conference, Proceedings of the 6th Central European Workshop on Embedded Systems Security (CEWESS)).
Authors: Dragan Vučković (outside co-author); Sofija Mirković (R0164); Miroslav Halupa (outside co-author).
Keywords: symbolic execution; MIPS; router firmware; stack buffer overflow; binary lifting.
This paper addresses automated detection of stack buffer overflows in MIPS-based router firmware images obtained without access to source code. We lift binary code to an intermediate representation using a custom lifter built on top of the Valgrind VEX framework and apply bounded symbolic execution with a path depth limit of 400 basic blocks. Concolic inputs are seeded from reconstructed network packet headers. We evaluated the approach on a corpus of 38 firmware images from four consumer router product families, totalling approximately 12 million binary instructions after unpacking. The analysis identified 23 previously unreported overflow sites, of which 14 were confirmed exploitable by manual review. Path explosion was mitigated using loop summarisation and a context-sensitive function merging strategy. False positive rate on a set of known-safe library functions was 6.2 percent. Runtime per image averaged 4.1 hours on a 16-core workstation. The results suggest that bounded symbolic execution is viable for lightweight triage of router firmware without vendor cooperation.

SYN-PUB-02135.title: Taint Propagation Across Shared Memory Regions in Multi-Process Embedded Firmware
SYN-PUB-02135.text:
Taint Propagation Across Shared Memory Regions in Multi-Process Embedded Firmware (2016, journal, Journal of Systems and Software – Security Track).
Authors: Dragan Vučković (outside co-author); Sofija Mirković (R0164); Katrin Felbermayer (outside co-author); Stefan Riedl (outside co-author).
Keywords: dynamic taint analysis; multi-process; shared memory; embedded firmware; DECAF.
Many network-attached embedded devices implement their control logic as a collection of cooperating processes that share data through POSIX shared memory or memory-mapped files. Standard dynamic taint analysis tools designed for single-process targets lose taint when data crosses process boundaries, producing high false negative rates. We extended the DECAF dynamic binary instrumentation framework to track taint through shared memory regions, anonymous pipes, and Unix domain sockets simultaneously. The modified framework was validated on three synthetic multi-process test cases with ground-truth taint flows, achieving 97 percent recall and 91 percent precision. We then applied the tool to six firmware images from industrial serial-to-Ethernet gateways, finding five cross-process injection vectors that single-process analysis missed entirely. The overhead of cross-process taint bookkeeping added approximately 34 percent to analysis wall-clock time compared to baseline DECAF. Instrumentation is implemented as a loadable plugin and does not require recompilation of the target firmware.

SYN-PUB-02136.title: Firmware Re-Hosting Without Hardware: Accuracy and Limitations of Full-System QEMU Emulation for Taint Analysis of ARM Cortex-A Devices
SYN-PUB-02136.text:
Firmware Re-Hosting Without Hardware: Accuracy and Limitations of Full-System QEMU Emulation for Taint Analysis of ARM Cortex-A Devices (2017, conference, Proceedings of the 13th International Conference on Embedded Security in Cars and Networks (ESCAN)).
Authors: Sofija Mirković (R0164); Nemanja Ostojić (outside co-author); Katrin Felbermayer (outside co-author).
Keywords: firmware re-hosting; QEMU; ARM; emulation accuracy; dynamic analysis.
Re-hosting firmware in software emulation is a prerequisite for applying dynamic analysis tools to devices for which physical hardware is scarce or inaccessible. We conducted a systematic study of QEMU full-system emulation accuracy for 29 ARM Cortex-A firmware images spanning five device categories: home routers, IP cameras, NAS units, VoIP adapters, and industrial Modbus gateways. For each image we compared behaviour during emulation against identical inputs on physical hardware across three metrics: network response correctness, filesystem state after operation, and taint flow completeness as measured by a reference taint analysis. Emulation was fully accurate for 17 images, partially accurate for 9, and failed to boot for 3. Peripheral emulation gaps were the dominant source of divergence, accounting for 74 percent of observed differences. We propose a lightweight peripheral stub library, PeriphStub, which resolves the most common MMIO read timeouts using heuristic default responses, improving full-boot success to 24 of 29 images. The results provide concrete guidance on when re-hosting is sufficient for security analysis purposes.

SYN-PUB-02137.title: Automated Discovery of Command-Injection Vulnerabilities in Web Interfaces of Embedded Devices Using Combined Symbolic and Concolic Execution
SYN-PUB-02137.text:
Automated Discovery of Command-Injection Vulnerabilities in Web Interfaces of Embedded Devices Using Combined Symbolic and Concolic Execution (2019, journal, IEEE Transactions on Dependable and Secure Computing).
Authors: Nemanja Ostojić (outside co-author); Bojana Đorđević (outside co-author); Luca Taverna (outside co-author); Sofija Mirković (R0164).
Keywords: command injection; concolic execution; CGI; web interface; firmware.
Embedded devices frequently expose administrative web interfaces whose CGI scripts pass user-supplied strings directly to shell commands. We describe a pipeline that automatically identifies such command-injection sinks. The pipeline unpacks a firmware squashfs image, identifies CGI binaries, lifts them to LLVM IR using McSema, and then applies a concolic executor seeded with HTTP request templates derived from static analysis of the web server configuration files. Taint labels are assigned to HTTP parameters at the point of recv or read system calls, and a sink oracle flags any tainted argument reaching execve, system, or popen. Evaluated on 51 firmware images from consumer and small-business routers, the pipeline found 31 exploitable command-injection paths across 18 devices. Eight of these were in CGI scripts that prior static analysis alone had classified as safe. The entire pipeline runs without analyst interaction and produces a ranked report with concrete HTTP proof-of-concept payloads. Average analysis time per device was 2.8 hours.
