SYN-PUB-02138.title: Binary Analysis Methods for Embedded System Security: A Survey of Techniques Applied to Network-Attached Devices
SYN-PUB-02138.text:
Binary Analysis Methods for Embedded System Security: A Survey of Techniques Applied to Network-Attached Devices (2022, book chapter, Handbook of Embedded Systems Security, edited by R. Holzer and M. Pranjić, Springer).
Authors: Dragan Vučković (outside co-author); Igor Starčević (R0738); Sofija Mirković (R0164).
Keywords: binary analysis; firmware security; survey; symbolic execution; taint analysis.
This chapter surveys static and dynamic binary analysis techniques as applied specifically to firmware of network-attached embedded devices, a class of targets that differs from conventional desktop software in architecture diversity, operating system variation, hardware dependency, and the absence of debug symbols. We organise the survey around four analysis primitives: disassembly and control-flow recovery, symbolic and concolic execution, dynamic taint tracking, and fuzzing. For each primitive we describe the core mechanism, list representative tools, and summarise results from published evaluations on real firmware corpora. We give particular attention to practical obstacles—path explosion, peripheral emulation gaps, multi-architecture support, and filesystem unpacking—and catalogue workarounds reported in the literature. The chapter concludes with a discussion of open problems including partial firmware images, encrypted storage partitions, and the challenge of ground-truth evaluation. Intended for graduate students and practitioners entering the field, the chapter cites 84 primary sources published between 2008 and 2022.

SYN-PUB-02139.title: Evaluating Constraint Solver Backends for Symbolic Execution of ARM Thumb-2 Firmware: Speed, Completeness, and Path Coverage
SYN-PUB-02139.text:
Evaluating Constraint Solver Backends for Symbolic Execution of ARM Thumb-2 Firmware: Speed, Completeness, and Path Coverage (2021, conference, Proceedings of the 18th Workshop on Binary Analysis Research (BAR)).
Authors: Sofija Mirković (R0164); Andrej Kovačević (outside co-author); Miloš Trifunović (outside co-author).
Keywords: SMT solver; symbolic execution; ARM Thumb-2; benchmark; path coverage.
The choice of SMT solver backend has a substantial effect on the throughput of symbolic execution for binary targets, yet comparative studies specific to embedded firmware are scarce. We implemented a harness that feeds identical symbolic execution workloads, derived from ten ARM Thumb-2 firmware images of industrial sensors, to four SMT solver backends: Z3, Bitwuzla, CVC5, and Yices2. Metrics collected were queries per second, unsatisfiable-core generation time, path coverage at fixed 30-minute timeout, and rate of spurious unsatisfiable results on manually verified satisfiable path conditions. Bitwuzla achieved the highest queries-per-second rate (mean 1 840 q/s versus 1 210 q/s for Z3) and the highest path coverage on six of ten images. CVC5 produced fewer spurious unsatisfiable results (0.8 percent versus 2.1 percent for Bitwuzla). We provide a recommendation matrix mapping firmware characteristics to preferred solver. All benchmark scripts and firmware images redacted of proprietary content are released under an open licence.

SYN-PUB-02140.title: A Taint-Guided Fuzzer for Discovering Memory Corruption in UPnP Service Handlers of Embedded Devices
SYN-PUB-02140.text:
A Taint-Guided Fuzzer for Discovering Memory Corruption in UPnP Service Handlers of Embedded Devices (2023, journal, ACM Transactions on Privacy and Security).
Authors: Andrej Kovačević (outside co-author); Ioana Constantin (outside co-author); Jovan Puzović (R0484); Sofija Mirković (R0164); Luca Taverna (outside co-author).
Keywords: fuzzing; taint-guided fuzzing; UPnP; memory corruption; embedded devices.
UPnP service handlers in embedded devices parse complex XML-encoded SOAP messages and are historically prone to memory corruption. We present TaintFuzz, a grey-box fuzzer that uses dynamic taint analysis to identify which bytes of a UPnP SOAP request influence memory allocation sizes and buffer copy lengths inside the service handler binary. Taint-labelled byte offsets are fed back to the mutation engine as high-priority mutation targets, focusing energy on inputs that reach dangerous data-flow paths. TaintFuzz was compared against AFL++, Boofuzz, and a random baseline on 12 UPnP-enabled firmware images running under QEMU. TaintFuzz achieved a mean unique crash rate 2.3 times higher than AFL++ and 4.7 times higher than Boofuzz within a four-hour campaign per target. Seventeen previously unreported memory corruption bugs were found across eight firmware images; six were assessed as reachable from the local network without authentication. Proof-of-concept payloads were shared with affected vendors under a 90-day disclosure policy.

SYN-PUB-02141.title: Recovering Structured Network Protocol Grammars from Firmware Binaries to Improve Fuzz Seed Generation
SYN-PUB-02141.text:
Recovering Structured Network Protocol Grammars from Firmware Binaries to Improve Fuzz Seed Generation (2024, conference, Proceedings of the 17th International Symposium on Software Testing and Analysis – Security Track (ISSTA-S)).
Authors: Sofija Mirković (R0164); Andrej Kovačević (outside co-author); Maja Florescu (outside co-author); Stefan Riedl (outside co-author).
Keywords: protocol reverse engineering; grammar recovery; fuzzing; static analysis; binary analysis.
Effective fuzzing of network-facing firmware requires structured seeds that exercise deep parsing logic. We describe ProtoRec, a static analysis tool that operates on stripped ARM and MIPS binaries and recovers a partial grammar of the expected network protocol by tracing data-dependent branches from the recv system call. ProtoRec uses symbolic backward slicing to identify comparisons against constants and length fields, assembles them into a context-free grammar fragment, and serialises the result as a Peach Pit–compatible specification file. We evaluated ProtoRec on 15 firmware images implementing proprietary binary protocols used in industrial automation equipment. Recovered grammars covered a mean of 68 percent of the message fields identified by a human analyst spending eight hours per protocol. Seeds generated from recovered grammars increased AFL++ branch coverage by a mean of 31 percent and crash discovery rate by 2.1 times compared to seeds generated by Peach with generic TCP templates. ProtoRec runs in under 20 minutes per binary on a standard workstation.

SYN-PUB-02142.title: Longitudinal Study of Patch Propagation Latency for Memory Safety Vulnerabilities in Consumer Router Firmware, 2018–2024
SYN-PUB-02142.text:
Longitudinal Study of Patch Propagation Latency for Memory Safety Vulnerabilities in Consumer Router Firmware, 2018–2024 (2025, journal, Computers and Security).
Authors: Sofija Mirković (R0164); Tatjana Jeremić (outside co-author); Ioana Constantin (outside co-author).
Keywords: patch latency; CVE; router firmware; vulnerability lifecycle; open-source components.
We investigated how quickly memory safety vulnerabilities that originate in third-party open-source components—primarily uclibc, busybox, and OpenSSL—appear in and are subsequently patched in consumer router firmware distributed across the European market. Starting from 61 CVEs published between January 2018 and December 2023 and affecting these three libraries, we downloaded all available firmware update archives for 22 router product lines sold under seven brand names, obtaining 847 firmware images spanning six years. For each CVE we determined the first image version to include the vulnerable code and the first to include the fix, computing patch latency as the difference. Median latency from CVE publication to a patched firmware release was 214 days; the 90th percentile exceeded 540 days. Six CVEs remained unpatched in at least one actively sold product as of December 2024. Brand-level regression showed a statistically significant correlation between firmware update frequency and patch latency (Spearman ρ = –0.71). These findings have direct implications for the firmware analysis community regarding the realistic window of exposure for discovered vulnerabilities.

SYN-PUB-02251.title: Open-Source Real-Time Target Benchmarking for Automotive HIL: A Five-Year Longitudinal Study
SYN-PUB-02251.text:
Open-Source Real-Time Target Benchmarking for Automotive HIL: A Five-Year Longitudinal Study (2025, journal, Journal of Embedded and Real-Time Computing Systems).
Authors: Darko Ninkov (R0356); Nikola Bogdanović (outside co-author); Dušan Tošić (R0174); Stefan Radovanović (outside co-author); Tomas Brezina (outside co-author).
Keywords: benchmarking; real-time Linux; Zynq UltraScale+; longitudinal study; HiL platform comparison.
This paper presents a longitudinal comparison of open-source real-time platforms evaluated in the authors' laboratory between 2019 and 2024, updating earlier single-point benchmarks with data from newer hardware generations and kernel versions. Platforms assessed include x86 mini-ITX systems, Raspberry Pi 3 and 4, Beaglebone AI-64, and Xilinx Zynq UltraScale+ MPSoC. For each platform, worst-case and mean task latency, model execution capacity (maximum state count at 1 ms step), CAN frame throughput, and approximate acquisition cost are tabulated. The dataset covers 14 440 individual measurement sessions totalling over 12 000 bench-hours. Results show that the Zynq UltraScale+ with a Xenomai partition achieves the best latency-to-cost ratio for step sizes at or above 0.5 ms, while x86 platforms retain an advantage for large model complexity. The paper identifies kernel version transitions and hardware errata that caused discontinuities in the latency data and documents the workarounds applied. All raw data and measurement scripts are provided in a public repository.

SYN-PUB-02482.title: Generating ISO 26262 test cases from Simulink models
SYN-PUB-02482.text:
Generating ISO 26262 test cases from Simulink models (2023, journal, Journal of Automotive Software).
Authors: Miroslav Petrović (outside co-author); Sandra Kovačević (outside co-author); Thomas Gruber (outside co-author); Igor Matić (R0193).
This paper presents a systematic methodology for automatically generating ISO 26262-compliant test cases directly from Simulink models used in automotive software development. The approach leverages model-based design artifacts to extract safety requirements and derive corresponding test objectives at the software unit and integration levels, ensuring traceability from the Automotive Safety Integrity Level (ASIL) decomposition down to executable test scripts. A custom toolchain was developed to parse Simulink block diagrams, identify safety-relevant signal paths, and produce structured test case descriptions compatible with both MIL and SIL environments. The proposed method was validated on two industrial case studies involving an electronic stability control module and a battery management system. Results demonstrate a significant reduction in manual test case authoring effort—approximately 47%—while maintaining full compliance with ISO 26262 Part 6 requirements. The paper also discusses integration with existing CI/CD pipelines and addresses scalability challenges for large subsystem models. The findings suggest that model-driven test generation can substantially improve both the efficiency and auditability of the software verification process in safety-critical automotive projects.

SYN-PUB-02483.title: A low-cost hardware-in-the-loop bench for body control modules
SYN-PUB-02483.text:
A low-cost hardware-in-the-loop bench for body control modules (2022, conference, Embedded Systems Conference).
Authors: Dragana Ilić (outside co-author); Nikola Savić (outside co-author); Lena Hoffmann (outside co-author); Igor Matić (R0193).
This paper describes the design, implementation, and validation of a low-cost hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) bench specifically targeting body control module (BCM) testing in automotive embedded systems. Conventional HIL platforms from major vendors impose significant cost barriers for small and medium enterprises as well as academic laboratories; the proposed bench achieves comparable functional coverage using commercial off-the-shelf single-board computers, open-source real-time operating system components, and a custom signal conditioning board developed in-house. The architecture supports CAN and LIN bus simulation, load simulation for actuators such as window motors and door locks, and fault injection at the electrical interface level. A set of standardized test sequences covering ISO 26262 hardware–software integration testing requirements was executed on a production BCM unit, and the results were compared against reference outputs from a commercial HIL system. Timing accuracy and signal fidelity measurements confirm that the bench meets the requirements for functional regression testing and early fault detection. The total bill of materials remains below 800 EUR, making it accessible for university laboratories and startup companies. The paper concludes with a discussion of current limitations and planned extensions toward AUTOSAR-aware test orchestration.

SYN-PUB-02484.title: AUTOSAR Classic to Adaptive migration patterns for high-performance automotive controllers
SYN-PUB-02484.text:
AUTOSAR Classic to Adaptive migration patterns for high-performance automotive controllers (2023, journal, IEEE Transactions on Vehicular Technology).
Authors: Igor Matić (R0193); Miroslav Petrović (outside co-author); Klaus Steinmetz (outside co-author).
Keywords: AUTOSAR Adaptive; AUTOSAR Classic; migration patterns; service-oriented architecture; ISO 26262.
The transition from AUTOSAR Classic Platform to AUTOSAR Adaptive Platform introduces significant architectural and toolchain challenges for automotive software teams. This paper systematically identifies and categorizes migration patterns applicable when porting existing Classic-based software components to the Adaptive Platform, focusing on service-oriented communication, POSIX-based execution environments, and updated memory protection models. A pattern catalog of fourteen recurring migration scenarios is presented, each accompanied by a rationale, structural transformation rules, and guidance on maintaining ISO 26262 compliance throughout the migration process. The patterns were derived from a combination of industrial case studies performed in collaboration with an automotive supplier in Novi Sad and from analysis of publicly available AUTOSAR specification documents. A prototype migration support tool implementing seven of the identified patterns was developed and evaluated on a real-time sensor fusion component. Evaluation metrics include migration effort in person-hours, residual defect density, and ASIL integrity preservation. The results indicate that structured pattern application reduces unplanned rework by approximately 38% compared to ad-hoc migration approaches. The paper concludes with an outlook on toolchain integration and standardization opportunities for the identified pattern catalog.

SYN-PUB-02485.title: Fault injection strategies for ASIL-D software components under AUTOSAR
SYN-PUB-02485.text:
Fault injection strategies for ASIL-D software components under AUTOSAR (2022, journal, Reliability Engineering and System Safety).
Authors: Igor Matić (R0193); Dragana Ilić (outside co-author); Petar Živković (outside co-author); Anke Bergmann (outside co-author).
Keywords: fault injection; ASIL-D; AUTOSAR; ISO 26262; diagnostic coverage; functional safety.
Fault injection is a cornerstone technique for verifying the robustness of safety-critical embedded software, yet its systematic application within AUTOSAR-structured software stacks remains underexplored. This paper proposes a structured fault injection framework targeting ASIL-D software components deployed on AUTOSAR Classic-compliant electronic control units. The framework defines three injection layers—source code mutation, binary instrumentation, and hardware-level signal perturbation—and maps each layer to specific ISO 26262 Part 6 verification objectives. A classification of relevant fault models is introduced, covering stuck-at faults in inter-runnable variable communication, timing violations in OS task scheduling, and corrupted PDU data on CAN bus interfaces. The framework was implemented as a set of Eclipse-based plugins integrated with an existing MBT workflow and validated on an adaptive cruise control software component. Coverage metrics based on fault detection rate and diagnostic coverage are reported, demonstrating that the combined three-layer approach achieves a diagnostic coverage of 94.6% for the tested component. The paper also discusses the overhead introduced by instrumentation and proposes lightweight profiling strategies to minimize impact on real-time behavior. Recommendations for integrating the framework into continuous integration pipelines for automotive projects are provided.

SYN-PUB-02486.title: Model-based coverage criteria for safety-critical automotive software: a comparative study
SYN-PUB-02486.text:
Model-based coverage criteria for safety-critical automotive software: a comparative study (2021, journal, Software Quality Journal).
Authors: Sandra Kovačević (outside co-author); Igor Matić (R0193); Filip Marković (outside co-author); Marie Leclerc (outside co-author).
Keywords: model-based testing; coverage criteria; MC/DC; ISO 26262; Simulink; automotive software.
Coverage criteria are essential for assessing the thoroughness of testing activities mandated by ISO 26262 for automotive software. While several coverage metrics exist—ranging from statement and branch coverage to modified condition/decision coverage (MC/DC)—their applicability and effectiveness within model-based development environments such as Simulink and TargetLink have not been comprehensively compared. This paper presents a controlled comparative study of six structural coverage criteria applied to model-based automotive software components across three ASIL levels (B, C, and D). Test suites generated using each criterion are evaluated with respect to fault detection effectiveness, test suite size, generation time, and alignment with ISO 26262 recommendations. The study uses a set of twelve Simulink subsystem models sourced from an industrial partner representing powertrain and chassis control domains. Results reveal that MC/DC consistently yields the highest fault detection rates for ASIL-C and ASIL-D components but incurs a test suite size penalty of up to 3.1× compared to branch coverage. A decision framework is proposed to guide engineers in selecting coverage criteria based on ASIL level, model complexity, and available testing budget. The paper also identifies gaps in current tool support for automated coverage measurement in model-based environments.

SYN-PUB-02487.title: Real-time OS scheduling analysis for AUTOSAR multi-core ECUs under safety constraints
SYN-PUB-02487.text:
Real-time OS scheduling analysis for AUTOSAR multi-core ECUs under safety constraints (2021, conference, ACM SIGBED International Conference on Embedded Software).
Authors: Aleksandar Đorđević (outside co-author); Igor Matić (R0193); Rolf Meier (outside co-author).
Keywords: multi-core scheduling; AUTOSAR; real-time OS; ISO 26262; timing analysis; ECU.
The adoption of multi-core processors in automotive electronic control units introduces complex scheduling challenges that directly affect functional safety compliance under ISO 26262. This paper analyzes real-time operating system scheduling strategies for AUTOSAR Classic multi-core configurations, focusing on task partitioning, inter-core communication latency, and deadline guarantee mechanisms. A formal timing analysis model based on response-time analysis is extended to account for AUTOSAR-specific constraints such as inter-runnable variable synchronization, OS counter resolution, and memory protection unit boundaries. The model is applied to three representative multi-core ECU configurations: a dual-core powertrain controller, a quad-core advanced driver assistance system module, and a dual-core body domain controller. Scheduling feasibility under worst-case execution time scenarios is evaluated, and the impact of different partitioning strategies on overall system latency is quantified. Additionally, the paper examines how ASIL decomposition across cores influences scheduling freedom and discusses trade-offs between safety isolation and computational efficiency. Experimental validation was performed on a development board equipped with a TriCore-class processor running an AUTOSAR-compliant RTOS. The results provide actionable guidance for engineers performing timing analysis during AUTOSAR-based ECU software integration.

SYN-PUB-02488.title: Systematic safety analysis integration in AUTOSAR software development workflows
SYN-PUB-02488.text:
Systematic safety analysis integration in AUTOSAR software development workflows (2020, journal, International Journal of Embedded and Real-Time Communication Systems).
Authors: Nikola Savić (outside co-author); Igor Matić (R0193); Vesna Radovanović (outside co-author); Hans-Peter Wölfle (outside co-author).
Keywords: FMEA; FTA; ISO 26262; AUTOSAR; model-driven engineering; safety analysis; traceability.
Safety analysis activities such as Failure Mode and Effects Analysis (FMEA) and Fault Tree Analysis (FTA) are required by ISO 26262 but are often performed in isolation from the software development workflow, leading to inconsistencies and rework. This paper proposes a methodology for tightly integrating FMEA and FTA into AUTOSAR-based software development using a model-driven engineering approach. The methodology defines bidirectional traceability links between AUTOSAR software component models, safety analysis artifacts, and ISO 26262 work products, enabling automated consistency checks and impact analysis when software architecture changes occur. A prototype implementation using Eclipse Modeling Framework and a custom AUTOSAR metamodel extension is described and evaluated through an industrial case study involving an electronic power steering controller developed at an automotive supplier in Novi Sad. Quantitative evaluation shows that the integrated approach reduces safety analysis update effort by 31% following architecture changes and decreases the number of traceability gaps found during safety audits by 62%. Qualitative feedback from engineers involved in the case study highlights improved awareness of safety implications during routine software design decisions. The paper discusses open research challenges including scalability to full vehicle-level safety cases and integration with systems engineering tools such as SysML.

SYN-PUB-02489.title: Embedded software testing for over-the-air update mechanisms in connected vehicles
SYN-PUB-02489.text:
Embedded software testing for over-the-air update mechanisms in connected vehicles (2024, conference, Automotive Software Engineering Workshop at ICSE).
Authors: Igor Matić (R0193); Dragana Ilić (outside co-author); Stefan Vuković (outside co-author); Lena Hoffmann (outside co-author).
Keywords: OTA update; AUTOSAR Adaptive; hardware-in-the-loop; functional safety; ISO 26262; connected vehicles.
Over-the-air (OTA) software update mechanisms are becoming standard features in modern connected vehicles, yet their interaction with safety-critical embedded software components raises unresolved testing and functional safety challenges. This paper investigates testing strategies for OTA update managers implemented within AUTOSAR Adaptive environments, with a focus on verifying that update procedures preserve ASIL integrity and do not introduce unsafe states during or after software installation. A risk-based test strategy is developed, identifying eleven critical test scenarios derived from ISO 26262 Part 6 and UNECE WP.29 cybersecurity regulation requirements. The paper describes a hardware-in-the-loop test environment extended with an OTA simulation backend to execute these scenarios under realistic network conditions including partial download failures, power interruptions during flashing, and rollback operations. The proposed test suite was applied to an OTA update manager prototype running on an Adaptive AUTOSAR stack, revealing three previously undiscovered fault handling deficiencies. Metrics including update success rate, recovery time, and post-update ASIL integrity indicators are reported and analyzed. The paper concludes with recommendations for standardizing OTA testing requirements within future revisions of automotive functional safety standards and proposes extensions to the existing HIL bench infrastructure described in prior work.

SYN-PUB-02636.title: Wavelet-Based Lossy Compression of Accelerometer Data for Rotating Machinery Monitoring
SYN-PUB-02636.text:
Wavelet-Based Lossy Compression of Accelerometer Data for Rotating Machinery Monitoring (2013, journal, Journal of Measurement and Instrumentation Engineering).
Authors: Vesna Knežević (R0206); Dragan Marković (outside co-author); Zoran Ilić (outside co-author); Nebojša Urošević (R0523).
Keywords: wavelet compression; accelerometer; bearing diagnostics; DWT thresholding.
This paper evaluates the use of discrete wavelet transform (DWT) decomposition for compressing vibration signals acquired from a bearing test rig spinning at 1500–3000 RPM. Accelerometer data were sampled at 25.6 kHz using a 16-bit ADC and stored as 10-second frames. Five wavelet families (Daubechies 4, 8, Symlet 5, Coiflet 2, and biorthogonal 3.5) were compared at compression ratios between 8:1 and 64:1. Reconstruction fidelity was assessed by signal-to-noise ratio and by the ability to recover characteristic defect frequencies in the 2–8 kHz band. Daubechies 8 with hard thresholding at the fourth decomposition level achieved a 32:1 ratio with an average SNR loss below 1.4 dB and preserved bearing outer-race defect signatures in 94% of test frames. The study provides a baseline reference for embedded compression pipelines and identifies the threshold selection step as the main sensitivity point for downstream fault detection accuracy.

SYN-PUB-02637.title: Comparison of Fixed-Rate and Demand-Driven Sampling Strategies for High-Speed Vibration Acquisition on ARM Cortex-M4
SYN-PUB-02637.text:
Comparison of Fixed-Rate and Demand-Driven Sampling Strategies for High-Speed Vibration Acquisition on ARM Cortex-M4 (2015, conference, Proceedings of the 22nd Telecommunications Forum TELFOR).
Authors: Aleksandar Vuković (outside co-author); Vesna Knežević (R0206); Danilo Uzelac (R0962).
Keywords: adaptive sampling; ARM Cortex-M4; DMA; STM32; vibration acquisition.
Continuous acquisition of vibration data at 51.2 kHz on a Cortex-M4 microcontroller (STM32F407) saturates the DMA bus and leaves insufficient cycles for any in-situ processing. This work quantifies the trade-off between sampling rate, buffer management overhead, and available compute by profiling three strategies: fixed-rate DMA, triggered burst acquisition using an external comparator threshold, and a software-paced polling loop. Experiments used a belt-drive test bench with two imbalance levels and two misalignment conditions. Triggered burst acquisition reduced average data volume by 41% compared to fixed-rate while retaining all transient impact events with a false-negative rate below 3%. Profiling showed a 28% reduction in CPU cycles consumed per second. The paper provides concrete cycle-count and memory-footprint figures that are directly applicable to STM32-family deployments and discusses how the choice of strategy affects downstream FFT and envelope analysis routines.

SYN-PUB-02638.title: Compressive Sensing Reconstruction of Vibration Spectra Using Bernoulli Measurement Matrices on a Low-Power Microcontroller
SYN-PUB-02638.text:
Compressive Sensing Reconstruction of Vibration Spectra Using Bernoulli Measurement Matrices on a Low-Power Microcontroller (2017, journal, Signal Processing: Embedded and Real-Time Systems).
Authors: Vesna Knežević (R0206); Miroslav Petrović (outside co-author); Luka Horvat (outside co-author).
Keywords: compressive sensing; basis pursuit; OMP; sparse spectrum; low-power microcontroller.
Compressive sensing (CS) offers a route to reducing the raw data volume before transmission by exploiting sparsity in the frequency domain. This paper applies CS to vibration signals from a spindle motor running at 900–2700 RPM, using Bernoulli random measurement matrices generated on-chip with a hardware RNG on an STM32L476 (ultra-low-power line). Measurement vectors of length 128, 256, and 512 were tested against original frames of 2048 samples. Reconstruction used basis pursuit denoising solved offline; for embedded use, a greedy OMP variant was also evaluated. At a compression ratio of 8:1 and 256-sample measurements, reconstruction error remained below 4.2% RMS for signals with up to 12 significant spectral components. Power consumption during the measurement phase dropped by 62% relative to full-rate sampling. Limitations of on-chip RNG quality for matrix generation are discussed, and a lookup-table workaround is proposed for deterministic deployment.

SYN-PUB-02639.title: On-Device Fault Classification for Rolling Element Bearings Using a Pruned Decision Tree Fitted to FFT Feature Vectors
SYN-PUB-02639.text:
On-Device Fault Classification for Rolling Element Bearings Using a Pruned Decision Tree Fitted to FFT Feature Vectors (2018, conference, Proceedings of the 5th International Conference on Electrical, Electronic and Computing Engineering (IcETRAN)).
Authors: Dragan Marković (outside co-author); Vesna Knežević (R0206); Nevena Đorđević (outside co-author); Bojan Tepić (outside co-author).
Keywords: fault classification; decision tree; FFT features; on-device inference; rolling bearings.
This work targets a scenario where a wireless sensor node must classify bearing condition locally and transmit only a one-byte label rather than raw waveforms. Vibration data from a dedicated four-bearing test rig were recorded under healthy, inner-race defect, outer-race defect, and rolling-element defect conditions at three load levels. Feature extraction used 18 spectral amplitude ratios computed from 1024-point FFT frames. A CART decision tree was trained on 7200 frames (80/20 split) and pruned to a maximum depth of six nodes to fit within 2 kB of flash. Accuracy on the hold-out set was 91.3% overall; the inner-race defect class showed the lowest recall at 87.6%, attributed to load-dependent frequency smearing. Inference time on an STM32F103 at 72 MHz was 0.34 ms per frame. The paper also reports the sensitivity of classification accuracy to FFT window length and overlap ratio.

SYN-PUB-02640.title: Adaptive Frame Length Selection for Vibration Signals Based on Spectral Stationarity Estimation on a RISC-V Microcontroller
SYN-PUB-02640.text:
Adaptive Frame Length Selection for Vibration Signals Based on Spectral Stationarity Estimation on a RISC-V Microcontroller (2021, journal, Journal of Embedded and Real-Time Signal Processing).
Authors: Marija Cvijić (outside co-author); Vesna Knežević (R0206).
Keywords: adaptive framing; stationarity detection; KL divergence; RISC-V; gear fault.
Fixed-length framing of vibration data wastes compute when the signal is stationary and may split transient events across frame boundaries. This paper presents a lightweight stationarity detector based on the Kullback–Leibler divergence between consecutive short-time spectral estimates, implemented entirely in integer arithmetic on a GD32VF103 RISC-V microcontroller running at 108 MHz. When divergence exceeds an empirically set threshold (calibrated per machine type in a 15-minute setup phase), the frame boundary is moved forward by one quarter-frame. Tests on a compressor drive-end dataset with injected gear-tooth crack events showed a 17% increase in the fraction of events fully contained within a single frame relative to fixed 256-sample framing, with a 6% increase in total processing time. Memory overhead is 420 bytes of RAM for the two spectral buffers. The detector adds no latency to the main acquisition path because it operates on a dedicated hardware timer interrupt.

SYN-PUB-02641.title: A Structured Pruning Workflow for MobileNet-Style Architectures Targeting Sub-100 kB Flash Budgets in Industrial Sensor Nodes
SYN-PUB-02641.text:
A Structured Pruning Workflow for MobileNet-Style Architectures Targeting Sub-100 kB Flash Budgets in Industrial Sensor Nodes (2022, book chapter, Advances in Embedded Intelligence for Industrial Applications (edited volume, Springer Verlag Belgrade Series)).
Authors: Luka Horvat (outside co-author); Nemanja Stojković (outside co-author); Vesna Knežević (R0206).
Keywords: structured pruning; MobileNet; TinyML; STM32CubeAI; vibration classification.
Depthwise-separable convolution architectures such as MobileNet-V1 have been adapted for audio and vibration tasks, but published variants still exceed the flash and RAM available on mid-range microcontrollers. This book chapter describes a reproducible structured pruning workflow: (1) train a baseline model on a four-class vibration dataset (healthy, unbalance, misalignment, looseness) using a standard 70/15/15 split; (2) apply iterative channel pruning guided by the L1 norm of batch-normalisation scale factors; (3) fine-tune for 20 epochs after each pruning round. Starting from a 1.2 MB baseline, six pruning rounds reached a 94 kB model with an accuracy drop from 94.1% to 91.8% on the held-out set. The chapter provides a PyTorch reference implementation and discusses the portability of the resulting model to STM32CubeAI and TensorFlow Lite for Microcontrollers, noting differences in operator support and latency.

SYN-PUB-02642.title: Over-the-Air Model Update Protocol for Embedded Fault Detectors on BLE-Equipped Sensor Nodes
SYN-PUB-02642.text:
Over-the-Air Model Update Protocol for Embedded Fault Detectors on BLE-Equipped Sensor Nodes (2023, conference, Proceedings of the International Conference on Embedded and Ubiquitous Computing (EUC-2023)).
Authors: Vesna Knežević (R0206); Tibor Fehér (outside co-author); Ana Simić (outside co-author); Martin Bartoš (R0587).
Keywords: OTA update; BLE; delta transfer; SPI flash; embedded model management.
An edge inference node must occasionally be updated when the machine it monitors undergoes maintenance or retooling, yet full firmware flashing over BLE is impractical for large models. This paper describes and evaluates a delta-update protocol that transfers only the changed weight chunks of a quantised int8 model stored in external SPI flash. The protocol uses a 32-bit CRC per 512-byte block for integrity checking and falls back to full transfer on more than 40% block mismatch. Experiments transferred 12 model versions—differing by 5–35% of weights—to an nRF52840-based node over a 2 Mbit/s BLE connection in a factory-floor-noise environment (2.4 GHz interference from three co-located Wi-Fi networks). Mean transfer time for incremental updates was 8.3 seconds versus 41 seconds for full transfer. Inference accuracy after each update matched the reference PC evaluation to within 0.1%, confirming correct SPI flash write and read back.

SYN-PUB-02643.title: Benchmarking Integer-Only Inference Engines for 1-D Vibration CNNs on Four Microcontroller Families
SYN-PUB-02643.text:
Benchmarking Integer-Only Inference Engines for 1-D Vibration CNNs on Four Microcontroller Families (2026, journal, IEEE Transactions on Industrial Embedded Systems (accepted, in press)).
Authors: Vesna Knežević (R0206); Tibor Fehér (outside co-author); Vesna Malešević (R0465); Miloš Janković (outside co-author).
Keywords: TFLite Micro; CMSIS-NN; benchmarking; int8 inference; Cortex-M; RISC-V.
Several open-source and vendor-supplied inference engines now claim to run int8 neural networks on Cortex-M and RISC-V targets, but published benchmarks rarely use identical models and datasets, making direct comparison difficult. This paper defines a fixed benchmark suite: two model sizes (small: 48 kB flash; medium: 92 kB flash), one standard four-class vibration dataset (25.6 kHz, 1024-sample input), and five microcontroller families (STM32H7, STM32F4, GD32VF1, ESP32-S3, RP2040). Inference engines evaluated are TFLite Micro, CMSIS-NN, uTensor, and a vendor SIMD library from one of the MCU suppliers. Results show that CMSIS-NN on STM32H7 at 480 MHz achieves the lowest per-frame latency (2.8 ms for the medium model), while RP2040 with TFLite Micro shows the highest variance (6.1 ± 1.9 ms) due to flash cache misses. The paper releases all benchmark scripts and model files under an open licence.

SYN-PUB-02734.title: Pretraga u realnom vremenu nad tokom vesti na srpskom jeziku s mešovitim pismom
SYN-PUB-02734.text:
Pretraga u realnom vremenu nad tokom vesti na srpskom jeziku s mešovitim pismom (2022, journal, Informatika i sistemi: Časopis za informacione tehnologije i računarstvo).
Authors: Stefan Dragić (R0349); Luka Đorđević (outside co-author); Dejan Vuković (outside co-author); Željko Đurić (R0213); Mónika Papp (R0524).
Keywords: pretraga u realnom vremenu; tok vesti; inkrementalni indeks; skalabilnost.
Sistemi za pretragu u realnom vremenu nad tokovima vesti zahtevaju inkrementalno ažuriranje indeksa s niskim kašnjenjem. Kada tok vesti dolazi iz više izvora koji koriste različita pisma, inkrementalni indekser mora da normalizuje pismo svake pristigle stavke pre umetanja. Ovaj rad opisuje arhitekturu sistema koji obrađuje do 1 200 novinskih članaka u minuti, sa prosečnim kašnjenjem indeksiranja od 340 ms na jednom serverskom čvoru s 16 jezgara. Normalizacija pisma i fonemska kanonizacija implementirane su kao paraleln cevovod koji dodaje manje od 15% vremenske cene u odnosu na sistem bez normalizacije. Evaluacija preciznosti pretrage sprovedena je na simuliranom toku od 2,1 miliona članaka prikupljenih tokom 30 dana. Sistem je prilagodljiv i može se horizontalno skalirati dodavanjem čvorova za normalizaciju nezavisno od čvorova za indeksiranje.

SYN-PUB-02735.title: Evaluating Pretrained Multilingual Embeddings for Mixed-Script Serbian Document Retrieval
SYN-PUB-02735.text:
Evaluating Pretrained Multilingual Embeddings for Mixed-Script Serbian Document Retrieval (2023, journal, Information Processing and Management).
Authors: Stefan Dragić (R0349); Nikola Petrović (outside co-author); Éva Gyöngyössy (outside co-author); Željko Đurić (R0213); Miroslav Ćirić (outside co-author).
Keywords: multilingual embeddings; transformer; dense retrieval; mixed-script; fine-tuning.
Pretrained multilingual transformer models encode text at the subword level and might be expected to handle script variation implicitly, since their vocabularies cover both Serbian scripts. This paper measures to what extent this expectation holds in practice. We fine-tuned three publicly available multilingual models of different sizes on SrMIR-1, the mixed-script Serbian retrieval benchmark, and compared their nDCG@10 scores against a script-normalizing BM25 baseline and a hybrid model. Without fine-tuning, the multilingual models rank below the BM25 baseline on mixed-script queries. After fine-tuning on 12 000 query–passage pairs, the best model reaches nDCG@10 of 0.601, above the hybrid BM25 baseline of 0.587. However, for queries and documents that mix scripts within a single sentence, fine-tuned models underperform by up to 9 percentage points relative to their performance on single-script inputs, indicating that subword tokenization does not fully resolve the alignment problem. We release the fine-tuning splits and evaluation scripts.

SYN-PUB-02944.title: Mutation Operators for Finite State Machine Specifications of Embedded Control Software
SYN-PUB-02944.text:
Mutation Operators for Finite State Machine Specifications of Embedded Control Software (2011, conference, Proceedings of the Central European Workshop on Software Engineering and Testing (CEWSET)).
Authors: Valentina Stojanović (R0233); Dragan Milošević (outside co-author).
Keywords: mutation testing; finite state machines; embedded software; test adequacy; mutation operators.
This paper defines a catalogue of 18 mutation operators tailored to finite state machine (FSM) specifications commonly used in embedded control firmware. Operators cover state deletion, transition guard modification, action substitution, and reset-condition negation. An experiment was conducted on four open-source microcontroller firmware projects totalling approximately 14,000 lines of C code. Mutants were seeded automatically using a custom Python tool, and an existing hand-written test suite was used as the baseline oracle. Mutation scores ranged from 41% to 67% across the four subjects, revealing systematic gaps in transition coverage. The paper reports the proportion of equivalent mutants identified through static analysis (approximately 12% of all seeded mutants) and discusses the effort required for manual equivalence classification. The results motivate the need for specification-driven test generation rather than ad hoc test suite growth.

SYN-PUB-02946.title: Automated Regression Test Selection for Firmware After Incremental Source Changes
SYN-PUB-02946.text:
Automated Regression Test Selection for Firmware After Incremental Source Changes (2015, journal, Journal of Embedded Computing and Control).
Authors: Valentina Stojanović (R0233); Srđan Popović (outside co-author); Elena Varga (outside co-author).
Keywords: regression test selection; change-impact analysis; binary instrumentation; firmware; continuous integration.
Regression testing of embedded firmware is expensive because full test suite execution on hardware targets can take hours. This paper presents a lightweight change-impact analysis technique that identifies which tests in an existing suite are affected by a given firmware patch without requiring full re-execution. The method instruments the firmware binary at basic-block granularity to record coverage during an initial full run, then uses static call-graph differencing to predict which blocks are reachable from changed functions. On a dataset of 120 patches drawn from the version history of three open-source firmware projects, the technique retained on average 31% of the original test suite while missing 2.1% of fault-detecting tests. False negative rates are characterised per patch type. The implementation is released as a set of scripts wrapping GCC and a custom binary instrumentation tool. Practical integration into a continuous integration pipeline is described.

SYN-PUB-02947.title: Contract-Based Specification of Interrupt-Driven Firmware for Model-Based Test Generation
SYN-PUB-02947.text:
Contract-Based Specification of Interrupt-Driven Firmware for Model-Based Test Generation (2016, conference, Proceedings of the International Conference on Formal Techniques for Embedded Systems (FTES)).
Authors: Valentina Stojanović (R0233); Anita Kovačević (outside co-author); Marco Ferreira (outside co-author).
Keywords: contract-based specification; interrupt-driven firmware; ISR testing; model-based test generation; ARM Cortex-M.
Interrupt-driven firmware presents challenges for model-based testing because interleaving of interrupt service routines (ISRs) with the main execution thread produces combinatorial state spaces. This paper proposes a contract language, IFContract, that allows engineers to annotate ISR entry and exit conditions, shared-variable invariants, and timing constraints using a syntax embedded in C comments. A parser translates annotations into an extended FSM representation. Test cases covering pairwise ISR–main-thread interactions are generated from this model. The approach was evaluated on firmware for a battery management unit implemented on an ARM Cortex-M4 microcontroller. The generated suite comprised 147 test cases and detected all 38 manually seeded interface faults. Compared with a randomly generated suite of the same size, the model-based suite found 23% more faults. Annotation effort was measured at 2.3 lines of contract per 10 lines of ISR code on average.

SYN-PUB-02948.title: Weak Mutation vs. Strong Mutation for Assessing Test Suite Quality in Resource-Constrained Environments
SYN-PUB-02948.text:
Weak Mutation vs. Strong Mutation for Assessing Test Suite Quality in Resource-Constrained Environments (2017, journal, Software Testing and Verification Journal).
Authors: Srđan Popović (outside co-author); Valentina Stojanović (R0233); Nataša Đurić (outside co-author).
Keywords: weak mutation; strong mutation; mutation score; embedded testing; test quality.
(no abstract)

SYN-PUB-02949.title: Model-Based Testing for Embedded Systems
SYN-PUB-02949.text:
Model-Based Testing for Embedded Systems (2019, book chapter, Handbook of Software Testing Methods for Embedded and Cyber-Physical Systems, Springer).
Authors: Tomáš Blažej (outside co-author); Katarina Knežević (R0982); Valentina Stojanović (R0233); Dragan Milošević (outside co-author).
Keywords: model-based testing; embedded systems; test generation; timed automata; coverage criteria.
This book chapter surveys the state of practice in model-based testing (MBT) as applied to embedded and cyber-physical systems. It covers modelling notations including UML statecharts, extended finite automata, and timed automata, and maps them to corresponding test generation algorithms. Coverage criteria are categorised into structural, fault-based, and requirements-based families. A discussion of toolchain integration addresses challenges specific to embedded targets: cross-compilation, hardware-in-the-loop execution, and limited observability. Two worked examples illustrate applying MBT to an automotive body control module and an industrial motor controller. The chapter closes with a discussion of open problems including scalability to large state spaces, handling of real-time constraints, and the lack of standardised interfaces between modelling and test execution tools.

SYN-PUB-02951.title: Automating Oracle Construction for Hardware-in-the-Loop Firmware Tests Using Signal Temporal Logic
SYN-PUB-02951.text:
Automating Oracle Construction for Hardware-in-the-Loop Firmware Tests Using Signal Temporal Logic (2021, journal, Journal of Systems and Software).
Authors: Valentina Stojanović (R0233); Marco Ferreira (outside co-author); Branislav Stojanović (R0641); Srđan Popović (outside co-author).
Keywords: test oracle; signal temporal logic; hardware-in-the-loop; automated testing; firmware verification.
Specifying correct output behaviour for hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) firmware tests is labour intensive because engineers must manually define acceptable signal ranges and timing windows for each scenario. This paper investigates the use of Signal Temporal Logic (STL) formulas as automatically checkable test oracles in HIL test environments. STL formulas are mined from a set of passing execution traces using a template-guided parameter synthesis procedure. The synthesised formulas are then used as oracles for new test runs. The approach was evaluated on a DC motor control firmware and a temperature regulation firmware, each executed on physical target hardware. Oracle construction time dropped from a median of 47 minutes per scenario (manual) to under 4 minutes (automated). False positive and false negative rates of synthesised oracles were 3.1% and 1.8% respectively across 310 test scenarios. Limitations related to non-deterministic hardware timing are discussed.

SYN-PUB-02952.title: Integration of Formal Specification Review into the Firmware Development Workflow: A Case Study at a Serbian Industrial Electronics Firm
SYN-PUB-02952.text:
Integration of Formal Specification Review into the Firmware Development Workflow: A Case Study at a Serbian Industrial Electronics Firm (2022, journal, Information and Software Technology).
Authors: Valentina Stojanović (R0233); Igor Starčević (R0738); Jelena Marković (outside co-author); Nataša Đurić (outside co-author).
Keywords: formal specification; industrial case study; firmware development; communicating automata; defect reduction.
Adopting formal specification practices in industry requires integrating review steps into existing development workflows without excessive overhead. This paper reports a two-year action research study conducted with a Serbian firm that develops programmable logic controllers. The study introduced a lightweight formalism based on communicating extended finite automata (CEFA) for specifying firmware modules, along with a peer-review checklist and a set of automated consistency checks. Defect data were collected for 34 firmware modules developed before and after adoption. Post-adoption modules showed a 29% reduction in defects found during system integration testing. Developer survey data indicate that engineers found the notation acceptable after a two-day training course. Barriers including tool fragmentation and version control of model artefacts are documented. The paper provides a replication package containing the checklist, consistency check scripts, and anonymised defect logs.

SYN-PUB-02953.title: SpecMutate: A Framework for Specification-Level Mutation Testing of Extended Finite Automata Models
SYN-PUB-02953.text:
SpecMutate: A Framework for Specification-Level Mutation Testing of Extended Finite Automata Models (2023, conference, Proceedings of the European Conference on Software Testing and Analysis (ECSTA)).
Authors: Valentina Stojanović (R0233); Jelena Marković (outside co-author); Tomáš Blažej (outside co-author); Luca Bianchi (outside co-author); Emilija Vranješ (R0749).
Keywords: mutation testing; extended finite automata; specification-level faults; model fidelity; test generation framework.
Most mutation testing tools operate at the source code level, but for model-based testing workflows it is useful to seed faults into the formal model rather than the implementation. SpecMutate is a framework that applies 23 mutation operators directly to extended finite automata (EFA) models serialised in an XML interchange format. Operators include guard weakening, output-action swapping, state-merge, and variable initialisation faults. The framework integrates with an open-source model-based test generator and reports the model mutation score alongside the implementation mutation score. An experiment on six firmware EFA models with a combined 312 states found that model mutation scores and code mutation scores diverged significantly for three of the subjects, indicating that the model had lower fidelity than assumed. Runtime for model mutation analysis was under two minutes per model on a standard workstation, making it suitable for pre-commit checks.

SYN-PUB-02954.title: Regression Test Prioritisation for Firmware Using Historical Fault Localisation Data
SYN-PUB-02954.text:
Regression Test Prioritisation for Firmware Using Historical Fault Localisation Data (2024, journal, IEEE Transactions on Software Engineering).
Authors: Srđan Popović (outside co-author); Elena Varga (outside co-author); Predrag Nedić (R1020); Valentina Stojanović (R0233); Luca Bianchi (outside co-author).
Keywords: test prioritisation; regression testing; fault localisation; APFD; history-based testing.
Test prioritisation orders a regression suite so that fault-detecting tests execute earlier, reducing feedback latency. This paper proposes a history-based prioritisation strategy that weights tests by the fault-localisation entropy of the code regions they cover across previous test campaigns. Coverage and fault data from nine firmware projects with histories spanning 12 to 31 releases were used to train and evaluate the strategy. The proposed approach achieved an average percentage of faults detected (APFD) of 0.78, compared with 0.61 for random ordering and 0.71 for a coverage-based baseline. Computational overhead of computing prioritisation order was below 90 seconds for all subjects. The paper also analyses how quickly the historical model degrades after a major refactoring event and proposes a simple reset heuristic triggered by structural change thresholds.

SYN-PUB-02955.title: Combining Model-Based Test Generation with Large Language Model Suggestions for Uncovered Firmware Scenarios
SYN-PUB-02955.text:
Combining Model-Based Test Generation with Large Language Model Suggestions for Uncovered Firmware Scenarios (2025, preprint, arXiv preprint arXiv:2503.XXXXX).
Authors: Valentina Stojanović (R0233); Jelena Marković (outside co-author); Tomáš Blažej (outside co-author).
Keywords: model-based testing; large language models; specification gaps; firmware testing; test scenario generation.
Model-based test generation is constrained by the completeness of the formal model: scenarios not captured in the specification are not tested. This preprint explores a workflow where an LLM is prompted with natural-language firmware documentation and existing EFA models to suggest additional test scenarios that may correspond to specification gaps. Suggested scenarios are reviewed by engineers and, if accepted, formalised as model extensions. The approach was piloted on three firmware modules from an industrial PLC project. Engineers accepted 41% of LLM suggestions after review; of those, 17 were formalised and added to the model. Subsequent mutation analysis showed an increase in model mutation score of 6.3 percentage points on average. The paper does not claim that LLM suggestions are reliable in general but characterises conditions under which they are useful as a complement to structured specification review.

SYN-PUB-02957.title: Predictive Maintenance Scheduling for Small Wind Turbines Using Gradient-Boosted Survival Models on Vibration and SCADA Data
SYN-PUB-02957.text:
Predictive Maintenance Scheduling for Small Wind Turbines Using Gradient-Boosted Survival Models on Vibration and SCADA Data (2024, conference, Proceedings of the European Workshop on Predictive Maintenance in Energy Infrastructure (EWPMEI)).
Authors: Igor Starčević (R0738); Valentina Stojanović (R0233); Branislav Stojanović (R0641); Srđan Kovačević (outside co-author); Petra Horáková (outside co-author); Milica Đorđević (outside co-author).
Keywords: survival analysis; wind turbine; vibration; SCADA; maintenance scheduling.
Small wind turbines installed on agricultural and industrial premises in Serbia are often maintained reactively due to the absence of dedicated condition monitoring. This paper fits gradient-boosted survival models—specifically, a discrete-time hazard model and a random survival forest—to a combined dataset of SCADA telemetry and tower-mounted accelerometer readings from 17 turbines over five years. Predictors include nacelle vibration root-mean-square in three frequency bands, rotor speed deviation, and nacelle temperature differential. The discrete-time hazard model achieved a concordance index of 0.73 on a held-out cohort, outperforming a Cox baseline at 0.65. Predicted 30-day failure probability was used to generate ranked maintenance schedules, which were evaluated in a retrospective simulation against actual maintenance logs, showing an estimated 22 % reduction in unscheduled downtime hours.

SYN-PUB-02958.title: Incremental Model-to-Text Generation for PLC Software: Handling Configuration Changes Without Full Regeneration
SYN-PUB-02958.text:
Incremental Model-to-Text Generation for PLC Software: Handling Configuration Changes Without Full Regeneration (2022, journal, Journal of Automation Software Engineering).
Authors: Veljko Pantelić (R0995); Dragana Milić (outside co-author); Ana Kovačević (outside co-author); Valentina Stojanović (R0233).
Keywords: incremental generation; model-to-text; Xtend; PLC; software product lines; model differencing.
Full regeneration of PLC source code from a configuration model is straightforward but can be impractical in projects where manually authored customisation sections exist alongside generated code. This paper presents an incremental generation strategy that identifies which model elements have changed between two configuration revisions and regenerates only the affected Structured Text compilation units, preserving protected regions in unaffected units. Change detection is implemented as a model differencing step operating on XMI serialisations of feature model configurations, producing a delta structure that drives selective Xtend template invocation. The strategy was evaluated on a synthetic benchmark of 50 configuration pairs derived from a packaging-machine product line model with 41 features. Regeneration time was reduced by a mean of 74% compared to full regeneration, with no instances of incorrect code produced across 1,200 generated file revisions as verified by a regression test suite. The paper formalises the notion of generation dependency to characterise when incremental regeneration is sound.

SYN-PUB-03011.title: Automated Derivation of CAN-CL Contracts from AUTOSAR System Descriptions: Tool Architecture and Validation
SYN-PUB-03011.text:
Automated Derivation of CAN-CL Contracts from AUTOSAR System Descriptions: Tool Architecture and Validation (2024, conference, Proceedings of the International Conference on Software Engineering for Embedded and Cyber-Physical Systems (ICEECS)).
Authors: Martina Lačoková (R0919); Radomir Janković (R0237); Katarina Ilić-Vukić (outside co-author); Nikola Bogdanović-Đurić (outside co-author); Slobodan Knežević (R1030).
Keywords: AUTOSAR; contract synthesis; ARXML; CAN-CL; tool automation.
(no abstract)

SYN-PUB-03012.title: Container-Aware Attack Surface Enumeration in Kubernetes Deployments
SYN-PUB-03012.text:
Container-Aware Attack Surface Enumeration in Kubernetes Deployments (2023, conference, Proceedings of the European Workshop on Systems Security).
Authors: Katarina Lukić (outside co-author); Radomir Janković (R0237); Bence Tóth (outside co-author); Dragana Petrov (outside co-author); Árpád Nagy (R0564).
Keywords: Kubernetes; container security; attack surface; SBOM; lateral movement.
Kubernetes-based deployments introduce attack surface components—pod-to-pod network policies, service mesh configurations, and shared kernel namespaces—that conventional host-centric scanning pipelines do not model. This paper extends an existing agent-based reconnaissance framework with three Kubernetes-aware modules: a policy extractor that reads NetworkPolicy and Ingress resources via the API server, a container-image vulnerability mapper that correlates image SBOMs with NVD records, and an inter-pod reachability analyser that annotates the attack graph with lateral-movement edges. The extended framework was evaluated on six synthetic Kubernetes clusters ranging from 20 to 180 pods. Compared to a host-centric baseline, the extended approach discovered 37% more reachability edges and mapped 51% more unique vulnerabilities. Runtime overhead of the additional modules was under 8 seconds per cluster for the largest evaluated configuration.

SYN-PUB-03147.title: FPGA-Based Analog Front-End Emulation for Knock Sensor Signal Generation in Engine HiL Testing
SYN-PUB-03147.text:
FPGA-Based Analog Front-End Emulation for Knock Sensor Signal Generation in Engine HiL Testing (2021, journal, IEEE Transactions on Instrumentation and Control (Regional Edition)).
Authors: Milica Stanković (outside co-author); Darko Zarić (R0248); Andrej Hanus (outside co-author); Darko Ninkov (R0356); Miroslav Đorđević (outside co-author).
Keywords: knock sensor emulation; FPGA waveform generation; DAC; engine HiL; signal synthesis.
Knock sensors produce broadband vibration signals in the 5–15 kHz range that engine ECUs process through bandpass filters and envelope detectors to identify combustion knock events. Emulating these signals accurately on a HiL bench requires waveform generation with sufficient bandwidth and amplitude resolution. This work presents an FPGA-based waveform generator implemented on an Artix-7 device that produces synthetic knock and non-knock signals based on parameterised cylinder pressure traces from a four-cylinder naturally aspirated engine model. The generator uses a 16-bit DAC at 250 kS/s per channel and a lookup-table synthesis approach with four independently configurable channels. Signal quality was assessed by comparing spectra from the emulated output against recordings taken from a motored engine on a dynamometer test bench. Spectral flatness error within the 5–15 kHz band was below 1.8 dB. An ECU under test correctly classified knock events in 97.3% of 600 injected test cases. The paper details the fixed-point filter coefficients, DAC interface timing, and calibration procedure.

SYN-PUB-03183.title: Embedded Wavelet Lifting for ECG Compression on Wearable Cortex-M0 Nodes
SYN-PUB-03183.text:
Embedded Wavelet Lifting for ECG Compression on Wearable Cortex-M0 Nodes (2015, journal, Biomedical Engineering: Applications, Basis and Communications).
Authors: Slobodan Dražić (outside co-author); Ivana Horvatić (outside co-author); Tibor Takács (R0251); Branislav Stojanović (R0641); Christoph Fiedler (outside co-author).
Keywords: ECG compression; wavelet lifting; wearable; Cortex-M0; BLE; PRD.
Electrocardiogram data transmitted from chest-patch wearables place a disproportionate load on BLE bandwidth. We ported a fixed-point integer lifting-scheme wavelet transform (5/3 Le Gall filter) to an ARM Cortex-M0 running at 48 MHz and paired it with a simple threshold quantiser and arithmetic coder. The implementation stores all intermediate coefficients in 12 kB of SRAM, fitting within the budget of low-cost microcontrollers. Compression was evaluated on 30-minute, two-lead recordings from 18 subjects sampled at 500 Hz. The scheme achieved a mean compression ratio of 9.4:1 at a percent root-mean-square difference (PRD) of 2.7%, which is within the clinically acceptable range for rhythm monitoring. QRS peak locations in reconstructed signals deviated by a mean of 1.2 ms from reference annotations. Runtime was 1.8 ms per 500-sample frame, leaving the processor idle for 64% of each sampling period. Power consumption during active compression was 3.1 mW.

SYN-PUB-03259.title: Morphological tagging of Serbian technical texts: a rule-based finite-state approach
SYN-PUB-03259.text:
Morphological tagging of Serbian technical texts: a rule-based finite-state approach (2006, conference, Proceedings of the 4th Workshop on Slavic Language Technologies, Bratislava).
Authors: Milena Ćirić (outside co-author); Aleksandra Paunović (R0483); Zoran Vukelić (R0258).
Keywords: finite-state morphology; Serbian; technical corpus; POS tagging.
This paper describes the construction and evaluation of a finite-state morphological tagger for Serbian, applied specifically to technical documentation in the automotive and machinery sectors. The tagger was built using the Stuttgart Finite State Transducer toolkit and a hand-crafted lexicon of approximately 48,000 lemmas with full inflectional paradigms. A test corpus of 310,000 tokens drawn from maintenance manuals and technical standards was annotated semi-automatically and then used for evaluation. The tagger achieved a lemmatization accuracy of 94.3% and a part-of-speech tagging accuracy of 91.7% on held-out data. Error analysis showed that the main source of mistakes was nominal compounds borrowed from German and not yet registered in the lexicon. The paper discusses strategies for extending the lexicon incrementally using a back-off mechanism based on suffix-stripping heuristics. Results are compared against a statistical baseline trained on a general-language corpus, which underperformed on domain-specific tokens by 6.4 percentage points.

SYN-PUB-03260.title: Serbian–German bilingual lexical database for the engineering domain: design principles and coverage
SYN-PUB-03260.text:
Serbian–German bilingual lexical database for the engineering domain: design principles and coverage (2008, journal, Terminology and Specialized Language: International Journal of Multilingual Term Banks).
Authors: Brigitte Schönfeld (outside co-author); Dragan Petković (outside co-author); Zoran Vukelić (R0258).
Keywords: bilingual lexicon; engineering terminology; Serbian; German; TermBase eXchange.
The paper reports on the design and initial population of a Serbian–German bilingual lexical database targeted at engineering terminology. The resource encodes 12,400 term pairs extracted semi-automatically from a 4.2-million-token parallel corpus of EU-translated technical standards and verified by two domain-expert translators. Each entry stores a canonical lemma, inflectional class, syntactic valency frame, domain label, and up to three usage examples drawn from the source corpus. The database schema follows an extended version of the TermBase eXchange format to ensure interoperability with existing translation memory systems. Coverage was assessed against a reference terminology list compiled by the Serbian Standards Institute, yielding recall of 71% for core engineering concepts. The paper also discusses the treatment of multi-word terms, which account for 38% of all entries, and the specific difficulties posed by prefixal verb derivation in Serbian when mapping to German particle-verb equivalents.

SYN-PUB-03262.title: Cross-lingual query expansion for Serbian–German document retrieval using morphology-aware translation lexicons
SYN-PUB-03262.text:
Cross-lingual query expansion for Serbian–German document retrieval using morphology-aware translation lexicons (2012, journal, Journal of Information Retrieval and Language Processing).
Authors: Zoran Vukelić (R0258); Tamás Váradi (outside co-author); Ana Kovačević (outside co-author).
Keywords: cross-lingual retrieval; query expansion; Serbian; German; compound decomposition.
Cross-lingual information retrieval between Serbian and German is complicated by the mismatch between Serbian's fusional morphology and German's compounding strategies. This paper presents a retrieval framework in which user queries formulated in Serbian are expanded using a morphology-aware translation lexicon before being matched against an indexed German document collection. The lexicon was derived from the bilingual database described in earlier work and extended with 3,800 compound decompositions on the German side. Experiments were conducted on a collection of 22,000 technical patent abstracts with 120 manually constructed query-relevance judgement pairs. Mean Average Precision improved from 0.41 for a baseline bag-of-words approach to 0.58 when using the expanded lexicon with morphological normalization on both sides. The largest gains were observed for queries containing deverbal nouns, which are frequent in technical language and morphologically opaque to naive stemming. Error analysis identified 14% of failures as due to false friends between the two languages.

SYN-PUB-03263.title: Loanword integration in Serbian technical registers: a corpus-based morphophonological study
SYN-PUB-03263.text:
Loanword integration in Serbian technical registers: a corpus-based morphophonological study (2013, journal, South Slavic Journal of Language Studies).
Authors: Jelena Marković (outside co-author); Zoran Vukelić (R0258).
Keywords: loanwords; Serbian; morphophonology; technical language; corpus linguistics.
Technical registers in Serbian have absorbed large numbers of loanwords from German, English, and Latin over the past century. This corpus-based study examines the morphophonological adaptation of 1,240 technical loanwords extracted from a 38-million-token corpus of Serbian professional writing spanning 1950–2010. Each token was annotated for source language, phonological adaptation strategy (substitution, deletion, epenthesis), and inflectional class assignment. Quantitative analysis shows that 67% of German-origin loanwords are assigned to the masculine a-declension, while English-origin items show greater variability. Temporal trends reveal increasing phonological retention of source-language consonant clusters after 1990, correlating with greater direct exposure to English-language technical literature. The findings have implications for lexicon design: inflectional class assignment for new technical borrowings cannot be predicted purely from phonological form and requires a probabilistic model with language-of-origin as a feature.

SYN-PUB-03264.title: Towards a SerbianWordNet: linking synsets to inflectional paradigms
SYN-PUB-03264.text:
Towards a SerbianWordNet: linking synsets to inflectional paradigms (2015, book chapter, Language Resources for Slavic Languages: Construction, Evaluation and Applications, Language Science Press, Berlin).
Authors: Cvetana Krstev (outside co-author); Ranka Stanković (outside co-author); Zoran Vukelić (R0258); Milena Ćirić (outside co-author).
Keywords: WordNet; Serbian; lexical semantics; morphology; lexical resources.
This book chapter describes the methodology and current state of SerbianWordNet, a lexical semantic network developed at the University of Novi Sad following the EuroWordNet model. The chapter focuses specifically on the problem of linking Princeton WordNet synsets to Serbian lemmas while preserving full morphological information. At the time of writing, the resource contained 32,000 synsets mapped from English, of which 21,400 had been manually verified by lexicographers. Each synset member is associated with an inflectional class identifier from the Serbian Reference Lexicon, enabling downstream applications to generate correctly inflected forms. The chapter discusses inter-annotator agreement on synset membership (Kappa 0.74) and describes a semi-automatic procedure for extending coverage by exploiting translational equivalents found in the Serbian–German bilingual database. Three application case studies are presented: a morphologically aware lexical simplification tool, a terminology extraction pipeline, and a query reformulation module for a Serbian patent search engine.

SYN-PUB-03265.title: Annotating semantic roles in a Serbian–German parallel corpus of legal texts
SYN-PUB-03265.text:
Annotating semantic roles in a Serbian–German parallel corpus of legal texts (2017, conference, Proceedings of the 12th International Conference on Language Resources and Evaluation for Slavic Languages, Warsaw).
Authors: Stefan Grujičić (outside co-author); Maja Miličević (outside co-author); Zoran Vukelić (R0258).
Keywords: semantic role labeling; parallel corpus; legal texts; Serbian; German.
Semantic role labeling in morphologically rich languages requires annotation schemes that can accommodate the greater word-order freedom that morphological case marking permits. This paper presents a semantic role annotation study conducted on a 280,000-token Serbian–German parallel corpus of EU legal texts. Annotation followed a PropBank-style scheme extended with five additional roles for beneficiary, causal, and concessive relations that occur frequently in legal prose. Inter-annotator agreement reached a Kappa of 0.69 for core roles and 0.54 for adjunct roles on a double-annotated subset of 40,000 tokens. The parallel structure of the corpus allowed contrastive analysis of how oblique arguments in Serbian, marked by morphological case, map to German prepositional phrases with varying degrees of ambiguity. Results suggest that automatic role labeling for Serbian can benefit from projection of labels from the German side using word alignment, increasing F1 from 0.61 to 0.68 in preliminary experiments.

SYN-PUB-03266.title: Evaluation of open-source morphological analyzers on Vojvodina regional administrative texts
SYN-PUB-03266.text:
Evaluation of open-source morphological analyzers on Vojvodina regional administrative texts (2018, journal, Computational Linguistics and Language Technology).
Authors: Borbála Szeghő (outside co-author); Zoran Vukelić (R0258).
Keywords: morphological analysis; Vojvodina; administrative language; benchmarking; multilingual.
Administrative and official texts produced by institutions in Vojvodina are characterized by frequent multilingual insertions from Hungarian and German, archaic Serbian inflectional forms, and specialized terminological layers absent from general-language training data. This paper benchmarks four freely available Serbian morphological analyzers—two rule-based and two based on conditional random fields—against a hand-annotated corpus of 95,000 tokens of Vojvodina administrative language collected from municipal websites and official gazettes between 2010 and 2016. Lemmatization accuracy ranges from 79.1% to 88.4% across systems; POS accuracy ranges from 82.3% to 90.1%. All systems degrade significantly on tokens containing Hungarian proper nouns used as base forms for Serbian derivative suffixation. The paper proposes a lightweight post-processing layer using a small hybrid lexicon of 2,100 regional-specific forms, which raises the best system's lemmatization accuracy to 92.6%.

SYN-PUB-03267.title: Bilingual term extraction from comparable corpora: Serbian and German annual reports in the financial sector
SYN-PUB-03267.text:
Bilingual term extraction from comparable corpora: Serbian and German annual reports in the financial sector (2020, journal, Terminology and Specialized Language: International Journal of Multilingual Term Banks).
Authors: Ivana Lazarević (outside co-author); Katrin Reimers (outside co-author); Zoran Vukelić (R0258).
Keywords: term extraction; comparable corpora; financial terminology; Serbian; German; cross-lingual embeddings.
This study presents a method for extracting bilingual financial terminology from comparable—rather than parallel—corpora. The source corpus consists of 180 Serbian and 210 German annual reports from banking and insurance companies published between 2012 and 2018, totaling approximately 9.4 million tokens across both languages. Candidate terms were first extracted monolingually using a C-value measure combined with morphological normalization; 6,700 Serbian and 7,200 German candidates were retained. Bilingual alignment relied on a combination of cross-lingual word embeddings trained on a small seed lexicon of 1,800 verified financial term pairs and a cognate-detection component handling Internationalismen shared by both languages. Precision at rank 10 reached 0.72 for the embedding-based method, compared to 0.59 for a translation-dictionary baseline. Manual post-editing by two professional financial translators produced a verified bilingual glossary of 4,100 entries, which has been deposited in the departmental lexical resource archive.

SYN-PUB-03268.title: Constructing a morphosyntactic lexicon for Serbian sign-language finger-spelled loanwords: a feasibility study
SYN-PUB-03268.text:
Constructing a morphosyntactic lexicon for Serbian sign-language finger-spelled loanwords: a feasibility study (2021, conference, Proceedings of the 9th Workshop on Balkan and South Slavic Languages and Linguistics, Ljubljana).
Authors: Nataša Đorđević (outside co-author); Nenad Arsić (R0309); Uroš Janković (R0431); Zoran Vukelić (R0258).
Keywords: Serbian Sign Language; finger-spelling; morphological lexicon; loanwords; accessibility.
Finger-spelled words in Serbian Sign Language frequently originate as borrowings from written Serbian, and their morphosyntactic behavior differs from both their source forms and from native sign constructions. This feasibility study investigates whether existing Serbian morphological lexicons can be adapted to handle the restricted inflectional behavior of finger-spelled forms. Data were collected through structured elicitation sessions with twelve deaf informants from Novi Sad and Belgrade, producing a corpus of 4,400 finger-spelled tokens covering 310 distinct base forms. Analysis shows that finger-spelled nouns behave like Serbian masculine a-declension nouns in 82% of contexts regardless of their source paradigm class, suggesting a default assignment rule. A small proof-of-concept lexicon module of 310 entries was integrated into the existing Serbian Reference Lexicon infrastructure and evaluated in a retrieval task, where it improved recall for documents mentioning finger-spelled technical terms by 11 percentage points.

SYN-PUB-03269.title: Low-resource neural lemmatization for Serbian: comparing data augmentation strategies using inflectional paradigm tables
SYN-PUB-03269.text:
Low-resource neural lemmatization for Serbian: comparing data augmentation strategies using inflectional paradigm tables (2022, journal, Journal of Information Retrieval and Language Processing).
Authors: Stefan Grujičić (outside co-author); Marko Tadić (outside co-author); Zoran Vukelić (R0258).
Keywords: lemmatization; data augmentation; Serbian; neural NLP; low-resource.
Neural sequence-to-sequence lemmatizers trained on small annotated corpora suffer from sparse coverage of infrequent inflected forms. This paper compares five data augmentation strategies for Serbian, all of which exploit the paradigm tables stored in the Serbian Reference Lexicon. Strategies range from simple oversampling of low-frequency paradigm cells to generating synthetic training sentences by substituting lemma slots in dependency-parsed gold sentences. Experiments use a base training set of 90,000 tokens from the SETimes corpus and evaluate on a held-out 18,000-token slice. A transformer-based lemmatizer trained on the base data achieves an accuracy of 91.3%; augmenting with paradigm-table oversampling raises this to 93.8%; the best-performing strategy—slot-substituted synthetic sentences combined with paradigm oversampling—reaches 95.1%. The gap relative to a fully supervised model trained on 500,000 tokens is 1.9 percentage points. Results suggest that morphological lexicons remain a cost-effective resource for low-resource lemmatization even in the neural era.

SYN-PUB-03270.title: Cross-lingual passage retrieval for Serbian–Hungarian bilingual administrative portals: a case study from Vojvodina
SYN-PUB-03270.text:
Cross-lingual passage retrieval for Serbian–Hungarian bilingual administrative portals: a case study from Vojvodina (2023, conference, Proceedings of the 14th Language Technologies Conference, Ljubljana).
Authors: Borbála Szeghő (outside co-author); Uroš Janković (R0431); Dávid Vincze (outside co-author); Ana Kovačević (outside co-author); Zoran Vukelić (R0258).
Keywords: cross-lingual retrieval; Serbian; Hungarian; Vojvodina; bilingual administration; passage retrieval.
Vojvodina's bilingual administrative portals publish documents in both Serbian and Hungarian, creating a practical need for cross-lingual search that allows users querying in one language to retrieve relevant passages in the other. This paper describes a retrieval system built for a corpus of 640,000 documents totaling 310 million tokens collected from eleven municipal portal archives between 2015 and 2021. The retrieval backbone uses BM25 with morphological normalization on both language sides; cross-lingual query translation relies on a bilingual lexicon of 28,000 administrative term pairs assembled from earlier terminology projects and extended with a cognate list. A dense retrieval component based on multilingual sentence embeddings fine-tuned on 12,000 manually aligned passage pairs was integrated as a re-ranking layer. On 200 test queries, NDCG@10 improved from 0.49 (BM25 baseline) to 0.63 (hybrid system).
