The paper discusses user acceptance issues and ongoing cooperation with the Provincial Secretariat for Administration.

SYN-PUB-03271.title: Multilingual named entity alignment across Serbian, German, and Hungarian in a shared industrial corpus: annotation scheme and baseline results
SYN-PUB-03271.text:
Multilingual named entity alignment across Serbian, German, and Hungarian in a shared industrial corpus: annotation scheme and baseline results (2024, conference, Proceedings of the 13th International Workshop on Balkan Language Resources, Skopje).
Authors: Zoran Vukelić (R0258); Stefan Grujičić (outside co-author); Katrin Reimers (outside co-author).
Keywords: named entity recognition; cross-lingual alignment; Serbian; German; Hungarian; industrial corpus.
Named entities—company names, product identifiers, standards codes, and role designations—constitute a structurally important layer in industrial documents and present particular challenges when texts circulate across Serbian, German, and Hungarian. This paper proposes an annotation scheme for multilingual named entity alignment that accounts for the grammatical integration of foreign entity names into Serbian morphology (case suffixation, possessive clitic attachment) and the compounding behavior of entity names in German. The scheme was applied to a 520,000-token corpus of industrial tender documents and procurement records contributed by three manufacturing companies from the NTP Novi Sad ecosystem. Fourteen annotator sessions produced a triple-annotated gold standard of 42,000 tokens with Cohen's Kappa of 0.81 for entity span detection and 0.74 for cross-lingual alignment links. A CRF-based baseline system trained on 80% of the data achieved F1 of 0.77 for Serbian and 0.71 for Hungarian entity spans; cross-lingual link precision was 0.66.

SYN-PUB-03272.title: Diachronic stability of Serbian inflectional paradigms in specialized registers, 1960–2020: evidence from a 200-million-token corpus
SYN-PUB-03272.text:
Diachronic stability of Serbian inflectional paradigms in specialized registers, 1960–2020: evidence from a 200-million-token corpus (2026, journal, Journal of Slavic Linguistics).
Authors: Milena Ćirić (outside co-author); Mojca Schlamberger Brezar (outside co-author); Zoran Vukelić (R0258).
Keywords: diachronic corpus; Serbian inflection; paradigm change; specialized registers; morphological variation.
Descriptive grammars of Serbian were largely codified in the mid-twentieth century, but the inflectional behavior of nouns in specialized professional registers has not been systematically tracked across time. This study uses a 200-million-token diachronic corpus spanning 1960–2020, drawn from digitized issues of twelve Serbian trade and professional journals, to track frequency distributions across competing inflectional variants for 380 lexemes that exhibit paradigm instability in contemporary usage. Mixed-effects logistic regression models, with decade, register, and domain as fixed effects, show statistically significant drift toward the -a genitive singular for masculine inanimate nouns in technical registers (OR 1.34 per decade, p < 0.001), consistent with analogical leveling toward the most productive paradigm. These findings have practical implications for the design of morphological analyzers: models trained on pre-2000 data systematically underperform on post-2010 technical text due to unmodeled paradigm drift.

SYN-PUB-03273.title: Polysemy Patterns in Serbian Newspaper Vocabulary: A Frequency-Based Pilot Study
SYN-PUB-03273.text:
Polysemy Patterns in Serbian Newspaper Vocabulary: A Frequency-Based Pilot Study (2014, journal, Годишњак Филозофског факултета у Новом Саду / Annual Review of the Faculty of Philosophy Novi Sad).
Authors: Đorđe Bošković (R1031); Zoran Vukelić (R0258); Strahinja Dragišić (R0767).
Keywords: polysemy; newspaper corpus; lexicographic annotation; sense extension; Serbian.
This study examines polysemy distribution in a 2.4-million-token corpus of Serbian daily newspaper articles drawn from three national dailies published between 2006 and 2010. Using frequency ranking and concordance analysis in SketchEngine, the author identifies 318 high-frequency lemmas exhibiting at least three distinguishable senses in context. Sense boundaries were established through manual annotation following adapted WordNet criteria. Results indicate that approximately 34% of polysemous nouns in political reporting acquire secondary evaluative senses not attested in standard lexicographic sources. The paper argues that journalistic register drives systematic sense extension in a relatively short time window and proposes a preliminary taxonomy of extension types. Findings are compared with analogous observations in Croatian and Polish newspaper corpora from published literature. The study serves as a baseline for subsequent automated approaches to Serbian lexical sense disambiguation.

SYN-PUB-03340.title: Building a Telephone Speech Corpus for Serbian: Collection Protocol and Baseline Recognition Results
SYN-PUB-03340.text:
Building a Telephone Speech Corpus for Serbian: Collection Protocol and Baseline Recognition Results (2023, conference, Proceedings of the 9th Workshop on Slavic Languages in Speech Technology (SlavSpeech 2023), Brno).
Authors: Emilija Kapor (R0265); Dragan Vukić (outside co-author); Milena Stojanović (outside co-author); Tomáš Bořil (outside co-author).
Keywords: speech corpus; Serbian; telephone speech; HMM-DNN; Kaldi; MFCC.
This paper describes the design and collection of TelSrp-100, a corpus of 103 hours of Serbian speech recorded over public switched telephone network and VoIP channels, spanning 412 speakers from four dialect regions of Serbia. Audio was downsampled to 8 kHz and passed through a narrowband codec simulation pipeline before annotation. Transcription was performed by trained annotators following guidelines adapted from existing South Slavic corpus projects. A hybrid HMM–DNN acoustic model was trained in Kaldi using 39-dimensional MFCC features with cepstral mean and variance normalisation. The baseline system achieved a word error rate (WER) of 24.3% on a held-out test set of 8.2 hours. Analysis of errors by channel type showed that VoIP segments introduced 18% more substitution errors than PSTN segments, attributed to packet-loss artefacts. The corpus and baseline recipe are made available under a Creative Commons licence through the CLARIN.SI infrastructure. The work establishes a reproducible benchmark for future Serbian telephone ASR research.

SYN-PUB-03341.title: Noise Adaptation Strategies for Serbian Telephone ASR Using Convolutional Front-End Augmentation
SYN-PUB-03341.text:
Noise Adaptation Strategies for Serbian Telephone ASR Using Convolutional Front-End Augmentation (2024, journal, Journal of Speech and Language Engineering — Central and Eastern Europe).
Authors: Emilija Kapor (R0265); Dragan Vukić (outside co-author); Ana Horvat (outside co-author).
Keywords: noise robustness; data augmentation; TDNN; SpecAugment; call centre; Serbian ASR.
This study examines the effect of three front-end augmentation strategies on the word error rate of a Serbian telephone speech recogniser when the channel introduces additive background noise, codec distortion, and linear convolutional reverberation. The baseline system is a time-delay neural network (TDNN) acoustic model trained on TelSrp-100. The three conditions evaluated are: (1) multi-condition training using simulated noise from the MUSAN noise set mixed at SNR levels between 0 and 20 dB, (2) SpecAugment applied during training, and (3) a learnable convolutional front-end replacing the fixed filterbank. All models are evaluated on 120 held-out recordings collected in three real call-centre environments in Vojvodina. Multi-condition training gave the largest absolute WER reduction of 4.1 percentage points compared to the clean-trained baseline. Combining multi-condition training with SpecAugment yielded an additional 1.3 percentage-point reduction. The learnable front-end offered marginal gains of 0.7 percentage points but increased training time by approximately 35%. Results suggest that data augmentation at the feature level remains more practical than architectural changes for low-resource conditions where the training set is under 200 hours.

SYN-PUB-03342.title: Transfer Learning from Multilingual Wav2Vec 2.0 for Low-Resource Serbian Telephone ASR
SYN-PUB-03342.text:
Transfer Learning from Multilingual Wav2Vec 2.0 for Low-Resource Serbian Telephone ASR (2026, conference, Proceedings of Interspeech 2026, Rotterdam).
Authors: Emilija Kapor (R0265); Dragan Vukić (outside co-author); Rastislav Nagy (outside co-author); Milena Stojanović (outside co-author).
Keywords: wav2vec 2.0; self-supervised learning; transfer learning; CTC; low-resource; Serbian telephone ASR.
Pre-trained self-supervised speech representations have shown strong results for low-resource languages, but their behaviour on narrowband telephone audio is not well characterised. This paper evaluates fine-tuning of a multilingual Wav2Vec 2.0 model (trained on 128 languages, excluding Serbian) on two Serbian telephone speech datasets: TelSrp-100 and a newly collected 22-hour set of customer-service calls, TelSrp-CS22. Fine-tuning was performed with connectionist temporal classification (CTC) loss using ESPnet2. Experiments examined the effect of fine-tuning data volume, ranging from 5 to 103 hours, and the effect of resampling the 16 kHz model inputs to simulate 8 kHz telephone bandwidth. With 103 hours of fine-tuning data and bandwidth-matched resampling, the model reached a WER of 16.7% on the TelSrp-100 test set, compared to 24.3% for the MFCC-TDNN baseline. With only 22 hours the model achieved 21.4% WER, suggesting useful transfer even with limited in-domain data. Error analysis found that digits and proper nouns remain the primary source of errors, accounting for 31% of substitutions.

SYN-PUB-03505.title: Towards a Unified Security Profile for Over-the-Air Firmware Update in IEC 62443 Compliant Industrial Installations
SYN-PUB-03505.text:
Towards a Unified Security Profile for Over-the-Air Firmware Update in IEC 62443 Compliant Industrial Installations (2026, journal, Computers and Security).
Authors: Ана Рајић (R0286); Ivana Novaković (R0280); Kateřina Horáčková (outside co-author); Miroslav Vukić (outside co-author); Nándor Takács (outside co-author).
Keywords: IEC 62443; firmware update; industrial security standards; security level; OTA compliance.
IEC 62443 defines security levels and component requirements for industrial automation and control systems but provides limited normative guidance on firmware update mechanisms. This paper analyses firmware update security requirements implied by IEC 62443-3-3 and IEC 62443-4-2 at Security Levels 1 through 3, identifying 23 specific requirements that a compliant OTA firmware update subsystem must satisfy. For each requirement, the paper maps existing technical mechanisms — from HMAC-based integrity checking to certificate-based authentication and monotonic rollback counters — and identifies three areas where current practice does not clearly satisfy the standard's intent: cryptographic agility, update transaction atomicity across power loss events, and audit logging on Class 1 devices. A reference architecture for a compliant firmware update service is outlined, and the paper estimates implementation effort in person-months for each architectural component at three device capability tiers. The analysis is illustrated using data from two anonymised industrial deployments reviewed during the study.

SYN-PUB-03561.title: A Lightweight Authenticated Bootloader Protocol for Wireless Sensor Nodes in Industrial SCADA Environments
SYN-PUB-03561.text:
A Lightweight Authenticated Bootloader Protocol for Wireless Sensor Nodes in Industrial SCADA Environments (2010, journal, Journal of Embedded and Real-Time Communication Systems).
Authors: Miroslav Vukić (outside co-author); Ана Рајић (R0286); Dragan Ostojić (outside co-author).
Keywords: authenticated bootloader; HMAC; IEEE 802.15.4; SCADA; firmware delivery.
This paper describes the design and evaluation of an authenticated bootloader protocol intended for 8-bit microcontroller-based sensor nodes communicating over IEEE 802.15.4 radio links in industrial SCADA deployments. The protocol uses HMAC-SHA256 for image authentication and a two-phase commit scheme to prevent partial writes during interrupted transmissions. Experimental evaluation was conducted on a testbed of 24 nodes deployed across a simulated substation environment, with artificial packet-loss rates ranging from 5% to 40%. Mean firmware delivery time for a 64 KB image increased from 38 seconds under ideal conditions to 147 seconds at 40% packet loss, while no corrupted images were accepted across 2 400 delivery trials. Code size overhead on the target MCU was 3.2 KB of flash. The paper also discusses replay-attack resistance and the limitations of symmetric key management at scale, proposing a zone-based key hierarchy as a practical mitigation for deployments with up to 500 nodes.

SYN-PUB-03562.title: Delta Patching for Constrained Devices: Reducing Over-the-Air Update Payload on Low-Rate Wireless Links
SYN-PUB-03562.text:
Delta Patching for Constrained Devices: Reducing Over-the-Air Update Payload on Low-Rate Wireless Links (2012, conference, Proceedings of the Workshop on Embedded Systems and Industrial Networks (WESIN)).
Authors: Ана Рајић (R0286); Tijana Marković (outside co-author).
Keywords: delta patching; bsdiff; VCDIFF; firmware update; constrained devices.
Firmware images for constrained devices rarely change more than a few percent between successive releases, yet most over-the-air update mechanisms transmit full images. This paper evaluates three binary delta algorithms — bsdiff, VCDIFF, and a purpose-built block-aligned differencer — applied to firmware images from four representative industrial sensor product lines. Patch sizes across 38 consecutive release pairs averaged 11.4% of full image size for bsdiff and 14.7% for the block-aligned approach, with the latter requiring 40% less RAM during reconstruction. Transmission time over a simulated 1.2 kbit/s channel, representative of 868 MHz narrowband industrial radio, was reduced from an average of 4.1 minutes to 28 seconds. Reconstruction failure rates under 10% artificial bit-error conditions were below 0.3% for all schemes when combined with a 16-bit CRC per block. The paper includes a complexity analysis and discusses applicability to devices with less than 8 KB of available RAM.

SYN-PUB-03563.title: Формална верификација протокола за испоруку фирмвера методом провере модела
SYN-PUB-03563.text:
Формална верификација протокола за испоруку фирмвера методом провере модела (2013, conference, Зборник радова Телекомуникациони форум ТЕЛФОР).
Authors: Нeнад Ћирић (outside co-author); Miroslav Vukić (outside co-author); Ана Рајић (R0286).
Keywords: формална верификација; SPIN; Promelamodel checking; firmware protocol; LTL.
У овом раду примењен је алат за проверу модела SPIN на протокол за аутентификовану испоруку фирмвера у бежичним телеметријским мрежама. Протокол је моделован у Прометеловом језику, а верификација је обухватила 14 безбедносних и животних особина формулисаних у линеарној темпоралној логици. Пронађена су три услова у којима поновна репродукција старе поруке може да доведе до инсталације претходне верзије фирмвера ако је монотони бројач секвенце нулиран након ресетовања уређаја. Предложено је проширење протокола са тrajnim бројачем у заштићеном нелетљивом меморијском простору. Исправљени протокол је верификован без кршења постављених особина у простору стања са до 2,1 × 10⁸ стања. Рад такође дискутује ограничења апстракције криптографских примитива у SPIN моделу и предлаже методологију за раздвојено моделовање протоколне логике и криптографских претпоставки.

SYN-PUB-03564.title: Key Distribution Schemes for Large-Scale Industrial Wireless Sensor Networks: A Comparative Study
SYN-PUB-03564.text:
Key Distribution Schemes for Large-Scale Industrial Wireless Sensor Networks: A Comparative Study (2015, journal, International Journal of Industrial Communication and Control Systems).
Authors: Ана Рајић (R0286); Momčilo Nedeljković (R0441); Gábor Fekete (outside co-author); Tijana Marković (outside co-author); Dragan Ostojić (outside co-author).
Keywords: key distribution; wireless sensor networks; industrial security; Blom scheme; 6LoWPAN.
Managing cryptographic keys across hundreds of constrained field devices is a practical bottleneck in industrial wireless deployments. This paper systematically compares five key distribution schemes — pre-shared master key, pairwise key pre-distribution, a Blom matrix scheme, a hierarchical certificate authority approach adapted for 6LoWPAN, and an elliptic-curve Diffie–Hellman bootstrapping protocol — across three criteria: memory footprint on a Cortex-M0 class device, time to complete key establishment after node power-on, and resilience to node capture. Measurements were taken on a physical testbed of 60 nodes. The Blom scheme achieved the best balance for networks under 200 nodes, requiring 1.8 KB RAM and completing key establishment in under 400 ms. The ECC bootstrapping protocol was the only scheme providing forward secrecy but demanded 14 KB RAM and 2.3 seconds for key exchange, making it unsuitable for the lowest-tier devices. Practical recommendations are derived for three deployment tiers based on device capability.

SYN-PUB-03565.title: Firmware Delivery Reliability Over LoRa at Sub-kbit/s Data Rates: Measurement Study in an Urban Industrial Site
SYN-PUB-03565.text:
Firmware Delivery Reliability Over LoRa at Sub-kbit/s Data Rates: Measurement Study in an Urban Industrial Site (2017, conference, Proceedings of the IEEE International Symposium on Industrial Electronics and Applications (ISIEA-EU)).
Authors: Ана Рајић (R0286); Stefan Bogdanov (outside co-author); Petar Vujanović (outside co-author); Tibor Pásztor (R0590).
Keywords: LoRa; LoRaWAN; firmware OTA; spreading factor; industrial site measurement.
LoRa physical layer spreading factors SF7 through SF12 offer data rates from roughly 250 bit/s to 5.5 kbit/s at the expense of airtime, a constraint with direct implications for over-the-air firmware update feasibility. This paper reports on measurements conducted at a chemical plant in Novi Sad over six weeks using a network of 18 end-devices at distances between 80 m and 1.4 km from a single gateway. Packet delivery ratio at SF12 averaged 91.3% under normal plant operation but dropped to 73.8% during periods of heavy crane and conveyor activity. A store-and-forward segmentation protocol with per-segment HMAC authentication was deployed, and mean time to complete a 32 KB firmware update was measured at 22 minutes at SF12. The paper proposes an adaptive spreading-factor selection policy that reduced average update time to 9.4 minutes while maintaining delivery success above 97% across all trials.

SYN-PUB-03566.title: Replay Attack Taxonomy and Countermeasure Classification for Over-the-Air Firmware Update Protocols
SYN-PUB-03566.text:
Replay Attack Taxonomy and Countermeasure Classification for Over-the-Air Firmware Update Protocols (2018, book chapter, Security Protocols for Embedded and Industrial Systems, Springer).
Authors: Ана Рајић (R0286); Kateřina Horáčková (outside co-author).
Keywords: replay attack; firmware update; countermeasures; taxonomy; constrained devices.
Replay attacks against firmware update protocols can result in downgrade to vulnerable firmware versions, denial of service, or unnecessary device reboots in safety-critical industrial settings. This book chapter surveys replay attack vectors specific to constrained wireless devices, classifying them along four axes: attacker capability (passive monitor, active injector, insider), network topology (star, mesh, multi-hop), device state (idle, update-in-progress, post-install reboot), and available countermeasure class (nonce-based, timestamp-based, monotonic counter, challenge–response). For each combination, the chapter provides an analysis of effectiveness and implementation cost in terms of RAM, non-volatile write cycles, and required time synchronization infrastructure. Fourteen representative firmware update protocols from research literature and three from open-source embedded projects are mapped onto the taxonomy. The chapter concludes with a decision framework that assists protocol designers in selecting countermeasure combinations appropriate to their threat model and device constraints.

SYN-PUB-03567.title: Integrity Verification of Incremental Firmware Patches Using Merkle Hash Trees on Cortex-M Microcontrollers
SYN-PUB-03567.text:
Integrity Verification of Incremental Firmware Patches Using Merkle Hash Trees on Cortex-M Microcontrollers (2019, journal, Microprocessors and Microsystems: Embedded Hardware Design).
Authors: Ана Рајић (R0286); Stefan Bogdanov (outside co-author); Miroslav Vukić (outside co-author); Lena Svensson (outside co-author).
Keywords: Merkle tree; firmware patch; ECDSA; integrity verification; Cortex-M.
Applying binary patches to firmware in the field requires verification mechanisms that can detect partial or corrupted patch delivery without storing the complete expected image. This paper proposes a Merkle hash tree construction adapted for delta patches, where leaf nodes correspond to fixed-size patch chunks and the root hash is authenticated by an ECDSA signature over NIST P-256. The scheme was implemented on an STM32L4 series microcontroller with 64 KB RAM. Hash tree construction over a 16 KB patch (32 leaves) required 210 ms and consumed a peak of 4.1 KB stack space. Verification of a partial delivery — detecting one corrupted chunk among 32 — required fewer than 50 ms. The paper compares this approach against full-image HMAC and rolling-hash alternatives in terms of detection granularity, storage requirements, and recovery strategy. A discussion of the tradeoffs in choosing tree depth is included, with measurements at depths 3, 4, and 5.

SYN-PUB-03568.title: Effect of Duty-Cycle Restrictions on OTA Firmware Update Latency in the 868 MHz ISM Band: An Analytical Model
SYN-PUB-03568.text:
Effect of Duty-Cycle Restrictions on OTA Firmware Update Latency in the 868 MHz ISM Band: An Analytical Model (2020, journal, Transactions on Industrial Wireless Communications and Networking).
Authors: Gábor Fekete (outside co-author); Ана Рајић (R0286); Tijana Marković (outside co-author).
Keywords: duty cycle; 868 MHz ISM; LoRaWAN; firmware update latency; queuing model.
Regulatory duty-cycle limits in the European 868 MHz ISM band constrain transmission time to 1% in sub-band 1, directly affecting over-the-air firmware update completion times for LPWAN devices. This paper develops a queuing-theory-based analytical model for firmware delivery latency under duty-cycle constraints, accounting for segmentation overhead, retransmission probability, and concurrent traffic from non-update messages. The model is parameterised using empirical measurements from a 30-node LoRaWAN testbed. Analytical predictions of mean delivery time matched measurements within 8% across all tested configurations. The model predicts that for a 64 KB image at SF10, mean delivery time under 1% duty cycle is 4.7 hours in a lightly loaded network and rises to over 18 hours under moderate concurrent telemetry load. A scheduling strategy that prioritises update segments during predicted low-traffic windows is described and shown analytically to reduce mean delivery time by 31%.

SYN-PUB-03569.title: Secure Multicast Firmware Delivery for Co-Located Industrial Sensor Clusters Over Zigbee
SYN-PUB-03569.text:
Secure Multicast Firmware Delivery for Co-Located Industrial Sensor Clusters Over Zigbee (2021, conference, Proceedings of the European Conference on Wireless Sensor Systems and IoT Security (ECWSSIS)).
Authors: Ана Рајић (R0286); Petar Vujanović (outside co-author); Stefan Bogdanov (outside co-author).
Keywords: Zigbee; multicast firmware; AES-CCM; industrial IoT; group key management.
When many co-located devices require the same firmware update simultaneously, unicast delivery multiplies airtime linearly with node count. This paper describes a secure multicast delivery scheme for Zigbee-based industrial sensor clusters, using AES-128 CCM* group encryption with individual per-device session key wrapping to prevent one node from decrypting another's update confirmation. The protocol was implemented on CC2530-based nodes and evaluated in a testbed of 8 and 16 node clusters. For a 48 KB image, multicast delivery to a 16-node cluster completed in 6.8 minutes versus 41.3 minutes for sequential unicast, a factor of 6.1 improvement. Delivery success rate was 98.7% at 16 nodes under representative packet loss of 8%. The paper analyses the key management overhead introduced by per-device key wrapping and discusses the session key refresh interval as a function of assumed node compromise rate.

SYN-PUB-03570.title: Certificate-Based Firmware Authentication for Resource-Constrained Devices Without Persistent Internet Connectivity
SYN-PUB-03570.text:
Certificate-Based Firmware Authentication for Resource-Constrained Devices Without Persistent Internet Connectivity (2022, journal, IEEE Transactions on Dependable and Secure Computing).
Authors: Kateřina Horáčková (outside co-author); Lena Svensson (outside co-author); Miroslav Vukić (outside co-author); Ана Рајић (R0286).
Keywords: X.509; offline certificate validation; firmware authentication; constrained devices; public key infrastructure.
Public-key certificate validation normally depends on online revocation checking, which is infeasible for industrial field devices that communicate only intermittently. This paper proposes an offline certificate validation scheme for firmware authentication in which short-lived leaf certificates, valid for a configurable window of 24–168 hours, are bundled with the firmware image and verified against a pre-installed intermediate CA certificate stored in device ROM. Certificate revocation is handled by expiry rather than CRL or OCSP. The scheme uses X.509 profiles trimmed to fit within 512 bytes using a custom DER subset. Implementation and evaluation were performed on an ARM Cortex-M3 device with 32 KB RAM; certificate parsing and verification completed in 310 ms using a software ECC library. The paper analyses the security implications of the short-lived certificate approach under various attacker models, including the case where the attacker can delay delivery to extend a certificate's apparent validity.

SYN-PUB-03572.title: Benchmarking Post-Quantum Signature Schemes for Firmware Authentication on Class 1 IoT Devices
SYN-PUB-03572.text:
Benchmarking Post-Quantum Signature Schemes for Firmware Authentication on Class 1 IoT Devices (2024, journal, Journal of Cryptographic Engineering).
Authors: Ана Рајић (R0286); Lena Svensson (outside co-author); Jovana Ilić (outside co-author); Nándor Takács (outside co-author).
Keywords: post-quantum cryptography; Dilithium; Falcon; SPHINCS+; firmware authentication; IoT benchmarking.
Anticipated deployment lifetimes of industrial sensor nodes of 10–20 years motivate evaluation of post-quantum signature algorithms for firmware authentication on severely constrained hardware. This paper benchmarks four NIST post-quantum signature candidates — CRYSTALS-Dilithium2, Falcon-512, SPHINCS+-SHA2-128s, and a lattice-based scheme submitted to the ongoing standardisation process — on two representative Class 1 IoT platforms: an ARM Cortex-M0+ at 48 MHz with 32 KB RAM and a Cortex-M4 at 120 MHz with 256 KB RAM. Metrics collected include signature verification time, public key and signature sizes, and peak RAM consumption. On the Cortex-M0+ platform, Falcon-512 verification completed in 480 ms consuming 28 KB RAM peak, which exceeds available memory, while SPHINCS+-SHA2-128s verified in 1 140 ms with 6.2 KB peak RAM, making it the only scheme feasible on the lower-end device. Dilithium2 was feasible on the Cortex-M4 at 94 ms. The paper discusses the practical tradeoffs for protocol designers choosing between these schemes given device capability distribution in a deployment.

SYN-PUB-03573.title: Adaptive Segmentation and Retransmission Scheduling for Firmware Delivery Over NB-IoT in Deep-Indoor Industrial Environments
SYN-PUB-03573.text:
Adaptive Segmentation and Retransmission Scheduling for Firmware Delivery Over NB-IoT in Deep-Indoor Industrial Environments (2025, journal, Transactions on Industrial Wireless Communications and Networking).
Authors: Ана Рајић (R0286); Jovana Ilić (outside co-author); Petar Vujanović (outside co-author).
Keywords: NB-IoT; adaptive segmentation; firmware delivery; deep indoor; CQI.
NB-IoT deployment in basement-level and shielded industrial environments produces highly variable signal conditions, with RSRP measurements in one monitored processing facility ranging from −85 dBm to −138 dBm across 22 fixed sensor positions. This paper describes an adaptive firmware delivery protocol that adjusts segment size and retransmission window based on real-time channel quality indicator reports available in the NB-IoT stack. Segment sizes were varied between 64 and 512 bytes; the adaptive scheme selected optimal sizes per device per update session. In a 22-device testbed deployment over four months, the adaptive protocol reduced total update time by 38% compared to a fixed 128-byte segment baseline and reduced the number of incomplete update sessions from 11.4% to 2.1%. Energy consumption per completed update was also measured on battery-powered nodes, with the adaptive scheme consuming 12% less energy due to fewer retransmissions. A lightweight predictor using a 5-point CQI moving average was sufficient to achieve near-optimal segment sizing.

SYN-PUB-03588.title: A lemmatizer for Serbian that handles both scripts
SYN-PUB-03588.text:
A lemmatizer for Serbian that handles both scripts (2023, journal, Journal of Slavic Linguistics Tools).
Authors: Katarina Nikolić (R0288); Milena Bogdanović (outside co-author); Dragan Šević (outside co-author).
This paper presents a rule-based and machine-learning hybrid lemmatizer designed specifically for Serbian, a morphologically rich language written in two scripts — Cyrillic and Latin. A major challenge in Serbian natural language processing is that the same lexeme may appear in either script within a single corpus, leading to fragmented frequency counts and unreliable concordances. The proposed system handles both scripts transparently by applying a unified internal representation before lemmatization, then restoring the original script in the output. The lemmatizer was trained on data drawn from the KORPUS-NS reference corpus and evaluated against a manually annotated gold standard of 120,000 tokens. Results show a lemmatization accuracy of 94.7% across both scripts, outperforming existing monoscript baselines by 6.2 percentage points. The paper discusses error analysis, focusing on ambiguous noun–adjective forms and irregular verbal paradigms, and outlines future integration with part-of-speech tagging pipelines. All models and evaluation datasets are released under an open licence.

SYN-PUB-03590.title: Designing KORPUS-NS: corpus architecture and annotation scheme for contemporary Serbian
SYN-PUB-03590.text:
Designing KORPUS-NS: corpus architecture and annotation scheme for contemporary Serbian (2021, journal, Corpus Linguistics and Linguistic Theory).
Authors: Milena Bogdanović (outside co-author); Aleksandar Popović (outside co-author); Katarina Nikolić (R0288); Tamara Lukić (outside co-author).
Keywords: corpus design; annotation scheme; contemporary Serbian; MULTEXT-East; morphosyntactic tagging.
This paper describes the design decisions underlying KORPUS-NS, a 500-million-token reference corpus of contemporary Serbian covering written and transcribed spoken language from 2000 to the present. We discuss the selection of text domains — journalism, fiction, academic prose, legal documents, social media and broadcast transcripts — and justify the proportional representation of each. The annotation scheme covers tokenisation, sentence segmentation, lemmatisation, part-of-speech tagging and morphosyntactic description using a tagset derived from the MULTEXT-East standard and extended to capture Serbian-specific categories such as verbal aspect and clitic position. Special attention is given to the treatment of orthographic variants, including the coexistence of Cyrillic and Latin scripts, Ekavian and Ijekavian dialect norms, and borrowing-related spelling inconsistencies. The paper also details the metadata schema used to encode source, domain, date and register for each document. A preliminary version of the corpus containing 120 million tokens is available through a web concordancer for academic users.

SYN-PUB-03591.title: Spelling variants in Serbian corpora: typology, frequency and normalization strategies
SYN-PUB-03591.text:
Spelling variants in Serbian corpora: typology, frequency and normalization strategies (2022, journal, Written Language and Literacy).
Authors: Katarina Nikolić (R0288); Jovana Ristić (outside co-author); Milena Bogdanović (outside co-author).
Keywords: spelling variants; orthographic normalization; script duality; Serbian; corpus linguistics.
Serbian written language exhibits a wide range of spelling variants arising from script duality, competing orthographic norms, dialect influence and unconstrained digital writing practices. This paper presents the first large-scale typological study of spelling variation in Serbian, drawing on a 200-million-token sample from the KORPUS-NS corpus. We identify six major variant classes: script-switching (ćao/chao), norm-competing variants (vjerovatno/verovatno), foreign-word adaptation variants (menadžer/manager), phonetic spelling (dođi/dodji), cliticisation variants and typographic variants. Frequency analysis reveals that script-switching and norm-competing variants account for over 70% of all variant pairs and that their distribution differs markedly across domains, with social media showing the highest variant density. We evaluate three normalization strategies — lookup-table replacement, phonological rule application and neural sequence-to-sequence mapping — on a held-out test set of 15,000 variant instances. The lookup-table approach achieves the highest precision while the neural model generalises better to unseen foreign borrowings. Practical implications for corpus building, lexicography and search are discussed.

SYN-PUB-03592.title: A morphological lexicon for Serbian derived from corpus evidence
SYN-PUB-03592.text:
A morphological lexicon for Serbian derived from corpus evidence (2023, journal, International Journal of Lexicography).
Authors: Dragan Šević (outside co-author); Katarina Nikolić (R0288); Nikola Vujičić (outside co-author).
Keywords: morphological lexicon; paradigm induction; Serbian; corpus-driven; inflection.
Morphological lexicons are foundational resources for natural language processing of inflectionally complex languages. Existing Serbian lexicons were largely constructed by hand and cover limited vocabulary, particularly in the domains of new borrowings and internet slang. This paper describes a semi-automatic method for building a broad-coverage morphological lexicon from the KORPUS-NS corpus using paradigm induction: candidate lemmas are identified through lemmatisation, and their full inflectional paradigms are hypothesised by a rule engine and then validated against corpus evidence. The resulting lexicon contains 187,000 lemmas with full or partial paradigm coverage across nouns, adjectives, verbs, numerals and pronouns. We evaluate quality through human expert judgement on a stratified sample of 2,000 entries, finding 91.3% paradigm correctness for common vocabulary and 78.6% for borrowings. The lexicon is integrated into the KORPUS-NS toolchain and released under a Creative Commons licence. We discuss how corpus-driven derivation captures productive neologisms that manual lexicography consistently misses.

SYN-PUB-03593.title: Morphological complexity and readability in Serbian administrative texts: a corpus study
SYN-PUB-03593.text:
Morphological complexity and readability in Serbian administrative texts: a corpus study (2021, journal, South Slavic Language Studies).
Authors: Katarina Nikolić (R0288); Branka Đorđević (outside co-author); Jovana Ristić (outside co-author).
Keywords: readability; morphological complexity; administrative language; Serbian; corpus study.
Administrative language is frequently criticised for being inaccessible to general readers, but quantitative evidence for Serbian is scarce. This paper uses a 12-million-token subcorpus of administrative texts from KORPUS-NS to examine the relationship between morphological complexity and readability. We operationalise morphological complexity through three measures: mean paradigm depth (the average number of inflectional categories per word form), type-to-token ratio computed at lemma level, and the proportion of analytically ambiguous forms — word forms that are compatible with more than one morphosyntactic reading. Readability is approximated using human judgement scores collected from 200 participants with varying educational backgrounds. Regression analysis shows that paradigm depth is the strongest predictor of perceived difficulty, explaining 34% of variance, while lexical TTR adds a further 12%. Comparison with journalistic and literary subcorpora reveals that administrative texts have significantly higher ambiguity ratios. The paper proposes a morphology-sensitive readability index for Serbian and discusses applications in plain-language reform and automated text simplification.

SYN-PUB-03594.title: Cross-script tokenisation challenges in Serbian social media corpora
SYN-PUB-03594.text:
Cross-script tokenisation challenges in Serbian social media corpora (2020, conference, Proceedings of the Workshop on Noisy User-Generated Text (NUT 2020)).
Authors: Katarina Nikolić (R0288); Tamara Lukić (outside co-author); Stefan Marinković (outside co-author).
Keywords: tokenisation; social media; script mixing; Serbian; noisy text.
Collecting and processing Serbian social media text presents tokenisation challenges that do not arise in standard corpus work: users freely mix Cyrillic and Latin scripts within a single sentence, use non-standard punctuation, employ emoji as discourse markers, and produce unconventional compounds through agglutinative typing conventions absent from the standard language. This paper reports on the construction of a 10-million-token Serbian social media subcorpus incorporated into KORPUS-NS and the tokenisation pipeline developed to handle it. We introduce a cross-script tokeniser that identifies script boundaries within tokens and normalises them before downstream processing, a hashtag and mention segmenter, and a rule set for emoji handling. Intrinsic evaluation on a manually tokenised gold standard of 50,000 tokens shows a token boundary F1 of 98.1%, compared to 91.4% for an off-the-shelf tokeniser not adapted for social media. Extrinsic evaluation through part-of-speech tagging accuracy shows a 3.8-point improvement when the social media tokeniser is used upstream. The tools are released openly.

SYN-PUB-03595.title: Inflectional paradigms of Serbian verbs: gaps, defectiveness and corpus evidence
SYN-PUB-03595.text:
Inflectional paradigms of Serbian verbs: gaps, defectiveness and corpus evidence (2024, journal, Morphology).
Authors: Katarina Nikolić (R0288); Milena Bogdanović (outside co-author); Petar Stanković (outside co-author).
Keywords: verbal morphology; paradigm gaps; defectiveness; corpus evidence; Serbian.
Serbian verbal morphology is characterised by a complex interaction of conjugation class, aspect, transitivity and reflexivity that generates paradigms of up to forty distinct synthetic forms per lemma. Theoretical grammars acknowledge paradigm gaps — cells in the paradigm that lack an attested form — but systematic empirical data on their distribution is lacking. This paper uses corpus evidence from KORPUS-NS to map gap distributions across 8,200 verbal lemmas, distinguishing absolute gaps (no attestation in 500 million tokens) from near-gaps (fewer than five attestations). We find that first and second person forms of weather verbs and cognition verbs show the highest gap rates, consistent with semantic defectiveness, while motion verbs and communication verbs exhibit near-complete paradigms. The paper also examines inter-speaker variation in defective paradigms, using regional subcorpus splits to test whether gaps are uniform across dialect regions. Findings have implications for the completeness requirements of morphological lexicons and for training data coverage in NLP applications.

SYN-PUB-03596.title: Using KORPUS-NS for automated spelling error detection in educational contexts
SYN-PUB-03596.text:
Using KORPUS-NS for automated spelling error detection in educational contexts (2023, conference, Proceedings of the International Symposium on Applied Linguistics and Language Technology).
Authors: Vesna Petrović (outside co-author); Katarina Nikolić (R0288); Nikola Vujičić (outside co-author); Dragan Šević (outside co-author).
Keywords: spell checking; educational technology; morphological lexicon; Serbian; error detection.
Automated spelling feedback tools for Serbian are hindered by the language's morphological richness: a correctly inflected form that is unusual in frequency may be flagged as an error, while a plausible but morphologically impossible form may pass undetected. This paper proposes a corpus-informed spelling checker that combines a statistical language model trained on KORPUS-NS with the morphological lexicon derived from the same corpus, enabling the system to distinguish unlikely-but-correct forms from genuinely erroneous ones. We evaluate the system on a corpus of 4,500 student essays from secondary schools in Vojvodina, annotated by trained linguists for spelling errors. The proposed system achieves a precision of 88.4% and recall of 83.7% on real-word errors, substantially outperforming both a commercial Serbian spell-checker and a frequency-only baseline. Error analysis highlights persistent difficulties with homograph resolution and Ekavian–Ijekavian alternations. The paper discusses deployment considerations for integration into learning management systems used at Serbian secondary schools.

SYN-PUB-03691.title: Pupil dilation as a real-time index of mental effort during sequential decision-making in trained versus untrained operators
SYN-PUB-03691.text:
Pupil dilation as a real-time index of mental effort during sequential decision-making in trained versus untrained operators (2012, journal, European Journal of Cognitive Ergonomics).
Authors: Mirela Horvatić (outside co-author); Ognjen Ninkov (R0386); Dragan Vuković (outside co-author); Katarina Nedeljković (R0297).
Keywords: pupillometry; mental effort; skill acquisition; operator training; decision-making.
Pupil dilation is sensitive to changes in mental effort, but its utility in distinguishing trained from untrained operators on the same task has received limited systematic attention. Thirty-two participants were split into a trained group (20 sessions on a fault-diagnosis simulator) and an untrained control group. Pupillometric data were recorded under controlled luminance conditions. The trained group showed a 14% smaller peak pupil dilation during the critical decision phase compared with controls (p < .001), alongside lower error rates (7% vs. 31%). Task-evoked pupillary responses correlated negatively with session number (r = −.62) across training, suggesting that pupil dilation tracks the progressive automatisation of decision steps. Baseline pupil diameter did not differ between groups, ruling out tonic arousal as a confound. These findings have practical implications for the objective monitoring of operator readiness in industrial settings.

SYN-PUB-03693.title: Measuring workload during laparoscopic skill training: a comparison of oculomotor, cardiovascular, and subjective indices
SYN-PUB-03693.text:
Measuring workload during laparoscopic skill training: a comparison of oculomotor, cardiovascular, and subjective indices (2015, journal, Journal of Applied Ergonomics Research).
Authors: Vesna Ristić (outside co-author); Ognjen Ninkov (R0386); Gordana Petrović (outside co-author); Lars Mäkinen (outside co-author); Katarina Nedeljković (R0297).
Keywords: laparoscopic training; fixation rate; heart rate variability; multimodal workload measurement; surgical education.
The study compared four workload indices during three stages of laparoscopic box-trainer practice in 24 surgical residents: pupil dilation, fixation rate, heart rate variability (SDNN), and the NASA-TLX. All four indices changed significantly from novice to intermediate to proficient performance levels (all p < .05), but divergence in sensitivity was evident. Fixation rate showed the greatest effect size across the novice–intermediate transition (η² = .41), while pupil dilation was most sensitive at the intermediate–proficient transition (η² = .35). Heart rate variability had lower discriminant validity between stages. Correlation among indices was modest (r range .21–.44), confirming that they tap partially independent aspects of workload. The multi-modal measurement approach is recommended for training assessment in surgical education, particularly where unobtrusive monitoring is required.

SYN-PUB-03795.title: Domain-Specific Language for Configuring AUTOSAR Communication Matrices
SYN-PUB-03795.text:
Domain-Specific Language for Configuring AUTOSAR Communication Matrices (2016, conference, Proceedings of the Workshop on Model-Driven Engineering for Embedded Systems).
Authors: Borislav Đorđević (outside co-author); Vukica Grujić (R0305); Andrea Mocci (outside co-author); Strahinja Radović (R0385); Mirjana Vidaković (R0948).
Keywords: DSL; Xtext; Xtend; communication matrix; AUTOSAR 4.2.
Communication matrix configuration in AUTOSAR involves mapping signals to PDUs, defining timing parameters, and assigning network identifiers, all expressed in verbose ARXML. This paper presents ComMatDSL, a textual domain-specific language designed to express communication matrix configurations concisely. The language was defined using Xtext and includes a type system aligned with AUTOSAR data types. A model-to-ARXML generator was implemented using Xtend. The language was evaluated with five engineers from a regional embedded-software consultancy, each of whom configured three bus networks of increasing complexity. Compared to direct ARXML editing, ComMatDSL configurations were on average 76% shorter in character count and contained 58% fewer syntactic errors in the first-draft stage. A round-trip test on 22 reference matrices confirmed semantic equivalence of the generated ARXML with manually authored originals. The DSL is available as an Eclipse feature and targets AUTOSAR 4.2.

SYN-PUB-03796.title: Ontology-Driven Normalisation of Heterogeneous Vulnerability Feed Data
SYN-PUB-03796.text:
Ontology-Driven Normalisation of Heterogeneous Vulnerability Feed Data (2021, conference, Proceedings of the Symposium on Applied Network Analysis and Security).
Authors: Katarina Lukić (outside co-author); René Dubois (outside co-author); Árpád Nagy (R0564); Slobodan Knežević (R1030); Vukica Grujić (R0305).
Keywords: vulnerability data; ontology; NVD; data normalisation; attack graph.
Vulnerability intelligence is distributed across NVD, vendor advisories, and commercial feeds whose data models differ in severity scoring, affected-product representation, and remediation guidance. This paper describes an OWL 2 ontology designed to normalise records from five distinct vulnerability data sources into a unified schema suitable for automated ingestion by attack-graph construction pipelines. The ontology contains 84 classes and 47 object properties; a mapping layer implemented in SPARQL handles source-specific identifier schemes. Evaluation on 6,400 vulnerability records shows that the normalisation procedure resolves 93.1% of duplicate entries that span two or more sources and reduces manual curation effort by an estimated 68% in a controlled analyst-time study involving four participants. The ontology and mapping scripts are released under an open licence. Integration with the incremental attack-graph tool described in earlier work is demonstrated on a 300-node test network.

SYN-PUB-03993.title: Inferring prerequisite structures among skills from observational response data: a constraint-based graphical modelling approach
SYN-PUB-03993.text:
Inferring prerequisite structures among skills from observational response data: a constraint-based graphical modelling approach (2026, journal, Journal of Educational Data Science).
Authors: Luka Đorđević (outside co-author); Marco Ferretti (outside co-author); Ognjen Ninkov (R0386); Sonja Babić (outside co-author); Emilija Zec (R0322); Luka Nedić (R0911).
Keywords: prerequisite structures; causal discovery; skill graphs; adaptive learning; mathematics.
(no abstract)

SYN-PUB-04185.title: A Metamodel for Compositional Enterprise Integration Patterns
SYN-PUB-04185.text:
A Metamodel for Compositional Enterprise Integration Patterns (2011, journal, Journal of Software Architecture and Middleware).
Authors: Milana Bošković (R0341); Dragan Petrović (outside co-author); Tatjana Kovač (outside co-author).
Keywords: metamodel; enterprise integration patterns; UML profile; OCL; composition.
Enterprise integration patterns (EIPs) are widely used as building blocks in message-oriented middleware, yet no formally grounded metamodel existed that captured their compositional semantics. This paper proposes a UML-profile-based metamodel covering 47 patterns drawn from canonical pattern catalogues, extended with OCL constraints that encode valid composition rules. The metamodel was validated against six open-source integration projects by manually mapping their routing logic to the proposed meta-level; conformance was measured at 89% of constructs successfully represented. A comparison with two earlier informal taxonomies shows that the proposed approach catches eight categories of composition error that the informal approaches do not distinguish. The work provides a foundation for automated tooling that checks integration model well-formedness before deployment.

SYN-PUB-04186.title: Formal Verification of Message-Routing Compositions Using Alloy
SYN-PUB-04186.text:
Formal Verification of Message-Routing Compositions Using Alloy (2013, conference, Proceedings of the Central European Conference on Formal Methods in Software Engineering (CEFoMSE)).
Authors: Milana Bošković (R0341); Dragan Petrović (outside co-author); Marko Ilić (outside co-author).
Keywords: Alloy; formal verification; message routing; deadlock; enterprise integration.
Routing logic in enterprise integration systems can exhibit subtle deadlocks and message-loss faults that surface only under specific load conditions. This paper encodes a subset of EIP routing patterns—splitter, aggregator, content-based router, and filter—as Alloy signatures and predicates, allowing exhaustive bounded-scope analysis. Seventeen integration scenarios derived from production healthcare data-exchange systems were modelled; the Alloy Analyzer found counterexamples in four scenarios within scopes up to size 8, two of which were confirmed as real faults in the reference implementations. The encoding approach is described in sufficient detail to be reproducible, and the full Alloy models are provided as supplementary material. Execution times on a standard workstation ranged from 1.2 seconds to 47 minutes depending on scope and constraint density.

SYN-PUB-04187.title: Survey of Model Transformation Approaches for Integration Architecture Migration
SYN-PUB-04187.text:
Survey of Model Transformation Approaches for Integration Architecture Migration (2015, journal, ACM Computing Surveys in Software and Systems).
Authors: Milana Bošković (R0341); Ivana Lazarević (outside co-author); Stefan Groß (outside co-author); Svetlana Kapor (R1033).
Keywords: survey; model transformation; ATL; QVT; migration; service-oriented architecture.
Legacy integration architectures are frequently migrated to service-oriented or event-driven platforms, yet the model transformation techniques employed are rarely compared systematically. This survey analyses 63 peer-reviewed papers published between 2003 and 2012 that describe transformation-based migration approaches. Papers are classified along five dimensions: source and target architectural style, transformation language used, degree of automation, evaluation method, and domain of application. ATL and QVT-Relations account for 54% of the surveyed approaches combined. Only 19 of the 63 papers report quantitative evaluation with more than one industrial case. The survey identifies gaps in traceability preservation and in handling of non-functional constraints during transformation, and proposes a research agenda for the subsequent five years. A replication package including the classification spreadsheet is available.

SYN-PUB-04188.title: Interface Contract Specification for Event-Driven Microservices Using a Formal Pattern Language
SYN-PUB-04188.text:
Interface Contract Specification for Event-Driven Microservices Using a Formal Pattern Language (2016, journal, Journal of Software Architecture and Middleware).
Authors: Milana Bošković (R0341); Dragan Petrović (outside co-author); Ana Horvat (outside co-author); Jovana Mladenović (R0734).
Keywords: interface contract; microservices; event-driven architecture; LTL; pattern language.
Microservice architectures that rely on asynchronous messaging lack a standardised means of expressing interface contracts that go beyond data schema. This paper introduces a formal pattern language, denoted IPL-EDA, in which each interface contract specifies permitted message sequences, routing obligations, and timing constraints using a combination of regular expressions over message types and linear temporal logic formulae. IPL-EDA contracts are expressed as annotations on a service's OpenAPI-style description and checked automatically using a prototype contract verifier. An evaluation against a synthetic benchmark of 120 service pairs and a real logistics platform with 14 services shows that the verifier detects 91% of injected contract violations with a false-positive rate of 3.2%. Annotation overhead averages 38 additional lines per service description.

SYN-PUB-04189.title: Towards a Formal Semantics for the Saga Pattern in Distributed Transaction Management
SYN-PUB-04189.text:
Towards a Formal Semantics for the Saga Pattern in Distributed Transaction Management (2019, journal, Electronic Notes in Theoretical Computer Science (Balkan Series)).
Authors: Marko Ilić (outside co-author); Milana Bošković (R0341); Claudia Ferencz (outside co-author); Ivan Zarić (R0575).
Keywords: Saga pattern; distributed transactions; operational semantics; SPIN; model checking.
The Saga pattern decomposes a distributed transaction into a sequence of local transactions with compensating actions, but existing descriptions in the literature are informal and implementation-dependent. This paper gives a formal operational semantics for Sagas using labelled transition systems, covering both choreography-based and orchestration-based variants. Fifteen Saga implementations taken from open-source repositories were encoded in the formal model; model checking with SPIN revealed two previously unreported scenarios in which compensating actions could be skipped under concurrent failure. The formalisation also clarifies the relationship between Sagas and the classical two-phase commit protocol, showing that two-phase commit is a degenerate Saga under additional locking assumptions. The paper is intended as groundwork for future tool support rather than an industrial deployment guide.

SYN-PUB-04190.title: Model-Driven Configuration of API Gateways from Architectural Intent
SYN-PUB-04190.text:
Model-Driven Configuration of API Gateways from Architectural Intent (2021, journal, Journal of Systems and Software Integration).
Authors: Milana Bošković (R0341); Nemanja Vukić (outside co-author); Stefan Groß (outside co-author); Jovana Đorđević (outside co-author).
Keywords: API gateway; DSL; ATL; configuration generation; architectural intent.
API gateway products such as reverse proxies and service meshes require extensive low-level configuration that must remain consistent with a system's intended integration architecture. This paper proposes a two-layer approach: an architecture-level model expressed in a lightweight DSL captures routing intent, authentication boundaries, and rate-limiting policies; a set of ATL transformations then generates gateway-specific configuration files for two target platforms. An evaluation conducted on a medium-sized e-commerce platform with 31 services compared manually written configuration with generated configuration on seven quality criteria. Generated configuration had fewer inconsistencies (4 vs. 19) and reduced configuration size by 28% on average through deduplication of repeated policy blocks. Round-trip regeneration after architectural change took under 90 seconds for the largest tested model.

SYN-PUB-04191.title: Consistency Checking Between Architectural Models and Runtime Integration Behaviour
SYN-PUB-04191.text:
Consistency Checking Between Architectural Models and Runtime Integration Behaviour (2023, conference, Proceedings of the European Conference on Software Architecture (ECSA)).
Authors: Milana Bošković (R0341); Ana Horvat (outside co-author); Radovan Marinković (outside co-author).
Keywords: architectural drift; runtime monitoring; graph homomorphism; message broker; consistency.
Architectural drift—the divergence between a documented software architecture and the system as actually deployed—is a common maintenance problem. This paper addresses drift detection in integration-heavy systems by instrumenting message brokers to capture runtime message-flow graphs and comparing them against the architectural intent model using a graph-homomorphism-based matching algorithm. The approach was evaluated on two industrial systems: a logistics information platform and a public-sector document-exchange infrastructure. In the logistics system, 11 undocumented message paths and three deprecated routes still receiving traffic were detected automatically within a 72-hour observation window. Precision was 94% and recall 88% relative to manually verified ground truth. The paper also discusses how detected deviations can be fed back to update the architectural model semi-automatically.

SYN-PUB-04192.title: Interface Adaptation Strategies for Heterogeneous IoT Device Integration: A Model-Driven Study
SYN-PUB-04192.text:
Interface Adaptation Strategies for Heterogeneous IoT Device Integration: A Model-Driven Study (2025, journal, IEEE Transactions on Industrial Informatics Integration).
Authors: Nemanja Vukić (outside co-author); Mirjana Simić (outside co-author); Lena Brandt (outside co-author); Milana Bošković (R0341).
Keywords: IoT; protocol adapter; MQTT; CoAP; model-driven; smart factory.
Industrial IoT deployments regularly combine devices that communicate over incompatible protocols—MQTT, CoAP, Modbus, and proprietary serial formats are common simultaneously. This paper applies the model-driven adapter generation framework developed in earlier work to IoT device integration, extending the original finite-state-machine interface model with data-type coercion rules and timing constraints specific to sensor data streams. Twelve device pairs from a smart-factory pilot in Vojvodina were used as test cases; nine generated adapters functioned correctly without modification, two required minor timing adjustments, and one could not be handled due to a stateful proprietary protocol. Adapter round-trip latency overhead was measured at 1.8 ms median on a Raspberry Pi 4, which was acceptable for all non-real-time use cases in the pilot.

SYN-PUB-04193.title: Specification and Automated Verification of Choreography Contracts in Event-Driven Systems: Lessons from Three Industrial Cases
SYN-PUB-04193.text:
Specification and Automated Verification of Choreography Contracts in Event-Driven Systems: Lessons from Three Industrial Cases (2026, journal, Journal of Software: Evolution and Process).
Authors: Milana Bošković (R0341); Radovan Marinković (outside co-author); Claudia Ferencz (outside co-author); Petra Novak (outside co-author).
Keywords: choreography; multiparty session types; contract verification; liveness; industrial case study.
Choreography-level contracts define the observable interaction obligations of multiple participants in a distributed system without centralising control. This paper reports on the application of a contract specification language based on multiparty session types to three real industrial systems: a regional healthcare interoperability platform, a customs document exchange service, and a retail supply-chain event bus. For each system, existing informal specifications were re-expressed as session-typed choreographies and checked for well-formedness and progress guarantees. The process uncovered two liveness violations in the healthcare system and one safety violation in the customs system that had manifested as intermittent timeout errors in production. The paper discusses the practical friction involved in eliciting the information needed for formal specification from integration teams unfamiliar with formal methods, and proposes a lightweight elicitation protocol.

SYN-PUB-04195.title: Benchmarking Embedded Lossy Compressors for Structural Health Monitoring on a 32-Node Piezoelectric Sensor Array
SYN-PUB-04195.text:
Benchmarking Embedded Lossy Compressors for Structural Health Monitoring on a 32-Node Piezoelectric Sensor Array (2023, journal, Mechanical Systems and Signal Processing).
Authors: Ivana Rašković (outside co-author); Milana Bošković (R0341); Marco Bertolini (outside co-author); Uroš Filipović (outside co-author); Tatjana Kovačević (outside co-author); Branislav Stojanović (R0641).
Keywords: structural health monitoring; piezoelectric array; vector quantisation; guided wave; damage localisation; benchmark.
Structural health monitoring of bridges and tunnels increasingly relies on dense piezoelectric sensor arrays generating sustained data rates of hundreds of kilobytes per second. This paper benchmarks seven embedded lossy compressors — including DPCM, adaptive PLA, Haar filterbank, spectral peak preservation, and three variants of learned vector quantisation — on a 32-node wireless array deployed on a pedestrian footbridge in Novi Sad over four weeks. Evaluation metrics include compression ratio, reconstruction SNR, preservation of guided-wave arrival time picks (used for damage localisation), and energy per sample. The learned vector quantiser with 256-centroid codebook trained offline on historical data achieved the best damage-localisation accuracy (mean error 4.8 cm at 8:1 compression) but required 24 kB of flash for the codebook. Adaptive PLA achieved competitive localisation accuracy (mean error 6.1 cm) with only 2.1 kB of code and data memory. Practical trade-off recommendations are given for deployment scenarios constrained by either memory or localisation precision requirements.

SYN-PUB-04278.title: Izgradnja invertovanog indeksa za srpske tekstove sa mešovitim pismom: osnovna metodologija
SYN-PUB-04278.text:
Izgradnja invertovanog indeksa za srpske tekstove sa mešovitim pismom: osnovna metodologija (2010, conference, Zbornik radova Konferencije o primeni računara i interneta u Srbiji (PRIS 2010)).
Authors: Milena Kovačević (outside co-author); Stefan Dragić (R0349).
Keywords: invertovani indeks; mešovito pismo; normalizacija; srpski jezik.
U radu se opisuje metodologija izgradnje invertovanog indeksa koji istovremeno obrađuje ćirilična i latinična pojavljivanja srpskih reči bez prethodnog potpunog prevođenja u jedno pismo. Predloženi postupak uključuje korak normalizacije tokena kojim se za svaki token generiše kanonska forma zasnovana na fonemskoj reprezentaciji, a zatim se fonemski ključevi koriste kao primarni identifikatori u indeksu. Eksperimenti su sprovedeni na korpusu od 120 000 novinskih članaka preuzetih iz tri srpska dnevna lista u periodu 2000–2008. Mere preciznosti i odziva upoređene su s dva bazična sistema koji koriste isključivo ćirilični, odnosno isključivo latinični indeks. Predloženi sistem postiže F1 vrednost od 0,81 u zadatku ad-hoc pretrage, što je povećanje od 14 procentnih poena u odnosu na bolji od dva bazična sistema. Rad takođe razmatra pitanje memorijskog otiska hibridnog indeksa i predlaže strategiju kompresije rečnika.

SYN-PUB-04279.title: Phoneme-Based Token Canonicalization for Serbian Script Unification
SYN-PUB-04279.text:
Phoneme-Based Token Canonicalization for Serbian Script Unification (2011, journal, Journal of Language Technology and Computational Linguistics).
Authors: Stefan Dragić (R0349); Milena Kovačević (outside co-author); Radovan Ostojić (outside co-author).
Keywords: phoneme canonicalization; Serbian; script unification; legal text retrieval.
Serbian is officially written in both Cyrillic and Latin scripts, and documents frequently contain tokens in both scripts within a single sentence or paragraph. This paper presents a token canonicalization procedure in which each token is mapped to a phoneme sequence using deterministic grapheme-to-phoneme rules derived from Serbian orthographic conventions, and the resulting phoneme string serves as the canonical form for retrieval purposes. We evaluated the approach on a manually annotated gold standard of 4 200 query–document relevance pairs drawn from a legal corpus of 38 000 court decisions. The phoneme-based canonical form reduced the out-of-vocabulary rate from 9.3% to 2.1% compared with a Latin-only baseline and from 11.7% to 2.4% compared with a Cyrillic-only baseline. Precision at rank 10 improved by 8 percentage points over both baselines. Edge cases involving foreign loanwords and proper nouns are discussed, and a set of override rules is proposed for the 230 most frequent exceptions identified in the corpus.

SYN-PUB-04280.title: Cross-Script Query Expansion Using Transliteration Variants in Serbian Web Search
SYN-PUB-04280.text:
Cross-Script Query Expansion Using Transliteration Variants in Serbian Web Search (2014, conference, Proceedings of the Central European Information Retrieval Symposium (CEIRS 2014)).
Authors: Stefan Dragić (R0349); Tomislav Blažević (outside co-author); Milena Kovačević (outside co-author).
Keywords: query expansion; transliteration; web search; Serbian; named entity.
Users searching Serbian-language web content often type queries in one script while relevant documents are stored in the other. This paper studies the effect of automatically expanding queries with their transliteration variants before submission to an inverted index. We constructed a test collection of 1 800 queries and 210 000 web pages crawled from .rs domains, with relevance judgments pooled from four assessors. Three expansion strategies were compared: (1) appending the full transliteration variant, (2) appending only tokens whose transliteration differs from the original by more than two characters, and (3) expanding only named entities detected by a rule-based tagger. Strategy 3 achieved the best mean average precision of 0.497, versus 0.431 for no expansion, while reducing index bloat to 6% over the baseline index size. We also report retrieval latency measurements on a commodity server, showing that the overhead introduced by expansion remains under 12 ms at the 95th percentile for queries up to eight tokens.

SYN-PUB-04281.title: Automatska detekcija i korekcija nedoslednosti pisma u srpskim digitalnim arhivima
SYN-PUB-04281.text:
Automatska detekcija i korekcija nedoslednosti pisma u srpskim digitalnim arhivima (2015, conference, Zbornik radova 23. Telekomunikacionog foruma TELFOR).
Authors: Bojan Marković (outside co-author); Stefan Dragić (R0349); Ana Vukić (outside co-author).
Keywords: detekcija nedoslednosti pisma; klasifikacija; digitalni arhivi; srpski jezik.
Digitalni arhivi srpskih novina i institucionalnih dokumenata često sadrže nedoslednosti gde je isti dokument delom u ćirilici, a delom u latinici, ponekad zbog grešaka pri skeniranju ili uredničkih intervencija. Ovaj rad predlaže metod automatske detekcije takvih nedoslednosti na nivou rečenice, korišćenjem klasifikatora koji kao atribute uzima raspodelu skriptnih blokova, učestalosti bigrama i morfosintaksičke signale. Klasifikator je treniran na 9 400 ručno označenih rečenica iz arhive jednog novosadskog lista i testiran na 2 100 rečenica iz arhive beogradskog lista. Postiže preciznost od 0,91 i odziv od 0,88 u klasi nedoslednih rečenica. Korak korekcije primenjuje fonemsku transliteraciju na detektovane nedosledne tokene. Eksperiment na donstremu (pretragom dokumenta) pokazuje da korigovana verzija arhive daje veću tačnost od nekorigovane za 7 procentnih poena u prosečnoj preciznosti.

SYN-PUB-04282.title: A Benchmark Corpus for Mixed-Script Serbian Information Retrieval
SYN-PUB-04282.text:
A Benchmark Corpus for Mixed-Script Serbian Information Retrieval (2017, conference, Language Resources and Evaluation Conference Proceedings (LREC-SE 2017)).
Authors: Stefan Dragić (R0349); Jelena Stanković (outside co-author); Nikola Petrović (outside co-author); Carla Manzoni (outside co-author).
Keywords: benchmark corpus; evaluation; mixed-script; BM25; retrieval models.
Reproducible evaluation of retrieval systems for Serbian requires a shared test collection that explicitly accounts for mixed-script documents. This paper describes the construction of SrMIR-1, a benchmark corpus comprising 95 000 documents from four genres — news, law, literature, and social media — with 600 topics and graded relevance judgments produced by 12 trained assessors following TREC-style pooling at depth 30. Approximately 41% of documents contain tokens in both scripts. Inter-assessor agreement, measured by Cohen's kappa, was 0.73 across all topics. The paper reports baseline results for five retrieval models: BM25, language modelling with Dirichlet smoothing, a transliteration-aware BM25 variant, a neural dense retrieval model fine-tuned on Serbian, and a hybrid sparse–dense model. The transliteration-aware BM25 variant achieves the highest nDCG@10 of 0.531 among sparse models, while the hybrid model reaches 0.587. The corpus is publicly available under a Creative Commons licence.

SYN-PUB-04283.title: Indeksiranje pravnih dokumenata sa heterogenim pismom: studija slučaja sudske prakse u Srbiji
SYN-PUB-04283.text:
Indeksiranje pravnih dokumenata sa heterogenim pismom: studija slučaja sudske prakse u Srbiji (2018, journal, Pravo i informatika: Časopis za pravnu informatiku i upravljanje znanjem).
Authors: Stefan Dragić (R0349); Radovan Ostojić (outside co-author); Bojan Marković (outside co-author).
Keywords: pravni dokumenti; pretraga; sudska praksa; normalizacija pisma.
Sudske odluke u Srbiji nastajale su kroz nekoliko decenija u različitim pisarskim praksama i sistemima za obradu teksta, što je rezultovalo korpusom u kome se isti pravni termin pojavljuje u ćiriličnom i latiničnom obliku, ponekad unutar istog paragrafa. Ovaj rad opisuje sistem za pretragu koji je prilagođen ovoj karakteristici i koji se koristi u pilot projektu jednog regionalnog suda. Sistem koristi troslojan pristup: normalizaciju pisma, pravno-specifičnu listu sinonima i rangirač koji uvažava strukturu dokumenta (izreka, obrazloženje, dispozitiv). Evaluacija je sprovedena na 5 800 upita sudskog osoblja tokom tromesečnog pilot perioda. Sistem je postigao prosečnu preciznost od 0,74, uz korisničku ocenu zadovoljstva 4,1 od 5. Rad diskutuje tehničke i organizacione izazove uvođenja pretražnog sistema u pravnu praksu.

SYN-PUB-04284.title: Script-Aware Passage Retrieval for Serbian Question Answering
SYN-PUB-04284.text:
Script-Aware Passage Retrieval for Serbian Question Answering (2021, conference, Proceedings of the 9th Workshop on Slavic Natural Language Processing (SlavicNLP 2021)).
Authors: Jovana Ilić (outside co-author); Stefan Dragić (R0349); Carla Manzoni (outside co-author); Luka Đorđević (outside co-author).
Keywords: passage retrieval; question answering; BM25; script normalization; Serbian.
Open-domain question answering over Serbian-language document collections requires a passage retrieval component that is robust to the script in which both the question and the passage are written. This paper describes an adaptation of a BM25-based passage retrieval pipeline in which the tokenizer applies script normalization before indexing and at query time. We built an evaluation set of 340 factoid questions with 1 to 4 correct passages each, drawn from a mixed-script encyclopedia-style corpus of 180 000 passages. We compared four configurations: BM25 with no normalization, BM25 with script normalization, a dense bi-encoder model trained on Serbian data, and a hybrid of the latter two. The script-normalized BM25 retrieves at least one correct passage in the top 20 for 72% of questions, a gain of 17 percentage points over unnormalized BM25. The hybrid model reaches 81%. Failure analysis highlights questions containing transliterated foreign proper nouns as the main remaining challenge.

SYN-PUB-04286.title: SrMIR-2: Extending the Mixed-Script Serbian Retrieval Benchmark to Social Media and Administrative Registers
SYN-PUB-04286.text:
SrMIR-2: Extending the Mixed-Script Serbian Retrieval Benchmark to Social Media and Administrative Registers (2025, journal, ACM Transactions on Information Systems).
Authors: Stefan Dragić (R0349); Luka Đorđević (outside co-author); Jelena Stanković (outside co-author); Carla Manzoni (outside co-author); Éva Gyöngyössy (outside co-author).
Keywords: benchmark; social media; administrative text; script mixing; evaluation.
SrMIR-1, released in 2017, covered news, law, literature, and general web content. Since then, social media posts and administrative e-government documents have become important retrieval targets, both exhibiting pronounced script mixing and informal orthography. This paper describes SrMIR-2, which adds two new document registers to the benchmark: 60 000 posts from a Serbian microblogging platform and 28 000 administrative forms and decisions from three municipal e-government portals. We created 280 new topics for these registers with relevance judgments from six trained assessors (kappa = 0.69). Baseline experiments show that script-normalizing BM25 outperforms unnormalized BM25 by a larger margin on social media (22 percentage points in nDCG@10) than on administrative documents (9 points), attributable to the higher rate of informal transliteration in social media. The benchmark is released with code for reproducible evaluation. We also report an ablation study isolating the contribution of named-entity handling in the normalization pipeline.

SYN-PUB-04287.title: Latency–Accuracy Trade-offs in Script-Normalizing Retrieval Pipelines Under Production Load
SYN-PUB-04287.text:
Latency–Accuracy Trade-offs in Script-Normalizing Retrieval Pipelines Under Production Load (2026, conference, Proceedings of the European Conference on Information Retrieval (ECIR 2026)).
Authors: Nikola Petrović (outside co-author); Stefan Dragić (R0349); Dejan Vuković (outside co-author).
Keywords: production retrieval; latency; accuracy; cascaded pipeline; query log analysis.
Deploying script-normalizing retrieval in production requires careful attention to latency, especially when normalization involves neural components. This paper presents a systematic study of trade-offs along the latency–accuracy spectrum for five pipeline configurations ranging from a purely deterministic rule-based normalizer to a full transformer-based normalizer, tested on a simulated production workload derived from query logs of a Serbian news aggregator with peak loads of 340 queries per second. We measure mean reciprocal rank, P@5, and end-to-end latency at the 50th, 90th, and 99th percentiles on a server cluster of four nodes. The deterministic normalizer adds 3 ms median latency with MRR of 0.61. The transformer-based normalizer achieves MRR of 0.68 but adds 47 ms at the 99th percentile. A cascaded configuration — deterministic normalizer with neural fallback triggered only for out-of-vocabulary tokens — reaches MRR of 0.66 with a 99th-percentile latency overhead of only 9 ms. Detailed profiling data and configuration files are provided.

SYN-PUB-04373.title: A PC-Based Real-Time Target for Engine Control Unit Testing Using RTAI-Linux and a Low-Cost DAQ Board
SYN-PUB-04373.text:
A PC-Based Real-Time Target for Engine Control Unit Testing Using RTAI-Linux and a Low-Cost DAQ Board (2011, journal, Journal of Embedded and Real-Time Computing Systems).
Authors: Branimir Vukić (outside co-author); Miroslav Đorđević (outside co-author); Darko Ninkov (R0356).
Keywords: RTAI-Linux; x86 real-time; engine ECU; CAN bus; low-cost HiL.
This paper describes the construction and validation of a low-cost hardware-in-the-loop (HiL) test bench built around a standard x86 PC running RTAI-Linux 3.8 and a commercially available 16-channel analog/digital acquisition board. The setup was used to emulate the sensor and actuator environment of a diesel engine management ECU supplied by a regional automotive Tier-1 supplier. A mean-value engine model with six state variables was implemented and executed at a fixed step size of 1 ms, achieving worst-case jitter below 35 µs across a 4-hour continuous run. CAN communication between the real-time host and the ECU was handled through a standard USB-to-CAN adapter operating at 500 kbit/s. Forty-two ECU software variants were tested against a library of 180 deterministic test cases covering cold-start, idle, and wide-open-throttle scenarios. The paper reports pass/fail statistics, timing overhead, and the cost breakdown of the bench, which totaled under 1 200 EUR in hardware. Limitations related to I/O bandwidth and USB latency are discussed and partly mitigated through interrupt coalescing.

SYN-PUB-04374.title: Modelling and Real-Time Implementation of a Brushless DC Motor Drive for HiL Emulation of Electric Power Steering Loads
SYN-PUB-04374.text:
Modelling and Real-Time Implementation of a Brushless DC Motor Drive for HiL Emulation of Electric Power Steering Loads (2013, conference, Proceedings of the 10th International Symposium on Intelligent Systems and Informatics (SISY)).
Authors: Darko Ninkov (R0356); Svetlana Kovačević (outside co-author); Andrea Krstić (R0521); Tomas Brezina (outside co-author).
Keywords: BLDC motor emulation; FPGA fixed-point; electric power steering; HiL; Spartan-6.
Electric power steering (EPS) systems place demanding requirements on HiL test benches because the steering column torque sensor and motor current feedback must be emulated at update rates below 500 µs. This work presents a BLDC motor model parameterised from bench measurements on a 48 V, 400 W motor taken from a mid-class passenger car.
