The model captures back-EMF harmonics up to the 7th order and includes a thermal sub-model with two lumped time constants. It was compiled to a Xilinx Spartan-6 FPGA using a fixed-point arithmetic pipeline operating at 50 MHz, achieving a simulation step of 20 µs. Analog outputs were generated through on-board 16-bit DACs. A comparison between the FPGA model and a reference floating-point Simulink simulation showed RMS current errors below 1.2% over standard SAE J266 steering manoeuvres. The paper also quantifies resource utilisation: 31% of available LUTs and 18% of DSP48 blocks on the target device.

SYN-PUB-04375.title: Fault Injection Framework for Automotive Body Control Module Testing on an Open-Source HiL Platform
SYN-PUB-04375.text:
Fault Injection Framework for Automotive Body Control Module Testing on an Open-Source HiL Platform (2015, journal, International Journal of Automotive Technology and Engineering).
Authors: Darko Ninkov (R0356); Aleksandar Petrović (outside co-author); Norbert Feher (outside co-author).
Keywords: fault injection; body control module; ISO 26262; Xenomai; solid-state relay.
Body control modules (BCMs) must tolerate a range of electrical faults including open circuits, shorts to battery and shorts to ground on their I/O lines. Commercial HiL systems provide programmable fault relays, but their cost is prohibitive for small development teams. This paper presents a fault injection board designed around solid-state relay arrays and a microcontroller interface, integrated with a Beaglebone Black running a Xenomai real-time patch as the simulation host. The board supports 32 independent fault channels switchable within 2 ms. A BCM with 28 digital outputs and 14 analog inputs was tested under 96 fault combinations derived from ISO 26262 FMEA tables. The framework detected seven previously unreported software anomalies in the BCM firmware relating to debounce timer behaviour under simultaneous multi-line faults. Replication cost for the fault injection hardware was 340 EUR per board. The design files and driver code are released under a permissive open-source licence.

SYN-PUB-04376.title: Latency Characterisation of Open-Source Real-Time Kernels for Automotive HIL Applications
SYN-PUB-04376.text:
Latency Characterisation of Open-Source Real-Time Kernels for Automotive HIL Applications (2016, journal, Real-Time Systems: Theory and Applications).
Authors: Darko Ninkov (R0356); Zoran Marković (outside co-author); Spasoje Petrović (R0868).
Keywords: RTAI; Xenomai; PREEMPT_RT; latency; real-time Linux; HiL benchmarking.
Several open-source options exist for turning a general-purpose Linux system into a deterministic real-time platform: RTAI, Xenomai 3, and the PREEMPT_RT patch. This paper provides a systematic comparison of all three on two hardware platforms—a standard Intel Core i5 desktop and an ARM Cortex-A9 single-board computer—under automotive HiL workloads. Latency was measured using a hardware timer circuit with 100 ns resolution over 72-hour test windows while simultaneously running a 23-state vehicle dynamics model, a CAN stack, and a UDP telemetry stream. Xenomai 3 with the Cobalt core achieved the lowest worst-case latency on the x86 platform at 18 µs, while PREEMPT_RT showed marginally better throughput at the cost of 47 µs worst-case. On the ARM platform, Xenomai 3 and PREEMPT_RT performed comparably. The paper provides configuration recipes, kernel version numbers, and patch sets used, making the results reproducible. Recommendations are given for selecting a kernel flavour based on step-size and I/O bandwidth requirements.

SYN-PUB-04377.title: Integration of a FlexRay Bus Interface into a Low-Cost FPGA-Based HiL Bench for Chassis Domain ECU Testing
SYN-PUB-04377.text:
Integration of a FlexRay Bus Interface into a Low-Cost FPGA-Based HiL Bench for Chassis Domain ECU Testing (2017, conference, Proceedings of the IEEE International Conference on Intelligent Engineering Systems (INES)).
Authors: Milica Stanković (outside co-author); Darko Ninkov (R0356); Péter Galajda (outside co-author); Branimir Vukić (outside co-author).
Keywords: FlexRay; FPGA VHDL; Artix-7; chassis ECU; ABS ESC testing.
FlexRay is used in safety-critical chassis domains such as active suspension and brake-by-wire. Integrating a FlexRay interface into a low-cost HiL platform is non-trivial because commercially licensed IP cores are expensive. This work documents the integration of an open FlexRay communication controller implemented in VHDL on a Xilinx Artix-7 FPGA with a Linux-based simulation host connected via PCIe. The controller supports static segment scheduling with a cycle time of 5 ms and up to 64 frame slots. Two ABS/ESC ECUs from a regional supplier were used as devices under test. The paper reports successful execution of 214 scheduled test sequences covering wheel speed sensor emulation, hydraulic pressure command injection, and inter-ECU synchronisation checks. Timing accuracy of the FlexRay frames was within ±250 ns of nominal, verified with a dedicated bus analyser. Integration effort and remaining limitations regarding the dynamic segment are also discussed.

SYN-PUB-04378.title: A Semi-Automated Test Case Generation Method for ECU Validation Based on Boundary-Value Analysis of CAN Signal Databases
SYN-PUB-04378.text:
A Semi-Automated Test Case Generation Method for ECU Validation Based on Boundary-Value Analysis of CAN Signal Databases (2018, journal, Journal of Automotive Software Engineering).
Authors: Darko Ninkov (R0356); Jovana Ilić (outside co-author); Cristian Morariu (outside co-author).
Keywords: test case generation; boundary-value analysis; CAN DBC; ECU validation; test automation.
ECU test suites are typically assembled manually from specification documents, which is time-consuming and incomplete. This paper describes a tool that parses CANdb++ DBC files to extract signal definitions—including physical ranges, factors, offsets, and initial values—and automatically generates boundary-value and equivalence-partition test cases for each signal. The tool was applied to two DBC databases: one covering a powertrain domain (312 signals, 47 message IDs) and one covering a body domain (198 signals, 31 message IDs). Test case counts of 1 847 and 1 203 were produced respectively and executed on the low-cost HiL bench described in earlier work. Execution time per test case averaged 4.3 seconds on the powertrain database. Twelve defects were identified in the body domain ECU firmware that manual testing had not found, including three out-of-range handling errors and two incorrect default value responses. The paper discusses integration with a lightweight Python-based test management framework and export to an XML format compatible with standard reporting tools.

SYN-PUB-04380.title: Containerised Deployment of Real-Time ECU Test Environments Using Docker and Xenomai on Embedded Linux Platforms
SYN-PUB-04380.text:
Containerised Deployment of Real-Time ECU Test Environments Using Docker and Xenomai on Embedded Linux Platforms (2022, journal, Software: Practice and Experience in Embedded Systems).
Authors: Darko Ninkov (R0356); Jovana Ilić (outside co-author); László Keviczky (outside co-author).
Keywords: Docker; Xenomai; containerisation; ECU test bench; reproducibility.
Reproducing a specific HiL software environment across multiple bench instances and over time is a persistent problem in automotive software development. This paper investigates whether Docker containers can be used to encapsulate the user-space components of a Xenomai 3 real-time application—model binaries, CAN stack configuration, test scripts—while the host kernel retains the Cobalt real-time core. Experiments were conducted on two identical Raspberry Pi 4 platforms running an identical Xenomai-patched kernel. Containerised and native deployments were compared for latency, throughput, and deployment time across three ECU test suites. Worst-case latency overhead introduced by the container runtime was 3 µs in all measured cases, considered acceptable for step sizes of 1 ms and above. Deployment time was reduced from approximately 45 minutes of manual setup to under 6 minutes. The paper also describes a versioning workflow using a private registry and discusses limitations when hardware access to GPIO and CAN interfaces is required inside the container.

SYN-PUB-04381.title: Ethernet-Based Time-Sensitive Networking as a Backbone for Distributed Automotive HiL Benches: Feasibility Assessment
SYN-PUB-04381.text:
Ethernet-Based Time-Sensitive Networking as a Backbone for Distributed Automotive HiL Benches: Feasibility Assessment (2026, preprint, arXiv (cs.SY)).
Authors: Jovana Ilić (outside co-author); Darko Ninkov (R0356); Péter Galajda (outside co-author).
Keywords: TSN; IEEE 802.1Qbv; distributed HiL; automotive Ethernet; time synchronisation.
As automotive architectures shift toward Ethernet-based in-vehicle networks, HiL benches must emulate Ethernet traffic alongside classical fieldbuses. This preprint reports preliminary measurements on using IEEE 802.1AS time synchronisation and 802.1Qbv time-aware shaper on a three-node distributed HiL bench where each node hosts a partial vehicle subsystem model. Nodes are connected through a managed switch with TSN support. Clock synchronisation accuracy between nodes was measured at 120 ns RMS over a 48-hour window using a shared GPS-disciplined reference. Model state exchange over scheduled Ethernet frames at 1 ms intervals showed zero missed deadlines in a 24-hour test. The preprint describes the network configuration, measurement methodology, and a preliminary cost comparison against dedicated real-time Ethernet solutions. Limitations include the current absence of a fault simulation capability for the TSN link itself. Full journal submission is planned after completing automotive protocol conformance tests.

SYN-PUB-04457.title: Exploiting Temporal Correlation in Multi-Sensor Nodes: Joint Source Coding Without Inter-Sensor Communication
SYN-PUB-04457.text:
Exploiting Temporal Correlation in Multi-Sensor Nodes: Joint Source Coding Without Inter-Sensor Communication (2026, journal, Signal Processing).
Authors: Nikola Bezbradica (outside co-author); Olivera Sredojević (R0363); Jovana Stević (outside co-author); Péter Vásárhelyi (outside co-author); Slobodan Knežević (R1030); Branislav Stojanović (R0641).
Keywords: joint source coding; multi-sensor; shared codebook; air quality; temporal correlation; Cortex-M0+.
When multiple sensors share a single microcontroller, their streams are often temporally correlated, but joint source coding typically requires a coordination step. This paper proposes a correlation-exploiting compressor that operates independently on each stream yet achieves joint compression gains by using a shared codebook trained offline on historical multi-sensor data. The codebook is partitioned by predicted correlation class, selected at runtime via a three-feature lightweight classifier running in 80 bytes of RAM. We evaluate the scheme on a 6-sensor indoor air-quality dataset (PM2.5, CO2, VOC, temperature, humidity, pressure) collected over 12 weeks in three office buildings in Novi Sad, totalling 41 million samples. Compared to independently trained per-sensor codebooks, the shared-codebook scheme reduces average bit rate by 17% at equal distortion. Codebook size is 6.8 kB, fitting in the flash of a Cortex-M0+. The classifier overhead is 12 cycles per sample. The paper analyses sensitivity to training-deployment distributional shift across seasons.

SYN-PUB-04527.title: Designing behaviour change messages for older adults: font size, colour contrast and comprehension of cardiovascular risk information
SYN-PUB-04527.text:
Designing behaviour change messages for older adults: font size, colour contrast and comprehension of cardiovascular risk information (2019, journal, Gerontological Communication and Health).
Authors: Branislava Lekić (R0413); Ognjen Ninkov (R0386); Teodora Krstić (R0369); Dragan Milosavljević (outside co-author); Biljana Đuričić (outside co-author); Ildikó Farkas (outside co-author).
Keywords: older adults; health literacy; readability; cardiovascular risk; eye-tracking.
Health information materials for older adults often fail to account for age-related perceptual and cognitive changes. This study assessed how systematic variation in font size (12 pt vs. 16 pt) and colour contrast ratio (4.5:1 vs. 7:1, per WCAG 2.1 AA and AAA standards) affected comprehension of a cardiovascular risk leaflet among adults aged 60–80 (N = 96, recruited from a Novi Sad community health centre). Comprehension was measured with a 10-item recall and inference test administered immediately after reading. Eye-tracking (Tobii TX300) recorded fixation duration and re-reading behaviour. Participants reading 16 pt text with 7:1 contrast achieved significantly higher comprehension scores (M = 7.8/10) than those reading 12 pt/4.5:1 text (M = 5.9/10; p < .001, d = 0.88). Re-reading rates were 34% lower in the high-legibility condition. These data provide a concrete evidence base for formatting standards in Serbian primary prevention materials targeting older adults.

SYN-PUB-04685.title: Prior Knowledge Heterogeneity and Learning Rate Differences Among New Factory Employees: A Longitudinal Field Study
SYN-PUB-04685.text:
Prior Knowledge Heterogeneity and Learning Rate Differences Among New Factory Employees: A Longitudinal Field Study (2013, journal, Journal of Occupational and Organisational Research).
Authors: Ognjen Ninkov (R0386); Tatjana Vuković (outside co-author); Miroslav Đorđević (outside co-author).
Keywords: prior knowledge; learning curves; onboarding; cognitive load; manufacturing.
This study examined how variability in prior domain knowledge affects the rate at which newly hired workers reach acceptable performance standards in a medium-sized manufacturing firm in Vojvodina. Forty-one employees hired over a six-month period completed a structured knowledge pre-assessment on their first day and were then tracked via weekly supervisor ratings and error-log records for sixteen weeks. Hierarchical linear modelling revealed that employees in the lowest quartile of prior knowledge took on average 9.3 weeks longer to reach the target performance threshold compared with the highest quartile, after controlling for educational attainment and job complexity. Notably, the relationship was non-linear: mid-range prior knowledge scores predicted steeper early learning curves than either extreme. Implications for adaptive onboarding sequencing are discussed, with reference to element interactivity as defined in cognitive load theory. The findings suggest that uniform onboarding programmes systematically under-serve both very experienced and very inexperienced new hires.

SYN-PUB-04686.title: Intrinsic and Extraneous Load in Paper-Based Versus Digital Onboarding Manuals: An Experimental Comparison
SYN-PUB-04686.text:
Intrinsic and Extraneous Load in Paper-Based Versus Digital Onboarding Manuals: An Experimental Comparison (2015, journal, Applied Ergonomics and Training Research).
Authors: Ognjen Ninkov (R0386); Jelena Savić (outside co-author).
Keywords: cognitive load; extraneous load; digital manuals; recall; instructional design.
Using a between-subjects design with 84 undergraduate volunteers acting as novice learners, this experiment compared cognitive load and immediate recall when training materials were presented in a conventional printed manual format versus a structured digital document with embedded hyperlinks and short video clips. Participants studied a realistic but fictional set of workplace procedures adapted from an administrative job description. Cognitive load was measured using a validated nine-item subjective rating scale administered immediately after the learning phase, and retention was assessed through a twenty-item cued-recall test thirty minutes later. The digital format produced significantly higher extraneous load ratings (M = 4.8 vs. 3.6 on a seven-point scale, p < .01) and marginally lower recall scores, an effect that was fully mediated by extraneous load. Split-attention effects in the digital condition, arising from simultaneous navigation demands, are proposed as the primary mechanism. Practical guidance for digital manual design is outlined.

SYN-PUB-04687.title: Situated Learning in a Bank Branch: How Peripheral Participation Shapes Procedural Knowledge Acquisition
SYN-PUB-04687.text:
Situated Learning in a Bank Branch: How Peripheral Participation Shapes Procedural Knowledge Acquisition (2017, journal, Work, Learning and Organisation: An International Journal).
Authors: Nataša Petrović (outside co-author); Bojan Ilić (outside co-author); Ognjen Ninkov (R0386); Claudia Merz (outside co-author).
Keywords: situated learning; community of practice; bank; procedural knowledge; informal learning.
This qualitative and quantitative mixed-methods study tracked eight newly hired customer service representatives at a regional bank over their first twelve weeks of employment. Using a combination of structured observation, semi-structured interviews at weeks two, six, and twelve, and a procedural knowledge test, the study examined how informal participation in routine branch activities contributed to competency development beyond that attributable to formal training sessions. Thematic analysis of interview transcripts identified five recurring situated learning mechanisms: observation of senior colleagues, informal question-answer exchanges, error correction in real transactions, gradual task responsibility expansion, and narrative sharing of past client cases. Regression analysis showed that self-reported frequency of informal learning activities at week six predicted procedural knowledge test scores at week twelve (β = 0.41, p = .008), above and beyond formal training hours. Results are discussed in relation to Lave and Wenger's community-of-practice model and its applicability to structured corporate onboarding design.

SYN-PUB-04688.title: Measuring Onboarding Programme Quality: Development and Initial Validation of the Structured Onboarding Assessment Inventory (SOAI)
SYN-PUB-04688.text:
Measuring Onboarding Programme Quality: Development and Initial Validation of the Structured Onboarding Assessment Inventory (SOAI) (2019, journal, Psihološka Istraživanja).
Authors: Ognjen Ninkov (R0386); Tatjana Vuković (outside co-author); Gordana Rakić (outside co-author).
Keywords: scale development; onboarding assessment; validation; HR; factor analysis.
This paper describes the construction and initial psychometric validation of the Structured Onboarding Assessment Inventory, a 32-item self-report instrument designed for use by HR practitioners and researchers to evaluate the quality of formal employee onboarding programmes across four dimensions: informational completeness, social integration support, role clarity facilitation, and workload pacing. Items were generated through a systematic review of existing onboarding literature and expert interviews with twelve HR managers from companies in Serbia and Croatia. An initial item pool of 61 items was administered to 267 employees from nine organisations who had been hired within the preceding six months. Exploratory factor analysis supported the four-factor structure, explaining 54% of total variance. Internal consistency was acceptable to good across subscales (Cronbach's α = .72–.84). Convergent validity was demonstrated through significant correlations with time-to-competency supervisor ratings. The instrument is made available in Serbian and English translations.

SYN-PUB-04689.title: Worked Examples Versus Problem-Solving Practice in IT Helpdesk Training: A Randomised Field Experiment
SYN-PUB-04689.text:
Worked Examples Versus Problem-Solving Practice in IT Helpdesk Training: A Randomised Field Experiment (2022, journal, Journal of Vocational Training and Workplace Learning).
Authors: Ognjen Ninkov (R0386); Jelena Savić (outside co-author); Aleksandar Tomić (outside co-author); Renata Szabo (outside co-author).
Keywords: worked examples; expertise reversal; IT training; randomised experiment; helpdesk.
Fifty-three newly hired IT helpdesk agents at a software services company in Novi Sad were randomly assigned to one of three training conditions during their second week of employment: (a) worked-example sequences for all twelve procedural modules, (b) problem-solving practice with minimal guidance, or (c) a faded worked-example schedule transitioning to independent problem-solving. Outcome measures were ticket resolution speed, first-contact resolution rate, and supervisor-rated quality at four and eight weeks post-training. At week four, the faded condition outperformed both alternatives on resolution speed (M = 7.1 min per ticket vs. 9.4 and 8.8) and supervisor quality ratings. By week eight, differences in resolution speed had attenuated, but first-contact resolution rate remained higher in the faded condition (74% vs. 61% and 65%). The results support the expertise reversal effect and suggest that static training designs which do not adapt to growing learner competence are suboptimal even over short time horizons.

SYN-PUB-04690.title: Remote Onboarding During Organisational Disruption: Knowledge Gaps and Social Integration Deficits Compared with In-Person Cohorts
SYN-PUB-04690.text:
Remote Onboarding During Organisational Disruption: Knowledge Gaps and Social Integration Deficits Compared with In-Person Cohorts (2023, journal, European Journal of Work and Organisational Psychology).
Authors: Ognjen Ninkov (R0386); Nataša Petrović (outside co-author); Ivana Lukić (outside co-author); Claudia Merz (outside co-author).
Keywords: remote onboarding; social integration; role clarity; hybrid work; tacit knowledge.
This retrospective comparative study examined outcomes for 112 employees onboarded entirely remotely during a period of organisational disruption against a matched group of 98 employees who had undergone standard in-person onboarding at the same set of six companies in Vojvodina and the Belgrade area in the preceding two years. Matching criteria included job family, seniority level, and educational background. Structured interviews at six months post-hire and archival records of supervisor performance ratings were used as outcome measures. Remote cohorts showed significantly lower scores on role clarity (d = 0.54) and social integration (d = 0.71) but comparable declarative knowledge test scores (d = 0.12, ns). Qualitative data indicated that remote new hires consistently reported difficulty identifying informal knowledge sources and experienced fewer spontaneous mentoring interactions. Practical recommendations for hybrid onboarding designs that preserve social and tacit knowledge transmission are presented.

SYN-PUB-04691.title: Microlearning Bursts Versus Massed Training Sessions for Procedural Skill Retention: A Six-Month Follow-Up
SYN-PUB-04691.text:
Microlearning Bursts Versus Massed Training Sessions for Procedural Skill Retention: A Six-Month Follow-Up (2025, journal, Learning and Instruction in Organisations).
Authors: Ognjen Ninkov (R0386); Miloš Stanković (outside co-author); Eva Horváth (outside co-author); Dragomir Vranješ (outside co-author).
Keywords: microlearning; spacing effect; retention; procedural skill; logistics.
This study compared two delivery formats for a standardised procedural training curriculum used in the logistics sector: a conventional massed format delivering four full training days in week one, and a microlearning format distributing the same content across twelve brief daily modules (15–25 minutes each) over three weeks, with two follow-up refresher modules at weeks six and twelve. Participants were 46 newly hired warehouse operations coordinators across two depots of the same logistics company in Serbia. Procedural skill was assessed using a standardised performance checklist at one month, three months, and six months post-training. At the six-month assessment, the microlearning group retained significantly more procedural steps correctly (M = 87% vs. 71%, t(44) = 3.21, p = .003) and committed fewer sequencing errors. Working memory load ratings during the training period, collected via daily brief surveys, were lower in the microlearning condition throughout. Results are interpreted in terms of spacing effects and germane load accumulation.

SYN-PUB-05246.title: Interference Graph Colouring Under Heterogeneous Register-File Constraints for Sparse Tensor Cores
SYN-PUB-05246.text:
Interference Graph Colouring Under Heterogeneous Register-File Constraints for Sparse Tensor Cores (2022, journal, Journal of Compiler Technology and Embedded Systems).
Authors: Luka Knežević (R0802); Valentina Bulatović (R0437); Anja Tešić (R0625); Katarina Lukić (outside co-author); Miroslav Đorđević (outside co-author).
Keywords: register allocation; graph colouring; heterogeneous register file; tensor core; Chaitin–Briggs.
Tensor accelerators often expose multiple register files with different widths and access latencies, one set for dense accumulators and another for sparse index buffers. Classical graph-colouring register allocation assumes a uniform register file, and adapting it to heterogeneous files requires modifications to both the interference graph construction and the colouring heuristic. This paper presents a two-phase allocation algorithm: the first phase colours accumulator-class values using a Chaitin–Briggs-style approach on a subgraph restricted to accumulator registers; the second phase handles index-class values using a bipartite matching formulation. Tested on a cycle-accurate model of a custom tensor core with 48 accumulator registers and 64 index registers, the algorithm reduces register-file conflict stalls by 34% compared with a single-phase allocator that treats all registers uniformly. Compilation overhead is below 5% in all tested kernels.

SYN-PUB-05483.title: Reinforcement Learning for Adaptive Scanning Strategy Selection
SYN-PUB-05483.text:
Reinforcement Learning for Adaptive Scanning Strategy Selection (2019, journal, Journal of Autonomous Agents and Multi-Agent Systems in Security).
Authors: Bence Tóth (outside co-author); Miroslav Krstić (outside co-author); Árpád Nagy (R0564); Predrag Ljubojević (R0460).
Keywords: reinforcement learning; scanning strategy; Q-learning; intrusion detection evasion; autonomous agents.
Automated reconnaissance systems often rely on fixed scanning strategies that are suboptimal in environments where detection risk varies by subnet or time of day. This paper frames scanning strategy selection as a Markov decision process in which an agent observes partial information about target responsiveness and detection thresholds and selects among six predefined scan intensities. A Q-learning agent is trained in simulation using a parameterised network model and then evaluated on an emulated testbed of 120 hosts with an intrusion detection system configured to log and block excessive probe rates. The trained agent reduces IDS-triggered alerts by 58% compared to a fixed-intensity baseline while achieving 91% of the baseline's host-discovery coverage within the same time window. Ablation experiments confirm that the reward function weighting of coverage versus stealth has a strong effect on the coverage-alert trade-off.

SYN-PUB-05923.title: Towards a Standardised Benchmarking Suite for Post-Quantum Cryptography on Embedded Targets
SYN-PUB-05923.text:
Towards a Standardised Benchmarking Suite for Post-Quantum Cryptography on Embedded Targets (2023, journal, ACM Transactions on Embedded Computing Systems).
Authors: Nikola Đorđević (outside co-author); Thibault Marin (outside co-author); Branislav Stojanović (R0641); Bogdan Petrescu (outside co-author); Milica Nikolić (R0503).
Keywords: benchmarking suite; post-quantum cryptography; embedded targets; reproducibility; methodology.
Comparing published implementation results for post-quantum schemes is difficult because researchers use different clock frequencies, compiler flags, measurement methods, and reporting conventions. This paper proposes a minimal benchmarking suite—PQBench-Embed—that specifies four representative hardware targets (ARM Cortex-M0+, Cortex-M4, RISC-V RV32IMC, and ESP32), a fixed GCC toolchain version and flag set, a cycle-counting harness based on hardware performance counters, and a structured JSON output format for result reporting. We validate the suite by collecting results for Kyber-512, Dilithium-2, Falcon-512, SPHINCS+-SHA2-128s, and Classic McEliece 348864 across all four targets. Results show that cross-architecture speedup ratios for the same algorithm vary by up to 3.1x depending on benchmarking methodology, confirming the need for standardisation. The suite and all collected data are released as a public repository. We also provide a discussion of what metrics matter most for different deployment scenarios such as TLS handshake, firmware signing, and device attestation.

SYN-PUB-05926.title: Traceability Between Requirements and ARXML Artefacts in AUTOSAR Development
SYN-PUB-05926.text:
Traceability Between Requirements and ARXML Artefacts in AUTOSAR Development (2021, journal, Journal of Embedded and Automotive Software Systems).
Authors: Milena Stanković (outside co-author); Mirjana Vidaković (R0948); Zorica Rakić (R1045); Milica Nikolić (R0503); Szilárd Farkas (outside co-author); Nikola Sremčević (outside co-author).
Keywords: traceability; ReqIF; ISO 26262; ARXML; impact analysis.
Establishing traceable links between functional requirements and AUTOSAR model artefacts is required by ISO 26262 for software at ASIL B and above, yet toolchain support for this is fragmented. This paper reports on a traceability framework, TraceAR, that stores bidirectional links between requirement identifiers in a ReqIF document and elements in one or more ARXML files, using a trace metamodel serialised as a lightweight XML sidecar. The framework was implemented as an Eclipse plug-in with a matrix view and impact analysis function. It was evaluated in a 12-week study with four engineers working on a powertrain control ECU with 284 functional requirements and a corresponding AUTOSAR model containing 1 140 traceable elements. Coverage analysis showed 91% of requirements linked after the study period; initial linkage completeness before tool adoption had been estimated at 47% based on project documentation. Engineers rated the impact analysis function as the most practically valuable feature in post-study interviews.

SYN-PUB-05929.title: Loop Nest Optimisation for Sparse Tensor Contractions on an Out-of-Order Accelerator with Prefetch Buffers
SYN-PUB-05929.text:
Loop Nest Optimisation for Sparse Tensor Contractions on an Out-of-Order Accelerator with Prefetch Buffers (2026, journal, ACM Transactions on Architecture and Compilation Techniques — Regional Edition).
Authors: Tobias Wehrle (outside co-author); Nemanja Simić (outside co-author); Luka Knežević (R0802); Ana Đukić (outside co-author); Milica Nikolić (R0503).
Keywords: loop tiling; sparse tensor contraction; prefetch; out-of-order execution; loop optimisation.
Sparse tensor contractions involve loop nests whose iteration spaces are implicitly defined by the sparsity pattern of one or more operands. Standard loop transformations such as tiling and interchange assume dense rectangular iteration spaces and do not directly apply. This paper reformulates loop tiling for sparse iteration spaces by treating the compressed index arrays as first-class objects during the transformation and deriving tile boundaries from statistical properties of the non-zero structure. Prefetch buffer allocation is handled by a separate pass that inserts prefetch instructions at tile entry points, guided by a cost model calibrated on the target accelerator. Experiments on an RTL-level simulation of a six-stage out-of-order accelerator show 19–27% reduction in stall cycles for eight tensor contraction benchmarks from quantum chemistry. The paper reports sensitivity to tile size and discusses interaction with register allocation.

SYN-PUB-06542.title: Automated Topology Discovery in Heterogeneous Enterprise Networks Using Passive and Active Probing
SYN-PUB-06542.text:
Automated Topology Discovery in Heterogeneous Enterprise Networks Using Passive and Active Probing (2010, journal, Journal of Network and Systems Engineering).
Authors: Miroslav Krstić (outside co-author); Tamás Varga (outside co-author); Árpád Nagy (R0564).
Keywords: topology discovery; passive probing; agent-based; network mapping; ARP.
This paper presents a hybrid reconnaissance framework that combines passive traffic observation with selective active probing to reconstruct network topology maps in heterogeneous enterprise environments. The system operates as a coordinated set of lightweight agents deployed at strategic vantage points; each agent collects ARP tables, SNMP MIB data, and sampled NetFlow records, which are then fused by a central correlator. Experiments were conducted on an emulated testbed comprising 240 virtual nodes distributed across six subnets with mixed operating systems. The resulting topology graphs achieved 94.3% node-coverage accuracy and 91.7% edge-accuracy compared to ground-truth configurations, while generating less than 1.2% overhead traffic. The approach outperformed three existing tools—Nessus-based scanning, a commercial agent suite, and a passive-only baseline—on both accuracy and stealth metrics. The paper also introduces a confidence-scoring mechanism that flags uncertain link inferences for manual review.

SYN-PUB-06543.title: Graph-Based Representation of Reachability Conditions for Vulnerability Chaining
SYN-PUB-06543.text:
Graph-Based Representation of Reachability Conditions for Vulnerability Chaining (2012, conference, Proceedings of the Central European Conference on Information Security).
Authors: Dragana Petrov (outside co-author); Zoltán Fehér (outside co-author); Árpád Nagy (R0564).
Keywords: attack graph; vulnerability chaining; reachability; CVE; penetration testing.
Combining vulnerability data with network reachability constraints allows analysts to reason about multi-step attack sequences that no single vulnerability would enable alone. This work formalises attack surfaces as directed multigraphs in which nodes represent hosts annotated with CVE entries and edges encode reachability relations derived from firewall rule sets and routing tables. A path-enumeration algorithm based on a modified Dijkstra variant is applied to identify exploit chains of length two through five within graphs of up to 1,800 nodes. The method was validated against twenty synthetic network configurations whose ground-truth attack paths were independently constructed by certified penetration testers. The algorithm recovered 87% of critical paths and produced no false-positive critical chains. Computational experiments show that graph construction and path enumeration complete in under 40 seconds for networks of 1,000 hosts on commodity hardware, making the approach feasible for periodic re-assessment cycles.

SYN-PUB-06544.title: Service Fingerprinting Under Protocol Obfuscation: A Probabilistic Approach
SYN-PUB-06544.text:
Service Fingerprinting Under Protocol Obfuscation: A Probabilistic Approach (2015, conference, Proceedings of the Symposium on Applied Network Analysis and Security).
Authors: Andreja Ilić (outside co-author); Árpád Nagy (R0564); Petra Novak (outside co-author).
Keywords: service fingerprinting; protocol identification; Naive Bayes; traffic analysis; reconnaissance.
Identifying services running on non-standard ports is a recurring challenge in automated reconnaissance when administrators deliberately obfuscate protocols. This paper describes a fingerprinting system that analyses packet-level behavioural features—inter-arrival times, payload-length distributions, and handshake sequencing—using a Naive Bayes classifier trained on 14 protocol classes captured from a controlled lab environment. The training corpus contained 120,000 labelled flows; the test corpus used 18,000 flows including five deliberately obfuscated configurations. Overall classification accuracy reached 88.4%, dropping to 79.1% on obfuscated flows alone. Error analysis identifies TLS-over-non-443 and custom binary protocols as the principal failure cases. The paper also quantifies the sensitivity of recognition rates to traffic volume, showing that reliable classification requires at least 30 payload-bearing packets per flow for the most ambiguous protocol pairs.

SYN-PUB-06545.title: Attack Surface Modelling for Industrial Control Networks: Differences from Enterprise IT
SYN-PUB-06545.text:
Attack Surface Modelling for Industrial Control Networks: Differences from Enterprise IT (2016, book chapter, Security of Cyber-Physical Systems: Methods and Practice (Springer series on Industrial Control Security, vol. 3)).
Authors: Borivoj Stanković (outside co-author); Klaus Hoffmann (outside co-author); Árpád Nagy (R0564).
Keywords: ICS security; SCADA; attack surface; operational technology; exploit path.
Industrial control networks differ from enterprise IT environments in their protocol diversity, deterministic traffic patterns, and tolerance for scanning-induced disruption. This book chapter surveys the adaptations required to apply attack-surface modelling methods—originally designed for IT networks—to operational technology environments including SCADA systems and distributed control systems. The chapter reviews fifteen published frameworks and categorises their assumptions about scanning intrusiveness, asset-discovery completeness, and protocol coverage. A taxonomy of ICS-specific attack-surface components is proposed, covering PLCs, historians, engineering workstations, and field-bus gateways. The chapter concludes with a case study of a simulated water-treatment network of 62 nodes in which a graph-based model identified seven latent exploit paths that a conventional IT-oriented scan missed entirely due to proprietary protocol constraints.

SYN-PUB-06546.title: Incremental Attack Graph Updates After Network Configuration Changes
SYN-PUB-06546.text:
Incremental Attack Graph Updates After Network Configuration Changes (2017, journal, Journal of Computer Security and Privacy).
Authors: Dragana Petrov (outside co-author); Orsolya Molnár (outside co-author); Árpád Nagy (R0564).
Keywords: attack graph; incremental update; configuration management; graph algorithms; network security.
Maintaining an up-to-date attack graph after routine configuration changes—such as firewall rule edits, patch deployments, or device additions—without rebuilding the entire graph from scratch is an open efficiency problem. This paper introduces an incremental update algorithm that identifies the subgraph affected by a declared configuration delta and re-evaluates only the relevant node and edge attributes. The algorithm is evaluated on a synthetic benchmark of 500 graphs with between 200 and 2,000 nodes, with configuration deltas of varying size. For deltas affecting fewer than 5% of nodes, incremental update reduces computation time by an average of 74% compared to full recomputation, with identical output. For larger deltas the advantage diminishes, and a threshold heuristic is derived to select between strategies. A plug-in implementation for an existing open-source attack graph tool is released alongside the paper.

SYN-PUB-06548.title: Mapping IPv6 Attack Surfaces: Challenges for Existing Agent-Based Scanners
SYN-PUB-06548.text:
Mapping IPv6 Attack Surfaces: Challenges for Existing Agent-Based Scanners (2020, journal, Journal of Network and Systems Engineering).
Authors: Andreja Ilić (outside co-author); Borivoj Stanković (outside co-author); Árpád Nagy (R0564).
Keywords: IPv6; host discovery; NDP; agent-based scanning; attack surface.
IPv6's vastly larger address space makes exhaustive address-space scanning computationally infeasible, requiring fundamentally different approaches to host discovery than those used in IPv4 environments. This paper systematically evaluates six agent-based scanning architectures against dual-stack and IPv6-only testbeds of 150 hosts and analyses their host-discovery rates, false-positive counts, and scan durations. Results show that methods relying on direct address-range sweeping achieve under 12% discovery on pure IPv6 segments compared to 97% on equivalent IPv4 segments. Neighbour Discovery Protocol exploitation, DNS reverse-zone enumeration, and passive traffic observation are assessed as alternatives, with the DNS-based method achieving 78% discovery on correctly configured networks. The paper derives a prioritised pipeline combining these sources and demonstrates its integration into an existing multi-agent scanning framework, raising combined discovery to 89%.

SYN-PUB-06549.title: Measuring Scan Footprint Detectability Across IDS Rule Sets
SYN-PUB-06549.text:
Measuring Scan Footprint Detectability Across IDS Rule Sets (2022, journal, Journal of Computer Security and Privacy).
Authors: Sonja Herak (outside co-author); Tomáš Blaho (outside co-author); Nikola Vujović (outside co-author); Árpád Nagy (R0564).
Keywords: IDS evasion; scan detectability; Suricata; penetration testing; alert reduction.
The extent to which a given scanning configuration is detectable depends on both the scan parameters and the rule set loaded into the intrusion detection system it faces. This paper introduces a detectability metric derived from the fraction of IDS rules that would fire for a given scan packet sequence, weighted by rule confidence scores. The metric is computed for 48 scanning configurations—varying probe rate, packet size, and port selection order—against three representative Suricata rule sets of different strictness levels. Experiments on a physical testbed of 60 hosts confirm a Spearman correlation of 0.81 between the metric and measured alert counts. The paper then uses the metric to guide a greedy optimiser that selects scan parameters minimising detectability for a target coverage level, achieving a 44% alert reduction against the strictest rule set relative to default scan settings.

SYN-PUB-06550.title: Temporal Dynamics of Attack Graphs: Modelling Vulnerability Disclosure and Patch Lag
SYN-PUB-06550.text:
Temporal Dynamics of Attack Graphs: Modelling Vulnerability Disclosure and Patch Lag (2024, journal, Journal of Computer Security and Privacy).
Authors: Orsolya Molnár (outside co-author); Nikola Vujović (outside co-author); Árpád Nagy (R0564).
Keywords: temporal attack graph; patch lag; CVE lifecycle; vulnerability disclosure; network security.
Attack graphs are typically computed as static snapshots, but the real vulnerability state of a network changes continuously as new CVEs are disclosed and patches are applied at varying rates across different asset classes. This paper introduces a temporal attack graph model in which vulnerability nodes carry activation and deactivation timestamps derived from NVD disclosure dates and patch deployment logs collected from a university IT infrastructure over a 36-month observation window. The dataset covers 214 unique hosts and 1,102 distinct CVE occurrences. Analysis of the resulting temporal sequence of graphs shows that the median window of exploitability for a newly disclosed critical vulnerability on an unpatched host is 23 days. The model is used to retrospectively identify four periods during which critical exploit paths existed that would not have appeared in any single static snapshot, underscoring the limitations of periodic scanning alone.

SYN-PUB-06551.title: LLM-Assisted Interpretation of Raw Scan Output for Structured Vulnerability Reports
SYN-PUB-06551.text:
LLM-Assisted Interpretation of Raw Scan Output for Structured Vulnerability Reports (2025, conference, Proceedings of the Central European Conference on Information Security).
Authors: Sonja Herak (outside co-author); René Dubois (outside co-author); Árpád Nagy (R0564).
Keywords: large language models; vulnerability reports; scan output parsing; information extraction; LLM evaluation.
Raw output from port scanners and vulnerability scanners is verbose, inconsistently formatted, and requires analyst effort to consolidate into structured reports. This paper evaluates the use of a locally hosted large language model (7-billion-parameter instruction-tuned variant) to parse and summarise raw scanner output into a fixed JSON schema covering host identity, open services, associated CVEs, and suggested remediation priorities. A corpus of 320 real scan outputs collected from an emulated testbed was used for evaluation; ground-truth structured records were produced by three independent human analysts. The LLM achieved field-level extraction precision of 91.3% and recall of 88.7%, with the lowest scores on free-text remediation fields. The paper also reports an error taxonomy: the most common failure mode is hallucination of CVE identifiers not present in the source text, accounting for 61% of all extraction errors. Processing latency averaged 4.1 seconds per report on a single consumer GPU.

SYN-PUB-06586.title: Comparative Evaluation of Lifetime Estimation Methods for Primary Lithium Cells in Static IoT Sensors
SYN-PUB-06586.text:
Comparative Evaluation of Lifetime Estimation Methods for Primary Lithium Cells in Static IoT Sensors (2023, journal, Sensors and Embedded Intelligence).
Authors: Luka Marjanović (outside co-author); Vuk Bačić (R0826); Zorica Jovanović (R0567); Tomáš Blaha (outside co-author); Milena Filipović (outside co-author).
Keywords: lifetime estimation; Gaussian process regression; Peukert; benchmark; IoT sensors.
Four lifetime estimation methods are benchmarked against each other using a common dataset of 60 Li/MnO₂ and 60 Li/SOCl₂ cells discharged under eight realistic IoT sensor profiles. The methods compared are: (i) Peukert-based capacity scaling, (ii) a lookup-table approach derived from manufacturer pulse-discharge curves, (iii) a two-RC equivalent-circuit model updated by EIS, and (iv) a Gaussian process regression model trained on early-discharge features. All methods are evaluated on prediction error at 80 % and 100 % cell depletion. The Gaussian process method achieves the lowest median absolute error (6.2 % at end-of-life) but requires 11 input features extracted during the first 5 % of discharge. The EIS-based model achieves 8.7 % median error with fewer inputs. The Peukert method is least accurate at 22 % median error. A decision flowchart is provided to help practitioners choose a method based on available hardware and tolerable error. All data and model code are published under a CC-BY licence.

SYN-PUB-06832.title: A Benchmark Suite for Multi-UAV Coverage Planning With Geofence and Energy Constraints
SYN-PUB-06832.text:
A Benchmark Suite for Multi-UAV Coverage Planning With Geofence and Energy Constraints (2026, journal, Robotics and Autonomous Systems).
Authors: Nenad Dimitrijević (R0592); Đorđe Latinović (outside co-author); Stefan Lukić (outside co-author); Péter Vásárhelyi (outside co-author); Lukas Gruber (outside co-author); Veljko Pantelić (R0995); Emilija Vranješ (R0749).
Keywords: benchmark; multi-UAV; coverage planning; open dataset; Vojvodina; evaluation harness.
Reproducible evaluation of multi-UAV coverage planners is hampered by the absence of standardised benchmark instances. This paper introduces a benchmark suite of 120 instances derived from publicly available land-use and airspace data for the Autonomous Province of Vojvodina. Instances are parameterised by area size (0.5–20 km²), fleet size (1–8 UAVs), number of no-fly zones (0–10), geofence complexity, and battery capacity class. For each instance, optimal or best-known solution values are provided via exhaustive search (small instances) or a portfolio of state-of-the-art solvers run for 24 CPU hours (large instances). Baseline results from six existing planners drawn from the literature are reported. The suite is released as an open dataset alongside a Python evaluation harness. Preliminary results indicate that no single planner dominates across all instance classes, motivating algorithm selection or portfolio approaches. The benchmark is intended to facilitate fair cross-paper comparisons.

SYN-PUB-06834.title: Consistency Checking Between ARXML System Descriptions and Deployment Configurations
SYN-PUB-06834.text:
Consistency Checking Between ARXML System Descriptions and Deployment Configurations (2013, conference, Softversko Inženjerstvo i Primenjene Tehnologije (SIPAT)).
Authors: Borislav Đorđević (outside co-author); Nenad Dimitrijević (R0592); Luka Knežević (R0802); Nikola Sremčević (outside co-author); Mirjana Vidaković (R0948).
Keywords: ARXML; OCL constraints; consistency checking; AUTOSAR deployment; Eclipse plug-in.
AUTOSAR system descriptions and their corresponding deployment configurations are maintained as separate ARXML files and can diverge during iterative development. This paper describes a rule-based consistency checker implemented as an Eclipse plug-in that operates on a merged in-memory model assembled from multiple ARXML artefacts. Forty-three consistency rules derived from the AUTOSAR 4.1 specification were encoded as OCL constraints. The checker was applied to six industrial-style test configurations provided by a regional automotive supplier, ranging from 12 to 78 ECUs per configuration. It detected an average of 8.4 rule violations per configuration that were not flagged by the supplier's existing tooling, most relating to signal mapping mismatches and unresolved component prototype references. False positive rate was 2.1% after a calibration phase involving two domain experts. The tool reduced manual configuration review time by approximately 40% in a two-week pilot.

SYN-PUB-07201.title: Thermal gradient mapping inside refrigerated road trailers using a 16-node wireless mesh
SYN-PUB-07201.text:
Thermal gradient mapping inside refrigerated road trailers using a 16-node wireless mesh (2012, conference, Proceedings of the 4th European Conference on Sensor Networks in Transport and Logistics).
Authors: Miroslav Pejić (outside co-author); Tomáš Blaho (outside co-author); Žarko Jakovljević (R0754); Dragana Tomić (outside co-author); Žarko Ivanović (R0630); Ivan Zec (R0903).
Keywords: refrigerated trailer; spatial temperature mapping; ZigBee mesh; ATP regulations; cold chain.
Spatial temperature heterogeneity inside refrigerated semi-trailers was characterised using a 16-node ZigBee mesh network mounted at three heights and four longitudinal positions. Measurements were conducted over 22 journeys between Novi Sad and Vienna covering a total of 14,300 km under summer and winter conditions. Nodes sampled at 1-minute intervals, producing approximately 1.1 million temperature records. Analysis identified a persistent warm zone near the rear doors, averaging 2.1 °C above the set-point of +4 °C during door-open events lasting more than 90 seconds. A principal component decomposition of the spatial profiles revealed that the first two components explain 81% of within-trailer variance. These findings were used to propose three alternative sensor placement strategies that reduce the probability of undetected warm zones by a factor of 2.4 compared to the single-probe standard practice currently mandated by ATP regulations.

SYN-PUB-07256.title: Adaptive EWMA Charts for Monitoring Autocorrelated Process Outputs: Simulation Study and Factory Trial
SYN-PUB-07256.text:
Adaptive EWMA Charts for Monitoring Autocorrelated Process Outputs: Simulation Study and Factory Trial (2017, journal, Quality and Reliability Engineering International).
Authors: Nataša Jovanović (outside co-author); Christoph Wenzel (outside co-author); Nevena Bogićević (R0636); Marija Ognjanov (R0817); Branislava Ostojić (R0773).
Keywords: EWMA; autocorrelation; adaptive smoothing; PLC; process monitoring.
Autocorrelation in process outputs is common when sampling is faster than the process time constant. Standard EWMA charts applied to autocorrelated data produce elevated false-alarm rates. This paper proposes an adaptive EWMA scheme in which the smoothing parameter λ is updated at each time step using a gradient-descent rule that minimises the one-step-ahead prediction error over a forgetting-factor-weighted window of past residuals. The scheme is compared with three baselines—fixed-λ EWMA on raw observations, fixed-λ EWMA on residuals from a fitted ARIMA model, and a T² chart on ARIMA residuals—across an AR(1) process with ρ ∈ {0.3, 0.6, 0.9} and mean shifts of 0.5 to 2.5σ. The adaptive scheme matched or exceeded ARIMA-residual EWMA in all tested conditions and was substantially easier to implement in a production PLC environment. A six-week trial on a bottling line confirmed an 11% reduction in false alarms.

SYN-PUB-07295.title: A Comparative Study of Delta Encoding Variants for Industrial Vibration Signals on ARM Cortex-M3
SYN-PUB-07295.text:
A Comparative Study of Delta Encoding Variants for Industrial Vibration Signals on ARM Cortex-M3 (2012, journal, Journal of Embedded and Real-Time Computing Systems).
Authors: Nenad Vuković (outside co-author); Aleksandra Petrović (outside co-author); Branislav Stojanović (R0641).
Keywords: delta encoding; vibration monitoring; Cortex-M3; Golomb-Rice coding; bearing fault.
Industrial vibration monitoring generates high-rate accelerometer data that must often be stored or transmitted by nodes with limited SRAM. We implemented five delta-encoding variants — first-order delta, second-order delta, delta with Golomb-Rice coding, delta with run-length extension, and an adaptive-threshold delta — on an STM32F103 microcontroller and tested them against a 48-hour dataset of bearing vibration signals sampled at 4 kHz from a conveyor drive unit. Each algorithm was profiled for compression ratio, signal-to-noise ratio of reconstructed waveforms, processing cycles per sample, and peak SRAM usage. Adaptive-threshold delta achieved the best compression ratio of 3.8:1 while retaining impact-event peaks within 2.1 dB SNR of the original. SRAM overhead across all variants ranged from 128 bytes to 640 bytes. Cycle counts varied from 6 to 41 per sample. The paper provides decision guidelines for selecting a variant based on spectral content and memory budget.

SYN-PUB-07296.title: Adaptive Nyquist-Rate Reduction Using Signal Variance Tracking for Low-Power Acoustic Sensors
SYN-PUB-07296.text:
Adaptive Nyquist-Rate Reduction Using Signal Variance Tracking for Low-Power Acoustic Sensors (2013, journal, IET Wireless Sensor Systems).
Authors: Bojana Milošević (outside co-author); Goran Peić (outside co-author); Branislav Stojanović (R0641).
Keywords: adaptive sampling; acoustic sensing; MSP430; energy harvesting; wildlife monitoring.
This work addresses the energy cost of continuous acoustic sensing in wildlife monitoring nodes powered by solar-harvesting supercapacitors. We propose a variance-tracking scheduler that estimates short-time variance in 20 ms windows and dynamically reduces the effective sampling rate from 16 kHz to as low as 2 kHz during low-activity periods, restoring full rate when variance exceeds a learned threshold. The threshold is updated via an exponential moving average with a decay constant tuned to avoid false rate reductions during transient silence. Experiments were conducted with a custom node based on an MSP430FR5969 microcontroller and a MEMS microphone deployed in a mixed forest environment for 14 days. Compared to continuous 16 kHz sampling, the adaptive scheme reduced flash write volume by 73% and cut average current draw from 4.1 mA to 1.4 mA, extending estimated node lifetime from 11 days to 31 days without missing a single detected bird call event. Spectral fidelity during active periods was indistinguishable from the full-rate baseline.

SYN-PUB-07297.title: Anomaly-Preserving Lossy Compression: Retaining Fault Signatures Under High Compression Ratios
SYN-PUB-07297.text:
Anomaly-Preserving Lossy Compression: Retaining Fault Signatures Under High Compression Ratios (2016, journal, IEEE Transactions on Industrial Informatics).
Authors: Miroslav Tanasić (outside co-author); Radovan Obradović (outside co-author); Branislav Stojanović (R0641).
Keywords: anomaly-preserving compression; CUSUM; DPCM; fault detection; industrial IoT; bit allocation.
Standard rate-distortion optimisation treats all signal samples equally, which can erase rare fault-indicative spikes at high compression ratios. This paper formalises the concept of anomaly-preserving compression (APC) for industrial sensor streams and proposes a two-stage pipeline: an online anomaly scorer based on a lightweight CUSUM detector flags candidate segments, and a segment-aware bit allocator assigns additional bits to flagged regions. The allocator operates within a fixed total bit budget so that overall compression ratio is unchanged. We tested APC on synthetic bearing-fault accelerometer traces (1000 trials per fault type) and on 60 hours of real motor current signals from a pump station. At a 12:1 target compression ratio, standard DPCM missed 31% of injected fault events, whereas APC missed 4.2% under identical bit constraints. The computational overhead of the anomaly scorer was 9 CPU cycles per sample on a Cortex-M4 at 168 MHz. The paper also provides an analytical bound relating CUSUM detection lag to false-anomaly rate.

SYN-PUB-07298.title: Fixed-Point FFT Optimisation for Spectral Feature Extraction on Cortex-M4 Without FPU
SYN-PUB-07298.text:
Fixed-Point FFT Optimisation for Spectral Feature Extraction on Cortex-M4 Without FPU (2017, conference, Proceedings of the Regional Conference on Signal Processing and Embedded Intelligence (RCSPEI), Belgrade).
Authors: Branislav Stojanović (R0641); Nikola Bezbradica (outside co-author).
Keywords: FFT; fixed-point arithmetic; Cortex-M4; tool wear; spectral features.
Many mid-range microcontrollers include an FPU-equipped Cortex-M4, yet FPU use in battery-constrained nodes is often disabled to save power. This paper details the design of a 256-point radix-2 Cooley-Tukey FFT using Q15 fixed-point arithmetic without FPU instructions. We compare three twiddle-factor storage strategies — full table, quarter-wave compression, and on-the-fly CORDIC — for their trade-offs between SRAM, ROM, and cycle count. Full-table FFT executes in 4,912 cycles at negligible numerical error (SNR 78 dB); CORDIC reduces ROM by 2 kB but costs 9,340 cycles. The implementation was used in a vibration-based tool-wear classifier where six spectral band energies serve as features. Classification accuracy on a 400-sample dataset of milling operations was 91.3% using a lookup-table nearest-centroid classifier consuming 1.2 kB RAM. Total feature extraction and classification latency was 0.31 ms, making real-time 1 kHz inference feasible.

SYN-PUB-07299.title: Lightweight Dictionary Coding for Repetitive Telemetry Payloads in LPWAN Networks
SYN-PUB-07299.text:
Lightweight Dictionary Coding for Repetitive Telemetry Payloads in LPWAN Networks (2018, journal, Sensors and Actuators: Physical and Cyber Systems).
Authors: Tatjana Kovačević (outside co-author); Péter Vásárhelyi (outside co-author); Dragana Lučić (outside co-author); Branislav Stojanović (R0641).
Keywords: dictionary coding; LZ78; LoRaWAN; agricultural IoT; soil sensing; LPWAN.
Low-power wide-area networks such as LoRaWAN impose strict payload size limits (typically 51 bytes in Europe at SF12) that force aggressive data reduction. Many agricultural IoT deployments generate highly repetitive soil-sensor payloads where values change slowly. We exploit this repetitiveness by implementing an LZ78-inspired dictionary coder with a bounded dictionary of 64 entries stored in 512 bytes of SRAM on an ATtiny3217. Across a 90-day deployment monitoring soil moisture, temperature, and electrical conductivity at four depths in a maize field, the coder achieved a mean payload reduction of 58% relative to raw quantised integers, enabling SF9 transmission and reducing time-on-air from 1.48 s to 0.62 s per burst. Monthly energy consumption fell by 34% compared to uncompressed transmission, extending estimated battery life from 14 months to 21 months. Decoding is performed server-side with negligible latency. The paper includes a simulation study covering payload entropy conditions where the scheme degrades gracefully to near-uncompressed size.

SYN-PUB-07300.title: On the Use of Haar Filterbanks for Compressive Aggregation in Wireless Sensor Trees
SYN-PUB-07300.text:
On the Use of Haar Filterbanks for Compressive Aggregation in Wireless Sensor Trees (2019, journal, Ad Hoc Networks).
Authors: Stefan Lukić (outside co-author); Marco Bertolini (outside co-author); Aleksandra Petrović (outside co-author); Branislav Stojanović (R0641).
Keywords: Haar filterbank; in-network compression; wireless sensor network; energy optimisation; tree topology.
(no abstract)

SYN-PUB-07301.title: Resource Budget Modelling for Co-located Compression and Inference Tasks on RISC-V MCUs
SYN-PUB-07301.text:
Resource Budget Modelling for Co-located Compression and Inference Tasks on RISC-V MCUs (2021, journal, Journal of Systems Architecture).
Authors: Miroslav Tanasić (outside co-author); Lukas Hofer (outside co-author); Nikola Bezbradica (outside co-author); Branislav Stojanović (R0641).
Keywords: RISC-V; resource budget; co-located inference; compression; Pareto frontier; air quality.
When a sensor node must run both a data compressor and a machine-learning inference engine simultaneously, their memory and compute demands interact in non-obvious ways. This paper proposes a static resource budget model that takes as inputs the compressor's working-set size, the inference model's layer dimensions, and the microcontroller's SRAM/flash/cycle budget, and outputs a Pareto frontier of achievable compression ratio versus inference accuracy trade-offs. We instantiate the model for four compressor types (DPCM, PLA, Haar, dictionary) and three classifier sizes (16, 64, 256 parameters) on two RISC-V targets: GD32VF103 and ESP32-C3. Empirical validation on an air-quality monitoring workload (6 sensors, 1 Hz) shows the model predicts achieved compression ratio within ±7% and classification accuracy within ±2 percentage points across 48 configuration combinations. The paper also discusses memory-bank partitioning strategies that reduce SRAM contention between the two tasks by 23% without hardware modification.

SYN-PUB-07303.title: TENT: A Tiny Entropy-Coded Transform for Ultra-Low-Power Sub-Threshold Microcontrollers
SYN-PUB-07303.text:
TENT: A Tiny Entropy-Coded Transform for Ultra-Low-Power Sub-Threshold Microcontrollers (2024, journal, IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems II: Express Briefs).
Authors: Lukas Hofer (outside co-author); Bojana Milošević (outside co-author); Branislav Stojanović (R0641).
Keywords: sub-threshold; integer DCT; Huffman coding; ASIC; ultra-low power; 65 nm CMOS.
Sub-threshold microcontrollers operating at supply voltages below 0.5 V achieve pico-joule-per-cycle energy figures but impose extreme constraints on code size and arithmetic complexity. This paper introduces TENT, a lightweight integer transform followed by a two-symbol static Huffman coder, implemented entirely within 1.4 kB of flash and 256 bytes of SRAM on a custom ASIC test chip fabricated in 65 nm CMOS running at 50 kHz and 0.4 V. TENT applies a 4-point integer approximation to a discrete cosine transform using only additions and one-bit shifts, quantises coefficients with a three-level dead-zone quantiser, and encodes symbols using a precomputed 16-entry Huffman table stored in ROM. On temperature, pressure, and light sensor streams sampled at 0.1 Hz, TENT achieves compression ratios of 3.1:1 to 5.8:1 at per-sample energy of 48 pJ. The paper presents silicon measurement results alongside a software reference implementation validated on an ARM Cortex-M0+.

SYN-PUB-07722.title: Detecting Abrupt and Gradual Faults in Hydraulic Actuator Systems Using a Combined CUSUM–Autoencoder Approach
SYN-PUB-07722.text:
Detecting Abrupt and Gradual Faults in Hydraulic Actuator Systems Using a Combined CUSUM–Autoencoder Approach (2022, journal, Mechanical Systems and Signal Processing).
Authors: Dragana Milošević (outside co-author); Branislava Ostojić (R0773); Radmila Jakovljević (R0687); Borivoj Stanković (outside co-author); Dunja Vojnović (R1002).
Keywords: hydraulic actuators; CUSUM; autoencoder; fault detection; gradual drift.
Hydraulic actuator faults manifest as either abrupt jumps in pressure or flow or as gradual drift in actuator efficiency. Standard CUSUM charts detect the former reliably but respond slowly to the latter, while autoencoder reconstruction error captures complex multivariate deviations but is insensitive to the direction of change. This paper proposes a two-stage detector: a shallow convolutional autoencoder generates a residual vector, and a sign-constrained CUSUM statistic accumulates this residual in the direction identified by an offline fault-mode analysis. The combined statistic is evaluated on the public Hydraulic System Condition dataset (2 205 cycles, 17 sensors, four fault types) and on a laboratory actuator testbed. For gradual efficiency-loss faults, the combined scheme reduced mean detection delay from 41 cycles (autoencoder alone) to 17 cycles at a matched false-alarm rate of 1%. No improvement over plain CUSUM was observed for abrupt pressure-drop faults, confirming complementary strengths.

SYN-PUB-07802.title: Wake-up receiver circuit for asynchronous event-driven body-area networks: design and measured sensitivity
SYN-PUB-07802.text:
Wake-up receiver circuit for asynchronous event-driven body-area networks: design and measured sensitivity (2021, journal, Microelectronics Journal).
Authors: Filip Mijatović (R0905); Christoph Brandner (outside co-author); Stefan Horvat (outside co-author); Aleksandar Jeremić (R0696).
Keywords: wake-up receiver; asynchronous MAC; envelope detector; 868 MHz; event-driven sensing.
Polling-based duty cycling requires a node to activate its main radio at fixed intervals regardless of whether data are ready, wasting energy between physiological events. A wake-up receiver (WuRx) circuit that remains continuously active at very low power can replace this periodic wakeup. This paper presents a WuRx designed in 130 nm CMOS consuming 4.2 µW from a 1.0 V supply. The circuit uses an envelope detector followed by a three-stage comparator with hysteresis to decode an amplitude-shift-keyed wake-up beacon at 868 MHz. Measured sensitivity was −62 dBm at a target false-alarm rate of one per hour. Selectivity to adjacent channels was verified in a shielded box with an interferer 3 MHz offset at levels up to −20 dBm. Die area was 0.19 mm². When integrated into a complete sensor node alongside a CC1310 main radio, the WuRx reduced mean idle-state current from 18.4 µA (timer-based duty cycle at 1% duty) to 6.7 µA under a traffic model representative of a cardiac event monitor with bursts averaging twice per hour.

SYN-PUB-08314.title: A watchdog-based self-recovery scheme for 802.15.4 sensor nodes in unattended deployments
SYN-PUB-08314.text:
A watchdog-based self-recovery scheme for 802.15.4 sensor nodes in unattended deployments (2013, journal, Journal of Embedded Computing and Sensor Systems).
Authors: Žarko Jakovljević (R0754); Miroslav Tešić (outside co-author); Dragana Vukić (outside co-author).
Keywords: watchdog timer; fault recovery; wireless sensor node; soil monitoring; ATmega.
Unattended wireless sensor nodes in field deployments frequently enter irrecoverable software states due to memory corruption, peripheral lockup, or stack overflow caused by transient power events. This paper presents a layered watchdog architecture implemented on an ATmega128RFA1 platform in which three independent timers supervise the operating system scheduler, the radio driver, and the analog front-end sequencer separately. When any tier detects a violation of its expected heartbeat window, a graduated recovery procedure is executed that avoids full device reset in roughly 74 percent of observed fault cases, thereby preserving the sensor's runtime context. The scheme was evaluated over a 90-day outdoor deployment of 18 nodes sampling soil moisture at 10-minute intervals. Mean time between unrecoverable resets increased from 11.3 days in the baseline configuration to 61.7 days with the proposed architecture. Current overhead introduced by the additional supervision circuitry was measured at 38 µA in active mode, representing less than 2 percent of total node consumption. The design is described in sufficient detail to be reproduced on comparable 8-bit and 16-bit microcontroller families.

SYN-PUB-08315.title: On-node detection of resistive humidity sensor drift using recursive least-squares residual monitoring
SYN-PUB-08315.text:
On-node detection of resistive humidity sensor drift using recursive least-squares residual monitoring (2018, journal, Sensors and Actuators: Methods and Applications).
Authors: Žarko Jakovljević (R0754); Ivan Zec (R0903); Tijana Ostojić (outside co-author); Péter Vásárhelyi (outside co-author).
Keywords: sensor drift; humidity sensor; recursive least squares; edge diagnostics; anomaly detection.
Capacitive and resistive humidity sensors used in long-term field deployments exhibit systematic drift attributable to membrane contamination, mechanical stress, and UV degradation of the sensing polymer. This study examines drift detection using a recursive least-squares estimator running on a 32-bit ARM Cortex-M0+ microcontroller with 64 kB RAM. The estimator maintains a sliding 72-hour model of sensor behaviour and raises a diagnostic flag when the standardised prediction residual exceeds a threshold calibrated to yield a 5 percent false-alarm rate under clean operating conditions. The method was validated against a controlled ageing experiment in which 24 SHT31-compatible sensors were exposed to accelerated UV and humidity cycling; 21 of 22 drift events exceeding 3 percent RH offset were detected within 8 hours of onset. Computational cost was benchmarked at 1.2 ms per update cycle at 48 MHz, consuming negligible battery capacity relative to the radio subsystem. The paper includes a discussion of threshold sensitivity as a function of sampling interval and recommends a minimum of 15-minute sampling for reliable operation.

SYN-PUB-08316.title: Energy-aware retransmission scheduling for IoT nodes operating on solar-harvested power under partial shading conditions
SYN-PUB-08316.text:
Energy-aware retransmission scheduling for IoT nodes operating on solar-harvested power under partial shading conditions (2020, book chapter, Handbook of Low-Power Sensing Systems for Environmental Applications (TechPress Academic, Vienna)).
Authors: Gordana Simić (outside co-author); Žarko Jakovljević (R0754); Ralf Brünner (outside co-author).
Keywords: energy harvesting; solar power; transmission scheduling; supercapacitor; duty cycle control.
Solar energy harvesting for IoT nodes in temperate climates is complicated by persistent partial shading from vegetation, cloud cover, and seasonal sun angle variation. This chapter reviews energy buffering and transmission scheduling strategies applicable to nodes where the harvester output drops to 10–40 percent of rated capacity for multi-hour periods. A discrete-time predictive controller is presented that adjusts the uplink reporting interval and transmission power based on a rolling 24-hour energy budget estimated from a small supercapacitor voltage sensor. Simulations using one-year solar irradiance data from three sites in the Pannonian Plain show that the controller maintains the reporting duty cycle above 85 percent of the target rate throughout the year compared with 61 percent for a fixed-interval baseline. The chapter also covers hardware design guidelines for solar panel placement and MPPT circuit selection, and discusses the trade-off between supercapacitor capacity, leakage current, and cold-start reliability in sub-zero conditions.

SYN-PUB-08317.title: Multi-metric data quality scoring at the gateway for heterogeneous agricultural IoT deployments
SYN-PUB-08317.text:
Multi-metric data quality scoring at the gateway for heterogeneous agricultural IoT deployments (2021, conference, IEEE International Conference on Agricultural IoT and Precision Farming (AIPF)).
Authors: Luka Horvatović (outside co-author); Žarko Jakovljević (R0754); Marija Đurić (outside co-author); Konstantinos Papadimitriou (outside co-author).
Keywords: data quality; gateway processing; agricultural IoT; anomaly flagging; heterogeneous networks.
Aggregation gateways in agricultural IoT networks receive streams from sensors operating under different power regimes, communication protocols, and environmental exposures. This paper proposes a gateway-side data quality scoring framework that assigns each incoming measurement a composite score based on four sub-metrics: timeliness (elapsed time since last message relative to expected interval), signal plausibility (z-score against a rolling peer-group distribution), battery state estimate, and historical reliability index derived from 30-day uptime statistics. The framework was implemented in Python 3.9 on a Raspberry Pi 4 gateway serving 61 nodes in a test vineyard in Fruška Gora, processing approximately 8,700 messages per day. Over a 5-month evaluation period, the composite score correctly flagged 93 of 97 manually confirmed measurement anomalies and produced 11 false positives. Score computation added a mean latency of 4.1 ms per message at gateway level. The scoring metadata is forwarded alongside raw measurements to a central time-series database, enabling downstream analytics to weight observations accordingly. Integration steps for two commercial farm management platforms are documented.

SYN-PUB-08318.title: Firmware update reliability over NB-IoT in low-signal rural environments: a field study
SYN-PUB-08318.text:
Firmware update reliability over NB-IoT in low-signal rural environments: a field study (2022, journal, Embedded Systems and Wireless Communications Letters).
Authors: Žarko Jakovljević (R0754); Aleksandra Ninković (outside co-author); Tibor Molnár (outside co-author).
Keywords: FOTA; firmware update; NB-IoT; rural deployment; link quality.
Over-the-air firmware updates (FOTA) are essential for maintaining security and functionality of deployed IoT nodes but are poorly characterised in weak-signal rural cellular conditions. This study documents 1,840 FOTA sessions conducted across 46 NB-IoT nodes installed at distances of 8–22 km from the nearest base station in the southern Bačka region of Serbia. Update payloads ranged from 48 to 192 kB and were delivered using a block-based transfer protocol with configurable block size and retry budget. Session success rate was 81.4 percent without adaptive configuration and rose to 94.6 percent when block size was reduced from 512 to 128 bytes and the retry budget was tripled. Failed sessions were traced primarily to receive-window mismatches during peak network load periods. Energy cost per successful update was measured between 0.9 and 3.4 mAh depending on retry overhead. The paper quantifies the dependency of success rate on RSRP and presents a simple heuristic for selecting block size based on a short link probe transmitted before each update session.

SYN-PUB-08319.title: Characterising the interaction between cellular network congestion and duty-cycle regulation in dense IoT deployments: a simulation and measurement study
SYN-PUB-08319.text:
Characterising the interaction between cellular network congestion and duty-cycle regulation in dense IoT deployments: a simulation and measurement study (2026, preprint, arXiv (cs.NI)).
Authors: Žarko Jakovljević (R0754); Luka Horvatović (outside co-author); Florian Kersting (outside co-author).
Keywords: NB-IoT congestion; duty cycle; dense IoT; network simulation; transmission scheduling.
When hundreds of IoT nodes sharing a single NB-IoT cell simultaneously enter their reporting window, uplink congestion increases packet delay and loss in ways that interact nonlinearly with node-level duty-cycle power management. This preprint reports a combined simulation and measurement study: a system-level LTE-M/NB-IoT simulator was configured to match the topology of a 312-node crop monitoring network in Srem, and its congestion behaviour was cross-validated against 8 weeks of gateway-side timestamps showing mean delay growth from 1.2 s to 14.7 s during morning reporting peaks. The simulator was then used to evaluate four transmission-window randomisation strategies across node densities from 50 to 500 nodes per cell. A jitter-and-backoff strategy combining a randomised initial delay drawn from a 0–300 s uniform window with an exponential backoff on contention reduced 99th-percentile delay from 41 s to 8 s and cut failed transmissions by 63 percent at 400 nodes per cell. Interaction effects with solar harvesting schedules are discussed and a recommended configuration table is provided for deployment engineers.

SYN-PUB-08483.title: A Multivariate CUSUM Scheme with Adaptive Estimation of Covariance Structure for Batch Chemical Processes
SYN-PUB-08483.text:
A Multivariate CUSUM Scheme with Adaptive Estimation of Covariance Structure for Batch Chemical Processes (2010, journal, Journal of Quality Technology and Statistical Engineering).
Authors: Miroslav Vukić (outside co-author); Tatjana Lončar (outside co-author); Branislava Ostojić (R0773).
Keywords: CUSUM; adaptive covariance; batch processes; multivariate SPC.
Classical multivariate CUSUM charts assume a fixed in-control covariance matrix, an assumption routinely violated in batch manufacturing where operating conditions shift between phases. This paper proposes replacing the static covariance estimate with a sliding-window estimator updated at each sampling instant, with the window length selected by minimising a penalised prediction error over a rolling validation segment. The scheme was evaluated on a publicly available benchmark dataset from a simulated batch reactor (50 process variables, 1 000 batches) as well as on data collected from a plastics-extrusion line at a partner facility. On the benchmark, the average run length to detection for mean-shift magnitudes between 0.5 and 2.0 standard deviations improved by 18–34% compared with the fixed-covariance baseline, at the cost of a 7% increase in false-alarm rate. Parameter sensitivity, computational cost per sample, and the practical question of selecting the penalty coefficient are discussed in detail. The method is implemented in a freely available R package accompanying the paper.

SYN-PUB-08485.title: Online Detection of Covariance Shifts in Industrial Sensor Arrays Using the Generalised Likelihood Ratio Test
SYN-PUB-08485.text:
Online Detection of Covariance Shifts in Industrial Sensor Arrays Using the Generalised Likelihood Ratio Test (2013, conference, Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Intelligent Systems and Informatics (SISY 2013)).
Authors: Zoran Petrović (outside co-author); Dragana Milošević (outside co-author); Branislava Ostojić (R0773).
Keywords: covariance change detection; GLR test; sequential analysis; sensor arrays.
