Changes in the covariance structure of a multivariate sensor stream can signal developing faults before any univariate indicator crosses a threshold. This paper applies a sequential generalised likelihood ratio (GLR) test to detect covariance shifts in an online, computationally efficient manner. The test statistic is computed over a sliding dual-window: a reference window of fixed length and a test window that grows until a detection is declared. Theoretical bounds on average run length are derived under a Wishart distribution model and confirmed by Monte Carlo simulation for dimensions p = 5, 10, 20 with 10 000 replicates each. The method is applied to a 14-channel temperature and pressure dataset from a district-heating substation, where it detected three confirmed maintenance events 40–120 seconds earlier than the plant's existing alarm system. Computational complexity is O(p²) per new sample after initial setup.

SYN-PUB-08486.title: Monitoring Nonlinear Process Dynamics with a Kernel Principal Component Analysis Control Chart: A Practical Assessment
SYN-PUB-08486.text:
Monitoring Nonlinear Process Dynamics with a Kernel Principal Component Analysis Control Chart: A Practical Assessment (2015, journal, Chemometrics and Process Analytics).
Authors: Branislava Ostojić (R0773); Aleksandar Đorđević (outside co-author); Petra Kovačević (outside co-author).
Keywords: kernel PCA; nonlinear SPC; Hotelling T²; fault detection.
Kernel principal component analysis (KPCA) projects nonlinear process data into a feature space where conventional Hotelling T² and Q statistics can be applied. Despite a substantial theoretical literature, practical guidance on kernel and hyperparameter selection for SPC purposes remains limited. This paper presents a systematic assessment of radial-basis-function and polynomial kernels across four industrial benchmark datasets (Tennessee Eastman process, simulated polymerisation reactor, rolling-mill dataset, and an in-house compressor dataset) using fault-detection rate and false-alarm rate as primary metrics. Cross-validation on in-control data was used to select the bandwidth parameter. Results show that RBF-KPCA outperforms linear PCA on three of four datasets, with the compressor data yielding the largest improvement (fault-detection rate 81% vs. 57% at a 1% false-alarm rate). The effect of the number of retained components is also analysed. An open-source Python implementation is included.

SYN-PUB-08487.title: Bayesian Change-Point Models for Multivariate Non-Stationary Time Series in Continuous Manufacturing
SYN-PUB-08487.text:
Bayesian Change-Point Models for Multivariate Non-Stationary Time Series in Continuous Manufacturing (2016, journal, Journal of Statistical Computation and Simulation).
Authors: Miroslav Vukić (outside co-author); Ilona Szabo (outside co-author); Branislava Ostojić (R0773).
Keywords: Bayesian change-point detection; BOCPD; Normal-Inverse-Wishart; continuous manufacturing.
Many continuous manufacturing processes operate under time-varying mean and variance due to raw-material variability and gradual equipment wear. Standard SPC methods tuned on historical data deteriorate in such environments. This paper formulates a Bayesian online change-point detection model (BOCPD) extended to multivariate observations under a Normal-Inverse-Wishart conjugate prior. The model simultaneously estimates the probability of a change and updates the predictive distribution after each new sample. Two variants are compared: one with a fixed hazard rate and one with a hazard rate estimated from past inter-change intervals using empirical Bayes. On simulated data with p = 8 variables, 500 change points, and signal-to-noise ratios between 0.5 and 3.0, the empirical-Bayes variant reduced the mean detection delay by 1.8 samples at a fixed false-alarm rate of 0.5%. The method was validated on accelerometer data from a CNC milling machine spindle over a six-month period.

SYN-PUB-08488.title: Unsupervised Segmentation of Industrial Time Series via a Penalised Piecewise-Stationary Model
SYN-PUB-08488.text:
Unsupervised Segmentation of Industrial Time Series via a Penalised Piecewise-Stationary Model (2018, journal, IEEE Transactions on Industrial Informatics).
Authors: Dragana Milošević (outside co-author); Borivoj Stanković (outside co-author); Ana Horvat (outside co-author); Branislava Ostojić (R0773).
Keywords: time series segmentation; piecewise stationarity; BIC; dynamic programming; cyber-physical systems.
Long industrial time series collected from cyber-physical systems rarely satisfy stationarity over their full length. This paper treats segmentation as a model-selection problem: a piecewise-stationary multivariate Gaussian model is fitted, and the number and positions of segments are chosen by minimising a modified BIC penalising both the number of segments and their minimum length. Optimisation uses a dynamic programming algorithm with complexity O(n²) in the number of observations. The approach is compared with binary segmentation and wild binary segmentation on 24 synthetic scenarios (varying segment lengths 50–500 and p = 4–16 variables) and on three industrial datasets: a paper-machine headbox, a wastewater treatment blower, and a refrigeration compressor. BIC-guided dynamic programming achieved the lowest mean absolute error in estimated change-point locations on 19 of 24 synthetic scenarios and recovered all manually labelled regime changes in the wastewater dataset.

SYN-PUB-08489.title: Statistical Process Control for Cyber-Physical Systems: A Survey of Methods and Open Challenges
SYN-PUB-08489.text:
Statistical Process Control for Cyber-Physical Systems: A Survey of Methods and Open Challenges (2019, book chapter, Handbook of Industrial Data Science (Edited Volume, Springer Academic Press)).
Authors: Branislava Ostojić (R0773); Miroslav Vukić (outside co-author); Marta Reinhardt (outside co-author).
Keywords: SPC survey; cyber-physical systems; online learning; anomaly detection; benchmark.
Cyber-physical systems produce streams of heterogeneous sensor data at high sampling rates, creating both opportunities and difficulties for statistical process control. This chapter surveys methods applicable to the monitoring of such systems, organising them along four dimensions: the stationarity assumption (static vs. adaptive), the observation structure (univariate vs. multivariate), the supervision level (supervised vs. unsupervised), and the computational setting (batch vs. online). For each combination, representative methods are described and their assumptions, strengths, and computational requirements are tabulated. Special attention is given to the interaction between control-chart theory and machine-learning approaches, including isolation forest, autoencoders, and one-class SVMs as anomaly scorers whose output feeds threshold-based alarms. Open challenges discussed include distribution shift under normal ageing, alarm rationalisation in dense sensor networks, and the absence of labelled fault data. The chapter concludes with a set of benchmark recommendations for the community.

SYN-PUB-08490.title: One-Class SVM Anomaly Scores as Control-Chart Statistics: Calibration, Threshold Setting, and Recalibration Frequency
SYN-PUB-08490.text:
One-Class SVM Anomaly Scores as Control-Chart Statistics: Calibration, Threshold Setting, and Recalibration Frequency (2020, journal, Computers and Industrial Engineering).
Authors: Aleksandar Đorđević (outside co-author); Branislava Ostojić (R0773).
Keywords: one-class SVM; anomaly score calibration; control chart; drift detection; edge deployment.
One-class support vector machines produce a real-valued decision score that can serve as a univariate control-chart statistic, enabling the combination of nonlinear pattern recognition with the interpretability of run rules and average-run-length guarantees. This paper addresses three practical questions: (1) how to calibrate raw SVM scores to approximate a false-alarm probability, (2) how to set the control limit given a desired in-control ARL, and (3) how frequently the SVM must be retrained to maintain calibration when the in-control distribution drifts slowly. Using a Platt-scaling calibration step and a bootstrap-based limit-setting procedure, the method achieves in-control ARLs within 5% of nominal across six simulated drift scenarios. Recalibration triggered by a secondary drift-detection statistic on residuals reduced worst-case ARL inflation from 43% to 9% on a simulated six-month conveyor-belt dataset with gradual load increase. The paper reports training times and discusses feasibility for edge deployment.

SYN-PUB-08491.title: Federated Learning for Distributed Statistical Process Monitoring Across Multiple Production Lines
SYN-PUB-08491.text:
Federated Learning for Distributed Statistical Process Monitoring Across Multiple Production Lines (2021, journal, Journal of Manufacturing Systems).
Authors: Nataša Jovanović (outside co-author); Ilona Szabo (outside co-author); Stefan Gruber (outside co-author); Branislava Ostojić (R0773).
Keywords: federated learning; distributed SPC; anomaly detection; heterogeneous data; production monitoring.
When identical or similar machines operate at multiple plants, it is attractive to pool monitoring knowledge across sites without centralising raw sensor data for privacy or bandwidth reasons. This paper adapts federated averaging to train a shared anomaly-detection model for multivariate SPC, with each plant training locally on its own data and contributing model updates to a central aggregator. Four federated aggregation strategies are compared against a centralised baseline and a local-only baseline on a network of five simulated production lines with heterogeneous fault-type distributions. Federated averaging with client-side control-limit adjustment achieved fault-detection rates within 4 percentage points of the centralised model on three of five sites, while local-only models lagged by 11–19 percentage points. Communication overhead, convergence speed, and the influence of data heterogeneity on model drift are quantified. Limitations regarding non-IID client data are discussed.

SYN-PUB-08492.title: Adaptive Threshold Selection for Streaming Anomaly Detectors Using Extreme Value Theory
SYN-PUB-08492.text:
Adaptive Threshold Selection for Streaming Anomaly Detectors Using Extreme Value Theory (2023, journal, Reliability Engineering and System Safety).
Authors: Miroslav Vukić (outside co-author); Petra Kovačević (outside co-author); Marta Reinhardt (outside co-author); Branislava Ostojić (R0773).
Keywords: extreme value theory; peaks over threshold; adaptive threshold; anomaly detection; streaming data.
(no abstract)

SYN-PUB-08493.title: Benchmarking Change-Point Detection Algorithms on Annotated Industrial Datasets: Methodology and Initial Results
SYN-PUB-08493.text:
Benchmarking Change-Point Detection Algorithms on Annotated Industrial Datasets: Methodology and Initial Results (2024, conference, Proceedings of the 12th International Conference on Data-Driven Process Control (DDPC 2024)).
Authors: Aleksandar Đorđević (outside co-author); Stefan Gruber (outside co-author); Vesna Todorović (outside co-author); Branislava Ostojić (R0773).
Keywords: change-point detection benchmark; PELT; BOCPD; evaluation methodology; annotated datasets.
Published evaluations of change-point detection algorithms are difficult to compare because they use different datasets, annotation conventions, and performance metrics. This paper proposes a reproducible benchmarking protocol and applies it to eight algorithms—including BOCPD, PELT, RUPTURES binary segmentation, wild binary segmentation, BOCD with student-t likelihood, L2-cost dynamic programming, a kernel change-point detector, and an LSTM-based method—on six annotated industrial datasets contributed by the authors and three collaborating groups. Annotations were produced by domain engineers and reviewed by a second engineer; disagreements were resolved by consensus. Metrics reported include F1 score at a tolerance of five samples, mean absolute error in change-point location, and computational time per 1 000 observations. No single algorithm dominated across all datasets. PELT performed best on datasets with large between-segment variance ratios, while the kernel method was most robust on datasets with covariance-only changes. The datasets and annotation files are deposited in a public repository.

SYN-PUB-08494.title: Monitoring Concept Drift in Online Anomaly Detection Models for Industrial IoT Streams
SYN-PUB-08494.text:
Monitoring Concept Drift in Online Anomaly Detection Models for Industrial IoT Streams (2025, journal, IEEE Internet of Things Journal).
Authors: Nataša Jovanović (outside co-author); Ilona Szabo (outside co-author); Branislava Ostojić (R0773).
Keywords: concept drift; isolation forest; Page–Hinkley test; Industrial IoT; incremental learning.
Anomaly detection models deployed in industrial IoT environments face concept drift: the statistical properties of normal operation change over months due to seasonal variation, equipment ageing, or production-mix changes. This paper proposes a two-level monitoring architecture in which a primary anomaly detector (isolation forest trained offline) is supervised by a secondary drift monitor based on the Page–Hinkley test applied to the score distribution's empirical mean and variance. When drift is confirmed, a lightweight incremental update procedure re-weights the forest using recent in-control samples without full retraining. The architecture is evaluated on 18 months of data from three IoT-connected air-compressor units at a manufacturing plant, comprising approximately 4.7 million observations per unit. The drift monitor correctly identified seven of eight documented operating-regime transitions with one false trigger. Post-update fault-detection rates recovered to within 3% of the initial model's performance within 2 000 samples of each transition.

SYN-PUB-08756.title: Encoding Compressed Sparse Row Layout in an SSA-Based Intermediate Representation
SYN-PUB-08756.text:
Encoding Compressed Sparse Row Layout in an SSA-Based Intermediate Representation (2016, conference, Proceedings of the Central European Workshop on Compiler Infrastructure).
Authors: Luka Knežević (R0802); Miroslav Đorđević (outside co-author); Annelies Verbrugge (outside co-author).
Keywords: SSA; intermediate representation; compressed sparse row; sparse kernels; RISC-V.
Standard SSA-based IRs represent memory accesses as load and store instructions with flat address arithmetic, which discards structural information present in compressed sparse formats. This work proposes an extension to a three-address SSA IR that introduces typed sparse-access nodes carrying row-pointer, column-index, and value streams as first-class operands. Thirty-two sparse kernels from graph analytics and scientific computing are re-expressed in the extended IR. A lowering pass translates the typed nodes to architecture-specific address sequences with a mean code-size increase of 4% compared to hand-written assembly. Static analysis on the extended IR detects 23 out of 25 injected out-of-bounds accesses at compile time. The paper reports compilation statistics for kernels compiled to a simulated 32-bit RISC-V target and discusses interaction with standard dataflow optimisations including constant propagation and dead-code elimination.

SYN-PUB-08757.title: Sparsity-Aware Instruction Scheduling for a Dataflow Accelerator with Heterogeneous Functional Units
SYN-PUB-08757.text:
Sparsity-Aware Instruction Scheduling for a Dataflow Accelerator with Heterogeneous Functional Units (2017, conference, Proceedings of the International Conference on Embedded Architectures and Compilers).
Authors: Nemanja Simić (outside co-author); Florian Bergmann (outside co-author); Luka Knežević (R0802).
Keywords: instruction scheduling; dataflow accelerator; sparse operations; list scheduling; functional unit utilisation.
(no abstract)

SYN-PUB-08758.title: Register Pressure Reduction Through Sparsity-Specific Live-Range Splitting in an LLVM Back-End
SYN-PUB-08758.text:
Register Pressure Reduction Through Sparsity-Specific Live-Range Splitting in an LLVM Back-End (2019, journal, ACM Transactions on Architecture and Compilation Techniques — Regional Edition).
Authors: Luka Knežević (R0802); Florian Bergmann (outside co-author); Katarina Lukić (outside co-author).
Keywords: live-range splitting; register pressure; spill code; LLVM; sparse linear algebra.
Dense compiler back-ends handle live-range splitting by inserting spill code at points where register pressure exceeds the physical register count. For kernels operating on sparse tensors, spill patterns are strongly correlated with non-zero structure, and generic spill heuristics incur unnecessary memory traffic. This paper evaluates three live-range splitting strategies—interval halving, def-chain splitting, and density-guided breakpoint selection—on a set of sparse linear algebra kernels running on a simulated accelerator with 32 general-purpose registers. Density-guided splitting reduces spill instruction count by 22% and improves kernel execution time by 9% on average compared with the LLVM default spiller. The paper also reports on integration into a continuous integration pipeline used to track regression across nightly LLVM builds. Benchmarks cover matrices from the Florida Sparse Matrix Collection with non-zero counts between 10k and 40M.

SYN-PUB-08759.title: A Taxonomy of Intermediate Representations for Domain-Specific Tensor Accelerators
SYN-PUB-08759.text:
A Taxonomy of Intermediate Representations for Domain-Specific Tensor Accelerators (2020, book chapter, Advances in Compiler Design for Heterogeneous Architectures, Springer).
Authors: Luka Knežević (R0802); Annelies Verbrugge (outside co-author); Petar Vuković (outside co-author).
Keywords: intermediate representation; taxonomy; tensor accelerators; sparsity; compiler survey.
This book chapter surveys IRs that have been proposed or deployed for tensor-processing hardware over the period 2008–2019, organising them along four axes: granularity (scalar, vector, tile, graph), sparsity awareness (none, hint-based, structural), target coupling (portable, vendor-specific, hybrid), and transformation support (limited, full algebraic, extensible). Thirty-one distinct IR designs are catalogued, drawn from academic papers, open-source compiler projects, and publicly disclosed industrial compiler documentation. The chapter identifies three recurring design tensions: expressiveness versus analysability, portability versus performance, and static shape information versus dynamic sparsity. Case studies are provided for three representative IRs, including compilation pipelines, supported hardware targets, and documented performance figures. The chapter concludes with a discussion of open problems in IR design for emerging sparse-dense mixed workloads.

SYN-PUB-08760.title: Compile-Time Density Estimation for Guiding Sparse–Dense Format Selection in a Kernel Compiler
SYN-PUB-08760.text:
Compile-Time Density Estimation for Guiding Sparse–Dense Format Selection in a Kernel Compiler (2024, conference, Proceedings of the European Symposium on Compilation and Architecture).
Authors: Luka Knežević (R0802); Dragana Kovačević (outside co-author); Lena Schreiber (outside co-author).
Keywords: density estimation; format selection; sparse tensors; static analysis; interval arithmetic.
A kernel compiler targeting mixed sparse–dense workloads must decide at compile time whether a tensor operand should be stored in a sparse format (CSR, COO, BCSR) or a dense layout. Wrong choices lead to format-conversion overhead at runtime. This paper proposes a static analysis pass that propagates density bounds through an SSA-based IR using interval arithmetic. The pass is evaluated on a suite of 44 tensor kernels drawn from graph neural network training and scientific simulation. Static estimation selects the correct format for 38 of 44 kernels when compared with a profile-guided oracle. For the remaining six cases, a lightweight runtime fallback is triggered. End-to-end compilation including format inference takes under 400 ms per kernel on a standard laptop. The paper analyses false-positive rates for density over-estimation and their impact on memory allocation.

SYN-PUB-08969.title: Discharge Behaviour of Li/SOCl₂ Cells Under Periodic Pulsed Loads at Low Ambient Temperature
SYN-PUB-08969.text:
Discharge Behaviour of Li/SOCl₂ Cells Under Periodic Pulsed Loads at Low Ambient Temperature (2016, journal, Journal of Applied Electrochemical Engineering).
Authors: Dragana Petrović (outside co-author); Vuk Bačić (R0826); Miroslav Kovačević (outside co-author).
Keywords: Li/SOCl₂; pulsed discharge; passivation; low temperature; capacity correction.
Primary lithium thionyl chloride cells are widely deployed in remote sensing applications where loads are intermittent and temperatures can fall below 0 °C. This study characterises the discharge behaviour of twelve commercially available Li/SOCl₂ cells subjected to pulse trains with duty cycles of 2 %, 5 %, and 10 % at temperatures of +25 °C, 0 °C, and −15 °C. Cell voltage recovery curves were logged at 100 ms resolution. A passivation-layer resistance term was extracted from each voltage dip using a two-RC equivalent-circuit model fitted by nonlinear least squares. Results show that at −15 °C and 10 % duty cycle, usable capacity drops by 34 % compared to room-temperature constant-current reference tests. The passivation resistance increases by a factor of 2.7 after the first 50 pulses and stabilises within 200 pulses. An empirical correction factor is derived that maps constant-current datasheet capacity to expected pulsed-load capacity as a function of temperature and duty cycle. The correction reduces capacity prediction error from 19 % to under 6 % across the tested conditions.

SYN-PUB-08970.title: A Parametric Equivalent-Circuit Model for Estimating Remaining Useful Life of Primary Lithium Cells in WSN Deployments
SYN-PUB-08970.text:
A Parametric Equivalent-Circuit Model for Estimating Remaining Useful Life of Primary Lithium Cells in WSN Deployments (2018, conference, Proceedings of the International Conference on Wireless Sensor Systems and Energy Harvesting (WSSEH)).
Authors: Vuk Bačić (R0826); Dragana Petrović (outside co-author); Aleksandra Vujić (outside co-author); Tomáš Blaha (outside co-author).
Keywords: remaining useful life; particle filter; Li/MnO₂; equivalent-circuit model; agricultural WSN.
This paper presents a parametric model for estimating the remaining useful life (RUL) of primary lithium cells powering wireless sensor nodes. The model is built on a two-branch RC equivalent circuit whose parameters—series resistance, charge-transfer resistance, double-layer capacitance, and open-circuit voltage—are updated periodically using electrochemical impedance spectroscopy measurements taken at 1 kHz and 10 Hz. Calibration data were collected from 30 Li/MnO₂ cells cycled under traffic profiles derived from a real agricultural monitoring deployment in Vojvodina. A particle-filter-based state estimator updates model parameters every 72 hours and extrapolates the voltage trajectory to a 2.8 V cut-off. Across a 14-month accelerated ageing campaign, the model predicted end-of-life timing with a mean absolute error of 9.3 days against actual cell exhaustion, outperforming the datasheet Peukert approach, which gave a 41-day mean error. Computational cost of the on-host particle filter is under 80 ms on a Cortex-M3 microcontroller at 8 MHz.

SYN-PUB-08971.title: Impedance Evolution of Li/SOCl₂ Cells Stored at Elevated Temperature: A Three-Year Longitudinal Study
SYN-PUB-08971.text:
Impedance Evolution of Li/SOCl₂ Cells Stored at Elevated Temperature: A Three-Year Longitudinal Study (2019, journal, Electrochimica Applicata — Central European Edition).
Authors: Vuk Bačić (R0826); Miroslav Kovačević (outside co-author); Nataša Đorđević (outside co-author).
Keywords: shelf life; storage degradation; impedance spectroscopy; Arrhenius; passivation layer.
Long shelf life is a principal selling point of primary lithium cells, yet systematic data on impedance evolution during storage at elevated temperature are scarce. This study tracks 24 Li/SOCl₂ cells stored continuously at 40 °C over 36 months, with electrochemical impedance spectroscopy measurements at 0.1 Hz–100 kHz taken every three months. Equivalent-circuit fits reveal that the passivation-layer resistance grows approximately linearly at 1.8 Ω month⁻¹ during the first 18 months and then slows to 0.6 Ω month⁻¹. The double-layer capacitance decreases by 22 % over the full period. Pulse-load discharge tests performed at months 0, 12, 24, and 36 show a 17 % reduction in capacity delivered above the 2.8 V cut-off after 36 months. A simple Arrhenius extrapolation calibrated against these data predicts that cells stored at 25 °C retain over 90 % usable capacity after 10 years, consistent with manufacturer claims but now supported by mechanism-level impedance data. The dataset is provided as a supplementary CSV file.

SYN-PUB-08972.title: Energy Budget Analysis for LoRaWAN End-Nodes Powered by Single Primary Cells: Field Measurements from a Flood-Warning Network
SYN-PUB-08972.text:
Energy Budget Analysis for LoRaWAN End-Nodes Powered by Single Primary Cells: Field Measurements from a Flood-Warning Network (2021, journal, IET Wireless Sensor Systems).
Authors: Vuk Bačić (R0826); Branislav Todorović (outside co-author); Jelena Stanković (outside co-author); Pieter van den Berg (outside co-author).
Keywords: LoRaWAN; energy budget; flood monitoring; spreading factor; primary cell lifetime.
This paper reports measured energy consumption data from 18 LoRaWAN end-nodes deployed along the Tisa river basin for flood-level monitoring over a 20-month period. Each node is powered by a single AA-size Li/MnO₂ cell. Current waveforms were logged at 1 ms resolution using a shunt-based data logger co-located on the PCB. The study decomposes total energy into four phases: sensor acquisition (7 %), radio transmission (61 %), idle sleep (29 %), and microcontroller housekeeping (3 %). Radio transmission current peaks ranged from 38 mA to 124 mA depending on spreading factor. An empirical energy model calibrated on the first six months of data predicted total charge drawn over the remaining 14 months with a 4.1 % root-mean-square error. Cells in nodes with high spreading factors (SF12) showed 28 % lower delivered capacity than those using SF7, attributable to larger pulse amplitude stressing the passivation layer. These findings suggest that adaptive data-rate policies can meaningfully extend primary-cell lifetime in flood-monitoring deployments.

SYN-PUB-08973.title: Effect of Duty Cycle and Inter-Pulse Interval on Voltage Recovery in Li/SOCl₂ Cells: Systematic Bench Tests
SYN-PUB-08973.text:
Effect of Duty Cycle and Inter-Pulse Interval on Voltage Recovery in Li/SOCl₂ Cells: Systematic Bench Tests (2022, journal, Journal of Power Sources and Applications).
Authors: Vuk Bačić (R0826); Dragana Petrović (outside co-author).
Keywords: voltage recovery; duty cycle; inter-pulse interval; Li/SOCl₂; state of discharge.
Voltage recovery after a current pulse is critical for reliable data transmission in intermittent wireless devices. This work examines how duty cycle (1 %–20 %) and inter-pulse interval (0.5 s–60 s) affect voltage recovery time and recovered terminal voltage in Li/SOCl₂ cells at three states of discharge (fresh, 50 % depleted, 80 % depleted). Tests were conducted on 45 cells across five lots from three manufacturers. Voltage recovery curves were fitted with a biexponential function; time constants τ₁ (fast, 0.1–0.9 s) and τ₂ (slow, 4–35 s) were extracted. τ₂ increases by a factor of 3.1 between fresh and 80 %-depleted states. At 20 % duty cycle and 0.5 s inter-pulse interval, recovered voltage at 80 % depletion falls 140 mV below the fresh-cell baseline—sufficient to cause transmission failure on 3.0 V-threshold radio modules. A simple lookup table parametrised on state-of-discharge and inter-pulse interval is proposed as a lightweight pre-transmission voltage check implementable on a Cortex-M0.

SYN-PUB-08974.title: Low-Power Embedded Energy Meters for In-Situ Primary Cell Characterisation on Deployed Sensor Nodes
SYN-PUB-08974.text:
Low-Power Embedded Energy Meters for In-Situ Primary Cell Characterisation on Deployed Sensor Nodes (2024, conference, Proceedings of the European Workshop on Wireless Sensor Systems (EW-WSS)).
Authors: Branislav Todorović (outside co-author); Vuk Bačić (R0826); Krisztián Molnár (outside co-author).
Keywords: energy meter; in-situ characterisation; sigma-delta ADC; low-power design; grain silo monitoring.
Characterising primary cells in situ on deployed sensor nodes is difficult because measurement hardware must not significantly perturb node energy consumption. This paper describes the design and validation of an embedded energy meter that draws under 9 µA average current from the measured cell and logs voltage, temperature, and accumulated charge to on-board flash at configurable intervals down to 100 ms. The meter uses a 24-bit sigma-delta ADC, a precision 10 mΩ current-sense resistor, and a Cortex-M0+ microcontroller in deep-sleep mode between samples. Calibration against a laboratory Keithley 2450 source-measure unit shows a current measurement error below 0.4 % over 0.1 mA–200 mA. The meter was validated on 12 nodes installed in a grain-silo humidity monitoring network. In-situ capacity estimates derived from logged data agreed with post-deployment laboratory capacity tests to within 3.8 % RMS. Board gerbers and firmware are published in an open repository.

SYN-PUB-08975.title: Temperature-Dependent Capacity Loss in Primary Lithium Cells: Separating Passivation and Electrolyte Conductivity Contributions via Frequency-Resolved Impedance
SYN-PUB-08975.text:
Temperature-Dependent Capacity Loss in Primary Lithium Cells: Separating Passivation and Electrolyte Conductivity Contributions via Frequency-Resolved Impedance (2025, journal, Journal of Applied Electrochemical Engineering).
Authors: Vuk Bačić (R0826); Nataša Đorđević (outside co-author); Dragana Petrović (outside co-author); Friederike Hartmann (outside co-author).
Keywords: DRT analysis; cold temperature; passivation; electrolyte conductivity; capacity loss.
At sub-zero temperatures, primary lithium cells lose usable capacity through two overlapping mechanisms: increased passivation-layer resistance and reduced electrolyte ionic conductivity. Disentangling these contributions is necessary for accurate cold-temperature lifetime models. This study applies distribution-of-relaxation-times (DRT) analysis to impedance spectra collected at nine temperatures between −20 °C and +45 °C on 36 Li/SOCl₂ cells at four states of discharge. DRT peaks are assigned to passivation, charge-transfer, and electrolyte processes using supporting DC polarisation data. The passivation contribution dominates the impedance increase below −5 °C, accounting for 68 % of total resistance rise at −20 °C, while the electrolyte contribution is dominant above +10 °C. An additive model combining both temperature functions fits the measured capacity-delivered data with an adjusted R² of 0.94 across all conditions. Implications for sensor-node deployment in unheated outdoor enclosures are discussed with reference to three case-study climatic zones in the western Balkans.

SYN-PUB-09629.title: A sub-threshold OTA topology for ECG front-ends in 180 nm CMOS with 320 nA supply current
SYN-PUB-09629.text:
A sub-threshold OTA topology for ECG front-ends in 180 nm CMOS with 320 nA supply current (2013, journal, Serbian Journal of Electrical Engineering).
Authors: Filip Mijatović (R0905); Dragan Vuković (outside co-author); Miroslav Petrović (outside co-author).
Keywords: sub-threshold OTA; ECG front-end; biopotential amplifier; CMOS 180 nm; low-power analogue.
This paper describes an operational transconductance amplifier designed to operate entirely in the sub-threshold region for use in single-lead ECG acquisition systems. The circuit was implemented in a 180 nm standard CMOS process. Biasing was set to achieve a quiescent current of 320 nA from a 1.2 V supply while maintaining an input-referred noise of 42 nV/√Hz at 100 Hz, sufficient for R-wave detection. The common-mode rejection ratio measured 78 dB across 20 fabricated dies. Electrode offset cancellation was addressed with a pseudo-resistor network whose impedance exceeded 10 GΩ at dc. Bandwidth could be digitally trimmed between 0.5 Hz and 150 Hz using a 3-bit switched-capacitor load. Measured results from twelve prototype boards equipped with dry Ag/AgCl electrodes showed SNR of 51 dB for a resting adult subject. Power consumption of the complete analogue chain, including a first-order high-pass filter, was 890 nW. The design occupies 0.041 mm² of active silicon area.

SYN-PUB-09630.title: Characterisation of packet collision statistics in IEEE 802.15.4 networks under periodic biomedical traffic patterns
SYN-PUB-09630.text:
Characterisation of packet collision statistics in IEEE 802.15.4 networks under periodic biomedical traffic patterns (2015, conference, Proceedings of the 22nd Telecommunications Forum TELFOR, Belgrade).
Authors: Filip Mijatović (R0905); Dragan Vuković (outside co-author); Ana Kovačević (outside co-author).
Keywords: IEEE 802.15.4; body-area network; CSMA/CA; packet delivery ratio; biomedical traffic.
Biomedical body-area networks impose deterministic, quasi-periodic traffic from multiple sensor nodes sampling at fixed physiological rates such as 250 Hz for EMG or 500 Hz for EEG. Standard CSMA/CA back-off procedures in IEEE 802.15.4 were evaluated through a combination of analytical modelling using a two-dimensional Markov chain and hardware experiments with fifteen custom nodes based on a CC2520 transceiver. Traffic was generated to emulate simultaneous ECG at 250 samples/s, SpO2 at 50 samples/s, and skin temperature at 1 sample/s. Packet delivery ratio dropped from 98.7% with a single node to 83.2% with six co-located nodes at the default back-off exponent settings. Adjusting the minimum back-off exponent from 3 to 5 and reducing the maximum number of back-offs from 5 to 3 recovered delivery ratio to 96.1% for six nodes, at the cost of a mean latency increase of 4.1 ms. The paper provides a lookup table of recommended parameter combinations for clinically relevant node counts.

SYN-PUB-09632.title: Duty-cycled MAC scheduling with deadline-aware slot allocation for implantable sensor nodes
SYN-PUB-09632.text:
Duty-cycled MAC scheduling with deadline-aware slot allocation for implantable sensor nodes (2018, journal, IEEE Transactions on Biomedical Circuits and Systems).
Authors: Filip Mijatović (R0905); Dragan Vuković (outside co-author); Christoph Brandner (outside co-author).
Keywords: MAC scheduling; deadline-aware; duty cycling; implantable sensor; IEEE 802.15.4.
This work, developed as part of the author's doctoral research, proposes a beacon-enabled superframe structure derived from IEEE 802.15.4 in which guaranteed time slots are assigned according to each sensor stream's sampling deadline rather than priority class alone. The scheduler runs on a body hub modelled as a 32-bit ARM Cortex-M3 at 4 MHz and accepts registration messages carrying a sampling period, payload size, and maximum tolerable latency for each node. A first-fit decreasing bin-packing heuristic assigns contiguous slots within each superframe. Simulation across 10,000 randomly generated workloads with 2–8 nodes showed that deadline miss rates remained below 0.3% for workloads at up to 80% superframe utilisation. Radio duty cycle for a six-node ECG plus EMG scenario was reduced to 1.8% compared with 6.4% under a fixed-slot baseline, yielding a projected 3.5-fold increase in node battery lifetime. The protocol was prototyped on a Cortex-M0 hub with four slave nodes and validated against simulated data.

SYN-PUB-09633.title: Low-power multi-electrode bioimpedance spectroscopy front-end for wearable fluid monitoring
SYN-PUB-09633.text:
Low-power multi-electrode bioimpedance spectroscopy front-end for wearable fluid monitoring (2019, journal, Sensors and Actuators A: Physical Circuits and Systems).
Authors: Filip Mijatović (R0905); Ana Kovačević (outside co-author); Jelena Marković (outside co-author); Tobias Weigand (outside co-author).
Keywords: bioimpedance spectroscopy; Howland current source; lock-in amplification; wearable; oedema.
Bioimpedance spectroscopy between 1 kHz and 1 MHz can track extracellular fluid shifts relevant to oedema management in heart failure patients. This paper describes a four-electrode analogue front-end implemented in discrete components on a flexible PCB targeting wrist-worn use. A current source based on a Howland pump injected 50 µA peak sinusoidal current; the driving waveform was generated by a DDS peripheral on a low-power ARM microcontroller. Voltage was sensed by an instrumentation amplifier with a gain-bandwidth product of 10 MHz and an input impedance exceeding 100 MΩ. Phase and magnitude were extracted by a hardware lock-in approach sampling at 50 kSa/s and performing 16-point coherent averaging on the microcontroller. Average system current consumption was 1.4 mA during a 200 ms measurement burst and 3.8 µA in sleep. Accuracy of extracted resistance and reactance was within 1.2% of values measured with a laboratory impedance analyser across a 30-sample tissue-equivalent phantom set covering the physiological range of 20–800 Ω.

SYN-PUB-09635.title: Energy harvesting from body heat for wearable ECG patches: thermoelectric generator characterisation and power management circuit
SYN-PUB-09635.text:
Energy harvesting from body heat for wearable ECG patches: thermoelectric generator characterisation and power management circuit (2023, journal, Journal of Power Sources Electronics).
Authors: Filip Mijatović (R0905); Ana Kovačević (outside co-author); Radovan Ilić (outside co-author).
Keywords: thermoelectric harvesting; wearable ECG; boost converter; MPPT; body heat.
Wearable ECG patches worn continuously on the thorax can harvest energy from the skin-to-air temperature gradient, which typically spans 3–8 K in indoor environments. This work characterises six commercial thermoelectric generator (TEG) modules with active areas of 10–40 mm² under a simulated skin load using a temperature-controlled copper plate and forced convection at 0.5 m/s. Open-circuit voltages ranged from 18 mV to 74 mV at a 5 K gradient. A boost converter based on the BQ25504 integrated circuit with an impedance-matching network achieved maximum power point tracking efficiency of 82% across the characterised voltage range. Harvested power delivered to a 4.7 µF storage capacitor reached 48 µW at 5 K gradient for the 30 mm² module. A duty-cycle controller using a comparator and a timer allowed the ECG front-end described in a previous paper to operate from the harvested supply alone when the gradient exceeded 4.2 K, as verified over 48-hour benchtop trials. Implications for electrode placement and garment integration are discussed.

SYN-PUB-09636.title: Compressed sensing reconstruction for sparse EEG signals acquired by sub-mW wireless nodes: a comparison of three recovery algorithms
SYN-PUB-09636.text:
Compressed sensing reconstruction for sparse EEG signals acquired by sub-mW wireless nodes: a comparison of three recovery algorithms (2025, journal, Biomedical Signal Processing and Circuits).
Authors: Filip Mijatović (R0905); Stefan Horvat (outside co-author); Milena Savić (outside co-author); Paweł Nowak (outside co-author).
Keywords: compressed sensing; EEG; sparse recovery; OMP; BPDN; wireless BAN.
EEG signals exhibit sparsity in the wavelet domain; compressed sensing (CS) can therefore reduce the number of samples transmitted over a wireless link, cutting radio energy. This paper evaluates three recovery algorithms — basis pursuit denoising (BPDN), orthogonal matching pursuit (OMP), and iteratively reweighted least squares (IRLS) — applied to EEG segments recorded from eight healthy subjects performing an eyes-open resting task. Compression ratios of 2×, 4×, and 8× were tested by randomly sub-sampling a 256 Hz, 16-channel stream at the sensor node simulated in MATLAB. At a 4× ratio, BPDN achieved a mean per-channel SNR of 28.3 dB, OMP 24.7 dB, and IRLS 27.9 dB. Clinical-grade feature detection for alpha-band power (8–13 Hz) was preserved with less than 5% relative error for BPDN and IRLS at 4× but degraded sharply at 8×. Transmission energy savings estimated from a Cortex-M0 radio model were 61% at 4× compression after accounting for the reconstruction overhead run on the hub.

SYN-PUB-09637.title: A 0.6 V, 210 nW instrumentation amplifier with reconfigurable gain for multi-modal biopotential acquisition in 65 nm CMOS
SYN-PUB-09637.text:
A 0.6 V, 210 nW instrumentation amplifier with reconfigurable gain for multi-modal biopotential acquisition in 65 nm CMOS (2026, journal, IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems I: Regular Papers).
Authors: Milena Savić (outside co-author); Filip Mijatović (R0905); Christoph Brandner (outside co-author); Luca Ferretti (outside co-author).
Keywords: instrumentation amplifier; CCIA; 65 nm CMOS; biopotential; sub-volt supply; reconfigurable gain.
This paper presents a capacitively-coupled instrumentation amplifier (CCIA) fabricated in a 65 nm low-power CMOS process and intended to serve both ECG (gain 40 dB, bandwidth 0.5–150 Hz) and EEG (gain 52 dB, bandwidth 0.5–80 Hz) acquisition modes selectable at run time via a 1-bit digital input. Supply voltage is 0.6 V drawn from an energy-harvesting rail. Total quiescent current across both amplifier stages is 350 nA. Input-referred noise integrated over the ECG band is 0.41 µVrms, and over the EEG band is 0.37 µVrms. The mid-band CMRR measured 91 dB for ECG mode and 88 dB for EEG mode. Electrode offset rejection was verified with offsets up to ±300 mV applied via a dc servo loop consuming 18 nA. The circuit was characterised on 20 dies; gain spread across dies was ±0.4 dB. Post-layout simulations and measured data are compared and show less than 6% discrepancy in noise and 3% in bandwidth.

SYN-PUB-09638.title: Cutting false atrial fibrillation alarms in patch ECG with motion-aware filtering
SYN-PUB-09638.text:
Cutting false atrial fibrillation alarms in patch ECG with motion-aware filtering (2024, journal, Journal of Biomedical Signal Analysis).
Authors: Maja Popović (R0906); Dragan Ilić (outside co-author); Sonja Vukić (outside co-author); Luka Horvat (outside co-author).
Patch-based ECG monitors are increasingly deployed for continuous ambulatory cardiac surveillance, yet their clinical utility is severely limited by high false-positive rates for atrial fibrillation (AF) alarms, largely attributable to motion artifacts. This paper presents a motion-aware filtering framework that fuses single-lead ECG signals with three-axis accelerometer data recorded simultaneously by the same wearable patch. The proposed method employs an adaptive notch filter whose coefficients are dynamically updated according to a motion-intensity index derived from accelerometer magnitude. A subsequent AF detector based on RR-interval irregularity metrics is applied to the cleaned signal. The system was evaluated on a dataset of 312 twenty-four-hour recordings collected from 89 volunteers performing standardized daily activities including walking, stair climbing, and cycling. Compared with a baseline detector operating on raw ECG, the proposed approach reduced false AF alarms by 61% while maintaining sensitivity above 94% on confirmed AF episodes verified by a board-certified cardiologist. Processing latency was benchmarked on an ARM Cortex-M4 platform, confirming real-time feasibility. The results demonstrate that tightly coupled motion-aware signal conditioning is essential for trustworthy AF screening in free-living conditions.

SYN-PUB-09639.title: Single-lead ECG arrhythmia classification on a microcontroller
SYN-PUB-09639.text:
Single-lead ECG arrhythmia classification on a microcontroller (2022, conference, Conference on Medical Devices Engineering).
Authors: Nemanja Đorđević (outside co-author); Maja Popović (R0906); Tijana Marković (outside co-author).
Arrhythmia classification in wearable cardiac monitors demands algorithms compact enough to execute entirely on the sensor node, eliminating reliance on continuous cloud connectivity. This paper describes the design and validation of a single-lead ECG arrhythmia classifier implemented on a low-power 32-bit microcontroller (ARM Cortex-M0+, 48 MHz, 32 kB RAM). The classifier distinguishes five rhythm classes—normal sinus rhythm, atrial fibrillation, premature ventricular contractions, supraventricular tachycardia, and noise—using a lightweight feature set comprising RR-interval statistics, QRS morphology descriptors, and a three-stage decision-tree ensemble. Memory-efficient quantization reduces all floating-point parameters to 8-bit fixed-point representations without measurable accuracy loss. Evaluated on a held-out split of 4,200 annotated 30-second segments, the on-device model achieved a macro-averaged F1 score of 0.87 and consumed an average of 1.4 mW during inference, enabling operation for more than 72 hours on a 180 mAh coin cell. The work demonstrates a practical pathway toward fully autonomous, battery-powered cardiac monitors suitable for remote patient monitoring in resource-limited settings.

SYN-PUB-09640.title: Activity recognition from chest-worn accelerometers
SYN-PUB-09640.text:
Activity recognition from chest-worn accelerometers (2021, journal, Wearable Sensing Review).
Authors: Maja Popović (R0906); Ana Stevanović (outside co-author); Miloš Radović (outside co-author).
Accurate activity recognition from chest-worn inertial measurement units is a prerequisite for context-aware physiological monitoring, yet most published benchmarks rely on wrist or hip placements. This study investigates the suitability of a single chest-mounted accelerometer for recognizing twelve daily-life activities including rest, walking, jogging, stair ascent and descent, cycling, and six sedentary postures. Features extracted in the time and frequency domains from three-axis acceleration signals were used to train and compare a k-nearest neighbor classifier, a random forest, and a support vector machine with radial basis function kernel. Data were collected from 45 healthy adults across a structured protocol lasting approximately 90 minutes per participant. The random forest achieved the highest overall accuracy of 92.3% in leave-one-subject-out cross-validation. A confusion analysis revealed that the chest location provides particularly strong discrimination between static postures, outperforming wrist placement on that sub-task. The findings support the integration of chest-worn accelerometers into ECG patch monitors for simultaneous cardiac and activity monitoring without additional sensor hardware.

SYN-PUB-09641.title: Benchmark dataset for motion-corrupted patch ECG and simultaneous accelerometry in free-living adults
SYN-PUB-09641.text:
Benchmark dataset for motion-corrupted patch ECG and simultaneous accelerometry in free-living adults (2023, journal, Data in Biomedical Engineering (Open Access Journal)).
Authors: Maja Popović (R0906); Sonja Vukić (outside co-author); Dragan Ilić (outside co-author); Petra Kovač (outside co-author).
Keywords: benchmark dataset; patch ECG; accelerometry; atrial fibrillation; motion artifact; open data.
High-quality annotated datasets pairing ambulatory ECG recordings with synchronised inertial data from the same wearable patch remain scarce, hampering reproducible research on motion-artifact suppression and context-aware cardiac monitoring. This paper describes the NovaSAD-PatchECG dataset: 128 recordings of 48 hours each, collected from 64 healthy volunteers and 64 patients with known arrhythmia history. Each recording includes single-lead ECG sampled at 500 Hz, three-axis accelerometer data at 100 Hz, and ground-truth rhythm annotations produced by two independent cardiologists with inter-annotator agreement reported via Cohen's kappa. Participants performed a standardized protocol encompassing controlled laboratory activities and unrestricted daily life. The dataset captures a diverse range of motion intensities, electrode contact qualities, and arrhythmia types. Baseline performance figures for three published AF detectors are reported to facilitate fair future comparisons. The dataset is released under an open-access licence and accompanied by Python-based loading utilities. We anticipate that this resource will accelerate development and fair benchmarking of wearable cardiac monitoring algorithms, particularly those addressing false-alarm reduction and real-time on-device inference.

SYN-PUB-09642.title: Federated learning for atrial fibrillation detection across heterogeneous wearable ECG devices
SYN-PUB-09642.text:
Federated learning for atrial fibrillation detection across heterogeneous wearable ECG devices (2024, journal, IEEE Transactions on Biomedical Engineering).
Authors: Luka Horvat (outside co-author); Maja Popović (R0906); Radovan Bešlin (outside co-author); Elena Ferreira (outside co-author).
Keywords: federated learning; atrial fibrillation; ECG; wearable; privacy-preserving; domain adaptation.
Training robust atrial fibrillation detectors on data pooled from multiple clinical sites raises significant patient privacy concerns. Federated learning (FL) offers a privacy-preserving alternative by training shared model parameters without centralizing raw recordings. This work presents a federated AF detection framework tailored to the heterogeneous signal characteristics encountered when aggregating data from four distinct wearable ECG patch platforms with differing sampling rates, electrode configurations, and noise profiles. A domain-adaptive normalization layer is inserted before each local model head to compensate for device-specific distributional shifts. Communication efficiency is improved through gradient sparsification with a threshold calibrated per round. Experiments conducted on data partitioned across five simulated client nodes demonstrate that the federated model achieves within 2.1 percentage points of a centrally trained oracle in terms of F1 score for AF detection, while keeping raw data entirely local. Convergence analysis shows stable training within 35 communication rounds. The proposed approach is directly applicable to collaborative model development between hospitals and medical device manufacturers operating under strict data governance constraints.

SYN-PUB-09643.title: Energy-efficient QRS detection on ultra-low-power microcontrollers for long-term cardiac patches
SYN-PUB-09643.text:
Energy-efficient QRS detection on ultra-low-power microcontrollers for long-term cardiac patches (2022, journal, Biomedical Microdevices and Embedded Systems Journal).
Authors: Maja Popović (R0906); Nemanja Đorđević (outside co-author); Marko Tešić (outside co-author).
Keywords: QRS detection; ultra-low-power; microcontroller; wearable ECG; integer arithmetic; cardiac patch.
Battery life is the dominant constraint for wearable cardiac patches intended for multi-week arrhythmia screening. This paper presents an ultra-low-power QRS detection algorithm specifically designed for deployment on a 16-bit microcontroller operating at 8 MHz with 4 kB of available SRAM. The algorithm adapts the classical Pan–Tompkins pipeline by replacing floating-point operations with integer arithmetic and replacing the bandpass filter with a computationally cheaper differentiator-squarer cascade whose coefficients are pre-quantized to powers of two, enabling shift-based multiplication. Threshold adaptation is reformulated as a recursive integer update requiring no division. The implementation is benchmarked on five publicly available ECG databases totalling over 120,000 annotated beats, achieving a detection sensitivity of 99.1% and positive predictivity of 98.9%. On the target microcontroller, the algorithm consumes 87 μW at 500 Hz input, extending projected patch lifetime from 9 to 21 days compared with a floating-point baseline at equivalent sampling rate. The source code is released openly to support reproducibility and adoption in resource-constrained medical device development.

SYN-PUB-09644.title: Combining heart rate variability and accelerometer features for stress detection in free-living conditions
SYN-PUB-09644.text:
Combining heart rate variability and accelerometer features for stress detection in free-living conditions (2023, conference, Sensors and Wearable Systems Conference).
Authors: Maja Popović (R0906); Ana Stevanović (outside co-author); Katarina Lukić (outside co-author).
Keywords: stress detection; heart rate variability; accelerometer; wearable; free-living; multimodal.
Continuous stress monitoring in everyday life has attracted growing interest as a tool for preventive mental health management, yet most validated methods require laboratory-controlled conditions. This paper investigates a multimodal approach that fuses heart rate variability (HRV) indices derived from a chest-worn ECG patch with accelerometer-based activity features to infer subjective stress levels in free-living adults. Thirty-six participants wore the sensor system continuously for five days while self-reporting stress events via a smartphone application. A total of 41 time-domain, frequency-domain, and nonlinear HRV features were extracted over non-overlapping five-minute windows and combined with six activity context features capturing posture and movement intensity. A random forest classifier trained with leave-one-day-out cross-validation achieved a binary stress/non-stress accuracy of 76.4%, improving by 8.3 percentage points over HRV-only baselines. Analysis of feature importance revealed that low-frequency HRV power and accelerometer-derived posture class were the two most discriminative predictors. The study highlights that activity context is an important confound in wearable stress detection and should be accounted for in algorithm design.

SYN-PUB-09645.title: Signal quality assessment for single-lead wearable ECG: a survey and comparative study
SYN-PUB-09645.text:
Signal quality assessment for single-lead wearable ECG: a survey and comparative study (2021, journal, Biomedical Signal Processing and Control).
Authors: Maja Popović (R0906); Dragan Ilić (outside co-author); Milena Vujović (outside co-author).
Keywords: signal quality assessment; wearable ECG; single-lead; arrhythmia detection; survey; embedded systems.
Reliable automatic interpretation of single-lead wearable ECG recordings is contingent upon accurate signal quality assessment (SQA), yet no consensus exists on the best methodology for this task. This survey reviews 38 SQA algorithms published between 2010 and 2022, categorizing them by feature type (statistical, spectral, template-based, and learned), classification strategy, and target application domain. We implement and comparatively evaluate nine representative approaches on two independent ECG datasets collected with chest-worn patches under both controlled and free-living conditions. Evaluation metrics include per-segment quality classification accuracy, computational cost on an ARM Cortex-M4 platform, and downstream impact on AF detector performance when SQA-based segment rejection is applied as a pre-processing gate. Results show that lightweight spectral flatness combined with kurtosis achieves the best accuracy-to-cost trade-off for real-time embedded use, while deep-learning approaches yield superior accuracy at much higher computational expense. The survey concludes with a discussion of open challenges including cross-device generalization and labelling inconsistencies across public datasets.

SYN-PUB-09646.title: Wearable biomedical systems: signal acquisition, processing and clinical translation
SYN-PUB-09646.text:
Wearable biomedical systems: signal acquisition, processing and clinical translation (2023, book chapter, Advances in Wearable Health Technology (Springer)).
Authors: Maja Popović (R0906); Dragan Ilić (outside co-author); Petra Kovač (outside co-author); Sonja Vukić (outside co-author).
Keywords: wearable systems; biomedical signal processing; ECG; clinical translation; medical device regulation; embedded algorithms.
This book chapter provides a comprehensive overview of the engineering challenges involved in translating wearable biomedical sensing systems from laboratory prototypes to clinically validated devices. The chapter covers the full signal chain from electrode–skin interface physics and analog front-end design through digital signal processing pipelines to clinical validation methodology. Particular attention is paid to the interplay between hardware constraints—power budget, memory, communication bandwidth—and algorithm design choices for cardiac and motion signals. The ECG acquisition and arrhythmia detection pipeline is used as a running example throughout, illustrating how design decisions at each layer propagate to end-to-end system performance. A dedicated section addresses regulatory considerations under the European Medical Device Regulation (MDR 2017/745) relevant to software-as-a-medical-device classification of on-device diagnostic algorithms. The chapter concludes with a roadmap for future research directions including personalized adaptive algorithms, multi-sensor fusion, and privacy-preserving distributed learning. It is intended as a graduate-level reference for students and practitioners entering the field of wearable medical technology.

SYN-PUB-09647.title: Personalized adaptive thresholds for arrhythmia detectors in long-term ECG monitoring
SYN-PUB-09647.text:
Personalized adaptive thresholds for arrhythmia detectors in long-term ECG monitoring (2020, conference, International Conference on Biomedical Signal and Image Processing).
Authors: Luka Horvat (outside co-author); Radovan Bešlin (outside co-author); Maja Popović (R0906).
Keywords: adaptive thresholds; arrhythmia detection; personalization; atrial fibrillation; wearable ECG; Bayesian update.
Fixed detection thresholds in ambulatory arrhythmia monitors fail to account for inter-individual variability in cardiac electrophysiology and body habitus, leading to systematically elevated false-positive rates in certain patient subgroups. This paper proposes a patient-adaptive threshold framework for wearable ECG arrhythmia detectors in which detection parameters are continuously updated using an online Bayesian update rule applied to a rolling window of high-confidence rhythm annotations from the preceding monitoring period. The method requires no pre-training on patient-specific data and is therefore directly applicable from the first hour of monitoring. Computational overhead is bounded to allow deployment alongside an existing QRS detector on an ARM Cortex-M4 microcontroller. The framework is evaluated on long-term recordings from 58 patients with documented paroxysmal AF. Compared with fixed-threshold detectors, the adaptive approach reduces the per-patient median false-alarm rate by 47% while maintaining sensitivity above 91% across all subgroups stratified by age, sex, and body mass index. The results support patient-adaptive personalization as a practical and computationally tractable strategy for improving specificity in clinical-grade wearable cardiac monitors.

SYN-PUB-09743.title: Generating Minimum-Size Covering Arrays for Constrained Parameter Spaces in Automotive Middleware
SYN-PUB-09743.text:
Generating Minimum-Size Covering Arrays for Constrained Parameter Spaces in Automotive Middleware (2013, conference, Proceedings of the International Workshop on Automated Software Testing in Embedded Systems (IASTES)).
Authors: Martina Lačoková (R0919); Branislav Tešanović (outside co-author); Miroslav Opačić (outside co-author).
Keywords: covering arrays; MAX-SAT; constraint handling; automotive middleware; t-way testing.
Automotive middleware stacks expose large parameter spaces whose valid combinations are restricted by physical and logical constraints. Unconstrained covering array construction tends to produce test suites containing infeasible configurations, inflating execution time and masking real faults. This paper formulates constrained t-way covering array generation as a weighted partial MAX-SAT problem and evaluates three solvers—Glucose, CryptoMiniSat and a custom greedy heuristic—on eight industrial parameter models taken from a CAN-based body-electronics platform. For strength t = 2 and t = 3, the SAT-based approach reduces suite size by 18–34% compared to the greedy baseline while keeping generation time below 90 seconds for models with up to 40 parameters and 120 constraint clauses. Fault detection rates were measured against a seeded mutation set of 480 faults; the constrained suites achieved 91.4% detection versus 89.7% for unconstrained suites of equal size.

SYN-PUB-09744.title: Interface Contract Specification for Multi-Supplier CAN Node Integration: A Formal Framework
SYN-PUB-09744.text:
Interface Contract Specification for Multi-Supplier CAN Node Integration: A Formal Framework (2015, journal, Journal of Embedded Software Engineering and Reliability).
Authors: Katarina Ilić-Vukić (outside co-author); Martina Lačoková (R0919); Péter Halmosi (outside co-author).
Keywords: interface contracts; assume-guarantee; CAN bus; AUTOSAR; formal specification.
When ECUs from different suppliers share a CAN bus, integration failures frequently arise from incompatible assumptions about message timing, signal encoding and error-handling behaviour. This paper presents a contract language, CAN-CL, based on assume-guarantee reasoning extended with real-time guards and bounded-integer signal domains. Contracts are written per node and per message group; a static checker verifies pairwise consistency before any hardware is available. The framework was applied retrospectively to a 14-node powertrain network. Among 37 documented integration bugs from the project history, static contract checking would have flagged 22 prior to bench testing, covering timing violations, byte-order mismatches and unhandled error frames. The paper details the contract syntax, the consistency-checking algorithm and its complexity, and discusses the mapping to AUTOSAR ComStack configurations.

SYN-PUB-09745.title: Evaluating Strength-3 Combinatorial Test Suites Against Real Field Faults in a CAN Stack Implementation
SYN-PUB-09745.text:
Evaluating Strength-3 Combinatorial Test Suites Against Real Field Faults in a CAN Stack Implementation (2019, journal, Empirical Software Engineering and Testing).
Authors: Miroslav Opačić (outside co-author); Martina Lačoková (R0919); Sonja Vraneš-Kovač (outside co-author).
Keywords: combinatorial testing; field faults; CAN stack; interaction order; coverage analysis.
Most empirical studies of combinatorial interaction testing rely on seeded or synthetic faults. This study evaluates t = 2 and t = 3 covering arrays against a corpus of 214 confirmed field faults extracted from maintenance records of a commercial CAN protocol stack used in agricultural machinery. Faults were classified by interaction order using a backward-coverage analysis: each fault was mapped to the smallest parameter interaction that would expose it. Results show 71% of faults are covered at t = 2 and 89% at t = 3, with diminishing returns beyond t = 3 (91% at t = 4). Suite sizes at t = 3 were 38–62% larger than at t = 2 across six parameter models; we quantify this cost against detection gain and discuss which fault categories resist coverage at any practical strength.

SYN-PUB-09746.title: Specification and Automated Checking of Timing Contracts for Multi-Frame CAN FD Messages
SYN-PUB-09746.text:
Specification and Automated Checking of Timing Contracts for Multi-Frame CAN FD Messages (2020, conference, Proceedings of the Symposium on Formal Methods for Industrial Embedded Networks (SFMIEN)).
Authors: Martina Lačoková (R0919); Katarina Ilić-Vukić (outside co-author); Péter Halmosi (outside co-author); Andrei Moldovan (outside co-author).
Keywords: CAN FD; timing contracts; timed automata; UPPAAL; multi-frame protocols.
CAN FD allows payloads of up to 64 bytes, enabling protocol designers to split application data across multiple frames within a single bus cycle. This introduces ordering and timing dependencies that are absent in classical CAN and are not addressed by existing contract formalisms designed for single-frame messages. We extend CAN-CL with frame-sequence guards, specifying allowable inter-frame gaps, mandatory acknowledgement windows and abort conditions. An automated checker based on timed automata model checking (UPPAAL 4.1) is implemented and evaluated on four CAN FD configurations. Verification of a 12-message sequence contract with 6 participating nodes completes in under 4 minutes on standard hardware. Three previously undetected timing hazards were found in one of the supplied configurations when contracts were tightened from their original loose bounds.

SYN-PUB-09747.title: A Benchmark Suite for Constrained Covering Array Generators: Construction, Characteristics and Baseline Results
SYN-PUB-09747.text:
A Benchmark Suite for Constrained Covering Array Generators: Construction, Characteristics and Baseline Results (2021, journal, Software Testing, Verification and Reliability — Special Issue on Testing Benchmarks).
Authors: Branislav Tešanović (outside co-author); Martina Lačoková (R0919); Luca Benedetti-Farro (outside co-author).
Keywords: covering arrays; benchmark suite; constraint density; generator comparison; reproducibility.
Progress in constrained covering array generation is hindered by the lack of a shared, publicly documented benchmark collection. We describe the construction of CovBench-CAN, a suite of 52 parameter models derived from real CAN-based embedded configurations with constraints anonymised for public release. Each model is characterised by parameter count (4–61), domain sizes, constraint density and tightness, and the number of valid t-tuples at t = 2 and t = 3. Baseline results are reported for five generators: ACTS, TestCoverage, an in-house SAT-based tool and two metaheuristic approaches. Across the suite, solver performance varies substantially: no single generator dominates on all metrics. The benchmark and scripts are released under an open licence to facilitate reproducible comparisons. We discuss lessons learned about constraint encoding and the sensitivity of generator performance to domain ordering.

SYN-PUB-09748.title: Incremental Test Suite Maintenance for Evolving CAN Interface Contracts
SYN-PUB-09748.text:
Incremental Test Suite Maintenance for Evolving CAN Interface Contracts (2022, journal, Journal of Systems and Software).
Authors: Miroslav Opačić (outside co-author); Martina Lačoková (R0919); Andrei Moldovan (outside co-author).
Keywords: incremental testing; covering array maintenance; software evolution; CAN interface; test suite repair.
(no abstract)

SYN-PUB-09749.title: Cross-Layer Interaction Faults in Multi-Supplier Embedded Stacks: A Taxonomy and Detection Study
SYN-PUB-09749.text:
Cross-Layer Interaction Faults in Multi-Supplier Embedded Stacks: A Taxonomy and Detection Study (2023, journal, IEEE Transactions on Software Engineering).
Authors: Martina Lačoková (R0919); Jochen Wernstedt (outside co-author); Tatjana Davidović-Šimić (outside co-author); Sonja Vraneš-Kovač (outside co-author).
Keywords: cross-layer faults; multi-supplier integration; fault taxonomy; combinatorial testing; automotive software.
Multi-supplier embedded stacks combine hardware abstraction layers, communication drivers, protocol stacks and application components from different vendors. Faults that manifest at integration time often involve interactions spanning two or more layers, yet testing strategies typically treat layers independently. This paper presents a taxonomy of cross-layer interaction faults assembled from post-mortem analyses of 19 integration projects in the automotive and industrial automation sectors, covering 312 documented faults. The taxonomy comprises 11 fault categories grouped under three themes: resource aliasing, contract silences and emergent timing. For each category we assess detectability by unit testing, pairwise integration testing and t-way combinatorial testing at t ∈ {2, 3, 4}. Categories involving three or more layers require t ≥ 3 for reliable detection. The taxonomy is proposed as a basis for checklist-driven integration reviews.

SYN-PUB-09750.title: Monitoring Overhead Profiles for CAN-CL Runtime Contracts Across Six Microcontroller Families
SYN-PUB-09750.text:
Monitoring Overhead Profiles for CAN-CL Runtime Contracts Across Six Microcontroller Families (2025, journal, Journal of Real-Time Systems and Embedded Architectures).
Authors: Martina Lačoková (R0919); Nikola Bogdanović-Đurić (outside co-author); Luca Benedetti-Farro (outside co-author); Andrei Moldovan (outside co-author).
Keywords: runtime monitoring; microcontroller benchmarking; CAN-CL; overhead profiling; embedded targets.
Earlier work demonstrated CAN-CL runtime monitoring on a single microcontroller target. This paper broadens the evaluation across six representative 32-bit microcontroller families (two ARM Cortex-M4 variants, one Cortex-M7, one RISC-V, one TriCore and one PowerPC e200) commonly used in automotive and industrial embedded systems. For each target, monitors were generated from the same set of 12 canonical contracts and instrumented into a reference CAN stack. CPU overhead, stack usage, code size and worst-case response time were measured. Overhead ranged from 1.8% to 5.6% CPU utilisation across targets, driven primarily by differences in interrupt latency and cache behaviour rather than core clock speed. Stack additions were uniformly below 320 bytes. The results inform compiler flag choices and memory allocation policies and are provided as a configuration guide for practitioners.

SYN-PUB-09804.title: A transformer model pre-trained on Serbian web text
SYN-PUB-09804.text:
A transformer model pre-trained on Serbian web text (2024, conference, Workshop on Slavic Language Technology).
Authors: Milan Petrović (R0925); Jovana Ilić (outside co-author); Dragan Vasiljević (outside co-author); Katarina Horvat (outside co-author).
This paper presents SrbBERT-Web, a transformer language model pre-trained from scratch on a large-scale crawl of Serbian web text comprising approximately 14 billion tokens. We describe the data collection and cleaning pipeline, which addresses noise specific to Serbian web content, including mixed-script documents, informal spelling variations, and code-switched passages. The model adopts a RoBERTa-style architecture and is trained with dynamic masking on deduplicated data. We evaluate SrbBERT-Web on four downstream tasks: named entity recognition, sentiment analysis, morphological tagging, and extractive question answering, comparing it against multilingual baselines such as mBERT and XLM-R, as well as against smaller domain-specific Serbian models. SrbBERT-Web consistently outperforms all baselines on three of the four tasks, with especially pronounced gains on question answering and sentiment analysis. We release the model weights, tokenizer, and pre-training corpus metadata under open licenses to support further research on Serbian language technology. We also provide a detailed analysis of tokenization efficiency, showing that a vocabulary trained specifically on Serbian text significantly reduces token-per-word ratios compared to multilingual vocabularies.

SYN-PUB-09805.title: Dense retrieval for Serbian customer-support questions
SYN-PUB-09805.text:
Dense retrieval for Serbian customer-support questions (2023, journal, Journal of Language Engineering).
Authors: Milan Petrović (R0925); Nevena Stanković (outside co-author); Luka Đorđević (outside co-author).
This paper investigates dense passage retrieval (DPR) for Serbian customer-support question answering. Customer-support interactions in Serbian present unique challenges: queries are short and colloquial, answers are embedded in lengthy policy documents, and the corpus contains both Latin and Cyrillic script. We construct a new benchmark dataset, SrbCSQA, containing 4,200 question–passage pairs collected from publicly available support portals and annotated by native speakers. We fine-tune a bi-encoder retrieval model initialised from a Serbian transformer checkpoint and compare it against BM25, a multilingual DPR baseline, and a cross-encoder re-ranker. Experiments show that our fine-tuned bi-encoder achieves a mean reciprocal rank of 0.73, outperforming BM25 by 18 percentage points and the multilingual baseline by 11 points. We further study the effect of script normalisation as a preprocessing step and show that it consistently improves retrieval quality. Error analysis reveals that lexical gaps between formal policy language and informal user queries remain the primary failure mode. We release the SrbCSQA benchmark and fine-tuned model under open licenses.

SYN-PUB-09806.title: Handling Latin and Cyrillic script in one embedding space
SYN-PUB-09806.text:
Handling Latin and Cyrillic script in one embedding space (2022, conference, Conference on Computational Linguistics in the Balkans).
Authors: Ana Mirković (outside co-author); Bojan Savić (outside co-author); Milan Petrović (R0925); Tijana Relić (outside co-author).
Texts in Serbian are written in both the Latin and Cyrillic scripts, often within the same corpus or even the same document. Existing multilingual embedding models treat these as largely separate character sequences, resulting in poor cross-script semantic alignment. This paper proposes a script-unified embedding approach that maps Latin-script and Cyrillic-script Serbian sentences to a shared vector space. We achieve this through a three-stage training procedure: (1) initialisation from a multilingual sentence encoder, (2) contrastive fine-tuning on automatically generated Latin–Cyrillic parallel pairs obtained by deterministic transliteration, and (3) hard-negative mining using nearest-neighbour retrieval. We evaluate semantic textual similarity and cross-script retrieval on newly constructed Serbian benchmarks and on a subset of the XSTS evaluation suite. Our model closes 84% of the cosine-similarity gap between same-script and cross-script sentence pairs while maintaining competitive performance on standard STS tasks. We release the model, training data, and evaluation scripts. The approach is lightweight, requiring no manual annotation of cross-script pairs, and can be extended to other language communities with dual-script traditions.

SYN-PUB-09807.title: SrbNER: a named entity recognition corpus and baseline models for Serbian
SYN-PUB-09807.text:
SrbNER: a named entity recognition corpus and baseline models for Serbian (2023, conference, Proceedings of the International Conference on Language Resources and Evaluation for South-East European Languages).
Authors: Jovana Ilić (outside co-author); Tijana Relić (outside co-author); Stefan Novaković (outside co-author); Milan Petrović (R0925).
Keywords: named entity recognition; Serbian NLP; annotation; transformer fine-tuning; sequence labelling.
Named entity recognition (NER) is a foundational NLP task, yet Serbian has lacked a large, openly licensed NER corpus with consistent annotation guidelines. This paper introduces SrbNER, a corpus of 120,000 tokens drawn from news, social media, and administrative text, manually annotated with seven entity categories: person, organisation, location, event, product, law, and date. We describe the annotation scheme, adjudication process, and inter-annotator agreement, which reached a Cohen's kappa of 0.87. We train and evaluate several baseline models: a CRF tagger with hand-crafted features, a BiLSTM-CRF model, and three transformer-based sequence labellers fine-tuned from mBERT, XLM-R, and SrbBERT-Web respectively. The transformer baselines substantially outperform the CRF and BiLSTM approaches, with SrbBERT-Web achieving an F1 of 89.4 on the test set. We analyse per-category performance and find that product and law entities are the most difficult, largely due to inconsistent surface forms and low frequency in the training data. SrbNER and all baseline model weights are released publicly to accelerate Serbian NLP research.

SYN-PUB-09808.title: Extractive question answering for Serbian: dataset construction and model evaluation
SYN-PUB-09808.text:
Extractive question answering for Serbian: dataset construction and model evaluation (2024, conference, ACL Findings).
Authors: Milan Petrović (R0925); Nevena Stanković (outside co-author); Dragan Vasiljević (outside co-author); Marta Filipović (outside co-author).
Keywords: question answering; extractive QA; Serbian NLP; span extraction; dataset construction.
We present SrbQA-Ext, the first large-scale extractive question answering dataset for Serbian, containing 11,400 question–answer pairs grounded in Wikipedia-derived passages. Questions were elicited from native-speaker annotators who read a passage and formulated answerable questions; each answer is a contiguous span within the passage. We additionally include 1,200 unanswerable questions to test model abstention. The dataset covers eight topic domains and is balanced across Latin and Cyrillic script versions to prevent script-specific overfitting. We establish baselines using mBERT, XLM-R-large, and our in-house SrbBERT-Web model fine-tuned with the standard span-extraction objective. SrbBERT-Web achieves an exact match of 62.1 and an F1 of 78.4 on the development set, surpassing XLM-R-large by 3.2 F1 points despite having fewer parameters. We analyse common error types, showing that multi-sentence reasoning and numerical inference are the leading sources of error. We also conduct a cross-lingual transfer experiment in which models trained on translated SQuAD data are compared against our natively constructed dataset, demonstrating the importance of domain-appropriate, language-native training data. All resources are publicly available.

SYN-PUB-09810.title: Retrieval-augmented generation for Serbian: adapting RAG pipelines to a morphologically rich language
SYN-PUB-09810.text:
Retrieval-augmented generation for Serbian: adapting RAG pipelines to a morphologically rich language (2024, conference, EMNLP 2024 Workshop on Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Knowledge-Intensive NLP).
Authors: Luka Đorđević (outside co-author); Stefan Novaković (outside co-author); Milan Petrović (R0925).
Keywords: retrieval-augmented generation; Serbian NLP; morphological richness; dense retrieval; generative models.
Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) combines a retrieval component with a generative language model to produce factual, grounded responses. Most RAG research targets English, where morphological simplicity makes keyword and dense retrieval effective. Serbian, as a morphologically rich language with six grammatical cases and free word order, poses distinctive challenges: inflected query terms may not match base forms in the index, and sentence boundary detection is complicated by enclitic clitics.
