This paper adapts a full RAG pipeline to Serbian by integrating our dense retrieval model with a multilingual generative model fine-tuned on Serbian instruction data. We introduce lemma-expanded dense retrieval, in which query embeddings are averaged over all inflected forms of content words as predicted by a morphological analyser. On the SrbCSQA benchmark, this approach improves ROUGE-L by 6.1 points over a vanilla bi-encoder retrieval baseline and reduces hallucination rate as measured by automatic factual consistency scoring. We also release a small test set of 400 long-form generation examples with human-annotated factuality labels to support future evaluation of Serbian generative NLP systems.

SYN-PUB-09811.title: Sentence embeddings for Serbian: benchmark construction and model comparison
SYN-PUB-09811.text:
Sentence embeddings for Serbian: benchmark construction and model comparison (2023, journal, Journal of Language Engineering).
Authors: Milan Petrović (R0925); Katarina Horvat (outside co-author); Ana Mirković (outside co-author); Vladislav Knežević (outside co-author).
Keywords: sentence embeddings; semantic textual similarity; Serbian NLP; contrastive learning; benchmark.
High-quality sentence embeddings are a prerequisite for semantic search, clustering, and question answering in any language. For Serbian, no systematic sentence-embedding benchmark has previously existed, leaving practitioners without a reliable way to compare models. This paper makes three contributions. First, we construct SrbSTS-22, a semantic textual similarity benchmark of 3,500 sentence pairs drawn from news headlines, online reviews, and conversational transcripts, scored by five native-speaker annotators on a 0–5 scale. Second, we adapt the NLI-based contrastive training paradigm to Serbian by automatically translating MultiNLI and SNLI into Serbian and fine-tuning sentence encoders from multiple base checkpoints. Third, we perform a systematic comparison of twelve sentence encoder variants—covering multilingual off-the-shelf models, cross-lingual knowledge distillation, and our natively trained models—on SrbSTS-22 and cross-script retrieval tasks. Our best model, fine-tuned from SrbBERT-Web using NLI pre-training followed by STS fine-tuning, achieves a Pearson correlation of 0.88 on SrbSTS-22. We release the benchmark, trained models, and evaluation toolkit.

SYN-PUB-09813.title: Zero-shot intent detection for Serbian chatbots using multilingual sentence encoders
SYN-PUB-09813.text:
Zero-shot intent detection for Serbian chatbots using multilingual sentence encoders (2022, conference, Proceedings of the International Conference on Spoken Language Processing and Dialogue Systems).
Authors: Stefan Novaković (outside co-author); Nevena Stanković (outside co-author); Radoslav Pejić (outside co-author); Milan Petrović (R0925).
Keywords: intent detection; zero-shot learning; chatbot; Serbian NLP; sentence encoders.
Intent detection is a core component of task-oriented dialogue systems. Deploying such systems for Serbian is hampered by the scarcity of labelled intent data; collecting annotated examples for every new domain is expensive and slow. This paper explores zero-shot intent detection, in which a model trained on seen intents in one or more high-resource languages is applied directly to Serbian without any Serbian-language training examples. We frame intent detection as nearest-neighbour classification in an embedding space and compare five multilingual sentence encoders, including our SrbBERT-Web-based sentence model, on a new Serbian intent detection benchmark covering four domains: banking, travel, e-commerce, and healthcare. Our Serbian sentence encoder, despite never seeing intent labels during training, achieves an accuracy of 71.3% in a zero-shot setting, outperforming the best general multilingual encoder by 8.4 points. We further show that adding as few as ten Serbian examples per intent in a few-shot extension pushes accuracy to 84.1%. We release the benchmark and all experimental code to support research on conversational Serbian NLP.

SYN-PUB-09973.title: Metamodel Definition for AUTOSAR Software Component Descriptors Using Ecore
SYN-PUB-09973.text:
Metamodel Definition for AUTOSAR Software Component Descriptors Using Ecore (2010, journal, International Journal of Embedded and Real-Time Communication Systems).
Authors: Dragan Luković (outside co-author); Predrag Rakić (outside co-author); Mirjana Vidaković (R0948).
Keywords: Ecore metamodel; AUTOSAR SWC; ARXML; ATL transformation; Eclipse Modeling Framework.
This paper presents a structured approach to defining an Ecore-based metamodel that captures the structural semantics of AUTOSAR software component (SWC) descriptors as specified in the AUTOSAR 3.2 standard. The metamodel covers port interfaces, runnables, inter-runnable variables, and timing constraints. Conformance was verified by instantiating 14 SWC types taken from a reference body-control-module specification and checking instance validity against the AUTOSAR schema. The metamodel was implemented as an Eclipse plug-in and exposed a tree-based editor. Transformation experiments using ATL showed that round-trip consistency between the Ecore model and hand-authored ARXML could be maintained with fewer than 0.3% structural deviations across 430 tested descriptors. The contribution is a reusable metamodel layer that decouples SWC authoring from the verbose ARXML syntax and enables downstream model-to-text generation without direct schema manipulation.

SYN-PUB-09974.title: Template-Based Generation of AUTOSAR RTE Stubs from Port Interface Models
SYN-PUB-09974.text:
Template-Based Generation of AUTOSAR RTE Stubs from Port Interface Models (2012, conference, Proceedings of the Eastern European Conference on Embedded Systems).
Authors: Mirjana Vidaković (R0948); Predrag Rakić (outside co-author); Tomáš Bureš (outside co-author).
Keywords: Xpand; RTE stub; AUTOSAR Classic; model-to-text; MISRA-C.
Runtime Environment (RTE) stub generation is a recurring manual effort in AUTOSAR development workflows. This work describes a model-to-text pipeline in which Xpand templates consume an Ecore-based port-interface model and produce syntactically correct RTE stub files for AUTOSAR Classic Platform 4.0. The pipeline was evaluated on three representative Electronic Control Unit (ECU) designs—a door-control unit, a seat-adjustment module, and a battery-management interface—together comprising 67 port interfaces and 112 runnables. Generation time averaged 1.4 seconds per ECU on a standard workstation. Generated stubs were compiled without modification using a commercial compiler suite and passed static analysis with no MISRA-C:2004 violations in 94% of cases; the remaining 6% required minor pointer-cast annotations. Manual effort for stub authoring was reduced from approximately four person-hours to under fifteen minutes per ECU, as measured in a controlled comparison with two experienced engineers.

SYN-PUB-09975.title: A Comparative Study of ATL and QVT-O for AUTOSAR Model Transformations
SYN-PUB-09975.text:
A Comparative Study of ATL and QVT-O for AUTOSAR Model Transformations (2014, journal, Journal of Systems and Software Engineering Practice).
Authors: Tomáš Bureš (outside co-author); Milena Stanković (outside co-author); Mirjana Vidaković (R0948).
Keywords: ATL; QVT-O; model transformation; AUTOSAR; benchmarking.
Model transformation language choice affects both the maintainability and execution performance of AUTOSAR toolchains. This study provides a systematic comparison of ATL and QVT-O for five representative AUTOSAR transformation tasks: SWC flattening, port interface normalisation, timing-model extraction, signal grouping, and ECU topology migration. Each transformation was implemented independently in both languages by two engineers with comparable experience. Metrics collected include lines of code, transformation execution time on models of three size classes (small: up to 50 elements, medium: 50–500, large: 500–5 000), and the number of defects found during a structured review. ATL required 18% fewer lines of code on average across the five tasks, while QVT-O executed 23% faster on large models. Defect counts were statistically indistinguishable. The paper provides a decision framework that maps transformation characteristics to language choice and discusses tooling maturity considerations relevant to industrial adoption.

SYN-PUB-09976.title: Integration of AUTOSAR Toolchains with Continuous Integration Pipelines Using ARXML Diffing
SYN-PUB-09976.text:
Integration of AUTOSAR Toolchains with Continuous Integration Pipelines Using ARXML Diffing (2017, journal, Software Quality and Process Engineering).
Authors: Nikola Sremčević (outside co-author); Ján Kolář (outside co-author); Mirjana Vidaković (R0948).
Keywords: ARXML diff; continuous integration; version control; model merge; AUTOSAR toolchain.
Applying continuous integration (CI) practices to AUTOSAR-based projects is hampered by the fact that ARXML files are large, schema-structured XML documents for which standard textual diff tools produce uninformative output. This paper presents an ARXML-aware diff and merge utility, ArxmlCI, that operates at the metamodel level, representing changes as typed edit operations on model elements rather than text lines. The utility was integrated into a Jenkins-based CI pipeline and evaluated on a series of 180 commits drawn from three development branches of an internal ECU project maintained over six months. ArxmlCI correctly attributed 97.2% of change operations to their originating model element; textual diff attributed 61.4% correctly for the same commits. Merge conflict rates dropped from 34% to 9% of multi-author commits after adoption. The paper also describes a lightweight conflict resolution protocol for common AUTOSAR-specific patterns such as concurrent SWC interface modifications.

SYN-PUB-09977.title: Generating AUTOSAR Adaptive Platform Service Instance Manifests from Service Architecture Models
SYN-PUB-09977.text:
Generating AUTOSAR Adaptive Platform Service Instance Manifests from Service Architecture Models (2019, conference, Proceedings of the Conference on Automotive Software Engineering and Testing).
Authors: Predrag Rakić (outside co-author); Marco Gennari (outside co-author); Mirjana Vidaković (R0948).
Keywords: AUTOSAR Adaptive Platform; service instance manifest; Acceleo; service architecture model; metamodel.
AUTOSAR Adaptive Platform introduces Service Instance Manifests (SIMs) that describe deployment-time binding of services to network endpoints. Authoring SIMs manually is error-prone because their content must be consistent with service interface definitions spread across multiple ARXML packages. This paper proposes a model-driven workflow in which a lightweight service architecture model, defined using a purpose-built metamodel, drives the generation of SIMs via Acceleo templates. The metamodel captures service interfaces, required and provided ports, transport protocol bindings, and QoS parameters. A transformation validates referential consistency before generation. The workflow was tested on an experimental adaptive ECU cluster consisting of four Processing Units running AUTOSAR AP 18.10, with 11 service instances and three transport protocols. All 11 generated SIMs were accepted by the AP execution environment without manual correction. Generation added less than four seconds to the overall build cycle.

SYN-PUB-09979.title: A Transformation Chain for Migrating AUTOSAR Classic SWC Models to Adaptive Platform Service Skeletons
SYN-PUB-09979.text:
A Transformation Chain for Migrating AUTOSAR Classic SWC Models to Adaptive Platform Service Skeletons (2022, conference, Proceedings of the European Conference on Software Architecture and Component Engineering).
Authors: Borislav Đorđević (outside co-author); Marco Gennari (outside co-author); Ján Kolář (outside co-author); Mirjana Vidaković (R0948).
Keywords: migration; AUTOSAR Classic; AUTOSAR Adaptive; transformation chain; service skeleton.
Migration from AUTOSAR Classic to Adaptive Platform is increasingly relevant as vehicle architectures shift toward high-performance compute nodes. This paper describes a three-step transformation chain that takes Classic SWC descriptions in ARXML 4.3 as input and produces Adaptive Platform service skeleton headers and SIMs conforming to AP 21.11. The first transformation normalises Classic port interfaces into a platform-independent intermediate model; the second maps the intermediate model to AP service interface definitions; the third generates C++ skeleton headers using Acceleo. Migration was applied to 38 SWCs from two body-domain ECU projects. Thirty-one SWCs migrated fully automatically; seven required manual completion of data type mappings that have no direct AP equivalent. The paper analyses the seven exceptions and proposes three extension points in the intermediate metamodel that would reduce manual effort in future migrations. Compilation of generated skeletons succeeded on an AP reference implementation without modifications.

SYN-PUB-09980.title: Measuring Transformation Coverage in ATL-Based AUTOSAR Toolchains
SYN-PUB-09980.text:
Measuring Transformation Coverage in ATL-Based AUTOSAR Toolchains (2023, journal, Journal of Systems and Software Engineering Practice).
Authors: Predrag Rakić (outside co-author); Andrea Mocci (outside co-author); Mirjana Vidaković (R0948).
Keywords: ATL coverage; mutation testing; transformation testing; AUTOSAR; Eclipse plug-in.
Testing ATL model transformations systematically is difficult because standard code-coverage criteria do not map directly onto ATL rule structures. This paper adapts four coverage criteria—rule coverage, binding coverage, lazy-rule invocation coverage, and guard predicate coverage—to ATL and implements them in a coverage measurement plug-in for Eclipse. The plug-in instruments transformation execution and produces coverage reports in a machine-readable format. The criteria were evaluated on five ATL transformations from an AUTOSAR toolchain ranging in size from 12 to 74 rules. A mutation testing experiment seeded 210 rule mutations across the five transformations; guard predicate coverage achieved the highest mutation detection rate at 78%, while rule coverage detected 49%. The paper also proposes a ranked test-suite augmentation procedure that adds model instances to improve coverage incrementally, and demonstrates its use on the largest of the five transformations.

SYN-PUB-09982.title: Toolchain-Independent Representation of AUTOSAR Timing Constraints Using a Standardised Metamodel
SYN-PUB-09982.text:
Toolchain-Independent Representation of AUTOSAR Timing Constraints Using a Standardised Metamodel (2025, journal, Embedded Systems Letters).
Authors: Dragan Luković (outside co-author); Tomáš Bureš (outside co-author); Milena Stanković (outside co-author); Mirjana Vidaković (R0948).
Keywords: AUTOSAR TIMEX; timing constraints; metamodel interoperability; model exchange; Acceleo.
Timing constraint specifications in AUTOSAR are expressed through the Timing Extensions (TIMEX) sub-schema, but the way authoring tools serialise TIMEX artefacts varies substantially, causing interoperability problems when exchanging models between organisations using different tools. This paper proposes a standardised intermediate metamodel for AUTOSAR timing constraints covering end-to-end latency constraints, synchronisation constraints, age constraints, and execution time annotations. Import adaptors were implemented for three commercial AUTOSAR authoring environments and validated on a set of 17 timing specifications of varying complexity collected from two automotive projects. The metamodel-normalised representations enabled automated comparison of semantically equivalent constraints authored in different tools; comparison detected four constraint semantics discrepancies that had gone unnoticed during manual review. An Acceleo-based exporter regenerates tool-specific ARXML from the normalised metamodel with measured round-trip fidelity of 98.6% across all constraint types.

SYN-PUB-09983.title: Incremental Regeneration of AUTOSAR RTE Code Under Model Changes: A Change-Impact-Driven Approach
SYN-PUB-09983.text:
Incremental Regeneration of AUTOSAR RTE Code Under Model Changes: A Change-Impact-Driven Approach (2026, preprint, arXiv preprint arXiv:2603.XXXXX).
Authors: Borislav Đorđević (outside co-author); Marco Gennari (outside co-author); Mirjana Vidaković (R0948).
Keywords: incremental generation; change impact analysis; RTE code generation; AUTOSAR 4.3; build time.
Full regeneration of AUTOSAR RTE code after each model change is time-consuming in large ECU projects; build cycles of 20–40 minutes are reported in practitioner surveys. This preprint presents an incremental regeneration strategy in which a change-impact analyser, operating on the AUTOSAR model graph, computes the minimal affected subset of RTE translation units before invoking code generators only for that subset. The impact analyser uses a dependency graph derived from the Ecore-based AUTOSAR metamodel and propagates change markers along typed dependency edges. The approach was prototyped for AUTOSAR 4.3 and evaluated on two ECU model snapshots with 54 and 121 SWCs respectively. For single-SWC modifications, regeneration time dropped from 23.4 minutes to 2.1 minutes (54-SWC case) and from 38.7 minutes to 3.6 minutes (121-SWC case). Full build correctness was confirmed by byte-level comparison of generated files with the results of reference full builds for all 90 tested change scenarios.

SYN-PUB-10239.title: Lightweight Anomaly Detection for Resource-Constrained ICS Gateways: A Quantisation and Pruning Study
SYN-PUB-10239.text:
Lightweight Anomaly Detection for Resource-Constrained ICS Gateways: A Quantisation and Pruning Study (2025, conference, Proceedings of the European Conference on Industrial Automation and Security (ECIAS)).
Authors: Mirjana Stošić (outside co-author); Dávid Szabó (outside co-author); Reinhilde Mayer (outside co-author); Krisztina Kiss (R1008); Andrea Jovanović (R0983); Vukica Ognjanov (R0979).
Keywords: model compression; quantisation; pruning; embedded deployment; autoencoder.
Many ICS sites route traffic through ARM-based gateways with 256 MB RAM and single-core processors. This paper evaluates the effect of weight quantisation (32-bit to 8-bit and 4-bit floating point) and structured pruning (removing 10%, 25%, 50% of autoencoder units) on detection performance and inference latency for traffic-based anomaly detectors. Experiments used three autoencoder architectures differing in depth (2, 4, 6 hidden layers) trained on Modbus/TCP and DNP3 captures. 8-bit quantisation reduced model size by 3.7× and inference time by 2.1× with an average AUROC reduction of 0.012. 4-bit quantisation introduced a 0.041 AUROC drop. Structured pruning at 25% improved inference speed by 1.4× with negligible performance loss; at 50%, AUROC declined by 0.028. A combined 8-bit quantised, 25%-pruned model achieved inference at 0.9 ms per 10-second window on an ARM Cortex-A7 target, fitting within a 10 ms cycle budget, making real-time deployment feasible without dedicated hardware accelerators.

SYN-PUB-10270.title: Evaluating EvoSuite Effectiveness on Java EE Enterprise Beans: A Replication Study
SYN-PUB-10270.text:
Evaluating EvoSuite Effectiveness on Java EE Enterprise Beans: A Replication Study (2015, journal, Journal of Software Testing and Verification (JSTV)).
Authors: Lidija Krstić (outside co-author); Andrea Jovanović (R0983); Radovan Sekulić (outside co-author).
Keywords: EvoSuite; Java EE; mutation score; enterprise components; replication.
A number of published EvoSuite evaluations focus on standalone Java classes, leaving enterprise components with container-managed transactions and dependency injection comparatively underexplored. This replication study reproduces the methodology of a 2011 benchmark evaluation and extends it to 30 stateless and stateful session beans extracted from four production-like Java EE applications. The study measures line coverage, branch coverage, and mutation score under EvoSuite's default whole-suite strategy and its DynaMOSA variant. On plain utility classes, results align closely with the original benchmark. For session beans, line coverage drops by an average of 18 percentage points, attributed primarily to unreachable paths behind container lifecycle callbacks. Mutation score degrades even more steeply, falling 23 points below plain-class baselines. The paper characterises the categories of mutations that escape detection and proposes a lightweight mock-injection wrapper that recovers approximately 9 coverage points with modest configuration effort.

SYN-PUB-10271.title: A Taxonomy of Testability Impediments in Monolithic Web Applications Scheduled for Cloud Migration
SYN-PUB-10271.text:
A Taxonomy of Testability Impediments in Monolithic Web Applications Scheduled for Cloud Migration (2017, journal, Software Quality and Process Improvement Journal (SQPIJ)).
Authors: Andrea Jovanović (R0983); Ivana Bjelopavlić (outside co-author); Nemanja Stanić (outside co-author); Ágnes Varga (outside co-author).
Keywords: legacy systems; testability; cloud migration; taxonomy; monolithic architecture.
Organisations migrating legacy monolithic web applications to cloud platforms routinely encounter testing challenges that are poorly documented in the literature. This paper presents a taxonomy derived from a mixed-methods study combining a survey of 47 software engineers from 12 Serbian and Croatian companies with a document analysis of 18 months of issue trackers from five open-source migration projects hosted on a public forge. Grounded coding of survey responses and issue descriptions yielded 34 distinct impediment types, grouped into five top-level categories: tight database coupling, absent seam points, implicit global state, hard-coded infrastructure assumptions, and missing observability hooks. The taxonomy is cross-referenced with testing technique applicability, showing that coverage-guided fuzzing is blocked by 19 of the 34 impediment types without preprocessing. The paper concludes with a prioritised refactoring roadmap linked to each impediment category.

SYN-PUB-10272.title: Instrumentation Overhead of Coverage-Guided Fuzzing in Resource-Constrained Containerised Environments
SYN-PUB-10272.text:
Instrumentation Overhead of Coverage-Guided Fuzzing in Resource-Constrained Containerised Environments (2019, conference, Proceedings of the International Workshop on Continuous Software Engineering and Testing (CWSET)).
Authors: Andrea Jovanović (R0983); Dušan Filipović (outside co-author).
Keywords: AFL; fuzzing; Docker; instrumentation; CI pipelines.
Coverage-guided fuzzers such as AFL and libFuzzer insert compile-time or binary-level instrumentation to track edge coverage. When these fuzzers are deployed inside containers with restricted CPU and memory quotas—as is common in cloud continuous integration pipelines—instrumentation overhead becomes a practical concern. This paper characterises overhead across four instrumentation strategies: AFL's compile-time SHM bitmap, AFL++'s LTO instrumentation, a LLVM SanitizerCoverage-based approach, and a binary-only QEMU mode, applied to five network-parsing libraries. Experiments are run inside Docker containers with CPU quotas of 0.5, 1, and 2 virtual cores and memory limits of 256 MB, 512 MB, and 1 GB. Results show that LTO instrumentation degrades throughput by 8–14% at 0.5 vCPU compared to 3–6% at 2 vCPU, while QEMU mode suffers 40–65% degradation regardless of quota. Memory quota has negligible effect above 512 MB. Practical guidance for CI pipeline configuration is derived.

SYN-PUB-10273.title: Search-Based Generation of REST API Test Suites During Microservice Decomposition
SYN-PUB-10273.text:
Search-Based Generation of REST API Test Suites During Microservice Decomposition (2020, journal, Journal of Software Engineering and Applications (JSEA)).
Authors: Andrea Jovanović (R0983); Marija Horvat (outside co-author); Christoph Mayer (outside co-author); Srđan Gajić (outside co-author).
Keywords: REST API testing; microservices; multi-objective optimisation; OpenAPI; decomposition.
When a monolithic application is decomposed into microservices, REST interfaces emerge incrementally and are often underspecified early in the process. This paper describes a search-based approach that generates test suites targeting emerging OpenAPI specifications, using a multi-objective evolutionary algorithm that balances endpoint coverage, status-code diversity, and response schema validity. The approach was applied to three industrial decomposition projects carried out by a software house in Novi Sad over an 18-month period. Across 87 newly created endpoints, the generated suites achieved 91% endpoint coverage and detected 23 integration faults not found by developer-written unit tests. The evolutionary algorithm converged in under 4 minutes per service on a standard CI agent. The paper analyses false-positive rates in schema validation assertions and proposes a relaxed matching strategy that reduces them by 61% without sacrificing fault detection.

SYN-PUB-10274.title: Regression Test Selection Under Continuous Deployment: An Empirical Comparison of Change-Impact and Coverage-Matrix Strategies
SYN-PUB-10274.text:
Regression Test Selection Under Continuous Deployment: An Empirical Comparison of Change-Impact and Coverage-Matrix Strategies (2021, conference, Empirical Software Engineering and Measurement Conference (ESEM-Adriatic Track)).
Authors: Andrea Jovanović (R0983); Bojan Lukić (outside co-author); Petra Novotná (outside co-author).
Keywords: regression test selection; continuous deployment; change-impact analysis; coverage matrix; empirical study.
Continuous deployment pipelines require fast regression feedback, making full suite execution impractical for large codebases. This paper compares two families of regression test selection strategies—static change-impact analysis and dynamic coverage matrix matching—across four Java microservice repositories with commit histories spanning 24 months and totalling 3 400 commits. For each commit, both strategies select a test subset; the selected subsets are evaluated against the full suite's fault detection record to compute selection safety (fraction of fault-revealing commits where at least one fault is surfaced). Change-impact analysis achieves 94.1% safety at a mean suite reduction of 68%, while coverage-matrix matching achieves 97.3% safety at 54% reduction. A hybrid configuration that applies coverage matrices to modified modules and change-impact to dependencies reaches 96.8% safety at 63% reduction. Execution time comparisons on a 4-core CI agent are provided for all strategies.

SYN-PUB-10276.title: Differential Testing of Containerised Legacy Versus Cloud-Native Rewrites Using Automatically Generated Input Corpora
SYN-PUB-10276.text:
Differential Testing of Containerised Legacy Versus Cloud-Native Rewrites Using Automatically Generated Input Corpora (2025, conference, Proceedings of the International Conference on Software Testing, Verification and Validation (ICSTVV)).
Authors: Andrea Jovanović (R0983); Marija Horvat (outside co-author); Sébastien Charlot (outside co-author); Dušan Filipović (outside co-author).
Keywords: differential testing; legacy migration; fuzzing; cloud-native; CI/CD.
When a legacy service is rewritten as a cloud-native application, developers need assurance that the two versions behave equivalently on all inputs relevant to production traffic. This paper applies differential testing—running both versions on the same inputs and flagging behavioural divergences—to three pairs of legacy-and-rewrite services from an anonymised financial sector client. Input corpora are generated by combining coverage-guided fuzzing on the legacy binary with a search-based strategy seeded from sanitised production request logs. Over 72-hour fuzzing campaigns, the approach surfaces 41 divergences across the three service pairs; 29 are confirmed bugs in the rewrite, 8 are intentional behavioural changes, and 4 are flaky due to timestamp sensitivity. Precision of the divergence detector (after automated timestamp normalisation) is 87%. The paper discusses the practical workflow for integrating this approach into a migration acceptance gate within a CI/CD pipeline.

SYN-PUB-10277.title: Seed Corpus Construction Strategies for Structure-Aware Fuzzing of Binary Serialisation Formats in Migrated Data Services
SYN-PUB-10277.text:
Seed Corpus Construction Strategies for Structure-Aware Fuzzing of Binary Serialisation Formats in Migrated Data Services (2026, preprint, arXiv preprint (submitted to Journal of Systems and Software)).
Authors: Andrea Jovanović (R0983); Valentina Oros (outside co-author); Andrej Molnár (outside co-author).
Keywords: structure-aware fuzzing; seed corpus; binary serialisation; data migration; grammar inference.
Data services migrated from on-premise deployments to cloud platforms often retain binary serialisation formats—such as custom TLV encodings or legacy ASN.1 schemas—that are poorly covered by mutation-based fuzzers operating on raw bytes. This preprint proposes and compares four seed corpus construction strategies for structure-aware fuzzers targeting such formats: (1) grammar extraction from decompiled code, (2) network capture replay with format inference, (3) generative model sampling trained on captured payloads, and (4) manual schema transcription. Each strategy is evaluated on three data services from an open benchmark of migrated applications, using edge coverage, unique crash count, and corpus construction time as metrics. Grammar extraction yields the highest edge coverage (mean 73.1%) but requires the most effort. The generative model strategy, trained on 10 000 captured payloads per service, reaches 68.4% coverage with substantially less manual work and scales better to format variants introduced during migration.

SYN-PUB-10372.title: A Metamodel for IEC 61131-3 Structured Text: Design Rationale and Conformance Checking
SYN-PUB-10372.text:
A Metamodel for IEC 61131-3 Structured Text: Design Rationale and Conformance Checking (2015, journal, Journal of Systems and Control Engineering Research).
Authors: Miroslav Đorđević (outside co-author); Veljko Pantelić (R0995); Tibor Farkaš (outside co-author).
Keywords: IEC 61131-3; Structured Text; metamodeling; Ecore; OCL; conformance checking.
IEC 61131-3 defines five programming languages for programmable logic controllers, yet no widely adopted formal metamodel exists for its Structured Text variant. This paper presents a metamodel covering the full grammar of Structured Text as defined in the third edition of the standard, implemented in Ecore within the Eclipse Modeling Framework. The metamodel comprises 47 metaclasses and 112 structural features. Conformance checking is realized through 34 OCL constraints covering type compatibility, scope resolution, and temporal execution order. The metamodel was validated against a corpus of 18 publicly available PLC project archives totalling approximately 120,000 lines of Structured Text, extracted from open automation repositories. Constraint violations found in the corpus are categorized by severity and related to common programming errors. The paper discusses design decisions around POUs, data types, and sequential function chart interoperability. The resulting artifact serves as a foundation for model-to-model and model-to-text transformation chains described in subsequent work.

SYN-PUB-10373.title: Mapping UML Class Diagrams to IEC 61131-3 Function Blocks via ATL Transformations
SYN-PUB-10373.text:
Mapping UML Class Diagrams to IEC 61131-3 Function Blocks via ATL Transformations (2017, conference, International Conference on Industrial Informatics and Automation (ICIIA)).
Authors: Miroslav Đorđević (outside co-author); Katarzyna Wiśniewska (outside co-author); Veljko Pantelić (R0995).
Keywords: UML; ATL; model transformation; function blocks; IEC 61131-3; code generation.
Function blocks in IEC 61131-3 exhibit structural similarity to classes in object-oriented formalisms, yet practitioners lack automated tooling to carry designs expressed in UML into executable PLC artifacts. This paper defines an ATL transformation that maps a restricted profile of UML class diagrams—covering classes, associations, aggregations, and a subset of stereotypes—to IEC 61131-3 Function Block Declaration bodies in Structured Text. The transformation handles inheritance by flattening class hierarchies into self-contained function block bodies, preserving interface semantics through input and output variable mappings. An evaluation was conducted on five industrial-style case studies ranging from conveyor-belt sequencing to batch-reactor control, each containing between 8 and 31 classes. Generated code was compiled and executed on Beckhoff CX5130 hardware. Cyclic execution times of generated programs stayed within 5% of manually written equivalents. The paper also reports on maintainability metrics comparing generated and hand-written code using McCabe complexity and comment density.

SYN-PUB-10374.title: Variability Modelling in PLC Software Families Using Feature Models and Configuration Constraints
SYN-PUB-10374.text:
Variability Modelling in PLC Software Families Using Feature Models and Configuration Constraints (2018, conference, European Workshop on Software Product Lines for Industrial Systems (EWSPLIS)).
Authors: Veljko Pantelić (R0995); Tibor Farkaš (outside co-author); Luca Ferretti (outside co-author); Miroslav Đorđević (outside co-author).
Keywords: software product lines; feature models; variability management; PLC; code generation; FeatureIDE.
Automation equipment manufacturers frequently produce families of machines that share a large fraction of control logic but differ in optional subsystems such as sensor types, drive configurations, or safety interlocks. Managing such variability through copy-paste code leads to maintenance burdens quantified here on a dataset of 14 PLC projects from a partner manufacturing firm. This paper proposes using FODA-style feature models, extended with numerical attributes for timing parameters, to represent the configuration space of a PLC software product line. A binding-time model distinguishes features configured at project generation time from those configured at runtime through parameter tables. A prototype implementation uses FeatureIDE for feature model editing and a Xtend-based generator to produce Structured Text artefacts for selected configurations. The approach was applied to a filling-machine product line with 23 optional features, yielding a single-source model from which 8 valid configurations were derived and verified against a test harness of 310 unit tests. Lines of code under manual maintenance were reduced by 61% compared to the previous fork-based approach.

SYN-PUB-10375.title: An Xtext Grammar and IDE Support for a Subset of IEC 61131-3 Structured Text
SYN-PUB-10375.text:
An Xtext Grammar and IDE Support for a Subset of IEC 61131-3 Structured Text (2019, journal, Journal of Automation Software Engineering).
Authors: Veljko Pantelić (R0995); Ana Kovačević (outside co-author).
Keywords: Xtext; IEC 61131-3; Structured Text; parser; IDE; domain-specific languages.
Development of domain-specific tools for PLC programming is hampered by the absence of reusable, open parser infrastructure. This paper describes an Xtext grammar covering approximately 92% of the Structured Text syntax defined in IEC 61131-3 third edition, excluding only deprecated GOTO constructs and certain vendor extensions. The grammar is accompanied by scope provider rules for cross-reference resolution across compilation units, a type-inference engine handling implicit numeric widening, and formatter and outline view implementations for Eclipse IDE integration. Error recovery strategies are documented, as PLC source files from industrial environments frequently contain partial programs during edit sessions. A user study involving 11 automation engineers from three companies measured error detection time for introduced syntax and type errors; the IDE reduced median detection time from 14.3 minutes to under 2 minutes compared to a plain text editor workflow. The tooling is released under an open-source license and has been adopted in three subsequent research projects at partner institutions.

SYN-PUB-10377.title: Integrating Safety Requirements into PLC Product-Line Models Using SysML Parametric Diagrams
SYN-PUB-10377.text:
Integrating Safety Requirements into PLC Product-Line Models Using SysML Parametric Diagrams (2021, conference, International Conference on Model-Driven Engineering and Industrial Automation (MDEIA)).
Authors: Dragana Milić (outside co-author); Stefano Cremonesi (outside co-author); Veljko Pantelić (R0995).
Keywords: safety requirements; SysML; product lines; IEC 62061; traceability; PLC.
Safety-critical PLC applications require that timing and operational constraints derived from hazard analyses be traceable through to implementation. This paper proposes a model-based workflow in which SysML parametric diagrams capture quantitative safety constraints—maximum response times, watchdog periods, and safe-state transition conditions—derived from a HAZOP analysis artefact. A model-to-model transformation maps parametric constraint blocks to annotations on a feature model, and a subsequent model-to-text step embeds the constraints as pragma comments and runtime assertion code in generated Structured Text. The approach was demonstrated on a palletizer control application with 17 identified safety functions. All 17 functions produced traceable artefacts from HAZOP table rows to compiled PLC code. A traceability matrix was generated automatically and verified by a safety assessor against IEC 62061 SIL 2 requirements. The paper discusses limitations arising from the restricted expressiveness of IEC 61131-3 assertions and proposes extensions.

SYN-PUB-10378.title: DSL Design for Conveyor Routing Logic: A Case Study in Abstraction Level Calibration
SYN-PUB-10378.text:
DSL Design for Conveyor Routing Logic: A Case Study in Abstraction Level Calibration (2024, conference, European Conference on Software Language Engineering (ECSLE)).
Authors: Veljko Pantelić (R0995); Péter Szalai (outside co-author); Dragana Milić (outside co-author).
Keywords: domain-specific languages; abstraction level; Xtext; conveyor control; user study; code generation.
Choosing the right abstraction level for a domain-specific language is a practical design problem with limited empirical guidance. This paper reports a case study in which three successive DSL versions were designed, implemented, and evaluated for expressing conveyor routing logic in a logistics automation context. The first version mirrored the structure of IEC 61131-3 function block networks closely; the second introduced a graph-based topology language with implicit signal routing; the third added a declarative routing-rule layer. Each version was implemented as an Xtext grammar with an Xtend code generator producing Structured Text. Evaluation involved six automation programmers who completed identical routing tasks under a think-aloud protocol. Task completion time, error rate, and post-task questionnaire scores were recorded. The graph-based version produced the lowest error rate at 0.8 errors per task; the declarative version had the shortest median task time at 11.4 minutes but required the longest learning period. The paper derives three abstraction-level heuristics for industrial DSL design.

SYN-PUB-10379.title: Towards Round-Trip Engineering for IEC 61131-3: Extracting Feature Models from Legacy PLC Codebases
SYN-PUB-10379.text:
Towards Round-Trip Engineering for IEC 61131-3: Extracting Feature Models from Legacy PLC Codebases (2025, journal, Journal of Systems and Software).
Authors: Ana Kovačević (outside co-author); Veljko Pantelić (R0995); Radu Constantin (outside co-author); Dragana Milić (outside co-author).
Keywords: round-trip engineering; feature extraction; clone detection; legacy code; PLC; product lines.
Many manufacturing firms operate legacy PLC codebases developed without explicit variability management. Migrating such code to a product-line architecture requires recovering implicit variation points from existing programs. This paper presents a semi-automated extraction approach that applies clone detection to a corpus of related PLC projects to identify recurring code patterns, clusters patterns by structural similarity using a tree-edit distance metric, and maps clusters to candidate features in a FODA feature model. The approach was applied to a set of 11 related projects from an anonymised food-processing equipment manufacturer totalling 84,000 lines of Structured Text. Extraction identified 38 candidate features, of which domain experts validated 29 as genuine variation points. Six features required manual refinement. The recovered feature model was used to derive a product-line architecture, and one configuration was re-generated and compared against the original project using cyclomatic complexity and test pass rate as metrics. Results indicate functional equivalence for the regenerated configuration on the existing test suite.

SYN-PUB-10380.title: A Benchmark Suite for PLC Code Generators: Construction, Metrics, and Baseline Results
SYN-PUB-10380.text:
A Benchmark Suite for PLC Code Generators: Construction, Metrics, and Baseline Results (2026, journal, Empirical Software Engineering).
Authors: Veljko Pantelić (R0995); Dragana Milić (outside co-author); Péter Szalai (outside co-author); Radu Constantin (outside co-author); Ana Kovačević (outside co-author).
Keywords: benchmark; code generation; PLC; IEC 61131-3; empirical evaluation; hardware-in-the-loop.
Reproducible evaluation of PLC code generators is difficult because published studies use heterogeneous, proprietary case studies. This paper describes the construction of an open benchmark suite comprising 24 PLC control scenarios spanning motion control, process automation, and safety interlock domains. Each scenario is specified at three levels: a natural-language requirements document, a structured functional specification, and a reference implementation in Structured Text manually written by two authors independently and reconciled. Benchmark metrics include correctness (pass rate on a hardware-in-the-loop test harness using Wago PFC200 controllers), code size ratio to reference, cyclomatic complexity ratio, and compilation time. Baseline results are reported for three existing open-source code generators and for the authors' own generator. No generator achieves above 81% correctness across all scenarios; motion control scenarios prove most difficult. The benchmark suite and harness scripts are released under an open licence to enable comparative evaluation in future work.

SYN-PUB-10472.title: Statistical Baseline Modelling of Modbus/TCP Traffic in a Substation Automation Network
SYN-PUB-10472.text:
Statistical Baseline Modelling of Modbus/TCP Traffic in a Substation Automation Network (2010, journal, Journal of Industrial Network Security).
Authors: Goran Milošević (outside co-author); Tibor Farkas (outside co-author); Krisztina Kiss (R1008).
Keywords: Modbus/TCP; statistical baseline; Mahalanobis distance; substation automation; one-class detection.
This paper describes the construction of per-register statistical baselines for Modbus/TCP traffic captured over six months on a live substation automation testbed. For each register address, empirical distributions of inter-request intervals, payload values, and function code sequences were estimated using kernel density estimation with a Gaussian kernel and bandwidth selected by cross-validation. A one-class detector based on Mahalanobis distance thresholding over a 20-feature vector was evaluated against 14 manually injected attack scenarios, including replay, coil-write injection, and scan sweeps. At a false positive rate of 0.5%, the detector achieved a true positive rate of 91.4% across all attack types. The paper also quantifies the effect of seasonal load variation on baseline drift and proposes a sliding-window recalibration schedule with a 72-hour update period that maintains detection performance without human intervention. Results are compared with a fixed-threshold rule-based baseline, which achieved 67% TPR at the same FPR. The testbed comprised three Siemens-compatible PLCs connected over a deterministic switched Ethernet fabric.

SYN-PUB-10473.title: One-Class SVM for Detecting Anomalous DNP3 Command Sequences in Water Treatment Control Systems
SYN-PUB-10473.text:
One-Class SVM for Detecting Anomalous DNP3 Command Sequences in Water Treatment Control Systems (2012, conference, Proceedings of the Central European Workshop on Industrial Communication Security (CEWICS)).
Authors: Tibor Farkas (outside co-author); Ágnes Varga (outside co-author); Krisztina Kiss (R1008).
Keywords: DNP3; one-class SVM; SCADA; n-gram features; water treatment.
One-class support vector machines (OC-SVM) were applied to detect anomalous DNP3 application-layer command sequences in a water treatment SCADA testbed. Feature vectors were constructed from 15-second sliding windows using n-gram frequency histograms of function code and object group pairs, yielding 128-dimensional vectors after principal component analysis retaining 95% of variance. The OC-SVM used an RBF kernel; the nu hyperparameter was swept from 0.01 to 0.20 and selected via leave-one-out cross-validation on a 90-day normal-operation capture (approximately 4.2 million packets). Attack scenarios—unauthorised control block writes, time-sync spoofing, and application-layer flooding—were injected during a separate 14-day test period. The detector achieved an F1 score of 0.87 for unseen attack types not represented during training. Computational overhead was measured at under 3% CPU utilisation on an ARM Cortex-A9 industrial gateway, supporting inline deployment feasibility.

SYN-PUB-10474.title: Characterising Normal Behaviour in Industrial Ethernet Networks: A Long-Term Measurement Study
SYN-PUB-10474.text:
Characterising Normal Behaviour in Industrial Ethernet Networks: A Long-Term Measurement Study (2013, journal, IEEE Transactions on Industrial Informatics).
Authors: Goran Milošević (outside co-author); Marko Đorđević (outside co-author); Reinhilde Mayer (outside co-author); Krisztina Kiss (R1008).
Keywords: traffic characterisation; industrial Ethernet; long-range dependence; measurement study; Hurst parameter.
This measurement study presents a 12-month passive capture of traffic from four industrial sites—two discrete manufacturing lines, one water utility, and one district heating plant—totalling approximately 680 GB of raw packet data. The study characterises normal traffic behaviour through 22 statistical descriptors per flow, including coefficient of variation of inter-packet gaps, entropy of destination port distributions, and autocorrelation structure of payload-length time series. Results show that industrial Ethernet traffic exhibits strong periodicity at scales of seconds to hours, with Hurst parameter estimates between 0.61 and 0.79 across sites, indicating long-range dependence. The study documents characteristic differences between Modbus, EtherNet/IP, and proprietary vendor protocols and quantifies seasonal variation. The dataset and feature extraction code are described in sufficient detail to support reproducibility. Findings inform design choices for unsupervised detectors and highlight risks of training on short captures.

SYN-PUB-10478.title: Evaluating the Effect of Protocol Encryption on Traffic-Based Anomaly Detection: OPC UA Security Mode Comparison
SYN-PUB-10478.text:
Evaluating the Effect of Protocol Encryption on Traffic-Based Anomaly Detection: OPC UA Security Mode Comparison (2019, conference, Proceedings of the Central European Workshop on Industrial Communication Security (CEWICS)).
Authors: Tibor Farkas (outside co-author); Marek Novotný (outside co-author); Krisztina Kiss (R1008).
Keywords: OPC UA; encryption; traffic features; one-class SVM; security mode.
OPC UA supports three security modes—None, Sign, and SignAndEncrypt—and this paper evaluates how each mode affects the discriminability of traffic features used in unsupervised anomaly detectors. Experiments were conducted on a testbed comprising an OPC UA server, two client applications, and an embedded data historian. Seventeen traffic features extractable from unencrypted traffic were assessed for their availability under Sign and SignAndEncrypt modes using packet capture before and after the application layer. Under SignAndEncrypt, 11 of 17 features became unavailable or uninformative at the packet level; however, timing, packet length distribution, and session-level handshake frequency remained discriminative. A reduced 6-feature one-class SVM trained on these surviving features achieved a detection rate of 0.83 against four attack scenarios, compared with 0.91 for the full 17-feature detector on unencrypted traffic. The paper discusses the implications for passive inline monitoring architectures and proposes a broker-based decryption approach for trusted network segments.

SYN-PUB-10480.title: Threshold Calibration for ICS Anomaly Detectors Under Imbalanced Operating Conditions
SYN-PUB-10480.text:
Threshold Calibration for ICS Anomaly Detectors Under Imbalanced Operating Conditions (2021, journal, Computers and Security).
Authors: Jelena Kovačević (outside co-author); Reinhilde Mayer (outside co-author); Krisztina Kiss (R1008).
Keywords: threshold calibration; false positive rate; beta mixture model; detector evaluation; ICS.
Anomaly detectors for ICS traffic are typically calibrated by fixing the decision threshold to achieve a target false positive rate estimated on a clean training set. This paper investigates the miscalibration that results when the actual false positive rate at deployment differs from the target, and proposes a post-hoc calibration procedure using a small set of unlabelled operational data. The procedure fits a two-component beta mixture model to the empirical score distribution and uses the mixture weight of the anomalous component as a proxy for the contamination fraction. Experiments on four detectors (OC-SVM, Isolation Forest, autoencoder, and kernel density estimator) across three ICS protocol datasets show that the calibration procedure reduces the gap between nominal and actual FPR from a mean of 3.1 percentage points to 0.4 percentage points. The paper also quantifies sensitivity to the choice of beta mixture initialisation and provides practical recommendations for operators setting alert thresholds.

SYN-PUB-10482.title: Comparing Score Aggregation Strategies for Multi-Protocol ICS Anomaly Detection
SYN-PUB-10482.text:
Comparing Score Aggregation Strategies for Multi-Protocol ICS Anomaly Detection (2024, journal, Computers and Security).
Authors: Jelena Kovačević (outside co-author); Goran Milošević (outside co-author); Krisztina Kiss (R1008).
Keywords: score aggregation; multi-protocol; Dempster-Shafer; EtherNet/IP; detection pipeline.
Industrial sites often run several ICS protocols concurrently; a single anomaly may manifest in traffic from multiple protocols or only one. This paper compares six score aggregation strategies—maximum, mean, product, Dempster-Shafer combination, learned linear combination, and a voting threshold rule—for combining per-protocol anomaly scores from Modbus, DNP3, and EtherNet/IP detectors deployed simultaneously on the same network segment. A testbed with all three protocol stacks was operated for 45 days, and 18 multi-protocol and single-protocol attack scenarios were injected over a 10-day evaluation period. The learned linear combination, trained on a 5-day clean holdout with synthetic contamination, achieved the highest balanced accuracy (0.91) but required labelled data for weight estimation. The Dempster-Shafer rule achieved 0.88 without labelled data. The maximum rule performed consistently below 0.80. Results provide concrete guidance for operators designing multi-sensor detection pipelines.

SYN-PUB-10483.title: Protocol-Agnostic Anomaly Detection Using Byte-Level Feature Extraction from ICS Application Payloads
SYN-PUB-10483.text:
Protocol-Agnostic Anomaly Detection Using Byte-Level Feature Extraction from ICS Application Payloads (2026, journal, Journal of Industrial Network Security).
Authors: Jelena Kovačević (outside co-author); Péter Horváth (outside co-author); Krisztina Kiss (R1008); Milutin Paunović (R1022).
Keywords: protocol-agnostic; byte-level features; proprietary protocols; one-class SVM; heterogeneous ICS.
Most ICS anomaly detectors are designed for a specific protocol and rely on parsed field values. This paper investigates a protocol-agnostic approach in which raw application-layer payload bytes from the first 64 bytes of each PDU are used to construct feature vectors via byte-frequency histograms augmented with bigram entropy and mean absolute deviation of byte values. A one-class SVM and an Isolation Forest were trained on mixed-protocol captures from a testbed running Modbus, DNP3, and a proprietary vendor protocol for which no parser was available. The proprietary protocol represented 31% of traffic. Against seven attack scenarios including vendor-protocol-specific command injection, the protocol-agnostic detectors achieved AUROC values of 0.89 and 0.87 respectively, compared with 0.94 for a protocol-aware Modbus detector applied only to Modbus traffic. The paper discusses cases where protocol-agnostic features are sufficient and where parsed fields remain necessary, providing a decision framework for practitioners deploying detectors on heterogeneous industrial networks.

SYN-PUB-10523.title: Unsupervised anomaly detection on Modbus traffic
SYN-PUB-10523.text:
Unsupervised anomaly detection on Modbus traffic (2024, journal, Journal of Industrial Security).
Authors: Vuk Đukić (R1015); Milena Ostojić (outside co-author); Dragan Kovač (outside co-author).
Industrial control systems increasingly rely on Modbus, a legacy serial communication protocol widely deployed in manufacturing and critical infrastructure environments. Despite its prevalence, Modbus lacks built-in security mechanisms, making it highly susceptible to network-based attacks. This paper presents an unsupervised anomaly detection framework specifically designed for Modbus traffic analysis. The proposed approach leverages autoencoder-based neural networks trained exclusively on benign traffic to establish a baseline behavioural profile of legitimate industrial communications. Anomalies are identified by measuring reconstruction error against learned normal patterns, without requiring labelled attack data. The framework is evaluated on a synthetic dataset generated from a real-world programmable logic controller testbed, covering scenarios such as unauthorised function code injection, coil manipulation, and replay attacks. Experimental results demonstrate detection rates exceeding 94% across all attack categories, with a false positive rate below 2%. The paper also analyses the impact of traffic window size and encoding granularity on detection performance, offering practical guidance for deployment in resource-constrained industrial environments.

SYN-PUB-10524.title: Threat modelling for smart building controllers
SYN-PUB-10524.text:
Threat modelling for smart building controllers (2022, conference, Conference on Applied Cybersecurity).
Authors: Vuk Đukić (R1015); Ana Petrović (outside co-author); Luka Stanković (outside co-author).
Smart building automation systems increasingly integrate heterogeneous controllers managing heating, ventilation, access control, and fire suppression, all connected over IP-based networks. This convergence introduces significant attack surfaces that are rarely addressed through systematic security engineering. This paper applies a structured threat modelling methodology—adapted from STRIDE and augmented with ICS-specific threat categories—to a representative smart building controller architecture. The analysis identifies seventeen distinct threat scenarios spanning spoofing of sensor inputs, tampering with actuator commands, and denial-of-service against building management gateways. For each threat, the paper proposes corresponding mitigations including cryptographic command authentication, rate-limiting policies, and network segmentation strategies. A comparative evaluation against an unmitigated baseline system is conducted using a simulation environment, demonstrating measurable risk reduction across all identified threat categories. The findings offer actionable security guidance for building automation vendors and facility managers deploying next-generation smart infrastructure.

SYN-PUB-10525.title: A comparative study of intrusion detection architectures for SCADA networks
SYN-PUB-10525.text:
A comparative study of intrusion detection architectures for SCADA networks (2023, journal, IEEE Transactions on Industrial Informatics Security).
Authors: Milena Ostojić (outside co-author); Vuk Đukić (R1015); Nemanja Filipović (outside co-author).
Keywords: SCADA security; intrusion detection; industrial control systems; anomaly detection; network security.
Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA) networks form the backbone of critical infrastructure sectors including energy distribution, water treatment, and transportation. Protecting these networks from cyber intrusions requires detection systems capable of operating on highly specialised industrial protocols while maintaining low false-positive rates in continuous operation. This paper conducts a systematic comparative evaluation of five intrusion detection architectures—signature-based, specification-based, statistical anomaly, deep learning, and hybrid approaches—applied to a common SCADA testbed. Each architecture is assessed across four attack categories: reconnaissance, command injection, man-in-the-middle, and denial-of-service. Performance is measured in terms of detection accuracy, latency, resource consumption, and adaptability to concept drift. Results show that hybrid architectures combining specification-based rules with neural anomaly scoring achieve the best overall balance, while purely deep-learning-based systems exhibit higher sensitivity to protocol version variability. The paper concludes with a decision framework to guide practitioners in selecting appropriate detection strategies based on operational constraints.

SYN-PUB-10526.title: Federated learning for distributed intrusion detection across IoT edge nodes
SYN-PUB-10526.text:
Federated learning for distributed intrusion detection across IoT edge nodes (2023, journal, Computers & Security).
Authors: Vuk Đukić (R1015); Ana Petrović (outside co-author); Rastko Mirković (outside co-author).
Keywords: IoT security; federated learning; intrusion detection; edge computing; anomaly detection.
Internet of Things deployments in industrial and smart city environments generate massive volumes of heterogeneous network traffic across geographically distributed edge nodes. Centralising this data for intrusion detection raises significant privacy and bandwidth concerns, particularly in multi-stakeholder environments. This paper proposes a federated learning framework for distributed intrusion detection, wherein each edge node trains a local anomaly detection model on its own traffic and periodically shares only model gradient updates with a central aggregation server. The aggregated global model is then redistributed to participating nodes, enabling collective knowledge improvement without raw data exposure. The framework is evaluated on a purpose-built IoT testbed consisting of twenty-four heterogeneous edge devices simulating smart metering, environmental sensing, and industrial actuation scenarios. Results demonstrate that the federated approach achieves detection accuracy within 3% of a centralised baseline while reducing data transmission overhead by over 80%. The paper also investigates the robustness of the framework against poisoning attacks introduced by compromised edge nodes.

SYN-PUB-10527.title: Threat modelling in IIoT supply chains: identifying lateral movement pathways
SYN-PUB-10527.text:
Threat modelling in IIoT supply chains: identifying lateral movement pathways (2022, journal, Journal of Cybersecurity and Privacy).
Authors: Vuk Đukić (R1015); Bojana Vuković (outside co-author); Luka Stanković (outside co-author).
Keywords: threat modelling; IIoT; supply chain security; lateral movement; industrial control systems.
Industrial Internet of Things supply chains encompass multiple layers of hardware vendors, firmware providers, system integrators, and end operators, each introducing potential vulnerabilities that adversaries may exploit for lateral movement across organisational boundaries. This paper presents a threat modelling methodology tailored to IIoT supply chain architectures, extending traditional STRIDE analysis with supply-chain-specific threat categories including firmware substitution, third-party library poisoning, and vendor credential reuse. A reference IIoT architecture involving a six-tier supply chain is modelled, and attack graphs are constructed to identify the most probable lateral movement pathways between tiers. Quantitative risk scores are assigned using a modified CVSS-based scoring system adapted for operational technology contexts. The analysis reveals that firmware update channels and remote maintenance interfaces constitute the highest-risk lateral movement vectors. Mitigation recommendations include cryptographic firmware signing, role-based access segmentation across supply chain tiers, and continuous behavioural monitoring of maintenance sessions. The framework is validated through a tabletop exercise with industrial practitioners.

SYN-PUB-10528.title: Network segmentation strategies for securing legacy OT environments
SYN-PUB-10528.text:
Network segmentation strategies for securing legacy OT environments (2021, conference, International Conference on Industrial Cybersecurity (ICICS 2021)).
Authors: Dragan Kovač (outside co-author); Ivana Jovanović (outside co-author); Vuk Đukić (R1015).
Keywords: network segmentation; OT security; industrial control systems; network security; legacy systems.
Operational technology environments in manufacturing and utility sectors frequently rely on decades-old equipment designed without cybersecurity considerations. Retrofitting strong security controls onto such systems is often impractical, making network segmentation one of the most effective available defences. This paper systematically evaluates five segmentation strategies—air-gapping, DMZ insertion, unidirectional gateways, micro-segmentation using software-defined networking, and VLAN-based isolation—across three representative legacy OT environments modelled after real-world process control architectures. Each strategy is assessed against a standardised threat catalogue derived from known ICS incident reports, covering scenarios such as ransomware propagation, historian server compromise, and remote access exploitation. The evaluation employs a simulation-driven methodology combining network topology modelling with attack path analysis. Results indicate that micro-segmentation combined with unidirectional gateways at critical zone boundaries provides the highest resilience against multi-stage attacks, though at significant configuration complexity. The paper provides a practical scoring matrix to assist security engineers in selecting segmentation approaches based on available resources and operational constraints.

SYN-PUB-10529.title: Detecting replay attacks on DNP3 protocol in smart grid communications
SYN-PUB-10529.text:
Detecting replay attacks on DNP3 protocol in smart grid communications (2020, conference, Workshop on Security of Cyber-Physical Systems (SCPS 2020)).
Authors: Nemanja Filipović (outside co-author); Stefan Lazić (outside co-author); Vuk Đukić (R1015).
Keywords: DNP3; replay attacks; smart grid; intrusion detection; network security.
DNP3 is a widely deployed communication protocol in smart grid environments, facilitating data exchange between substations, remote terminal units, and control centres. Despite extensions introduced in DNP3 Secure Authentication version 5, many deployments remain vulnerable to replay attacks due to misconfiguration or the use of older protocol variants. This paper presents a lightweight detection mechanism for DNP3 replay attacks based on temporal sequence analysis of application-layer message fields. The proposed detector monitors request-response timing patterns, sequence counter consistency, and message fragment ordering to identify anomalous retransmission behaviour indicative of replay activity. The mechanism is implemented as a passive network probe requiring no modifications to existing field devices. Evaluation on a hardware-in-the-loop smart grid testbed shows that the detector correctly identifies replay attacks with 97.3% precision and 95.8% recall, while maintaining a processing latency below 12 milliseconds per packet—well within operational requirements. The paper further discusses integration of the detector into existing security information and event management pipelines used in utility control centres.

SYN-PUB-10531.title: Intrusion detection in resource-constrained IoT devices using lightweight recurrent models
SYN-PUB-10531.text:
Intrusion detection in resource-constrained IoT devices using lightweight recurrent models (2024, journal, IEEE Internet of Things Journal).
Authors: Vuk Đukić (R1015); Milena Ostojić (outside co-author); Rastko Mirković (outside co-author).
Keywords: IoT security; intrusion detection; recurrent neural networks; resource-constrained devices; anomaly detection.
Deploying intrusion detection directly on resource-constrained IoT devices such as microcontroller-based sensors and actuators presents fundamental challenges in terms of memory footprint, computational overhead, and energy consumption. This paper investigates the feasibility of implementing lightweight recurrent neural network models—specifically truncated LSTM and GRU variants—on devices with fewer than 256 KB of RAM. A model compression pipeline is developed that combines quantisation, pruning, and knowledge distillation to reduce model size by up to 94% relative to full-precision baselines, while preserving detection accuracy above 90% across standard IoT attack benchmarks. The compressed models are deployed on three representative IoT platforms and evaluated under realistic workload conditions. Power consumption measurements indicate that continuous on-device inference adds less than 4 mW overhead, making deployment feasible even on battery-powered nodes. The paper also proposes an adaptive inference strategy that dynamically reduces model complexity during high-load periods to prevent resource exhaustion. Results suggest that on-device intrusion detection is practically achievable for a broad class of constrained IoT deployments.

SYN-PUB-10624.title: Measuring Knowledge Transfer in Post-Training Environments: Instrument Development and Validation for Manufacturing Contexts
SYN-PUB-10624.text:
Measuring Knowledge Transfer in Post-Training Environments: Instrument Development and Validation for Manufacturing Contexts (2015, journal, Andragogical Studies: European Journal for Adult Education Research).
Authors: Tanja Simić (R1027); Dragan Lazić (outside co-author); Bojana Ristić (outside co-author).
Keywords: knowledge transfer; scale validation; manufacturing; adult training; psychometrics.
The study reports on the development and psychometric validation of the Technical Knowledge Transfer Scale (TKTS), a 34-item self-report instrument designed to capture knowledge application behaviours three months after formal training completion. Scale items were generated through expert panel review (n=9 practitioners and academics) and iteratively refined across two pilot rounds involving 87 trainees in Serbian manufacturing companies. The final instrument was validated on a sample of 241 participants from seven companies in the Vojvodina region. Exploratory and confirmatory factor analyses yielded a four-factor structure: procedural recall, contextual adaptation, peer knowledge sharing, and error detection. Internal consistency was acceptable across all subscales (Cronbach's α = 0.71–0.84). Criterion validity was established against supervisor performance ratings. The TKTS is made available under an open licence for use in non-commercial research and training evaluation projects.

SYN-PUB-10625.title: Comparing Classroom and Blended Delivery Formats for Technical Upskilling Programmes: A Quasi-Experimental Study
SYN-PUB-10625.text:
Comparing Classroom and Blended Delivery Formats for Technical Upskilling Programmes: A Quasi-Experimental Study (2017, conference, Proceedings of the Balkan Conference on Educational Technology and Adult Learning).
Authors: Tanja Simić (R1027); Nataša Horvat (outside co-author); Gábor Fekete (outside co-author).
Keywords: blended learning; CNC training; quasi-experiment; knowledge retention; delivery format.
This quasi-experimental study compared learning outcomes across three delivery formats—fully face-to-face, blended (40% online), and blended (70% online)—in a 60-hour technical upskilling programme for CNC machine operators. Participants (n=198) were drawn from four companies in Novi Sad and Subotica. Pre-training, immediate post-training, and 12-week follow-up assessments were administered using structured practical tests and the TKTS instrument developed in previous work. At immediate post-test, no statistically significant differences were found between formats (F(2,195)=1.42, p=0.24). At 12-week follow-up, learners in the 40% online condition showed higher retention scores than the fully face-to-face group (Cohen's d=0.31). Learner satisfaction was highest in the face-to-face condition. The findings suggest that moderate blending can support retention without sacrificing learner acceptance, provided that the online components align tightly with hands-on procedural content.

SYN-PUB-10626.title: Competency Frameworks in Engineering Continuing Education: A Comparative Analysis of Accreditation Standards Across Four Countries
SYN-PUB-10626.text:
Competency Frameworks in Engineering Continuing Education: A Comparative Analysis of Accreditation Standards Across Four Countries (2019, book chapter, Continuing Engineering Education in Central and Eastern Europe (edited volume, University of Pécs Press)).
Authors: Tanja Simić (R1027); Ildikó Molnár (outside co-author); Lucian Bărbuță (outside co-author); Andrej Košir (outside co-author).
Keywords: competency frameworks; engineering CPD; accreditation; comparative analysis; cross-border recognition.
Continuing professional development programmes for engineers are governed by different accreditation bodies across Europe, resulting in heterogeneous competency frameworks that complicate cross-border recognition. This book chapter presents a comparative document analysis of accreditation standards in Serbia, Hungary, Romania, and Slovenia, focusing on how competency descriptors are articulated and at what level of specificity. A coding scheme of 48 categories was applied to 31 framework documents. Results indicate substantial variation in the granularity of behavioural descriptors: Serbian and Slovenian frameworks tend toward broad outcome statements, while Hungarian documents included more fine-grained task-level indicators. The chapter discusses implications for instructional designers who must map training content to multiple national standards and proposes a minimal harmonisation layer based on common descriptor patterns identified across all four frameworks.

SYN-PUB-10627.title: LMS Log Data as a Proxy for Learner Engagement in Technical Adult Courses: Possibilities and Limitations
SYN-PUB-10627.text:
LMS Log Data as a Proxy for Learner Engagement in Technical Adult Courses: Possibilities and Limitations (2021, journal, Journal of Technology-Enhanced Learning in Professional Contexts).
Authors: Tanja Simić (R1027); Stefan Đurić (outside co-author).
Keywords: LMS log data; learner engagement; Moodle; predictive analytics; GDPR.
Learning management systems generate detailed interaction logs that are increasingly used as indicators of learner engagement. This study assessed whether log-derived metrics—session frequency, resource access counts, forum contributions, and quiz attempt patterns—could predict knowledge transfer outcomes in a 12-week technical adult course delivered via Moodle at two Serbian employers. The dataset comprised 143 learners and 2.7 million log events. Regression analysis showed that session frequency (β=0.28, p<0.01) and repeated quiz attempts (β=0.19, p<0.05) significantly predicted post-training TKTS scores, but together explained only 19% of variance, indicating that log data captures a limited portion of the learning process. Resource access counts were not predictive after controlling for session frequency. The paper argues for combining log analytics with periodic self-report data rather than relying on logs alone, and proposes a data collection protocol compatible with GDPR constraints applicable in Serbian industry contexts.

SYN-PUB-10628.title: Designing Assessment Rubrics for Competency-Based IT Retraining Programmes: Lessons from a Cross-Sector Pilot
SYN-PUB-10628.text:
Designing Assessment Rubrics for Competency-Based IT Retraining Programmes: Lessons from a Cross-Sector Pilot (2022, journal, European Journal of Curriculum and Instructional Studies).
Authors: Tanja Simić (R1027); Maja Petrović (outside co-author); Tamara Varga (outside co-author).
Keywords: assessment rubrics; competency-based assessment; IT retraining; inter-rater reliability; action research.
This paper reports on a 14-month action research cycle in which assessment rubrics were developed, implemented, and iteratively revised for three IT retraining programmes targeting adult workers transitioning from non-IT sectors. The programmes were delivered in partnership with two training providers in Vojvodina and covered topics including database administration basics, network configuration, and software testing. A rubric design team comprising instructional designers, subject-matter experts, and HR representatives collaboratively authored dimension definitions and anchor descriptors. Rubrics were piloted with 94 participants; inter-rater reliability testing (using Cohen's weighted kappa) between trainer pairs ranged from κ=0.58 to κ=0.74 across dimensions, with procedural accuracy dimensions scoring most consistently. Post-pilot revision reduced ambiguous descriptors by 37% as rated by a blind review panel. The study highlights the central role of anchor examples drawn from authentic work tasks in achieving rater alignment, and provides a rubric template adaptable to other technical domains.

SYN-PUB-10629.title: Supervisor Involvement in Pre- and Post-Training Activities: Effect on Knowledge Application in Technical Workplaces
SYN-PUB-10629.text:
Supervisor Involvement in Pre- and Post-Training Activities: Effect on Knowledge Application in Technical Workplaces (2024, journal, Journal of Workplace Learning and Human Resource Development).
Authors: Tanja Simić (R1027); Petar Nikolić (outside co-author); Vesna Stanković (outside co-author).
Keywords: transfer of training; supervisor support; workplace learning; industrial training; field experiment.
Transfer of training research consistently identifies workplace environment as a stronger predictor of knowledge application than training design variables. This study examined the specific contribution of direct supervisor involvement—operationalised as pre-training briefing, goal-setting conversations, and post-training debriefs—to knowledge transfer outcomes among 167 employees completing mandatory safety and technical update courses at industrial firms in Novi Sad, Zrenjanin, and Kikinda. A three-group design compared workers whose supervisors received structured involvement prompts (n=58), those whose supervisors received only informational materials (n=54), and a no-intervention control (n=55). Six-week follow-up TKTS scores were significantly higher in the structured prompt group (M=3.61, SD=0.52) compared to control (M=3.14, SD=0.59; t(111)=4.87, p<0.001). Effect size was moderate (d=0.84). Cost analysis estimated that the supervisor preparation materials required approximately 45 minutes per cohort to administer, suggesting a favourable effort-to-outcome ratio for routine deployment in industrial training programmes.

SYN-PUB-10630.title: Aligning Micro-Credential Course Architecture with National Qualifications Framework Levels: A Practitioner's Guide for Serbian Training Providers
SYN-PUB-10630.text:
Aligning Micro-Credential Course Architecture with National Qualifications Framework Levels: A Practitioner's Guide for Serbian Training Providers (2025, preprint, EdArXiv Preprints).
Authors: Tanja Simić (R1027); Nataša Horvat (outside co-author).
Keywords: micro-credentials; national qualifications framework; non-formal education; Serbia; course design.
The Serbian National Qualifications Framework (SNQF) provides eight reference levels, but published guidance on how short non-formal courses should map their learning outcomes to these levels remains sparse. This preprint presents a step-by-step workflow developed and tested with six training providers in the ICT and construction sectors during 2024–2025. The workflow includes an outcome statement audit, a level-descriptor comparison matrix, an evidence documentation template, and a gap-closure planning sheet. Three providers completed the full workflow and submitted micro-credential programmes for SNQF referencing; two received recognition at level 4 and one at level 5. Feedback from accreditation reviewers at the National Qualifications Agency is included as anonymised commentary. The guide is intended as a working document for practitioners and will be revised following a broader consultation planned for late 2025.

W2906498146.title: DeepAnT: A Deep Learning Approach for Unsupervised Anomaly Detection in Time Series
W2906498146.text: IEEE Access, 2018. Traditional distance and density-based anomaly detection techniques are unable to detect periodic and seasonality related point anomalies which occur commonly in streaming data, leaving a big gap in time series anomaly detection in the current era of the IoT. To address this problem, we present a novel deep learning-based anomaly detection approach (DeepAnT) for time series data, which is equally applicable to the non-streaming cases. DeepAnT is capable of detecting a wide range of anomalies, i.e., point anomalies, contextual anomalies, and discords in time series data. In contrast to the anomaly detection methods where anomalies are learned, DeepAnT uses unlabeled data to capture and learn the data distribution that is used to forecast the normal behavior of a time series. DeepAnT consists of two modules: time series predictor and anomaly detector.
